Workspace.Name: AutomotiveRadar_FMCW_TDM-MIMO
Workspace.Description:
Automotive Radar FMCW MIMO Example

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

Simulation Task 

This workspace illustrates an Automotive Radar MIMO Radar FMCW-based (the Tx waveform in consecutive time slots) example with 4*4 MIMO radar architectures. The range, velocity and AoA (Angle Of Arrival) measurements are presented.

 

Workspace Description

 

This example is based on typical 3-layer radar simulation architecture. The baseband waveform design is based on TDM-FMCW MIMO radar design, with 4 Tx channels transmitting the FMCW waveform in consecutive 4-slot time range.

With 4 Rx channels, the radial range, radial velocity and AoA measurements are conducted, with results compared with preset values.

In this example, MIMO Radar antenna array is placed on X-Y plane (horizontally in x-axis for 1-D antenna array radar). Targets are placed in X-Z plane, and only the azimuth angle (AoA) is measured for 1-D antenna array radar. For each target, the measurement results are proposed as:

1.      Range: the radial distance between the antenna array center and the target in X-Z plane.

2.      Velocity: the radial velocity between radar and the target, only the velocity in the direction from radar antenna to the target.

3.      AoA:  target azimuth angle of arrival in X-Z plane.

 

Also after the simulation, the following diagram will be shown:

1.      Channel-1 Range-Doppler Spectrum Before CFAR

2.      Channel-1 Range-Doppler Spectrum After CFAR

3.      Target Positions in X-Y Coordinate (without velocity information)

 

The Step02-RangeDoppler_Spectrum_Plot equation displays Range-Doppler Spectrum and Step03-Target_XYCorr_Plot outputs target range diagrams in X-Y coordinates after the simulation.

 

All the parameters are defined in the Step01-System_Equations equation including:

1.      System parameters

2.      Antenna array parameters

3.      FMCW chirp parameters

4.      ADC/FFT/LNA parameters for receiver

5.      Phase Noise Parameters

6.      Target Parameter (for this example, two targets are placed)

 

In the schematic design, users can tune some of parameters defined in the Step01-System_Equations equation (also can use the sliding bars in the schematic design) as follows to easily observe the different results with various parameter settings

1.      Enable FFT window in Range-Doppler FFT or not

2.      Set RF Tx power

3.      Set transmit antenna setting mode with a fixed antenna gain or import a customized antenna pattern file

4.      Enable phase noise simulation or not (the actual phase noise data is defined in PN_Data variable in the Step01-System_Equations equation)

5.      Enable thermal noise or not

 

After the simulation is finished, the following results are shown in the text windows:

·         Target Range True Values

·         Target Range Measured Values

·         Target Velocity True Values

·         Target Velocity Measured Values

·         Target Angle True Values

·         Target Angle Measured Values

 

Note:

1.      If you are not familiar with the three-layer radar simulation architectures, please refer to other radar/automotive radar examples for more information.

 

2.      In current Rx design, there is no filter added before DownSample model to reduce the noise output of signal bandwidth. This is not the same as generic RF design noise floor changing and will decrease input noise level.

      To compensate the noise level, the noise added in AddNDensity model is set with an offset of (-10*log10(ADC_DS_Ratio)). If users want to add a filter to reduce the noise out of signal bandwidth, then they need to adjust measured range result by removing the filter delay introduced by the filter.

3.   There are two built-in functions applied in this example, one is DisplayRangeDopplerSpectrum() and the other is DisplayTargetsInXYCoordinate(). The function usage note is given here and please refer to the "Step02" and "Step03" equations for application details.

Workspace.Name: AutomotiveRadar_RayTracing_Demo
Workspace.Description:
Automotive Radar RayTracing Scenario Modeling

Double Car and Complex Scenarios

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

Simulation Task

This workspace demonstrates the detailed analysis using MRT (Multiple Ray Tracing) generated ray files for complex scenario modeling in automotive applications. In this workspace, two typical scenarios are provided, the 1st is the double car scenario, and the 2nd is the complex scenario of one typical realistic urban automotive driving condition.

 

For signal processing and target identification analysis, the example shows how to use MIMO antenna architecture (2T4R) to process the echo signal, obtain the target ranges, velocities and angles, also proposes method to generate the mmW multi-scatter point-cloud plot by predefined target peak searching algorithm. 

 

Please note that MRT scenario simulation is a two-step process. For the 1st step, the user is required to run the MRT complex scenario calculation in the MRT GUI (Tools -> Applications -> Ray Tracing Scenario Editor) to obtain the .bin file (contains radar and returned effective echo). The sample MRT scenario file and .bin ray echo files for the two-car and complex scenarios used in this workspace analysis are stored in the compressed packages for user evaluation.

 

For the 2nd step, the user applies SystemVue to run system-level analysis for overall system design and signal processing to evaluate complex scenario impacts on target detections. (Therefore, running this example requires licensing of both W1908 (Automotive Radar Design) and W1725 (Multiple Ray Tracing).)

 

Workspace Description

Ø Top level design

The workspace consists of four parts: transmitter, the MRT channel modeling, receiver and signal processing (target info extraction).

 

§  Transmitter Modeling

      In this part, the workspace specifies the waveform parameters in model AutomotiveRadar_CW, and divides the Tx signal to MIMO architecture by AutomotiveRadar_Tx_DBS_2D and AutomotiveRadar_MultiCH_Tx. The waveform related parameters are defined in the System_Level_Params Equation.

This workspace defines the waveform parameters as below:

The pulse width Tp = 25.6e-6,

The idle time TIdle = 4.4e-6,

The PRI = 30e-6,

The bandwidth = 200e6.

 

§  MRT Channel Modeling

      In this part, the workspace uses the model AutomotiveRadar_RayTracingChannel. The customer can customize the antenna parameters in this model, import different types of antenna pattern files, and apply the ray tracing file to generate the complex EM echo for further signal processing. The MIMO antenna architecture and phase shift calculations both at Tx and Rx are also addressed by this model.

 

The calculated ray echo and radar position data are in the DbCar/CplxSce_ProjectTracing_SystemVueRays.bin file, which are generated by the MRT GUI as explained above.

 

§  Receiver Modeling

      In this part, the receiver channels and architecture are established. For all four Rx channels, the mmW envelop type echo signal mixes with the local oscillator signal, hence it is down converted to near DC. The down converted signal sample rate is 10 MSPS, then the BLACKMAN windows are applied for all Rx channels data to perform 2D-FFT for range-doppler mapping.

§  Target Information Extraction

In this part, the workspace performs target detection and information extractions. Firstly, this block uses CFAR model to detect the target (CFAR type is SOCA, yet the best type for automotive radar would probably be the OS). The peak searching method is applied to find all the effective scatters, and the matlab script RVAMes model is designed to extract the target ranges, velocities and planar AoA angles (all in the dimensions of effective received number of target scatters).

 

NOTE:

1, The workspace uses the Range-Doppler Plot and Target Scatter Plot equation to plot the range doppler spectrum result and the target multi-scatter distributions (point-cloud like responses).

2, The MRT scenario file for this example is attached for the user to run ray tracing echo analysis in the MRT GUI. (Please extract the RayTracing result file (.bin) from the compression file using the 7-zip SW before running this simulation example.)

Workspace.Name: AutomotiveRadar_RayTracing_SignalVerification
Workspace.Description:
Automotive Radar Ray Tracing

Signal Verification Example

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

Simulation Task

This workspace illustrates how to evaluate the MRT (Multiple Ray Tracing, W1725) computation accuracy by both the radar range equation on received power, and comparisons between the MRT measured PEC (PerfEct Conductor) Sphere RCS values. Both methods have shown that MRT calculation results are in close agreement with theoretical values.

 

Workspace Description

Ø Top level design

Firstly, the verification scenario is established by MRT GUI, and the sphere with radius of 0.1m is imported into the MRT GUI calculation scenario. The sphere is set at 1000 meter’s range from the radar aperture to guarantee the far field condition. The scenario file name is MRT_Signal_Verification.ema.

 

§  Waveform/Transmitter Modeling

 

In this part, the workspace specifies the waveform parameters in model AutomotiveRadar_CW. The radar waveform parameters are:

The pulse width Tp = 51.2e-6 sec;

The idle time TIdle = 8.8e-6 sec;

The PRI = 60e-6 sec;

The bandwidth = 200e6 Hz.

Other generic parameter definitions are made in the System_Level_Params Equation.

 

§  MRT Channel Modeling

 

In this part, the workspace uses the model AutomotiveRadar_RayTracingChannel. The customer can customize the antenna parameters in this model, import different type antenna pattern file, and import the ray tracing file to generate the complex EM echo. The calculated MRT echo and returned ray result data are in the ProjectTracing_SystemVueRays.bin file.

 

In this example, we provide two modes to verify the radar equation and RCS.

 

The 1st mode is the “Isotropic” TRx antenna mode, for which we define both Tx and Rx antenna gains as 1 or 0 dB.

 

The 2nd mode is the “Pattern Imported” mode, for which we use external Tx and Rx antenna pattern files, and the antenna gains should be defined manually. (In this case we use their boresight maximum gain values of 6.507 dB, since the radar aperture is pointing to the PEC sphere along its boresight direction (Use MRT GUI to view the scenario for details.))

 

§  Receiver Modeling

 

In this part, the receiver channels and architecture are defined. The echo signal mixes with the local oscillator signal, and the beat signal max frequency is lowered down near DC. In the subnet BeatFreq model the beat signal is down sampled to 10e6 SPS sample rate, then the receiving channels data performs 1D/Range FFT. For both antenna characterization modes, the Range graph displays that the PEC target is detected at 999.75m.

 

Please note that there is a separate auto-cal equation (RangeAxis), and a separate parameter “FIRTapNum” in the System_Level_Params equation. This is the fixed inherent delay caused by the FIR filter, and we use an offset RangeAxis to display the correct ranges of detected targets for the MRT results.

 

§  Received Power, RCS and Range Verifications

 

In this part, we designed two equations to verify both the received power (by radar range equation) and calculated PEC sphere RCS.

 

From Step01_Radar_Equation_Verification equation, user could look at the method to compare the standard received power from radar range equation and the actual received power from MRT results. For mode-2, the power difference is less than 0.2 dB. (The equation will report warning if difference is larger than 0.5 dB.)

 

From Step02_PECSphere_RCS_Verification equation, user could observe RCS differences between theoretical values and calculated values from MRT results. For mode-2, the RCS difference is about 0.14 dB (The equation will report warning if RCS error is larger than 0.5 dB). Also this equation calculates the range error, which would also be very small.

Workspace.Name: AutomotiveRadar_PhaseNoise_Basic
Workspace.Description:
Automotive Radar Phase Noise Impairment Example

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

Simulation Task 

This workspace illustrates an Automotive FMCW-based Radar example with phase noise impairment modeling capabilities.

Workspace Description

This example is from a typical customer requirement that phase noise impairment is critical for automotive radar applications.

Firstly, phase noise is modeled with mixer and modulator parts with different configurations but almost identical phase noise modeling results, both in Time Domain and Freq Domain.

Secondly, as most automotive radar Tx is based on PLL+VCO architecture, phase noise modeling with VCO is proposed. Because of part functional limitations, VCO voltage tuning and phase noise modeling are represented by the modulator part. Phase noise modeling results are given in Time Domain.

For both cases, phase noise settings are done in the oscillator part.

Note:

Please run the simulation and refer to the figures for a clearer understanding of phase noise modeling results.

Workspace.Name: AutomotiveRadar_PhaseNoise_TarMasking
Workspace.Description:
Automotive Radar Phase Noise Target Masking Example

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

Simulation Task 

This workspace illustrates an Automotive FMCW-based Radar example with phase noise impairment modeling capabilities, and compares two cases with distinct transmitter VCO phase noise levels.

Target masking effects in Range-Doppler spectrum plots are clearly demonstrated.

Workspace Description

This example is designed to address phase noise impairment impacts on automotive radar target detection performances.

Firstly, phase noise is modeled with modulator model to simulate PLL+VCO-based transmitter architectures with phase noise capabilities.

Secondly, two 1Tx-1Rx pairs are realized in the schematic design. The light blue blocks show the pair with a good phase noise profile (No Phase Noise, NPN case), while the magenta blocks show the other pair with worse phase noise profile (With Phase Noise, PN case).

The RCS data are taken from the HRL Lab & General Motors measured results (Scenario-02 in VehicleScenario.wsv workspace). The nearest target is a truck with highest RCS and lowest velocity. The other two vehicles with longer distances are one van and one sedan.

We use the 2D-FFT 3D plots to demonstrate phase noise impacts on the noise floor levels. For the NPN case, the floor is covered by dark blue colors (under -55 dB approx.), while for the PN case, the noise floor around the two targets is dominated by light green colors (up to -40 dB approx.).

Regarding the target peaks, for the NPN figure, three peaks are clearly visible, while for the PN case, only the truck (nearest to radar and with highest RCS) could be discernable while the other two targets with weaker returns are barely visible and buried under the noise floor.

For CFAR and binary detection results, for both NPN and PN cases, only the truck is detected.

Range-Doppler Plotting Note

A generic 2D-FFT (Range-Doppler) spectrum plotting function is BUILT-IN for Automotive Radar Library and typical calling codes are given in "Step03_Range-Doppler_Plot" equation file.

The user is advised to try customized cases specifically for the dedicated radar design. For instance, if the target ranges are much further, the phase noise impacts on 2D-FFT noise floor (low SNR cases) could be insignificant, while target masking are governed by other factors such as range attenuation or thermal noise floor. 

For both cases, phase noise settings are done in the Step02_System_Equation file, and the profile vector is transferred to Tx_VCO_UpConv subnet.

Please run the Step01 and Step02 first, then run the simulation and the Range_Doppler_Plot for simulation analysis and 2D-FFT figure plotting.

References:

 

1, K.Geary, Joseph S. Colburn, etc., (Joint work by HRL Lab and General Motors), Automotive Radar Target Characterization from 22 to 29 GHz and 76 to 81 GHz, IEEE Radar Conference, 2013.

Workspace.Name: AutomotiveRadar_RFImpairment_Tx2LvlUpConv
Workspace.Description:
Automotive Radar AoA measurement with TRx RF Impairments

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Workspace

 

Simulation Task

This workspace illustrates an Automotive Radar AoA (Angle of Arrival) measurement system with typical TRx RF impairments enabled with behavior models. The traditional 2-level upconversion Tx architecture is modeled, then beat frequency is used for target detection then AoA measurements are performed.

 

Workspace Description

  • Top level design

The workspace consists of three layers.

·        Trajectory Layer

In this layer, the Tx radar platform and Rx radar platform is defined using AutomotiveRadar_Platform model. In this scenario, Tx radar and Rx radar is both at origin point of cartesian coordinates. And two targets' position is defined using AutomotiveRadar_TargetScatterLocation model. One target is at (-5,0,8.66) and the other is at (1, 0, 20). 

·        Antenna Layer

In this layer, AutomotiveRadar_LocInAntennaFrame model is used to calculate the targets' antenna theta and phi degree.

In this scenario, XY-Plane antenna frame is used. It means that, the antenna array is positioned at XY-Plane. X axis is along horizontal orientation and Y axis is along vertical orientation. And the beam radiates along +Z axis.

So, in this XY-Plane,

·        The antenna theta of target (-5, 0, 8.66) is 30 degrees and its AoA is -30 degrees.

·        The antenna theta of target (1, 0, 20) is 2.86 degree and its AoA is 2.86 degree.

·        Signal Processing Layer

In this layer, mmW automotive radar TRx are modeled, then AoA measurements are performed. The user may alter phase noise, noise floor, IF/RF PA/LNA/Mixer and filter parameters to investigate corresponding impacts on AoA measurement results. 

 

To observe RF impairment modeling results more clearly, the general architectures are introduced below for each sub-system as:

·        System_Equations:

o   All system-level parameters are set in this equation file at the highest level (workspace level) to avoid confusing parametric definitions in different locations (workspace level, design level, schematic parameter/equation pages)

·        Baseband signal generation:

o   AutomotiveRadar_CW model is used to generate one kind of linear FMCW signal with PRI of 61.2 us, bandwidth of 500 MHz, then with Tx modeling the BB signal is upconverted to mmW carrier frequency of 77 GHz.

o   The Chirp duration is 51.2 us, and in the Rx side signal processing the signals are chopped accordingly. 

·        Tx RF modeling:

o   2-level upconversion modeling is proposed, with modulator to generate IF signal and Mixer to generate RF signal at 77 GHz.

o   Noise densities (AddNDensity), Amplifiers and Filters are used in Tx for impairment modeling.

·        Free-space signal propagation and receiving:

o   Tx Antenna: AntennaArray Tx is used to setup the transmit antenna. In this scenario, two Tx element antennas are used, so the parameter of TxNum_H and TxNum_V is set as to 2 & 1. All Targets' antenna theta and phi from Antenna Layer are as input of the Tx antenna model.

o   Target Echo Generation: AutomotiveRadar_EchoGenerator model is used to generate all targets' echo. The position of all targets and radar platform from Trajectory Layer is as its input.

o   Rx Antenna:AntennaArray Rx is used to setup the transmit antenna. In this scenario, 4 antenna elements in horizontal orientation are used, so RxNum_H is set as 4; RxNum_V is set as 1. All Targets' antenna theta and phi from Antenna Layer are as input of the Rx antenna model.

o   Please note that for the AoA algorithm in this example, Rx antennas can only be plotted as one dimensional array in H(horizontal).

·        Rx RF modeling: traditional beat-frequency target detection is provided for each Rx channel.

o   Beat Frequency: Each Rx element is connected to Amplifier and then IQ Mixer to down-convert Rx signals to obtain the beat frequencies. The CH1 RF TRx and beat frequency spectrum graphs are shown.

o   ADC: The SampleRate of this design is set as 1.2 GSas, DownSampler is used prior to ADC block to get real ADC sampling rate. In this scenario, the ADC_Rx. Fs is set as 40 MSas. The user could set clock phases, jitter, nonlinearity, SNR, SINAD, etc. for ADC distortion modeling.

o   Pre- & Post ADC filters are also provided for user control for spectrum observations.

·        AoA measurements:

o   RangeFFT Subnet: FFT_Cx processor is used to get the frequency domain data of beat frequencies.

o   CFAR Subnet(CH1 ONLY): AutomotiveRadar_Detector, AutomotiveRadar_CFAR and AutomotiveRadar_BinaryDetector are used to cancel the noise. The RangeFFT & CFAR graph is provided for quick checks on target detection results.

o   Average Phase Difference: The phase difference between every two adjacent antenna elements are calculated and then averaged by the channel numbers.

o   AoA measurement: One MATLAB script model AoAMeasurement is used to calculate all targets’' AoA.

o   AoA display and visualization: realized by the Equation_AoACalc Equation file in each file, by default it is set to auto-calculate. Please ignore any related errors at workspace launches.

  • Note

RF impairment modeling and dynamic range tuning may seem tricky, observations by sink/spectrum analyzer at each component output may be required to ensure valid target detection (CFAR) results. In general, RF parameter changes would result in slight AoA result variations.

The user could also change the target information (distance, location, No. of targets, etc.) to evaluate other automotive radar test scenarios.

Please refer to section III. PHASE DIFFERENCE OF ARRIVAL in reference [1] for basic concept.

Reference

[1] HH. C. Chen, T. H. Lin, H. T. Kung, C. K. Lin and Y. Gwon, "Determining RF angle of arrival using COTS antenna arrays: A field evaluation," MILCOM 2012 - 2012 IEEE Military Communications Conference, Orlando, FL, 2012, pp. 1-6.

Workspace.Name: AutomotiveRadar_RFImpairment_TxVCO
Workspace.Description:
Automotive Radar AoA measurement with TRx RF Impairments

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Workspace

 

Simulation Task

This workspace illustrates an Automotive Radar AoA (Angle of Arrival) measurement system with typical TRx RF impairments enabled with behavior models. The VCO-based RF Tx is modeled, then beat frequency is used for target detection then AoA measurements are performed.

 

Workspace Description

  • Top level design

The workspace consists of three layers.

·        Trajectory Layer

In this layer, the Tx radar platform and Rx radar platform is defined using AutomotiveRadar_Platform model. In this scenario, Tx radar and Rx radar is both at origin point of cartesian coordinates. And two targets' position is defined using AutomotiveRadar_TargetScatterLocation model. One target is at (-5,0,8.66) and the other is at (1, 0, 20). 

·        Antenna Layer

In this layer, AutomotiveRadar_LocInAntennaFrame model is used to calculate the targets' antenna theta and phi degree.

In this scenario, XY-Plane antenna frame is used. It means that, the antenna array is positioned at XY-Plane. X axis is along horizontal orientation and Y axis is along veritical orientation. And the beam radiates along +Z axis.

So in this XY-Plane,

·        The antenna theta of target (-5, 0, 8.66) is 30 degrees and its AoA is -30 degrees.

·        The antenna theta of target (1, 0, 20) is 2.86 degree and its AoA is 2.86 degree.

·        Signal Processing Layer

In this layer, mmW automotive radar TRx are modeled, then AoA measurements are performed. The user may alter phase noise, noise floor, IF/RF PA/LNA/Mixer and filter parameters to investigate corresponding impacts on AoA measurement results. 

 

To observe RF impairment modeling results more clearly, the general architectures are introduced below for each sub-system as:

·        System_Equations:

o   All system-level parameters are set in this equation file at the highest level (workspace level) to avoid confusing parametric definitions in different locations (workspace level, design level, schematic parameter/equation pages)

·        Baseband signal generation:

o   AutomotiveRadar_CW model is used to generate one kind of linear FMCW signal with PRI of 61.2 us, bandwidth of 500 MHz, then with Tx modeling the BB signal is upconverted to mmW carrier frequency of 77 GHz.

o   The Chirp duration is 51.2 us, and in the Rx side signal processing the signals are chopped accordingly. 

·        Tx RF modeling:

o   VCO + PA modeling is proposed, with VCO to generate RF signal and PA to amplify RF signal at 77 GHz.

o   VCO, Noise densities (AddNDensity), Amplifiers and Filters are used in Tx for impairment modeling.

·        Free-space signal propagation and receiving:

o   Tx Antenna: AntennaArray Tx is used to setup the transmit antenna. In this scenario, two Tx element antennas are used, so the parameter of TxNum_H and TxNum_V is set as to 2 & 1. All Targets' antenna theta and phi from Antenna Layer are as input of the Tx antenna model.

o   Target Echo Generation: AutomotiveRadar_EchoGenerator model is used to generate all targets' echo. The position of all targets and radar platform from Trajectory Layer is as its input.

o   Rx Antenna:AntennaArray Rx is used to setup the transmit antenna. In this scenario, 3 antenna elements in horizontal orientation are used, so RxNum_H is set as 3; RxNum_V is set as 1. All Targets' antenna theta and phi from Antenna Layer are as input of the Rx antenna model.

o   Please note that for the AoA algorithm in this example, Rx antennas can only be plotted as one dimentional arrary in H(horizontal).

·        Rx RF modeling: traditional beat-frequency target detection is provided for each Rx channel.

o   Beat Frequency: Each Rx element is connected to Amplifier and then IQ Mixer to down-convert Rx signals to obtain the beat freqencies. The CH1 RF TRx and beat frequency spectrum graphs are shown.

o   ADC: The SampleRate of this design is set as 1.2 GSas, DownSampler is used prior to ADC block to get real ADC sampling rate. In this secnario, the ADC_Rx.Fs is set as 40 MSas. The user could set clock phases, jitter, nonlinearity, SNR, SINAD, etc for ADC distortion modeling.

o   Pre & Post ADC filters are also provided for user control for spectrum observations.

·        AoA measurements:

o   RangeFFT Subnet: FFT_Cx processor is used to get the frequency domain data of beat frequencies.

o   CFAR Subnet(CH1 ONLY): AutomotiveRadar_Detector, AutomotiveRadar_CFAR and AutomotiveRadar_BinaryDetector are used to cancel the noise. The RangeFFT & CFAR graph is provided for quick checks on target detection results.

o   Average Phase Difference: The phase difference between every two adjacent antenna elements are calculated and then averaged by the channel numbers.

o   AoA measurement: One MATLAB script model AoAMeasurement is used to calculate all targets’' AoA.

o   AoA display and visualization: realized by the Equation_AoACalc Equation file in each file, by default it is set to auto-calculate. Please ignore any related errors at workspace launches.

  • Note

RF impairment modeling and dynamic range tuning may seem tricky, observations by sink/spectrum analyzer at each component output may be required to ensure valid target detection (CFAR) results. In general, RF parameter changes would result in slight AoA result variations.

The user could also change the target information (distance, location, No. of targets, etc) to evaluate other automotive radar test scenarios.

Workspace.Name: MIMO_SM_STC_BER_Test
Workspace.Description:
MIMO_SM_STC_BER

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This example workspace demonstrates uncoded BER performance for basic MIMO and STC transmitter and receiver under Rayleigh Fading Channel.

 

For MIMO SM (Spatial Multiplexing) mode, multiple symbol streams are transmitted over antennas. In the receiver side, the MIMO decoder model is to recover the symbols with different decoder methods. In general, the ML method has the best performance, and non-linear SIC (Successive Interference Cancellation) with ZF and MMSE has the suboptimal performance. At last the traditional linear method with ZF and MMSE has worst performance.

In this workspace, simulation results for SM 2x2 QPSK system with different methods have been provided.

 

For TD (Transmit Diversity) mode, the same symbol is transmitted on all antennas, so the symbol rate is not increased compared to SISO case. In this release, NumTx only supports 2 and 4, and the precoding matrix defined in 6.3.4.3 of 36.211 for LTE is used in this example for both NumTx=2 and NumTx=4.

 

To run the simulation, please follow the instructions below.

1.       Define MIMO antennal configurations. Set the NumTx and NumRx parameters. For SM mode, NumRx should be equal to or greater than NumRx. For TD, mode, currently NumTx just supports 2 and 4, and NumRx could be any value.

2.       Set the transmission mode, from TD or SM.

3.       Set the modulation type for the symbols. The types supported is the same as the types defined in the Mapper model.

4.       For SM mode, select the decoder method, and SNR value which is required by some methods, such as Linear MMSE and SIC MMSE.

5.       Set the number of symbols (samples) for the simulation.

6.       All of above are set in the Parameter tab of the MIMO_STC_SM_Fading design. At last, set the SNR sweep points.

 

In the meanwhile, the SISO_AWGN_Fading design is provided for SISO uncoded BER performance under Rayleigh Fading Channel and AWGN Channel as a comparison.

Workspace.Name: 3GPPFDD_BS_Rx_ACS
Workspace.Description:
3GPP FDD: BS Rx Adjacent Channel Selectivity (ACS)

Keysight Technologies SystemVue 

 

This example measures BS receiver characteristics: Adjacent Channel Selectivity (ACS).

This measurement is defined in section 7.4 of 3GPP specification TS.25.104.

1. The UL reference measurement channel includes DPCCH and DPDCH, and DPCCH/DPDCH=0.7333.

2. The wanted signal is calibrated to be -115 dBm. The modulated interfering signal is a WCDMA signal

with one code. Its power is -52 dBm and is 5 MHz away from center frequency. BER of DTCH and DCCH shall be better than 0.1%.

The DPDCH BER is the BER of data after the CCTrCh multiplexer.

3. Users can set up the system parameters or replace a component according to their particular requirements.

4. The simulation results are shown in Table Design1_BER.

5. The simulation time is about 2 minutes on a Core 2 Duo 2.4G/2G PC, powered by SystemVue 2010 and Windows XP.

Workspace.Name: 3GPPFDD_BS_Tx_ACLR
Workspace.Description:
3GPP FDD: BS ACLR (Adjacent Channel Leakage Power Ratio) measurement:

 

This example measures ACLR (Adjacent Channel Leakage Power Ratio) of the downlink signal.
This measurement is defined in section 6.6.2.2 of 3GPP specification TS.25.104.

 

1. The test model 1 includes 16/32/64 DPCH channels, one PICH channel, one Primary CPICH channel and one PCCPCH+SCH channel. One SCCPCH is included in the test model 1 in the version 2002-03. The spreading factor of DPCH channel is 128.

 

2. ACLR_FilterBank contains the receiver side filters for the main and adjacent upper and lower channels. U5 is upper 5 MHz, U10 is upper 10 MHz, L5 is lower 5 MHz, L10 is lower 10 MHz.

 

3. Carrier Frequency is 2140MHz, Signal Power is 10dBm.

Specification ACLR requirements:

+5 MHz or -5 MHz

45 dB

+10 MHz or -10 MHz

50 dB

If the adjacent channel power is greater than -50dBm, then the ACLR shall be higher than the above value.

 

4. The simulated channels power values can be found in Table "Channel Powers".

The simulated ACLR values can be found in Table "ACLR".

Workspace.Name: 3GPPFDD_ConvCode_BER
Workspace.Description:
3GPP Channel Decoding: Rate 1/2 and 1/3 Convolutional Coding

Keysight Technologies SystemVue 

 

1. This design tests the 3GPP convolutional coding performance over AWGN channel.

2. The random bit stream is generated and convolutional coded by the ChannelCoding model, then it's modulated as antipodal signals. The channel is AWGN channel.

3. The coding block size and number of blocks to be coded depend on the transport format specified. For specific transport format, model 3GPPFDD_TrCH_Cal can be used to calculate the block size and block number.

4. The results are displayed by Designs_Data_Display.

5. The simulation time is about 3 minutes by a Core 2 Duo 2.4G/2G PC, powered by SystemVue 2010 and Windows XP.

Workspace.Name: 3GPPFDD_DL_2fingers_Rake
Workspace.Description:
Two Fingers DownLink Rake Receiving

 

1.

In this example, only DPCH data is used for rake receiving. After spreading and scrambling, the DPCH data goes through RRC shaping filter and two fingers channel, and then is received by 3GPPFDD_DL_rake model.

 

2.

The parameters for two fingers channel and AWGN noise can be set in Equation of Schematic.

 

Parameters: 

 

SNR

Setting SNR (dB) to control AWGN noise power. Signal power is controlled to 1.

Path1Gain

Setting gain of path1.

Path1Delay

Setting delay of path 1.

Path2Gain

Setting gain of path2.

Path2Delay

Setting delay of path2.

 

For the two fingers channel, the total channel gain is normalized to keep the signal power is 1 after going through the channel.

                                  

3.

In 3GPPFDD_DL_Rake model, you can select two receiving modes -- ChannInfo Known or ChannInfo Estimated.

    

Chann Known

The channel information is known, and you need input channel information to this model.

In Equation of Schematic, you should set parameter "ChannelInfo" to 0. In addition, you should set parameter "PathNum" as 2 to represent channel path number and set "PathDelaySample" to represent delay samples numbers of the two paths.

Note: there is a constant 128 samples delay caused by RRC shaping filter.

From "inChM" input pin, the gain of two paths should be inputted.

Chann Estimated

The channel information is estimated.

In Equation of Schematic, you should set parameter "ChannelInfo" to 1. In addition, you should set parameter "PathNum" as 2 to represent channel path number and set "PathDelaySample" to [0,0], which the path gain and delay will be estimated by 3GPPFDD_DL_rake model.

 

4.

In "Two_Fingers_Rake_Table", 1 frame estimation outputs of 3GPPFDD_DL_Rake are listed.

 

SlotIndex

Index of slot. There are 15 slots in a frame. So it is 0~14.

Path1_Delay_out

Output delay samples number of path1.

Path2_Delay_out

Output delay samples number of path2.

DPCH_SNR_Combined_dB

Estimated SNR of signal that combines two paths, unit is dB.

DPCH_SNR_Path1_dB

Estimated SNR of path1 signal, unit is dB.

DPCH_SNR_Path2_dB

Estimated SNR of path2 signal, unit is dB.

Path1ChM_slot

Channel gain of path1 for each slot.

Path2ChM_slot

Channel gain of path2 for each slot.

       

Note: For ChannInfo Estimated mode, these values are estimated by 3GPPFDD_DL_Rake model. Output of these values have "SearchSlotsNum" slots delay. For ChannInfo Known mode, these values are gotten from input parameters. Output of these values have 1 slot delay.

 

5.

3GPPFDD_DL_Rake model does descrambling, despreading and MRC combining, and then it outputs DPCH bits. Because the output bits need align with the boundary of frame, it is delayed 1 frame (15 slots). A comparison between original bits and received bits has been done. The difference between the two sequences is "DPCH_Compare" in "Two_Fingers_Rake_Data".

Workspace.Name: 3GPPFDD_UE_Rx_RefLevel
Workspace.Description:
3GPP FDD: UE Rx Reference Sensitivity Level

Keysight Technologies SystemVue 

 

This example measures UE receiver characteristics: Reference Sensitivity Level. This measurement is defined in section 7.3 of 3GPP specification TS.25.101 v3.5.0.

1. The down link signal source includes the 12.2 kbps reference measurement channel, PCCPCH, PSCH, SSCH, CPICH and PICH.

2. The gain factors are: CPICH_Ec/DPCH_Ec=7 dB, PCCPCH_Ec/DPCH_Ec=5 dB, SCH_Ec/DPCH_Ec=5 dB, PICH_Ec/DPCH_Ec=2 dB. These factors are given in Table E 3.2 of TS 34.121 version 3.3.0 annex E and assure DPCH_Ec/Ior to be -10.3 dB.

3. BER of DTCH and DCCH shall be better than 0.1%.

The DPCH BER is the BER of data after the CCTrCh multiplexer.

4. In this example 4 frames are simulated as demonstration. To obtain a reasonable BER results, more frames shall be tested.

5. Users can set up the system parameters or replace a component according to their particular requirements.

6. The simulation results are shown in Table Design1_BER.

7. The simulation time is about 1 minute on a Core 2 Duo 2.4G/2G PC, powered by SystemVue 2010 and Windows XP.

Workspace.Name: 3GPPFDD_UE_Tx_ACLR
Workspace.Description:
3GPP FDD: UE ACLR (Adjacent Channel Leakage Power Ratio) measurement:

 

This example measures the uplink ACLR, as  defined in section 6.6.2.2  of 3GPP specification TS.25.101.

 

1.

The UL reference measurement channel includes two code channels consisting of one 15kbps DPCCH and one 60kbps DPDCH. The spreading factor is 256 for the DPCCH and 64 for the DPDCH. One 2.4kbps and one 12.2kbps transport channel are multiplexed and mapped to DPDCH after rate matching and channel coding.

 

2.

ACLR_FilterBank contains the receiver side filters for the main and adjacent upper and lower channels. U5 is upper 5 MHz, U10 is upper 10 MHz, L5 is lower 5 MHz, L10 is lower 10 MHz.

 

3.

Carrier Frequency is 1950MHz, Signal Power is 24dBm.

Specification ACLR requirements:

+5 MHz or -5 MHz

33 dB

+10 MHz or -10 MHz

43 dB

If the adjacent channel power is greater than -50dBm, then the ACLR shall be higher than the above value.

 

4.

The simulated channels power values can be found in Table "Channel Powers".

The simulated ACLR values can be found in Table "ACLR".

Workspace.Name: BS_TX_VSA
Workspace.Description:
CDMA2K: Forward Source with VSA Demodulation

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Workspace

 

In this example, "CDMA2K_FwdRCsrc" subnet is used to generate CDMA2000 SR1 forward source signal. This subnet can generate Forward RC3, Forward RC4 and Forward RC5 source signals. Then the transmission signal can be demodulated by VSA. Using VSA, you can observe CDP(Code Domain Power), Spectrum, Composite Constellation, Composite EVM, Specific code channel EVM and Specific code channel constellation.

 

In this example, a traffic channel is transmitted on Walsh code index 8. Pilot channel is on Walsh code index 0; paging channel is on Walsh code index 1; synchronization channel is on Walsh code index 32. Besides, OCN (Orthogonal Channel Noise) is added to simulate the interference from other users.

 

You can set parameter "UserNum" and "RemoveOCN" in equation of Design1 schematic to control the simulation.

Parameter "UserNum" is the number of users.

Parameter "RemoveOCN", Yes: remove OCN (orthogonal channel noise); No: add OCN.

 

When you set "RemoveOCN" as Yes, OCN will not be added to composite signal. You can observe the improvement of EVM of traffic channel.

 

This example needs Keysight VSA 89600 software. You can find setup file "BS_TX_VSA.set" of VSA 89600 in the same directory as the workspace.

Workspace.Name: Forward_AWGN_RC3
Workspace.Description:
CDMA2K: Performance of forward traffic channel in AWGN channel

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Workspace

 

This example shows performances of a forward link for AWGN, RC3, 9600bps data rate, and 20ms frame. One pilot channel and one fundamental channel are included. It is assumed that pilot channel occupies 20% of total power and the fundamental channel occupies 3% of total power. The ratio of a traffic channel power to total power = (1 - ratio of pilot power to total power) / UserNum. No paging, sync channel and OCN (orthogonal channel noise) are added in this example.

 

In equation of Design1 Schematic, you can specify the following parameters to control the simulation:

 

Parameters

Description

DataRate

Data rate

RF_Freq

Carrier frequency

UserNum

The number of traffic channel users

 

BER and FER curves are drawn in figure "BER_Curve" and "FER_Curve" respectively. The red curves in both figures are theoretical bound under ideal condition. The blue curves are simulation results. The performance decrease of the simulation results is caused by channel estimation and power control bit puncture.

 

Simulation time: Core2 Duo CPU 3GHz, 1.96G memory, Windows XP, approximately 8.5 hours.

Workspace.Name: Forward_Rake
Workspace.Description:
CDMA2K: Forward link Rake Receiver

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Workspace

 

This example gives an application of forward link Rake receiver, including channel estimation, AFC loop and maximum ratio combination. A pilot channel and a traffic channel are included. No channel coding is used.

 

The transmission signal goes through a multipath Rayleigh fading channel and is added AWGN noise. You can specify the parameters (delay and coefficients) of each path by setting parameters of "CDMA2K_ClassicChannel" model.

 

In equation of Design1 Schematic, you can set the following parameters to control the simulation:

 

Parameters

Description

WalshLength

The length of Walsh code

TrifIndx

The index of Walsh code for traffic channel

EstiWin

Window size for estimating channel coefficients in terms of symbols

FingerNum

Specifying the number of fingers for rake receiver

EbN0_dB

Eb/n0 (unit: dB)

BER_Samples

The number of simulated samples for calculating BER

 

The delay and coefficient of each finger can be detected by "CDMA2K_FwdChnlEstimate" model. In "Design1_B4_BER" Table, the delays and coefficients of the three detected fingers are listed. Besides, BER is also shown in this table.

 

In figure "Design1_S1", the detected channel fingers information are drawn. The X-axis represents the detected fingers delay in terms of sampling periods. (Sampling period = 1/(4*1.2288e6) sec) The Y-axis represents the magnitude of corresponding fingers response.

Workspace.Name: MS_RX_AdjacentSelectivity_RC3
Workspace.Description:
CDMA2K: MS RX Adjacent Channel Selectivity Performance

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Workspace

 

This example verifies the ability to receive a CDMA signal on the assigned channel frequency in the presence of another CDMA signal that is offset from the center frequency of the assigned channel by 2.5 MHz for Spreading Rate 1, as defined in section 3.5.4 of 3GPP2 C.S0011-A.


1. Forward Pilot and Fundamental Channel are included.


2. Ec/Ior is -15.6 dB; Iorr is -101dBm/1.23MHz; Adjacent channel power density is -36dBm/1.23MHz;


3. Ec/Ior can be changed by setting User in CDMA2K_FwdRCsrc. When user = 19, Traffic Ec/Ior = ( 1-0.2(pilot) - 0.0471(sync) - 0.188(paging) )/19 * 11/12(power control bit) = -15.6db.

 

4. The FER in each test shall not exceed 1% with 95% confidence.


5. User can set up the system parameters or replace a component according to their particular requirements.

 

6. This test is applicable to Band Class 6 mobile stations only.


Simulation time: Intel Core2 Duo 3.0GHz ,1.96GB memory, Windows XP, approximately 1.5 hours.

Workspace.Description:
AM Suppression Measurements

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

This example demonstrates the test of the AM Suppression characteristics of BTS and MS receiver.

 

AM Suppression is a measure of the ability of the receiver to receive a modulated wanted input signal in the presence of an unwanted TDMA modulated interferer.

 

For BTS receiver test, please set the parameter ChannelType as Uplink data channel type, and the test is based on the specifications and requirements in 7.8 of 3GPP TS 51.021 and corresponding GSM / EDGE documents.

 

For MS receiver test, please set the parameter ChannelType as Downlink data channel type, and the test is based on the specifications and requirements in 14.8 of 3GPP TS 51.010-1 and corresponding GSM/EDGE documents.

 

 

The tests can be performed at any RF channels by set parameter ARFCN and run DF_AMSuppression. The measurement results are displayed in figure AMSuppression_Data.

 

The MS receiver with TCH/FS at 935.2 MHz is tested in this design as the default case. The wanted signal power and the unwanted signal power for this case is set by parameter Ps and PI in design Parameters field.

 

To test other cases of BTS and MS receiver, user should set parameters ChannelType, PI and Ps in design Parameters field according to the specifications. And then set the measurement RF channel in equation field and run it.

 

 

Test Benches:

Test condition: MS receiver with  TCH/FS with wanted signal power of -98dBm, unwanted GMSK interferer power of -31dBm

 

About 10 seconds in the machine with Intel Core2 Duo 2.4GHz, 4G RAM, Windows 7 system.

Workspace.Name: GSM_RxRefInterferenceLevel
Workspace.Description:
Reference interference level Measurements

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

This example demonstrates the test of the  reference interference level of BTS and MS receiver.

 

The reference interference level is a measure of the capability of the receiver to receive a wanted modulated signal without exceeding a given degradation due to the presence of an unwanted modulated signal at the same carrier frequency (co-channel interference) or at any adjacent carrier frequencies (adjacent channel interference).

 

For BTS receiver test, please set the parameter ChannelType as Uplink data channel type, and the test is based on the specifications and requirements in 7.5 of 3GPP TS 51.021 and corresponding GSM / EDGE documents. And the LinkDirection of fading channel model should be set to Reverse.

 

For MS receiver test, please set the parameter ChannelType as Downlink data channel type, and the test is based on the specifications and requirements in 14.18 of 3GPP TS 51.010-1 and corresponding GSM/EDGE documents. And the LinkDirection of fading channel model should be set to Forward.

 

 

The test can be performed at any RF channels by sweep parameter ARFCN and run SweepRxRefInterferenceLevel. The measurement results are displayed in SweepRxRefInterferenceLevel_BLER.

 

The BTS receiver with PDTCH/MCS5 at 890 MHz and in the presence of a co-channel interference is tested in this design as the default case. The wanted signal power and the unwanted signal power for this case is set by parameter Ps and PI in design Parameters field.

 

To test other cases of BTS and MS receiver, users should set parameters ChannelType, CtoIc and Ps in design Parameters feild and set the parameter Gain of model RF_Gain in schematic according to the specifications. 

 

To test adjacent channel interference, users can set the parameter FreqOffset_I according to the specifications. And then set the measurement RF channel in equation field and run it.

 

 

Test Benches:

Test condition: BTS receiver with  PDTCH/MCS5, Blocking Characteristics Measurement, FC 900MHz on B, M and T.

About  16 minutes in the machine with Intel Core2 Duo 2.4GHz, 4G RAM, Windows 7 system.

Workspace.Name: GSM_System_ConnectionSolution
Workspace.Description:
GSM System Connection Solution

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Template Workspace

This template is a simple example of a GSM connection solution workspace that can be used as a starting point to create more complicated designs.

GSM System Connection Solution

Two designs are provided

GSM_Source Design for generating GSM system test data

This design is to demo how to generate GSM test data. In the design, a GSM transmitter is included and the simulation data is generated. A SignaldownloadE4438C is used to link to the Keysight E4438C signal generator. Before running the simulation please make sure that the IP address for the signal generator is set right.

 

GSM_Receiver Design for recovering the original GSM data

This design is to demo how to recover the GSM test data. In the design, a VSA source model is used to capture the test data from MXA/PSA/VSA/Scope/PXA and then send the data to a GSM receiver. For receiver measurements, VSA software is not right tool to demod, decode, deframe the data. We need the GSM receiver from systemVue to recover the original data. The BER can be measured using this design.

 

Notice:

1.  Before using this workspace, users need connect the VSA source model to a MXA/PSA/VSA/Scope/PXA by using Keysight Connection Expert software, and in the VSA software, select the right hardware for data source.

2. Users can use ControlEq for convenience, this equation can run the two design sequentially.

3. This is only a starting point to help users to create connection solution, so the length of data downloaded into signal generator is fixed, so that the number of block for BER test is fixed.

Workspace.Name: GSM_Tx_FreqHopping
Workspace.Description:
GSM Frequency Hopping

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Workspace

This example demonstrates the typical GSM Frequency hopping process. The frequency hopping is added in Baseband. So the hopping frequency here is relative to the base frequency of each frequency band.

 

In the GSM_FreqHopping Model, Users can set the StartFN,HSN, MA list, MAIO to decide the hopping frequencies. Be sure that the ARFCNs in the MA list in the same band. Furthermore, the ARFCNs should match with the RF_Freq in the workspace parameter tab. The table below shows their relationships:


P-GSM 900

Fl(n) = 890 + 0.2*n

   1 £  n £  124

Fu(n) = Fl(n) + 45

E-GSM 900

Fl(n) = 890 + 0.2*n

   0 £  n £  124

Fu(n) = Fl(n) + 45

 

Fl(n) = 890 + 0.2*(n‑1024)

   975 £  n £  1 023

 

R‑GSM 900

Fl(n) = 890 + 0.2*n

0 £ n £ 124

Fu(n) = Fl(n) + 45

 

Fl(n) = 890 + 0.2*(n‑1024)

955 £ n £ 1023

 

DCS 1 800

Fl(n) = 1710.2 + 0.2*(n‑512)

512 £  n £  885

Fu(n) = Fl(n) + 95

PCS 1 900

FI(n) = 1850.2 + 0.2*(n-512)

512 £  n £  810

Fu(n) = FI(n) + 80

GSM 450

Fl(n) = 450.6 + 0.2*(n-259)

259 £ n £ 293

Fu(n) = Fl(n) + 10

GSM 480

Fl(n) = 479 + 0.2*(n-306)

306 £ n £ 340

Fu(n) = Fl(n) + 10

GSM 850

Fl(n) = 824.2 + 0.2*(n-128)

128 £ n £ 251

Fu(n) = Fl(n) + 45

where Fl means the lower Frequency for uplink, Fu means the upper Frequency for downlink.

 

Note that, the hopping Frequency should not exceed the half of SampleRate.  So if a high value ,e,g, 100 is set into MA list, the SampleRate should exceed 100*200k*2= 40M, that is, SamplesPerChip > 148.

 

If the values in the MA list are high and close to each other, e,g, MA = [101,105,110,120], there is a way to decrease the SampleRate. Users can increase the RF_Freq to RF_Freq+100*200k, and then set MA = [1,5,10,20] to get the same hopping effect but get a much lower sample rate.

Workspace.Name: GSM_Tx_ORFS
Workspace.Description:
Output RF spectrum measument

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

This example demonstrates the test of Output RF spectrum measument of BTS and MS receiver.

 

Output RF spectrum is the relationship between the frequency offset from the carrier and the power, measured in a specified bandwidth and time, produced by the MS or BTS due to the effects of modulation and power ramping.

 

All the parameters are set in equation 'GlobalParam '.

 

For BTS , please set the parameter BTS_or_MS as 0, and the test is based on the specifications and requirements in 6.5 of 3GPP TS 51.021v10.5.0 and corresponding GSM / EDGE documents.

 

For MS , please set the parameter BTS_or_MS as 1, and the test is based on the specifications and requirements in 13.4, 13.17.4 and 13.17.4a of 3GPP TS 51.010-1v10.1.0  and corresponding GSM/EDGE documents.

 

The tests can be performed by running Sweep_TxORFS. The measurement results are displayed in figure ORFS_Mod_Spec and ORFS_Switch_Spec. In figure, masks are added to verify if the spectrum conform to specification. 

 

The MS transmitter with GMSK in timeslot 0 is tested in this design as the default case. 

 

To test other cases of BTS and MS transmitter, user should set parameters in GlobalParam  according to the specifications.

 

 

Test Benches:

Test condition: BTS transmitter with  GMSK in timeslot 0, expected power set to 31dBm.

About 9.43 seconds in the machine with Intel Core2 Duo 2.4GHz, 4G RAM, Windows 7 system.

Workspace.Name: HSDPA_UE_Rx_HSSCCH_Detection_TS1_PA3
Workspace.Description:
HSDPA: HS-SCCH Detection Single Link Performance           

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example 

 

This example measures UE receiver performance.

This measurement is defined in section 9.4 of 3GPP specification TS.34.121.

 

1. The downlink channel includes P-CPICH, P-CCPCH, SCH, PICH, DPCH, HS-SCCH, HS-DSCH, OCNS.

 

2. The detection performance of the HS-SCCH is determined by the probability of event Em, which is declared

when the UE is signaled on HS-SCCH-1, but DTX is observed in the corresponding HS-DPCCH ACK/NACK

field. The probability of event Em is denoted P(Em).

 

3. The measured P(Em) shall be less than or equal to the corresponding specified value of P(Em). For the

TestNumber = 1, P(Em) = 0.05;

TestNumber = 2 or 3, P(Em) = 0.01.

Workspace.Name: DC_UE_Tx_ACLR
Workspace.Description:
DC-HSUPA: UE ACLR(Adjacent Channel Leakage Power Ratio)

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This example measures the HSUPA ACLR, as defined in section 6.6.2.2 of HSUPA/3GPP Specification TS 25.101(v9.4.0)

1. The uplink channel includes multiple code channels which includes one DPCCH and may include one DPDCH, one HS-DPCCH, one E-DPCCH and one or more E-DPDCH according to the settings.

 

2. ACLR_FilterBank contains the receiver side filters for the main and adjacent upper and lower channels. U5 is upper 5 MHz, U10 is upper 10 MHz, L5 is lower 5 MHz, L10 is lower 10 MHz.

 

3. Carrier Frequency is 1950MHz, Signal Power is 22dBm.

 

Specification ACLR requirements:

+5 MHz or -5 MHz

33 dB

+10 MHz or -10 MHz

43 dB

If the adjacent channel power is greater than -50dBm, then the ACLR shall be higher than the above value .

 

4. The simulated channels power values can be found in Table "Channel_Power_dBm".The simulated ACLR values can be found in Table "ACLR_dB".

+5 MHz or -5 MHz

33 dB

+10 MHz or -10 MHz

43 dB

Workspace.Name: NR_DL_BeamAcquisition
Workspace.Description:
NR DL BeamAcquisition

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This example builds an end-to-end simulation for 3GPP NR downlink beam acquisition based on SS/PBCH blocks in FR2. In this example, users may explore different phased array structure in both transmitter and receiver side and check beam acquisition performance. Also, one simple LOS channel is provided based on DF phased array models with the support of user-defined AoD/AoA and antenna element patterns. Users can replace this simple model with complicated 5G MIMO channel for more accurate simulation.

 

Overall the followings are the features supported in the example.

1.     SS/PBCH signal generation

2.     Tx RF channel modeling and Tx phased array structure

3.     Tx Beam sweeping setting for SS/PBCH blocks

4.    LOS MIMO channel with custom antenna pattern input (may also support 5G MIMO channel)

5.     Thermal noise

6.     Rx RF channel modeling and Rx phased array structure

7.     Rx Beam sweeping setting for SS/PBCH blocks

8.     Synchronization and Beam Measurement

 

The followings are the results after simulation:

1.     Transmit waveform and receiver waveform (see TxRxWaveform Graph)

2.     Measured power for each SS/PBCH block (see SSB_Power Graph)

3.     Synchronization information (see SyncInfo Table)

4.    The measured angle with maximum power in Tx/Rx beams (see MaxTxRxBeam Table)

 

 

Note that for this release only FR2 Numerology 3 120KHz is supported. FR2 Numerology 4 240K is not supported in SS/PBCH signal generation.

 

Note that in SSB_Power Graph, it shows the power for each SS/PBCH block with the length SSB_Lmax_Len*NumRxBeams, where SSB_Lmax_Len is equal to 64 which is the number of SS/PBCH blocks in one SS/PBCH Periodicity, and NumRxBeams is the number of sweeping beams in the receiver got from RxPhiTable variable.

 

The input parameters are all in GlobalParameters equation where users can set parameters for NR SS/PBCH, RF and beams, Tx/Rx antenna arrays, channel, SNR etc.

 

The details for each part are described as below.

 

3GPP NR SS/PBCH Signal Generation

 

In this part, NR SS/PBCH for FR2 (Numerology 3 (120KHz)) is generated. There are several parameters defined in GlobalParameters equation for SS/PBCH signal generation:

 

Numerology = 3; %3-> 120KHz, 4-> 240KHz

SSB_RBOffset = 10; %offset RB index in Carrier bandwidth

SSB_Lmax = 2; %L = 64

SSB_Periodicity = 0; %5ms, 10ms, 20ms, 40ms, 80ms, 160ms

 

Tx Beam Sweeping for SS/PBCH Blocks

 

In this part, BeamformerWeights model is used to generate the weights for the beam of each SS/PBCH block. Note that by default, we allocate different SS/PBCH block into different azimuth angle (Phi), and the theta angle is fixed. The beam sweeping in azimuth angles is defined TxPhiTable variable in GlobalParameters equation which should contain at least 64 angles. Here users can add additional impairments to RF and Phased array, such as windowing, gain compression, phase shifter quantization and errors, etc.

 

LOS channel with AoD/AoA

 

In this part, AntennaArrayTx model is used to generate the signal from transmit antenna array at given AoD direction, and then a certain delay is added. Finally, AntennaArrayRx is used to reproduce the signals at receiver antenna array with given AoA direction. Note that in both AntennaArrayTx and AntennaArrayRx models, custom antenna patterns can be imported to evaluate the performance of antenna array.

 

Noise

 

In this part, the thermal noise is added onto each receiver antenna element with input SNR variable in GlobalParameters equation. Note that SNR variable does not take transmit beamforming gain into account. So, the actual SNR may be larger if there is a big transmit beamforming gain. However, for receiver beamforming gain, it has no effect on SNR as the noise is added onto receiver antenna element.

 

Rx Beam Sweeping for SS/PBCH Blocks

 

This part is like Tx beam sweeping. Users may define different receiver beams in RxPhiTable variable in GlobalParameters equation.

 

Synchronization and Beam Measurement

 

NR_DL_FrameSync model is used for timing and frequency synchronization. After the synchronization is finished, this model will also measure the power of each SS/PBCH block. From this model, the following results are output:

 

1.     Measured power for each SS/PBCH block (see SS/PBCH_Power Graph)

2.     Synchronization information (see SyncInfo Table)

3.     The measured the angles with maximum power in Tx/Rx beams (see MaxTxRxBeam Table). Note CalMaxTxRxBeam equation is used to calculate these angles from measure SS/PBCH power.

 

Note that

1.     NR_DL_FrameSync will introduce one SS/PBCH periodicity delay. The SS/PBCH periodicity is defined by SSB_Periodicity parameter.

2.    For FR2 SS/PBCH blocks, the SSB index(0~63) is denoted by 6 bits. The three least significant bits are indicated by the DMRS for PBCH. The three most significant bits are carried in BCH bits. Those 6 bits are extracted from the received SSB with the maximum rho (correlation value between received PSS and reference PSS).

3. SyncInfo is comprised of 3 values. The first value is the SSB index with the maximum rho; the second value is the half frame index of that SSB; the third value is RX beam index on which the peak SSB resides.

4. Datasheet is deleted because of the size of example is too big. Please rerun analysis to get the datasheet.

Workspace.Name: NR_DL_Throughput
Workspace.Description:
NR DL Throughput

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This example showcases New Radio downlink system working in Frequency Range 1 (FR1) and Frequency Range (FR2). Upon the designs, throughput and BER can be measured. Seven designs are in this workspace: SISO case, SISO BF case, MIMO 2x2 case, MIMO 2x2 BF case, SIMO switch diversity case, SIMO switch diversity BF case, SISO HARQ case and MIMO 2x2 HARQ case. Parameters FrequencyRange and Bandwidth is used in these examples and the realationship between bandwidth and number of RBs are shown in 38.104 table 5.3.2-1 and table 5.3.2-2, listed hereby in Appendix.

 

 

SISO Case

In the SISO case, AWGN channel is used to help measure performance under different SNR values. SystemConfiguraion specifies two types of NR signal configuration. One is FRC which are defined by A.3.2 for FDD and A.3.3 for TDD in 38.101-1 (V15.4.0). And the other is User Defined that user can configure the signal by specifying the parameters in the design SISO's Equation. The settings used by this case is FRC defined in Table A.3.3.2.-1(Fixed Reference channel for receiver requirements (SCS 15kHz, TDD, QPSK 1/3)), and the Bandwidth is 10MHz. Switching to other FRC tables can be done by setting OperationMode and FRC_Table in the Equation.

After the simulation, fractional throughput curve and uncoded BER curve are obtained. The simulated uncoded BER curve is compared with an ideal BER curve calculated by berawgn in MATLAB, where 0.1dB gap is observed. Please note that parameter "MMSE_RBWinLen" in the receiver would influence the performance in some degree. Run Sweep_SISO equation to get the following curves:

1. Uncoded BER vs. SNR

2. Througput (%) vs. SNR

 

Note that in the SISO case, the sweep parameter in Sweep_SISO equation could be SNR or receiver power depending on the SweepMode parameter. If SweepMode is 0, SNR is swept and receiver power is calculated with thermal noise of -174 dBm/Hz. If SweepMode is 1, receiver power is swept and SNR is calculated with thermal noise of -174 dBm/Hz.

Note that if RF models in the design have noise figure (NF), set NF value accordingly in the equation to get expect results (i.e. calculated receiver power for SweepMode 0 or SNR for SweepMode 1).

 

 

SISO BF Case

In the SISO BF Case, beamforming architecture is introduced. Both TX and RX do beam training at the same time.

After the beam training, PDSCH transmission starts based on the optimal TX and RX beam.

Some notes related to current design:

  1. PDSCH associated with port 1000 are transmitted in TX side and received in RX side to measure the performance.
  2. SSB associated with port 4000 is used to do beam training for both of TX side and RX side.
  3. Two TX RF chains and three RX RF chains are deployed.
  4. Port 1000 is associated with PDSCH transmission and port 4000 is associated with SSB transmission. PortRFMappingMatrix defines the mapping relationship between ports and TX RF chains. For example, PortRFMappingMatrix = [1;0;0;1] is the vectorization of the mapping matrix with dimension NumOfTxRFChains-by-NumOfPorts, which indicates PDSCH in port 1000 are mapped to TX RF chain #0 and SSB in port 4000 is mapped to TX RF chain #1.
  5. SSB number, SSB_Lmax in the example’s Parameters List, determines the maximum available TX beams’ number, which is 4 in this example. The beam direction of each SSB is specified by TxThetaTable([90;90;90;90]) and TxPhiTable([60;20;340;300]) in the Equations of design.
  6. DataRcvRxRFChainsList and BeamTrainingRxRFChainsList are introduced in the RX side to indicate the usage of RX RF chains. For example, in current design, NumRxRFChains = 3, DataRcvRxRFChainsList = [0] and BeamTrainingRxRFChainsList = [1;2] indicate the RX RF chain #0 to receive PDSCH and RX RF chains #1 and #2 to receive SSB to perform beam training.
  7. NumberBeamTrainingRounds and the number of RX RF chains associated with beam training (=length(BeamTrainingRxRFChainsList)) together determine the number of maximum available RX beams which equals to NumberBeamTrainingRounds multiplying the number of RX RF chains associated with beam training. In current design, NumberBeamTrainingRounds = 2 and two RX RF chains for beam training imply 4 available RX beams. The beam direction of RX beams are specified by RxThetaTable([90;90;90;90]) and RxPhiTable([60;20;340;300]) in the Equations of design.
  8. NumTxAnts and NumRxAnts specify the real phase array topology.
  9. A 3D channel model is used to model a LOS channel, whose ClusterAoD = 340 and ClusterAoA = 20. Therefore, the optimal TX beam is the 3rd one, and the optimal RX beam is the 2nd one.

 

MIMO 2X2 Case

In the MIMO case, 2X2 SU MIMO is simulated with 3D channel model to emulate the MIMO channel, where UMi is used as default. For MIMO case, there is no benchmark for BER vs. SNR.

 

 

MIMO 2x2 BF Case

In the MIMO BF Case, beamforming architecture is introduced. Both TX and RX do beam training at the same time. After the beam training, PDSCH transmission starts based on the optimal TX and RX beam.

Some notes relate to MIMO BF design, only aspects different from SISO BF Case are elaborated hereby:

  1. PDSCH associated with port 1000 and port 1001 are transmitted in TX side and received in RX side to measure the performance
  2. Three TX RF chains and four RX RF chains are deployed.
  3. Upon the configuration of PortRFMappingMatrix = [1;0;0;0;1;0;0;0;1] BeamTrainingRxRFChainsList = [2;3] and DataRcvRxRFChainsList = [0;1]. In both TX side and RX side, the first and second RF chains are used to transmit data. In TX side, the third RF chain is used to do beam training. In the RX side, the third and the fourth RF chains are used to do beam training.
  4. For demo purpose, four avaliable TX beams and four avaliable RX beams are included in the simulation, say TxThetaTable = [90;90;90;90]/180*pi; TxPhiTable = [60;20;340;300]/180*pi; RxThetaTable = [90;90;90;90]/180*pi; RxPhiTable = [60;20;340;300]/180*pi;
  5. Accordingly, ChTxTheta = TxThetaTable([2,4])/pi*180; ChTxPhi = TxPhiTable([2,4])/pi*180; ChRxTheta = RxThetaTable([1,3])/pi*180; and ChRxPhi = RxPhiTable([1,3])/pi*180; are configured for channel modeling to accommodate two layer transmission.

 

SIMO Switch Diversity Case

In the SIMO case, a parameter "DiversityOption" is added to the receiver to specify if diversity takes effect:

1. If DiversityOption=0, the diversity would be enabled, where the branch with higher power would be picked for demodulation and decoding.

2. If DiversityOption=1, only the first branch takes effect.

3. If DiversityOption=2, only the second branch takes effect.

In the SIMO diversity case, two branches in RX side are deployed to dynamically switch the effective receiving path upon power estimation.

 

 

SIMO Switch Diversity BF Case

Beamforming procedure is added to the conventional diversity case. In this case, only one stream in each diversity branch is supported. In the receiver side, one diversity branch is selected from the two diversity branches upon a simple metric which compares DMRS power in both diversity branches.

 

 

SISO HARQ Case

In SISO HARQ case, NR downlink closed-loop HARQ is supported to measure Throughput under different SNR in AWGN channel.

Four typical FRC (Fixed Referenced Channel) are available in this example, two for FDD and the other two for TDD according to Table A.3.2.2-1, A.3.2.2-2 and A.3.3.2-1, A.3.3.2-2 in 38.101-1 (V15.5.0). Different FRC table can configured through variable FRC_Config in Equation. Default bandwidth in this case is 10MHz, which is also configurable. When simulation is over, fractional throughput curve is plotted on figures. Running Sweep_SISO_AWGN_HARQ equation to get the following curves:

1. Througput (%) vs. SNR

 

The following settings and instructions should be paid attention to in order to support HARQ simulation:

  1. Set appropriate synchronization settings for NR_DL_Numerology_Rcv. One way to support HARQ simulation is setting 'AutoFrameSync' as NO, which then requires manual setup of time and frequency synchronization offset to the received signal through 'DesiredDelay' and 'DesiredFreqOffset'. For AWGN channel, 'DesiredDelay' will usually be 0 if no additional time delay is introduced in simulation link. For other multipath channels, however, it is recommended to observe the auto-detected result from TO output of NR_DL_Numerology_Rcv by setting 'AutoFrameSync' to YES and 'HARQ_Enable' to NO. Using the auto-detected TO result to configure 'DesiredDelay'. 'DesiredFreqOffset' is set to 0 if there is no additional frequency offset in simulation link. Another way to support HARQ simulation is setting 'AutoFrameSync' to YES while selecting 'CP+DMRS Synchronization' for 'SyncMethod'. This way, receiver will perform automatic frame synchronization by using cyclic prefix and DMRS of the received signal. 
  2. Set 'HARQ_Enable' parameter in both NR top-level source and receiver. In this example, users can just set the HARQ_Enable in the Parameters Tab.
  3. Set 'NumHARQ' parameter to specify the number of HARQ processes.
  4. Set 'MaxHARQTrans' parameter to specify maximum number of HARQ transmission; The 'RV_Sequence' parameter specifies the redundancy version coding sequence. Its array size should be equal to that of 'MaxHARQTrans' parameter.
  5. In HARQ simulation, output delay in NR top-level receiver is one slot (1ms for Numerology 0 and 0.5ms for other Numerology setting). As HARQ is not supported by setting YES for 'AutoFrameSync' and 'SSB Synchronization' for 'SyncMethod', MaxSSBIndex and SSBPower outputs are invalid and shown as -999. When 'AutoFrameSync' is set to YES and 'SyncMethod' is set to 'SSB Synchronization', which is only valid for non-HARQ case, NR top-level receiver output delay is SSB_Periodicity*NumBeamTrainingRounds.

  6. Connection of output port 'HARQ_Bits' of NR_DL_Numerology_Rcv with input port 'HARQ_Bits' of NR_DL_Source. A Delay value of (NumHARQ-HarqRxDelay) is required between these two ports to support HARQ simulation. For Numerology 0 and 1, HarqRxDelay is 1 since delay of output from receiver is one time slot for HARQ simulation where CP+DMRS Synchronization or AutoFrameSync OFF is adopted. While for Numerology 2 and 3, as the minimum output delay of the receiver is 0.5ms, which corresponds to 2 time slots for Numerology 2 and 4 time slots for Numerology 3, HarqRxDelay therefore should be 2 and 4 for SCS 60kHz and 120kHz setting. Note that HARQ is not supported by Numerology 4.

  7. FIR Filter in the top-level source will introduce additional reception delay. Hence, SpectrumShapingType is highly recommended to be 0 for HARQ simulation.

 

MIMO 2x2 HARQ Case

In the MIMO HARQ case, 2X2 SU MIMO is simulated with 3D channel model to emulate the MIMO channel, where CDL-A is used as default. The same as SISO HARQ case, four typical FRC settings are used in this example according to Table A.3.2.2-1, A.3.2.2-2 for FDD and A.3.3.2-1, A.3.3.2-2 for TDD in 38.101-1 (V15.5.0). FRC tables can be selected by setting FRC_Config in the Equation. Default bandwidth in this case is 10MHz, which is also configurable. When simulation is over, fractional throughput curve is plotted on figures. Running Sweep_MIMO_HARQ equation to get the following curves:

1. Througput (%) vs. SNR

 

 

Signal Power Setting

In each design, there is one or several Oscillators following the NR_DL_Source. The Oscillator is used to tune the signal power to a specific power level, together with NR_DL_Source.

If there are one port and one RF chain for the signal transmission, the signal power setting is straightforward:

If you specify the Power Parameter to, say 20, in Oscillator with unit dBm, the signal would be tuned to be with power 20dBm/15kHz in the frequency range where it's allocated.

No matter what subcarrier spacing is used, the power spectrum would be 20dBm/15kHz in the frequency range where it's allocated.

That means if 30kHz subcarrier spacing is specified, it results in 23dBm/30kHz.

 

Normally, multiple ports would be configured. Therefore the resulting signal power spectrum would vary upon different configurations.

Let's assume Power is still set to 20. and Let's take an example: if three ports are configured: port 1000 and port 1001 for PDSCH transmission and port 4000 for SSB transmission. Three RF chains are equipped for the transmission.

If PortRFMappingMatrix = [1 0 0 1 1 1], the first RF chain transmit both port 1000 signal and port 4000 signal. Considering port 4000 signal is only transmitted in limited slots, the power spectrum would be still 20dBm/15kHz in the frequence range where PDSCH is allocated. The same thing happens for the second RF chain.

If PortRFMappingMatrix = [1 1 1 1 1 1], which means signals associated with port 1000, port 1001 and port 4000 are all transmitted in both RF chains. In this case, the power spectrum would be 23dBm/15kHz in the frequency range where PDSCH transmission is allocated.

The setting PortRFMappingMatrix = [1 1 1 1 1 1] doesn't make sense if you want to succeed the transmission, but it's a good example to elaborate the power setting hereby.
