Workspace.Name: NR_DL_Throughput_PolarizedSystem
Workspace.Description:
NR DL Throughput (Polarized System)

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This workspace showcases New Radio polarized downlink system working in Frequency Range 1 (FR1) and Frequency Range (FR2). Upon the designs, throughput and BER can be measured. Besides, antenna element radiation pattern files can be imported into the design to refine the evaluation.

 

Three designs are included in this workspace:

  • MIMO 2x2 BF Polarized Case
  • SISO BF MRC Polarized Diversity Case
  • MIMO 2x2 BF Polarized Diversity Case

 

In each schematic, green part handles signals for the first polarization and Pink part handles signals for the second polarization. Information pertinent to polarization is included in MIMO_3DChannel Configuration section.

 

All definitions of number of RF chains, number of antenna elements in each schematic refer to the number per polarization.

 

Appendix about frequently used bandwidth configuration would help users configure the system easily.

 

Below are the details of these designs.

 

MIMO 2x2 BF Polarized Case

 

In this case, dual-polarized antenna arrays are deployed in both TX and RX sides. Only one channel direction is modelled in the 3D channel model and two streams of the MIMO transmission are transmitted in two polarizations respectively.

 

Four RF chains are deployed in TX side. Two are for one polarization and the other two are for the other polarization. One RF in the two RFs for whichever polarization is used for data transmission and the other one is for SSB transmission.

 

Four RF chains are also deployed in RX side. Two are for one polarization and the other two are for the other polarization, just as same as the deployment in TX side. Similar, regarding two RFs in RX side for one polarization, one is for data receiving and the other one is for SSB receiving.

 

The channel is set up with only one path and is configured to Dual Polarized mode to accommodate 2x2 MIMO transmission.

 

 

SISO BF MRC Polarized Diversity Case

 

In this case, dual-polarized antenna arrays are deployed in both TX and RX sides. Only one channel direction is modelled in the 3D channel model and the same stream is transmitted in both two polarizations.

 

The basic structure is as same as the structure used in the above case. The difference is that only one stream is transmitted in the system. In the receiver side signals from two polarizations are combined to get the only stream. The 1-layer signal is demodulated upon signals from two polarizations by MRC algorithm in the Equalizer.

 

Throughput curves are obtained based on MRC, branch #1 and branch #2 respectively, where MRC outperforms receiving only on branch #1 or branch #2 by 3dB.

 

MIMO 2x2 BF Polarized Switch Diversity Case

 

In this case, two patches equipped in RX side are used for diversity purpose. One of the two patches would be selected at certain slots and data receiving would be based on the selected branch.

 

The structure in Tx side is as same as the structures used in above two designs.

 

Regarding RX side, the structure in above design appears twice in current design to mimic two diversity branches. Signal from one diversity branch is selected for demodulation.

 

Each patch associated with specific branch in RX side is comprised of a 2x2 dual-polarized array, which means one 2x2 array corresponds to one polarization and the other 2x2 array corresponds to the other polarization. Two streams are transmitted in two polarizations, one for each.

 

MIMO_3DChannel Configuration

 

Signals associated with two polarizations from source are reconstructed before being connected to channel model and signals output from channel model are also reconstructed before being connected to subsequent modules. These refactoring assures signals associated with specific polarization are placed in order.

 

Mechanism of Beams Scheduling

 

When there are multiple NR_DL_BeamsScheduler modules in the design, they may need to cooperate.

 

For example, in the switch diversity case, multiple patches associated with specific branches are deployed in the RX side, each of which can be conducted to specific directions to receive signal, but in the TX side, only one patch is deployed. TX side must decide the TX transmitting direction upon the feedback from multiple diversity branches.

 

The parameters NumDiversityBranches, BranchIndex, together with input port named TxBeamsTrigger of NR_DL_BeamsScheduler module are responsible for the cooperation mechanism in diversity case.

 

Firstly, parameter NumDiversityBranches informs each module that how many NR_DL_BeamsScheduler modules are there in the design and BranchIndex informs the index of the module.

 

Secondly, TxBeamsTrigger, as a common signal to all NR_DL_BeamsScheduler modules, indicates which NR_DL_BeamsScheduler’s  BI_TxRFChains output takes effect, which means only the modules with BranchIndex equalling to TxBeamsTrigger indication take effects and others keep outputting zeros. Most of the time, it’s true. The exception is at very beginning, before SSBPower input becomes valid, the NR_DL_BeamsScheduler with BranchIndex=1 takes responsible for outputting beam index for initial beam training.

 

 

Simulation Notes

 

All three designs are based on fading channels, so it’s critical to setup the simulation and RX algorithm parameters correctly before simulation.

 

The most confusing part is how to setup the simulation slots for collecting reasonable BER and calculating throughput. The most important aspect is velocity configured in channel model, from which we can derive maximum doppler shift. Then, coherent time can be gotten upon the maximum doppler shift. The number of simulation slots should at least cover 5~10 coherent time to get expected average power.

 

Fmax and Tmax in RX side should be setup carefully according to channel configuration. Please refer to RX receiver guide to learn how to setup them correctly.

 

 

Signal Power Setting

In each design, there is one or several Oscillators following the NR_DL_Source. The Oscillator is used to tune the signal power to a specific power level, together with NR_DL_Source.

If there are one port and one RF chain for the signal transmission, the signal power setting is straightforward:

If you specify the Power Parameter to, say 20, in Oscillator with unit dBm, the signal would be tuned to be with power 20dBm/15kHz in the frequency range where it's allocated.

No matter what subcarrier spacing is used, the power spectrum would be 20dBm/15kHz in the frequency range where it's allocated.

That means if 30kHz subcarrier spacing is specified, it results in 23dBm/30kHz.

 

Normally, multiple ports would be configured. Therefore the resulting signal power spectrum would vary upon different configurations.

Let's assume Power is still set to 20. and Let's take an example: if three ports are configured: port 1000 and port 1001 for PDSCH transmission and port 4000 for SSB transmission. Three RF chains are equipped for the transmission.

If PortRFMappingMatrix = [1 0 0 1 1 1], the first RF chain transmit both port 1000 signal and port 4000 signal. Considering port 4000 signal is only transmitted in limited slots, the power spectrum would be still 20dBm/15kHz in the frequence range where PDSCH is allocated. The same thing happens for the second RF chain.

If PortRFMappingMatrix = [1 1 1 1 1 1], which means signals associated with port 1000, port 1001 and port 4000 are all transmitted in both RF chains. In this case, the power spectrum would be 23dBm/15kHz in the frequency range where PDSCH transmission is allocated.

The setting PortRFMappingMatrix = [1 1 1 1 1 1] doesn't make sense if you want to succeed the transmission, but it's a good example to elaborate the power setting hereby.

Workspace.Name: NR_DL_TM
Workspace.Description:
3GPP NR Downlink Test Model

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This workspace generates 3GPP new radio (NR) downlink test model signals.

 

Test Models are provided in this workspace according to 3GPP TS 38.141 V16.1.0 (2019-09) . You can select TestModel, Bandwidth and DuplexType to configure different test models.

 

In this example, test model defined in TS38.141-1 (16.1.0)and TS38.141-2(16.1.0) are used. TDD and FDD are supported for FrequencyRange 1 (FR1) for Numerology 15kHz, 30kHz and 60kHz with normal cyclic prefix in this example. Only TDD model is supported for FrequencyRange 2  (FR2)  for Numerology 60kHz with normal cyclic prefix, and 120kHz.

 

SignalPower is defined the power of PDSCH. Number of RBs of PDSCH is given in Equation of different TestModel. PDCCH and PDSCH is not overlaped in time domian, the SignalPower may not be accurate when PDCCH is transmitted.

 

The ideal lowpass filter for spectrum shaping can be turned on/off by parameter EnableTxFilter. The number of taps can be set by FIR_Taps. If EnableTxFilter is set to NO, no spectrum shaping would be applied.

 

A sink is used to save the generate signal from 0 to 10ms in FDD modd and from 0 to 20 ms in TDD mode.

 

Try to change the parameters, run NR_DL_Tx_Analysis and check the simulation results.

 

To measure EVM, both VSA sink model and EVM subnet provided in this workspace are available. Please enable VSA_89600B_Sink or TestModel_EVM. Make sure the version of 89600B installed on your PC is 2019 Update 1.0 (Revision 24.20) or later. Run the simulation and after VSA is booted up, on the menu, select MeasSetup->New Measurement->Cellular->5G NR. And then select MeasSetup->5G NR Demod Properties... On the shown-up window click button "Apply Test Model...", and set the parameters properly according to the settings in this example.

 

To correlate EVM measurement results of TestModel_EVM with VSA_89600B_Sink model, please make sure your setup matches with VSA.

Workspace.Name: NR_DL_Tx
Workspace.Description:
NR DL Tx

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This example workspace demonstrates spectrum, constellation, EVM, ACLR and CCDF measurements for an NR downlink transmitter. The performance for FR1 and FR2 are shown in different folds. And for FR1, there are two folders for SSB and BWP in one numerology and in two different numerologies.

Folder: FR1 One Numerology, SSB and BWP are in the same numerology (15kHz). There are two BWPs (PDSCH) and SSB in the 15kHz CC.

Folder: FR1 Two Numerologies, SSB and BWP are in different numerology (PDSCH &SSB: 15kHz; PDSCH: 30kHz). There are two BWPs (PDSCH) in both 15kHz CC and 30kHz CC.

Folder: FR2, SSB and BWP are in the same numerology (120kHz). There are one BWP (PDSCH) and SSB in the CC.

Folder: FRC. FRC downlink cases in 3GPP 38.101-1 are shown in this folder.

 

Overall the followings are the features supported in the example.

1. NR transmitter signal with multiple numerologies  

2. Spectrum, constellation, EVM, ACLR and CCDF measurements are supported

3. EVM vs SNR graph is supported with non-linear PA in the simulation

4. AWGN channel is added

5. Performance in VSA are shown with pre-configured VSA setup-file

6. Tx RF channel modeling and Tx phased array structure for FR2

7. EVM measurements in FR2 are based on the average of EVM on different Rx direction

8. EIRP and TRP measurements in FR2

9. VSA setup file generation is supported based on VSA 2018 Update 1.0

 

The followings are the results after simulation:

1.  Transmit spectrum (see Spectrum Graph) using the data in Design Analysis_Design_Data

2.  Constellation for different BWP (see Constellation Graph) using the data in Design Analysis_Design_Data

3.  EVM vs SNR with/without non-linear PA (see SNR vs. EVM Graph) using the data in WorkspaceVariables

4.  ACLR (see ACLR_Table Table) using the data in Design Analysis_Design_Data

5.  Beam pattern (Dynamic3D Graph) for FR2

6.  EIRP pattern (see EIRP_Pattern Graph) using the data in WorkspaceVariables

7.  TRP (See TRP Table) using the data in WorkspaceVariables

  

3GPP NR EVM measurement

 

The EVM measurement in SystemVue is based on EVM model.EVM model support multi-BWPs in different Numerologies. Make sure the parameters for source and receiver are consistent. In this example, one frame signal is used to do demodulation and get EVM result in one time defined by parameter MeasInterval. Please update this value if more signal is used for demodulation. 

For FR1, input EVM vs SNR graph is gotten by sweep SNR vs. EVM with/without no-linear PA by using PAEnable in Equations. In FR1 One Numerology, Bandwidth =50Mhz, (CarrierNumRBs = 270), EPRE = -10 (dBm/15kHz) the power of CC is 10*log10(270*12)-10 = 25.1dBm and dBc1out of PA is set to 32dBm considering the PAPR.

 

For FR2 EVM measurement, it is based on a set of specific directions from the AAS (active antenna system) BS (base station) which is of interest rather than the average or total EVM over the entire sphere. In this design, the direction of transmitter beam is fixed by parameters ZoD_Cen, AoD_Cen. And the receive path is set by parameters ZoD and AoD which is used in AntennaArrayTx model. 5 different position of ZoD and AoD is set to calculate the EVM in those 5 different directions. The EVM is average of those five EVM value. And it is gotten in Equation CalcuEVM.  In CalcuEVM, SNR is swept and EVM vs SNR can be get. Please disable the models for EIRP measurement to avoid long simulation time while running Equation CalcuEVM.

 

Filter is added to the demodulated signal if UseMcFilter (EVM model) is set to Yes and the same filter is used in VSA model by default setup file. According to the definition of SNR in 3GPP, it is the signal to noise ratio in bandwidth. In this model, if filter is not used, noise will be calculated on the whole band of samplingrate, in this case, EVM result may be 3dB worse when OversamplingOption is set to Ratio 2 compared to set to Ratio 1. If filter is used, impairment of filter may introduce performance degradation in noiseless scenario, EVM may around -70dB instead of -120dB, but this degradation disappears in noisy scenario.

 

ACLR measurement

 

ACLR is calculate by equation ACLR using spectrum data in Design Analysis_Design_Data. Please keep the parameters in ACLR equation shown below consistent with the parameters in Design.

FR1

bandwidth = 50e6; %%%Hz

FCarrier = 2e9; %%% Hz

CarrierNumRBs = 270;

SCS = 15e3; %%%Hz

FR2

bandwidth = 100e6; %%%Hz

FCarrier = 28e9; %%% Hz

CarrierNumRBs = 66;

SCS = 120e3; %%%Hz

 

Please run the equation if spectrum data are updated.

SpectrumShapping is added in Source to ensure ACLR performance. 

 

EIRP and TRP Measurement

  

In this example, transmitter beam is fixed to AoD_Cen and ZoD_Cen. We get EIRP (power) after transmitter in different directions by using Sweep1 on AoD which is set in AntennaArrayTx model (A4). To fast the simulation, we put different ZoD for 64 different SSB. Value of ZoD are set by RxThetaTable in Equations.  Resolution of EIRP can be set by RxThetaTable and AoD. Resolution of AoD is set in Sweep1. In this example, Phi (AoD)is in the range [0:360) degree and Theta(ZoD) is in the range [0:90] for EIRP pattern. When Sweep1 is done, please run Equation CalcuEIRP to get the pattern of EIRP and TRP. TRP is the total radiated power in upper hemisphere. Please disable the models for EVM mearsurement in EIRP measurement while using Sweep1.

 

Noise Density Calculation

  

In this part, the thermal noise is added by NDensity_dBm in AddNDensity model which is calculated in Equation. In FR2 folder, antenna gain is removed when calculate noise density. If beam pattern is added, please remove the beam pattern gain to make sure SNR is right. SNR is set in Equation in FR2 while it is set in Parameters in other two folders. EPRE is defined in dBm/15kHz for every numerology and it is set in Osillator model to adjust the power.

 

FRC

FDD FRC table in A.3.2 and TDD FRC table in A.3.3 in 38.101-1 (V15.4.0) are supported. HAQR, TRS and PRB bunlding are not supported. Paremeters for different table are set in Equation. The rest of parameters which are not list in A.3.2/A.3.3 are set in Source model and EVM model. Please make sure parameters consistent for those two models. For SCS 15kHz and SCS 30kHz, SSB_Numerology is set as the same SCS with Numerology. But for SCS 60kHz, because there is no SSB of SCS 60kHz, SSB_Numerology is set to 30kHz in Equation. To steer clear of SSB slot, the first and second slots of SCS 60kHz are muted. For table A.3.2.2, table A.3.2.3, table A.3.3.2 and table A.3.3.3, MCS Table 5.1.3.1-1 in 38.214 is used.For table A.3.2.4 and table A.3.3.4, MCS Table 5.1.3.1-2 in 38.214 is used. When Fill_OCNG is set to YES, EVM model can not demodulated correctly, so Fill_OCNG is set to NO in this design. This FRC design is based on FR1.

 

How to set parameters for NR_DL_Source

1. NumBWPs is number of all BWPs and the size of Numerology should equal to one or NumBWPs.

2. Numerology_k0 is  k0 for each BWP numerology when ResourceGridEnable is disable. Size of Numerology_k0 is number of Numerology without repetition and the order of Numerology_k0 should be consistent with unique Numerology. For example, NumBWPs = 3, Numerology = [1,1,2], size of Numerology_k0 should be 2 and Numerology_k0 = [0, 1]. Numerology_k0 is 0 subcarrier for numerology 1 and 1 subcarrier for numerology2. 

4. Enumeration for Numerology and for SSB_Numerology can be different. SSB_Numerology_k0 is k0 for SSB numerology when ResourGridEnable is disable and SSB_Enable is set to YES. SSB_Numerology_k0 will be ignored if SSB_Numerology is a repetition in Numerology.

5. Size of other array parameters should equal to one or NumBWPs.

6. Bus width of input port PDSCH_Bits should equal to NumBWPs and the order should be consistent with BWPs setting. For example, NumBWPs = 3, Numerology = [1,1,2], bus 0,1 of PDSCH_Bits is for numerology1 and bus 2 of PDSCH_Bits is for numerology2.

7. Bus width of output port ChannelBits/ModSymbols should equal to NumBWPs and the order should be consistent with BWPs setting. For example, NumBWPs = 3, Numerology = [1,1,2], bus 0,1 of ChannelBits/ModSymbols is for numerology1 and bus 2 of ChannelBits/ModSymbols is for numerology2.

8. There are three types of time domain signal output: SSBOut, BWPOut and PortsOut. Let me take an example to articulate the output form:

Given NumBWPs = 2, PDSCH_DMRS_NumPort =[2, 4], PDSCH_DMRS_PortList  = [1000, 1001, 1000, 1001, 1002, 1003], SSB_Enable = YES (All these parameters are set in Source GUI)

Then, there are two BWPs, the first BWP (BWP#0) holds 2 PDSCH ports: port 1000 and port 1001. the second BWP (BWP#1) holds 4 PDSCH ports: port 1000, port 1001, port 1002 and port 1003.

SSB is configured, the port of which is 4000 per 38.211 definition.

SSBOut would output SSB signal alone, which is a single port, since we do not support multiple SSB in one numerology.

BWPOut would output signals with buswidth 6, the order is consistent with the order predefined in BWP_PortList  = [1000, 1001, 1000, 1001, 1002, 1003].

PortsOut would output signals with buswidth 4, each of which holds one specific port, say port 1000, port 1001, port 1002, port 1003.

In this configuration, two ports' signal of BWP#0 would be transmitted in first two lines of the output and four ports's signal of BWP#1 would be transmitted in all four lines of the output accordingly.

9.The size of PortstoRFMatrix is (unique(PDSCH_DMRS_PortList)+1)* NumTxRFChains if PDCCH is not enabled. 1 in above formula means SSB ports and SSB ports is always the last ports in the matrix.

For example, BWP_PortList=[1000,1005,1003,1000], NumTxRFChains =2 and the size of PortstoRFMatrix should be 4*2 = 8, considering PortstoRFMatrix is [1, 0,1,1,1,1,1,1]. unique input ports are in ascending order considering SSB port as port 4000, input port is 1000, 1003,1005,4000. First 2 elements ([1,0]) is ports 1000 mapping matrix to RF chain1 and not mapping to RF chain2, and for the third and 4th elements [1,1], so ports 1003 is mapping to RF chain1 and RF chain2. It is the same case for ports 1005 and 4000, they are mapping to RF chain1 and RF chain2.

10. The size of PortstoRFMatrix is (unique(PDSCH_DMRS_PortList)+2)* NumTxRFChains if PDCCH is enabled. PDCCH port is in the second last. 

11. When ResourceGridEnable is set to YES, N_GridStart and SSB_N_GridStart will set grid start of BWP numerologies and SSB numerology. SSB_N_GridStart will be invalid when SSB_Numerology is a repetition in Numerology.

 

Note that

1.    Receiver will introduce one SS/PBCH frame delay.

2.    PBCH decoding is supported if parameters of PBCH_Decoding_Enable is set to Yes.

3.   Run Design3 Analysis with EVM measurement and EIRP measurement enable, we will get the one EVM value at beam direction and EIRP with Phi equals to beam direction and Theta from [0:90) degree.

4    SSB and BWP in two different numerologies is not supported in VSA, so BWP2 in FR1 Two Numerologies can't be demodulated in VSA.

5.   VSA in FR2 takes lots of time because of the high sampling rate and mass of data to synchronization in VSA.

6.   VSA setup file is based on VSA 2018 Update 1.0. Please exist VSA instance before starting new simulation.

7.   Only SSB synchronization is supported in NR DL receiver, so SSB should be enable in this example. EVM measurement is taken on PDSCH, so PDSCH should also be enable in this example. 

8.   Change the parameters of spectrum shapping in Source will affect ACLR.

9.   SSB and BWP overlapping in frequency domain is not allowing in this example.

10. SSB_RBOffset is based on 15kHz when SCS of SSB is 15kHz and 30kHz and SSB_RBOffset is based on 60kHz when SCS of SSB is 120kHz.

11. 240kHz SSB is not supported now. 

12. EVM model is based on 3GPP specification version 15.2.0

13. Datasheets are deleted because of the size of example, please rerun analysis to get the datasheet.

14. Constellation will not be shown in figure Constellation unless the parameter SaveConstellation of EVM is set to YES. In case SaveConstellation is NO, errors might be posted when opening constellation figures since no related data is available. However, the errors will not have any impact on the simulation and the results of EVM and other measurements. 

15.For Design3, please set OversamplingOption to Ratio 4 or more to run analysis and get ACLR. Now OversamplingOption is set to Ratio 1 to reduce the size of this example.

16.Number of slots of demodulated PDSCH is set to 5 (except FRC folder )by parameters EVM_NumSlots which is set in Equation in order to speed up plot of constellation when SaveConstellation is set to Yes.

17.Parameters Bandwidth is used in this example and the realationship between bandwidth and number of RBs are shown in 38.104 table 5.3.2-1 and table 5.3.2-2. The configuration of subcarrier spacing 240kHz is also shown below. FrequencyRange is gotten by parameter FCarrierTx.

18.EVM model will internally calculate Numerology_k0 and SSB_Numerology_k0 with the configured GridStart and SSB_GridStart according to definition in 5.3 of 38.211. EVM measurements might be wrong in case of multiple different Numerologies setting with ResourceGridEnable for NR_Source disabled, where Numerology_k0 and SSB_Numerology_k0 are set manually by users, unless these two parameters are calculated and set correctly. Therefore, ResourceGridEnable is set to YES by default in this example.

Workspace.Name: NR_DL_Tx_OTA
Workspace.Description:
NR DL Tx_OTA

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This example workspace demonstrates spectrum, constellation, EVM, SSB gain power and ACLR measurements for an NR downlink transmitter in far field and near field. SCS 120kHz (FR2) is selected in this example with antenna beam.

Fold: FR2, SSB and BWP are in the same numerology (120kHz). There are one BWP (PDSCH) and SSB in the CC.

 

Overall the followings are the features supported in the example.

1. NR transmitter signal with multiple numerologies 

2. Spectrum, constellation, EVM, SSB gain power and ACLR measurements are supported

3. EVM vs SNR graph is supported with non-linear PA in the simulation

4. AWGN channel is added

5. Performance in VSA are shown with pre-configured VSA setup-file (not yet)

6. Tx RF channel modeling and Tx phased array structure for FR2

7. EVM vs SNR measurements in FR2 are based on the average of EVM on different Rx direction

8. All above performance for near field and far field.

9. VSA setup generation is based on VSA 2018 Update 1.0

 

The followings are the results after simulation:

1. Transmit spectrum (see Spectrum Graph) using the data in Design Analysis_Design_Data

2. Constellation for different BWP (see Constellation Graph) using the data in Design Analysis_Design_Data

3. EVM vs SNR (see SNR vs. EVM Graph) in far field and near field using the data in WorkspaceVariables

4. ACLR (see ACLR_Table Table) using the data in Design Analysis_Design_Data

5. Beam pattern (Dynamic3D Graph) for FR2

6. EVM vs Phi (see EVM vs Phi Graph) for far field and near field using the data in Sweep data

7. SSB Gain power vs Phi (see Power vs Phi Graph) for far field and near field using the data Sweep data

8. EVM pattern in upper hemisphere for near field (see EVMPattern DAV) using the data in WorkspaceVariables

9. SSB Gain power pattern in upper hemisphere for near field (see PowerPattern DAV) using the data in WorkspaceVariables

  

EVM/SSB_Power vs Phi measurement

Beam direction is set to theta 30 degrees and phi 45 degrees. In EVM/SSB_power vs phi measurement, theta is fixed to 30 degree and phi is swept from -45 degree to 135 degree. Result in near field with lambda set to 10, 50 and result for far field with lambda set to 500 are plot in EVM/Power vs Phi graph. The results are gotten by running Sweep1. If you want to sweep on theta, please set ZoD in Equation as tune and change the sweep variable in Sweep1. Number of result SSB_Power for one direction is 64, because there are 64 SSB in 120kHz. We use the average of the 64 values as the result of power.

 

EVM/SSBPower Pattern

EVM/SSB_power pattern is gotten by running equation NearFieldPattern. EVM pattern and Power Pattern are get in near field with OversamplingOption ration 1 and FileterEnable No to speed up. There are two parts in equation NearFieldPattern, the first part is to calculate the EVM and gain power for upper hemisphere and the second part is to show the pattern. We use the value of EVM times with -1 to plot the EVM pattern.

In this example, beam direction is set to theta 30 degrees and phi 45 degrees, and the results are given in upper hemisphere and the resolution is 5 degrees. Select the far field or near field scenario by parameter Distance in Equation.

 

SSB power accuracy for EIRP measurement near/far

Output power accuracy for EIRP is defined in Directional requirement in TR37.843 which means measurements is gotten in coverage ranges over which the beam can be steered. SSB power (SSB EIRP) is provided to verify the accuracy of output power. Equation SSBAccuracyEIRP define the sweep step of AOD/ZOD in maximum steering range and then get the SSB EIRP in the specified AOD/ZOD when the scenario is near filed with nonline PA. EIRP is achieved to within an accuracy interval range at many(declared) directions which is state in TR37.842. Then errors between SSB ERIP and SSB power calculated by formula are also given out in declared directions. The measurement results, SSB_Accuracy and SSB_EIRP_err, are in the Workspace Variables.

 

NR EVM vs SNR measurement

For FR2 EVM measurement, it is based on a set of specific directions from the AAS (active antenna system) BS (base station) which is of interest rather than the average or total EVM over the entire sphere. In this design, the direction of transmitter beam is fixed by parameters ZoD_Cen, AoD_Cen. And the receive path is set by parameters ZoD and AoD which is used in TesT_OTA model. 5 different position of ZoD and AoD is set to calculate the EVM in those 5 different directions. The EVM is average of those five EVM value. And it is gotten in Equation CalcuEVM. Select the far field or near field scenario by parameter distance in Equation. Lambda for the near field result in this example is set to 10. We recommend disabling models for power measurement to speed up in EVM vs SNR measurement.

 

ACLR measurement

 

ACLR is calculated by equation ACLR using spectrum data in Design Analysis_Design_Data. Please keep the parameters in ACLR equation shown below consistent with the parameters in Design.

bandwidth = 100e6; %%%Hz
FCarrier = 28e9; %%% Hz
CarrierNumRBs = 66;
SCS = 120e3; %%%Hz

Please run the equation if spectrum data are updated.

Spectrum shapping is added to ensure ACLR performance.  

Noise Density Calculation

  

In this part, the thermal noise is added by NDensity_dBm in AddNDensity model which is calculated in Equation. In FR2 fold, antenna gain is removed when calculate noise density. If beam pattern is added, please remove the beam pattern gain in order to make sure SNR is right. SNR is set in Equation and for EVM vs SNR measurement, SNR is swept in Equation CalcuEVM. EPRE is defined in dBm/15kHz for every numerology and it is set in Oscillator model to adjust the power. The power of near field is normalized in Test_OTA model by set parameter Normalization to Yes.

 

Power, SSB Power and TRP

In this NR example, downlink transmitter signal power varied time considering SSB is existed or not. After beamforming and channel, accurate start time of power should be set to get accurate power/EIRP which is not easy to get. SSB is used to do synchronization, after synchronization power is easy to get. So, we use SSB power to represent the treat of EIRP. Another reason to show SSB power is that SSB is used to do beam measurement and it is very interest to compare SSB EIRP pattern with SSB antenna pattern. And the RIB (radiated interface boundary) power at beam peak is consisted of two parts: baseband power and antenna gain. In this example, baseband power is set by EPRE mentioned above. For example, EPRE is set to 0dBm/15kHz, the baseband power of SSB can be calculated as 10*log10(20*12*(120e3/15e3)) = 32.8 dBm. For 8x8 antenna, the antenna gain is about 10*log10(8*8) = 18.1 dBm. So, the peak SSB beam power should be around 32.8+18.1 =50.9 dBm which is shown in SSB power pattern. TRP is should be equal to baseband power of SSB without impairment. For the PDSCH beam peak power in this example, it should be 10*log10(66*12*(120e3/15e3)) + 10*log10(8*8) = 58 dBm.  

 

How to set parameters for NR_DL_Source

1. NumBWPs is number of all BWPs and the size of Numerology should equal to one or NumBWPs.

2. Numerology_k0 is  k0 for each numerology. When SSB is disable or SSB numerology is one of BWP numerology, the size of Numerology_k0 is number of numerology without repetition and the order of Numerology_k0 should be consistent with Numerology. For example, NumBWPs = 3, Numerology = [1,1,2], SSB_Numerology = 1: 30kHz, size of Numerology_k0 should be 2 and Numerology_k0 = [0, 1]. Numerology_k0 is 0 subcarrier for numerology 1 and 1 subcarrier for numerology2. When SSB is enable and SSB numerology is not one of BWP numerology, the size of Numerology_k0 is number of numerology without repetition +1 and the order of Numerology_k0 should be consistent with Numerology, and the last number is the number of RB for SSB numerology. For example, NumBWPs = 3, Numerology = [1,1,2], SSB_Numerology = 0: 15kHz, size of Numerology_k0 should be 3 and Numerology_k0 = [0, 1,2]. Numerology_k0 is 0 RBs for numerology 1, 1 RBs for numerology2 and 2 RBs for numerology0.

4. Enumeration for Numerology and for SSB_Numerology can be different.

5. Size of other array parameters should equal to one or NumBWPs.

6. Bus width of input port PDSCH_Bits should equal to NumBWPs and the order should be consistent with BWPs setting. For example, NumBWPs = 3, Numerology = [1,1,2], bus 0,1 of PDSCH_Bits is for numerology1 and bus 2 of PDSCH_Bits is for numerology2.

7. Bus width of output port ChannelBits/ModSymbols should equal to NumBWPs and the order should be consistent with BWPs setting. For example, NumBWPs = 3, Numerology = [1,1,2], bus 0,1 of ChannelBits/ModSymbols is for numerology1 and bus 2 of ChannelBits/ModSymbols is for numerology2.

8. There are three types of time domain signal output: SSBOut, BWPOut and PortsOut. Let me take an example to articulate the output form:

Given NumBWPs = 2, PDSCH_DMRS_NumPort =[2, 4], PDSCH_DMRS_PortList  = [1000, 1001, 1000, 1001, 1002, 1003], SSB_Enable = YES (All these parameters are set in Source GUI)

Then, there are two BWPs, the first BWP (BWP#0) holds 2 PDSCH ports: port 1000 and port 1001. the second BWP (BWP#1) holds 4 PDSCH ports: port 1000, port 1001, port 1002 and port 1003.

SSB is configured, the port of which is 4000 per 38.211 definition.

SSBOut would output SSB signal alone, which is a single port, since we do not support multiple SSB in one numerology.

BWPOut would output signals with buswidth 6, the order is consistent with the order predefined in BWP_PortList  = [1000, 1001, 1000, 1001, 1002, 1003].

PortsOut would output signals with buswidth 4, each of which holds one specific port, say port 1000, port 1001, port 1002, port 1003.

In this configuration, two ports' signal of BWP#0 would be transmitted in first two lines of the output and four ports's signal of BWP#1 would be transmitted in all four lines of the output accordingly.

9.The size of PortstoRFMatrix is (unique(PDSCH_DMRS_PortList)+1)* NumTxRFChains if PDCCH is not enabled. 1 in above formula means SSB ports and SSB ports is always the last ports in the matrix.

For example, BWP_PortList=[1000,1005,1003,1000], NumTxRFChains =2 and the size of PortstoRFMatrix should be 4*2 = 8, considering PortstoRFMatrix is [1, 0,1,1,1,1,1,1]. unique input ports are in ascending order considering SSB port as port 4000, input port is 1000, 1003,1005,4000. First 2 elements ([1,0]) is ports 1000 mapping matrix to RF chain1 and not mapping to RF chain2, and for the third and 4th elements [1,1], so ports 1003 is mapping to RF chain1 and RF chain2. It is the same case for ports 1005 and 4000, they are mapping to RF chain1 and RF chain2.

10. The size of PortstoRFMatrix is (unique(PDSCH_DMRS_PortList)+2)* NumTxRFChains if PDCCH is enabled. PDCCH port is in the second last. 

 

 

Note that

1.Please set distance (lambda) in Equation to set the scenario as near filed or far filed.

2.Receiver will introduce one SS/PBCH frame delay.

3.PBCH decoding is supported by if parameter PBCH_Decoding_Enable is set to Yes.

4.Design Analysis_Design_Data in this example is for near field with lambda 10.

5.240kHz SSB is not supported now.

6.If VSA model is enabled, it takes more time and memory to simulate, we recommend to disable the models after VSA in the simulation. VSA setup file is update to 2018 Update 1.0

7. EVM model is based on 3GPP specification version 15.2.0

8.Datasheets are deleted because of the size of example, please rerun analysis to get the datasheet.

9.Parameter Bandwidth is used in this example and the realationship between bandwidth and number of RBs are shown in 38.104 table 5.3.2-1 and table 5.3.2-2. The configuration of subcarrier spacing 240kHz is also shown below. FrequencyRange is gotten by parameter FCarrierTx.

10.Filter is added to the demodulated signal if UseMcFilter (EVM model) is set to Yes and the same filter is used in VSA model by default setup file. According to the definition of SNR in 3GPP, it is the signal to noise ratio in bandwidth. In this model, if filter is not used, noise will be calculated on the whole band of samplingrate, in this case, EVM result may be 3dB worse when OversamplingOption is set to Ratio 2 compared to set to Ratio 1. If filter is used, impairment of filter may introduce performance degradation in noiseless scenario, EVM may around -70dB instead of -120dB, but this degradation disappears in noisy scenario.

11. When window is added in BeamformerWeights model, please connect magnitudes to Amplifier_M (A3) to control the magnitude.

12. Please active Amplifer_M (A1) to see result on non-linear PA.

13. If plotting on constellation is too slow, please decrease the parameter EVM_NumSlots in Equation to decrease number of slots on demodulated PDSCH.

14. Constellation may be slow because of the huge number of data, so constellation graph is set as only plot every 500 points of the data. If it is still slow, please change EVM_NumSlots to a smaller one to decrease the number of data in constellation graph.

15. Suggest to disable spectrum model when runing equation to get EIRP and pattern.

Workspace.Name: NR_LDPC_BLER_Measurement
Workspace.Description:
5G NR LDPC BLER Measurement

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This example workspace demonstrates BLER vs SNR measurements to evaluate the performance of LDPC decoding for 5G NR in AWGN (Additive White Gaussian Noise) channel. 

 

In this example, LDPC encoder and constellation mapper act as the source. Accordingly, a constellation demapper and LDPC decoder compose of the receiver. The results of this simulation can be used as the baseline when evaluated the performance of a complete NR system. 

 

NR has defined two base graphs for LDPC coding. Base graph 1 is designed to optimize BLER performance for block lengths from 512 to 8448 bits and code rates from 1/3 to 8/9. Base graph 2 is designed to optimize BLER performance for smaller block lengths, from 40 to 2560 bits and code rates from 1/5 to 2/3.

 

Many company have proposed their evaluation results to 3GPP. In this simulation, we select certain cases to compare with Huawei’s. The simulation results show a good conformance with Huawei’s results despite of limited SNR gap.

0.4

0.5

 

Note: The sweeping starts at (Sweep Start + Disparity) dB, increases in increment of Sweep Step, and terminates when reach (Sweep End + Disparity) dB. The ‘Sweep Start’ and ‘Sweep End’ refer to Huawei’s results. For BG1, refer to Figure 12. And for BG2, refer to Figure 36.

 

Simulation Instruction

  1. “TransBlockSize” and “CodingRate” are to set the TBS and coding rate respectively.
  2. Select Base Graph 1 by setting “LDPCBaseGraph” to 0, and Base Graph 2 by setting “LDPCBaseGraph” to 1;  
  3. When select the LDPC Algorithm to “Sum Product”, it’s equivalent to Huawei’s Flooding Belief Propagation algorithm.
  4. To avoid the use of the knowledge of SNR, “Normalized Min-Sum” algorithm can be used. In this case, it’s better to set “LDPC_ScalingFactor” to 0.8. Compared with “Sum Product”, this algorithm has less computing complexity. Therefore, it’s widely used by the hardware implemented LDPC decoder.

Workspace.Name: NR_PolarCode_BLER_Measurement
Workspace.Description:
5G NR Polar Code BLER Measurement

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This example workspace demonstrates BLER vs SNR measurements to evaluate the performance of Polar decoding for 5G NR in AWGN (Additive White Gaussian Noise) channel. 

 

In this example, Polar encoder and constellation mapper act as the source. Accordingly, a constellation demapper and polar decoder compose of the receiver. The results of this simulation can be used as the baseline when evaluated the performance of a complete NR system. 

  

Many company have proposed their evaluation results to 3GPP. In this simulation, we select certain cases to compare with Polaran’s [1]. The simulation results show a good conformance with Polaran’s results of decoder list number 1, as the polar decoder of SystemVue model uses the basic successive cancellation algorithm.

 

The simulation case is Number of Information Bits =104, Target Rate = 1/4 case in Table 1 of Reference [1]. The simulation results conform to the curve of Rate 1/4, List 1 case in Figure 1 of Reference [1]. It needs to consider the disparity 3dB, because it's 1x2 MIMO configuration in Reference [1] and SISO configuration in this simulation, which causes 3dB disparity in AWGN channel.

 

 

Reference

[1]  “A comparison of polar and LDPC codes for URLLC”, Polaran,  R1-1808541, 3GPP TSG RAN WG1 94 Meeting Gothenburg, Sweden, Aug 20-24, 2018.

Workspace.Name: NR_UE_OTA_ACS_Blocking
Workspace.Description:
NR_UE_OTA_ACS_Blocking

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This example can be configured to simulate two OTA measurements for UE receiver when the system is operating at FR2. The first measurement is Adjacent Channel Selectivity  and the other is In-band Blocking.

 

Adjacent Channel Selectivity is defined by section 7.5 of 3GPP TS 38.101-2 v15.4.0. Adjacent Channel Selectivity (ACS) is a measure of a receiver's ability to receive a NR signal at its assigned channel frequency in the presence of an adjacent channel signal at a given frequency offset from the centre frequency of the assigned channel. Its throughput shall meet or exceed 95% for the specified measurement channels.

 

In-band Blocking is defined by section 7.6.2 of 3GPP TS 38.101-2 v15.4.0. In-band blocking is defined for an unwanted interfering signal falling into the UE receive band or into the spectrum equivalent to twice the channel bandwidth below or above the UE receive band at which the relative throughput shall meet or exceed 95% for the specified measurement channels.

 

Both of these two measurements are measuring throughput while receiving the wanted signal with the presence of an interfering signal. For ACS, the interfering signal is located at the lower or upper adjacent channel whose bandwidth is equal to UE's channel bandwidth. While, for in-band blocking, the interfering signal falls into UE's receive band or into the spectrum equivalent to twice the channel bandwidth below or above the UE receive band. By specifying F_InterfererOffset in Hz in this example, both of these two measurements can be simulated.

 

NR signal configuration

FCarrier - the center frequency of wanted signal, which should be in the range defined by FR2(24250MHz~52600MHz).

F_InterfererOffset - the frequency offset between the center frequency of interfering signal and the center frequency of wanted signal in Hz.

Bandwidth - 0: 50MHz; 1: 100MHz; 2: 200MHz; 3: 400MHz. Refer to the Table 1 in the Appendix for the maximum number of RB contained in the bandwidth.

OversamplingOption - 0: Ratio 1; 1: Ratio 2; 2: Ratio 4; 3: Ratio 8; 4: Ratio 16; 5: Ratio 32; 6: Ratio 64.

P_WantedSignal - mean power level of wanted signal in dBm.

P_Interferer - mean power level of interferer signal in dBm.

Ephi - phi component of OTA polarization

Etheta - theta component of OTA polarization

NoiseFigure - the noise figure of UE receiver in dB.

SystemConfiguration - 0: FRC; 1: User Defined. If FRC is selected, the NR downlink signal is configured according to section A.3 in 3GPP TS 38.101-2. In design Blocking's Equation, FRC_Table specifies the FRC table to be used. 0: A.3.3.2-1; 1:A.3.3.2-2.  If User Defined is selected, user can configure the signal in design Blocking's Equation.

EnableTxFilter - wheter enable the low pass filter in transmitter(source model).

TxFIR_Taps - the number of low pass filter taps. It's valid when EnableTxFilter is YES.

EnableRxFilter - whether enable the band pass filter for receiving. It controls the BandPassFilter model in the design.

 

Measurement setup

The UE under test is equipped with a 4 x 4 antenna array. The radiation pattern of each antenna element is Three Sector Antenna for Y-Z URA, which is defined in Table 7.1-1 of 36.873. Its boresight direction, (φ=0, θ=90), is also the RX beam peak direction. According to standard, ACS and in-band blocking are measured when the AoA of the incident wave of the wanted signal and the interfering signal are both from the RX peak direction. ‘AoA_REF’ = 0 and ‘ZoA_REF’ = 90 are defined in the Equation of Design ‘Blocking’.

Incident downlink NR signal to the UE is simulated by the signal input into a probe of ‘OTA_TestRx’ model. The incident signal direction is specified by 3-D location of the probe, ProbeX, ProbeY and ProbeZ, which are calculated according to ‘Distance’, ‘AoA_REF’ and ‘ZoA_REF’ in the Equation of Design ‘Blocking’. Where, the ‘Distance’ can be used to specify whether the measurement happens in near field or far field.

The receiving beam direction of UE's antenna array is the same as that of incident signal. It’s specified by ‘Phi’ and ‘Theta’ of ‘BeamformerWeights’ model.

According to standard, the wanted and interfering signals apply to all supported polarization under the assumption of polarization match. Therefore, the polarization of incident wave and UE's receiving antenna elements are the same, specified by parameters 'Ephi' and 'Etheta'.

According to standard, both of the wanted signal and interfering signal are configured according to the reference measurement channels as specified in Annexes A.3.2 of 38.101-2. 

Throughput is measured within a duration of 100ms. To change it, please modify 'NumSimulationSlots' in the equation of design 'Blocking'.

 

Note :

   1. EnableTxFilter would reduce the out-band regrowth of wanted signal and interfering signal, but the filtering would make the simulation much slower than it's off.

   2. When the 'F_InterfererOffset' is large, the sampling rate of the source side would be very high. It will make the synchronization in the receiver side very slow. To avoid this unnecessary high sampling rate to be used in receiver, a downsampling model is used before receiver. In this case, please enable 'EnableRxFilter'.

 

 

Measurement Procedure

According to standard, the performance applies to all frequency offset, lower and upper range of power and all the polarization. Therefore, this simulation should performed by the various combinations of paramters, such as 'FCarrier', 'F_InterfererOffset', 'Bandwidth', 'P_WantedSignal', 'P_Interferer', 'Ephi' and 'Etheta'. The measurement pass if all of their throughput exceed 95%. This example just provides a single run. Users are recommended to add equation to go through the combination by running this example many times. 

 

Measurement Results

'Spectrum' shows the spectrum of wanted signal, interfering signal and their composite signal.  

Table 'TestResults' shows the measured throughput, and the pass/fail flag. 1 is pass and 0 is fail.

Workspace.Name: NR_UE_OTA_EIS
Workspace.Description:
NR_UE_OTA_EIS

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This example demonstrates two OTA measurements for UE receiver when the system is operating at FR2. The first measurement is the reference sensitivity power level REFSENS and the other is EIS spherical coverage.

 

Reference Sensitivity 

It provides a measurement of reference sensitivity power level according to section 7.3.2 of 3GPP TS 38.101-2 v15.4.0. The reference sensitivity power level REFSENS is the EIS level(total component) at the center of the quiet zone in the RX beam peak direction, at which the throughput shall meet or exceed 95% for the specified reference measurement channel.

 

NR signal configuration

FCarrier - the operating frequency has to be in the range defined by FR2(24250MHz~52600MHz).

Bandwidth - 0: 50MHz; 1: 100MHz; 2: 200MHz; 3: 400MHz. Refer to the Table 1 in the Appendix for the maximum number of RB contained in the bandwidth.

NoiseFigure - the noise figure of UE receiver in dB.

OversamplingOption - 0: Ratio 1; 1: Ratio 2; 2: Ratio 4; 3: Ratio 8; 4: Ratio 16; 5: Ratio 32; 6: Ratio 64.

SystemConfiguration - 0: FRC; 1: User Defined. If FRC is selected, the NR downlink signal is configured according to section A.3 in 3GPP TS 38.101-2. In design RefSen's Equation, FRC_Table specifies the FRC table to be used. 0: A.3.3.2-1; 1:A.3.3.2-2.  If User Defined is selected, user can configure the signal in design RefSen's Equation.

 

Measurement Setup

The UE under test is equipped with a 4 x 4 antenna array. The radiation pattern of each antenna element is Three Sector Antenna for Y-Z URA, which is defined in Table 7.1-1 of 36.873. Its boresight direction, (φ=0, θ=90), is also the RX beam peak direction. ‘AoA_REF’ = 0 and ‘ZoA_REF’ = 90 are defined in the Equation of Design ‘RefSen’.

Incident downlink NR signal to the UE is simulated by the signal input into a probe of ‘OTA_TestRx’ model. The incident signal direction is specified by 3-D location of the probe, ProbeX, ProbeY and ProbeZ, which are calculated according to ‘Distance’, ‘AoA_REF’ and ‘ZoA_REF’ in the Equation of Design ‘RefSen’. Where, the ‘Distance’ can be used to specify whether the measurement happens in near field or far field.

The receiving beam direction of UE's antenna array is the same as that of incident signal. It’s specified by ‘Phi’ and ‘Theta’ of ‘BeamformerWeights’ model.

The polarization of incident signal and UE’s receiving antenna elements are always aligned. They are specified by ‘PolarizationE_theta’ and ‘PolarizationE_phi’ in the Equation of Design ‘RefSen’.

The power level of incident signal is specified by the ‘SignalPower’ in the Equation of Design ‘RefSen’. It’s the signal’s power at the input of ‘OTA_TestRx’ model.

 

Measurement Procedure

Run equation ‘MeasSensitivity ~A’ to measure the REFSENS.

1)  Determine EIS(PolMeas= θ, PolLink= θ) for θ-polarization. Set  PolarizationE_theta = 1.0 and PolarizationE_phi = 1.0, which is 45 degree linear polarization. Sweep the power in a coarse step, 3dB, first. And then sweep the power in a fine step, 0.5dB, until the throughput exceeding 95%.

2)  Determine EIS(PolMeas= φ, PolLink= φ) for φ-polarization. Set  PolarizationE_theta = 1.0 and PolarizationE_phi = -1.0, which is -45 degree linear polarization. Sweep the power in a coarse step, 3dB, first. And then sweep the power in a fine step, 0.5dB, until the throughput exceeding 95%.

3)  Calculate the resulting averaged EIS as:

            EIS = 2/[1/EIS(PolMeas= θ, PolLink= θ) +1/EIS(PolMeas= φ, PolLink= φ)]

Measurement Results

Go to dataset ‘RefSen_Analysis_RefSen_Data’. ‘EIS_Etheta’ is EIS(PolMeas= θ, PolLink= θ), and ‘EIS_Ephi’ is 1/EIS(PolMeas= φ, PolLink= φ). ‘REFSENS’ is the reference EIS at the RX beam peak direction, and it’s also shown in Table ‘MeasSensitivity_REFSENS’.

 

EIS Spherical Coverage 

It provides a measurement of EIS spherical coverage according to section 7.3.4 of 3GPP TS 38.101-2 v15.4.0. EIS spherical coverage is defined as the maximum EIS at the 85th percentile of the CCDF of EIS measured over the full sphere around the UE. 

This measurement requires EIS is measured at each point on the spherical coverage grids. This is quite time consuming. A fast approach is adopted by this example. Instead of measuring EIS, RSRP (Reference signal receiving power) is measured. With the knowledge of REFSENS and its RSRP at the RX beam peak direction, it's readily to derive the EIS at a given direction according to its RSRP.

            EIS(φ, θ) = REFSENS + (REF RSRP - RSRP(φ, θ))

WARNING : This approach is only feasible for downlink signal with single layer.

                      Please make sure the signal configuration and phase array antenna setup are consistent in design 'RefSen' and 'RSRP_SphericalCoverage'.

 

To measure the RSRP, NR downlink signal is configured like, PDSCH taking all RBs in the carrier and all symbols in the slot. SSB is disabled. For the receiver side, a power meter is used to measure the power over 0.5ms duration.

 

NR signal configuration

FCarrier - the operating frequency has to be in the range defined by FR2(24250MHz~52600MHz).

Bandwidth - 0: 50MHz; 1: 100MHz; 2: 200MHz; 3: 400MHz. Refer to the Table 1 in the Appendix for the maximum number of RB contained in the bandwidth.

OversamplingOption - 0: Ratio 1; 1: Ratio 2; 2: Ratio 4; 3: Ratio 8; 4: Ratio 16; 5: Ratio 32; 6: Ratio 64.

 

Measurement Setup

The UE under test is equipped with a 4 x 4 antenna array. The radiation pattern of each antenna element is Three Sector Antenna for Y-Z URA, which is defined in Table 7.1-1 of 36.873.

The incident direction of  downlink NR signal to the UE and UE's receiving beam direction is always aligned. They are changing steering direction simultaneously every 0.5ms.

The incident signal direction is controlled by the inputs of 'OTA_TestRx' model. They are 3-D location of the probe, ProbeX, ProbeY and ProbeZ, which are calculated according to ‘Distance’, ‘AoA’ and ‘ZoA’ in the Equation of Design ‘RSRP_SphericalCoverage’. Where, the ‘Distance’ can be used to specify whether the measurement happens in near field or far field.

The receiving beam direction of UE's antenna array is controlled by inputs of ‘BeamformerWeights’ model,  ‘Phi’ and ‘Theta’.

The polarization of incident signal and UE’s receiving antenna elements are always aligned. They are specified by ‘PolarizationE_theta’ and ‘PolarizationE_phi’ in the Equation of Design ‘RefSen’.

The power level of incident signal is specified by the ‘SignalPower’ in parameter list of Design ‘RSRP_SphericalCoverage’. It’s the signal’s power at the input of ‘OTA_TestRx’ model.

Three different spherical coverage measurement grids are considered.

  • 47 test points with equal density around the sphere, which is extended to full sphere based on Figure 4 in R4-1700100.
  • Constant step size grid type which has the azimuth and elevation angles uniformly distributed. It’s proposed by G.1.2 in 38.810-g10. It has 266 test points in total.
  • Constant density grid type which has measurement points that are evenly distributed on the surface of the sphere with a constant density. It’s proposed by G.1.2 in 38.810-g10. Charged particle grid implementation is used by this example. It has 266 test points in total.

The test points for each grid type are plotted in graph ‘47TestPoints’, ‘ConstDensityTestPoints’ and ‘ConstStepTestPoints’ respectively.

 

Measurement Procedure

There are three equations to measure the EIS spherical coverage, ‘EIS_47points ~A’, ‘EIS_ConstDensity ~A’ and ‘EIS_ConstStep ~A’. Their measurement procedure are the same except using the different spherical grids.

1)      Set polarization of probe and antenna element to 45 degree linear polarization.

2)      Measure the RSRP at RX beam peak direction, RSRP_REF;

3)      Steering to each test points on the surface of sphere, and measure RSRP(φ, θ);

4)      Calculate EIS_pol1(φ, θ) = REFSENS + (RSRP_REF - RSRP(φ, θ))

5)      Set polarization of probe and antenna element to -45 degree linear polarization.

6)      Repeat step 2) to 4), obtain EIS_pol2(φ, θ);

7)      Calculate the resulting averaged EIS as:

EIS(φ, θ)  = 2/[1/ EIS_pol1(φ, θ) +1/ EIS_pol2(φ, θ)]

8)      Calculate CCDF of EIS. When using constant step size measurement grids, a theta-dependent correction shall be applied. The PDF probability contribution for each measurement point is scaled by sin(θ).

9)      Calculate the EIS at 85% of the CCDF.

Measurement Results

The results are save in dataset ‘EIS_Results’.

The CCDF trace of each type of spherical grid is plotted in ‘EIS_CCDF’. The measured EIS spherical coverage are in table ‘EIS_at_85th_percentile_CCDF’.

EIS_Pattern shows -EIS_pol1(φ, θ) of constant step grid in 3-D graph by running equation 'PlotEISPattern'.

 

'47TestPoints', 'ConstDensityTestPoints' and 'ConstStepTestPoints' show the test points on the surface of a full sphere for the 3 grid types respectively.

 

Running equation 'PlotRxBeamPattern' can plot the RX beam pattern at  φ=0, θ=90.

Workspace.Name: NR_UL_PRACH
Workspace.Description:
NR Uplink PRACH Tx

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This example workspace demonstrates spectrum and waveform for a NR uplink PRACH generator according to 38.211 v15.4.0 (December 2018).

In this example, where PRACH is enabled, all parameters are set in Equations with detailed description except for FCarrier set in Parameters.

PRACH is configured according to Table 6.3.3.2-2 with PRACH Configuration Index 27 in this example. Two individual PRACH preambles are generated to emulate preambles from two different UEs. Parameters for each preamble are configured by individual PRACH parameters as PRACH_PowerBoosting, PRACH_TimingOffset, PRACH_PreambleIndex, PRACH_FrameOffset, PRACH_SubFrameSlotNumber, PRACH_nRAt, PRACH_nRAslot and PRACH_nRAf. Each of these parameters includes 2 elements with the first one for the first preamble and the second one for the second preamble.

In this example, the first preamble is set to be transmitted in subframe 0 of every frame and the second preamble is transmitted in subframe 5. Two time domain waveforms of the two preambles are plotted in PRACH_SeperatePreambleWaveform Graph. In frequency domain, two preambles are also set to different frequency resources with the first preamble's PRACH_nRAf set to 0 and the second one to 7. Therefore two preambles can also be distinguished from each other easily in PRACH_Spectrum Graph. More information about PRACH preambles is posted in Simulation Log box.

 

Following results are stored and plotted in graphs after simulation:

  1. Each time domain waveform of the two preambles are plotted in PRACH_SeperatePreambleWaveform Graph.
  2. Combined time domain waveform of the two preambles is plotted in PRACH_CombinedWaveform Graph.
  3. Frequency domain spectrum is plotted in PRACH_Spectrum Graph.

PRACH demodulation with VSA is also supported in this example with a pre-configured VSA setup-file. The target demod PRACH preamble is the first one of the two preambles transmitted in this example. VSA setup file generation is based on VSA 2019 Update 1.0. To ensure VSA simulation, please make sure to Exit Vector Signal Analyzer (89600 VSA) under Action tab before new simulation. 

 

Please run the analysis to check results of this example.

Workspace.Name: NR_UL_Throughput
Workspace.Description:
NR UL Throughput

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This example showcases New Radio uplink system. Upon the designs, throughput and BER can be measured. 

 

SISO Case

In the SISO case, AWGN channel is used to help measure performance under different SNR values. After the simulation, fractional throughput curve and uncoded BER curve are obtained. The simulated uncoded BER curve is compared with an ideal BER curve calculated by berawgn in MATLAB, where minor gap is observed. Please note that parameter "MMSE_RBWinLen" in the receiver would influence the performance in some degree. Run Sweep_SISO equation to get the following curves:

1. Uncoded BER vs. SNR

2. Througput (%) vs. SNR

 

Note that in the SISO case, the sweep parameter in Sweep_SISO is SNR.

 

 

Signal Power Setting

In the design, there is one Oscillator following the NR_UL_Source. The Oscillator is used to tune the signal power to a specific power level, together with NR_UL_Source.

If there are one port and one RF chain for the signal transmission, the signal power setting is straightforward:

If you specify the Power Parameter to, say 20, in Oscillator with unit dBm, the signal would be tuned to be with power 20dBm/15kHz in the frequency range where it's allocated.

No matter what subcarrier spacing is used, the power spectrum would be 20dBm/15kHz in the frequency range where it's allocated.

That means if 30kHz subcarrier spacing is specified, it results in 23dBm/30kHz.

 

Normally, multiple ports would be configured. Therefore the resulting signal power spectrum would vary upon different configurations.

Let's assume Power is still set to 20. and Let's take an example: if three ports are configured: port 0 and port 1 for PDSCH transmission and port 1000 for SRS transmission. Three RF chains are equipped for the transmission.

If PortRFMappingMatrix = [1 0 0 1 1 1], the first RF chain transmit both port 0 signal and port 1000 signal. Considering port 1000 signal is only transmitted in limited slots, the power spectrum would be still 20dBm/15kHz in the frequence range where PUSCH is allocated. The same thing happens for the second RF chain.

If PortRFMappingMatrix = [1 1 1 1 1 1], which means signals associated with port 0, port 1 and port 1000 are all transmitted in both RF chains. In this case, the power spectrum would be 23dBm/15kHz in the frequency range where PUSCH transmission is allocated.

The setting PortRFMappingMatrix = [1 1 1 1 1 1] doesn't make sense if you want to succeed the transmission, but it's a good example to elaborate the power setting hereby.

Workspace.Name: NR_UL_TM
Workspace.Description:
3GPP NR Uplink Test Model

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Workspace

This workspace provides a test bench to generate 3GPP new radio (NR) uplink signal defined by Table 6.1-1 in 3GPP 38.521-1/38.521-2(V16.1.0 - 2019.09).

NR uplink signal configuration:

  • Bandwidth specifies the full bandwidth of signal. Numerology determines the subcarrier spacing used by OFDM. Refer to 3GPP 38.101-1 Table 5.3.2-1 for the valid combination of Bandwidth and Numerology, and the maximum number of RB derived from them.
  • CommonConfig_FR1 specifies the RB allocation type defined by Table 6.1-1 in 3GPP 38.521-1. FCarrier operating in FR1(450 MHz ~ 6000 MHz) .
  • CommonConfig_FR2 specifies the RB allocation type defined by Table 6.1-1 in 3GPP 38.521-2. FCarrier operating in FR2(24250 MHz ~ 52600 MHz) .
  • OFDM_Type specifies whether PUSCH is DFT-S-OFDM or CP-OFDM.
  • Modulation specifies the modulation format used by PUSCH.
  • NumSubframes specifies the output signal length in terms of 1ms.
  • EnableTxFilter enables an ideal low pass filter for spectrum shapping.
  • FIR_Taps specifies the number of filter taps when EnableTxFilter is true.

Try to change the parameters, run NR_UL_Tx_Analysis and check the simulation results.

  • Graph Waveform shows the transmitted time domain waveform.

To measure EVM for the selected test model, please enable EVM model.

Workspace.Name: NR_UL_Tx
Workspace.Description:
NR UL Tx

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This example workspace demonstrates spectrum, EVM, ACLR and CCDF measurements for an NR uplink transmitter. FRC uplink cases in 38.101-1 are also shown in design FRC.

In Design 1, numerology is 15kHz and bandwidth is set to 50MHz (270 RB). PUSCH is transmitted with RB 0~269 and symbol 1~13.

Overall the followings are the features supported in the example.

1. NR transmitter signal with multiple numerologies 

2. Spectrum, EVM, ACLR and CCDF measurements are supported

3. EVM measurement is based on VSA with auto generated VSA setup-file

 

The followings are the results after simulation:

1.  Transmit spectrum (see Spectrum Graph)

2.  Waveform of uplink transmitter (see Waveform Graph)

4.  ACLR (see ACLR_Table Table)

5.  CCDF (see CCDF Graph)

  

NR EVM measurement

 

The EVM measurement is based on VSA and version of VSA should be VSA 2018 Update 1.0 or later version. Please exit VSA instance before starting new simulation.

 

EVM model is based on 3GPP specification version 15.2.0.

 

Filter is added to the demodulated signal if UseMcFilter (EVM model) is set to Yes and the same filter is used in VSA model by default setup file. According to the definition of SNR in 3GPP, it is the signal to noise ratio in bandwidth. In this model, if filter is not used, noise will be calculated on the whole band of samplingrate, in this case, EVM result may be 3dB worse when OversamplingOption is set to Ratio 2 compared to set to Ratio 1. If filter is used, impairment of filter may introduce performance degradation in noiseless scenario, EVM may around -70dB instead of -120dB, but this degradation disappears in noisy scenario.

 

ACLR measurement

 

ACLR is calculate by equation ACLR using spectrum data in Design Analysis_Design_Data/FRC Analysis_FRC_Data. Please keep the parameters in ACLR equation shown below consistent with the parameters in Design. Please set OversamplingOption no less than 2(Ratio 4) when calculated ACLR.

FR1

bandwidth = 50e6; %%%Hz

FCarrier = 1e9; %%% Hz

CarrierNumRBs = 270;

SCS = 15e3; %%%Hz

 

Please run the equation if spectrum data are updated.

Spectrum shanpping is added in Source to ensure ACLR performance. 

 

CCDF measurement

Reference curve (CCDF of white gaussian noise) is also plotted on these graphs.

 

Refer to subclause 6.1.4 of TS38.214, using parameters Modulation, TBS and location of PUSCH, same frame configuration can be set. Please refer to Note of example NR_DL_Tx on How to set MCS using parameters in example.

 

FRC

FRC design is based on A.2 of 3GPP 38.101-1 v15.4.0. If there are several cases of different number of allocated resource block in the same bandwidth in one table, please use parameter TestCase to choose different case. Number of RBs of Case1 to Case 6 is in ascending order, for example, in table A.2.2.1-1 for bandwidth 5MHz, number of RBs for Case 1 is 1, Case 2 is 12 and Case 3 is 25. This design is based on FR1. Paremeters for different table are set in Equation. The rest of parameters which are not list in A.2 are set in Source model and EVM model. Please make sure parameters consistent for those two models. PUCCH is not enabled. OCNG is not supported in EVM model, so Fill_OCNG is set to NO in source model in this desgin.

 

If OperationMode is FDD, FRC_Table specifies the tables defined in A.2.2. If it's TDD, FRC_Table selects the tables defined in A.2.3.

In TDD mode, EVM model only measure the first active slot in a radio frame.

 

Note:

Some results in datasheet are deleted to decrease the size of this example, please run simulation to get the results.

NR uplink numerology source is updated to 3GPP specification v15.3.0. The version of EVM model is v15.2.0. In order to make the demodulation successful, it is important to make the parameters make sense for those two models.

Some results in datasheet are deleted because the size of this example. Please rerun analysis to get the total results.

Constellation can be shown when parameter SaveConstellation set to YES in EVM model.Constellation Graph may take more time to plot the graph due to huge number of points, in this case, please set parameter EVM_NumSlots in Equation which is the number of slots of demodulated PUSCH to shorten the time plotting constellation. For now, EVM_NumSlots is set to 5 in Design1 and it is set to different value in FRC by different cases.

EVM model will internally calculate Numerology_k0 with the configured GridStart according to definition in 5.3 of 38.211. EVM measurements might be wrong in case of multiple different Numerologies setting with ResourceGridEnable for NR_Source disabled, where Numerology_k0 is set manually by users, unless it is calculated and set correctly. Therefore, ResourceGridEnable is set to YES by default in this example.

Workspace.Name: NR_UL_Tx_OTA
Workspace.Description:
NR UL Tx OTA

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This example workspace demonstrates spectrum, EIRP (CDF), TRP and ACLR measurements for an NR uplink transmitter. SCS 120kHz (FR2) is selected in this example with antenna beam. BWP is in 120kHz. There is one PUSCH in the CC. Distance is set to 300 lambda which is treated as far field scenario.

 

Overall the followings are the features supported in the example.

1. NR transmitter signal with multiple numerologies 

2. Spectrum, CCDF, ACLR, EIRP TRP and CDF on EIRP measurements are supported

3. Performance in VSA are shown with pre-configured VSA setup-file

4. Tx RF channel modeling and Tx phased array structure for FR2

 

The followings are the results after simulation:

1. Transmit spectrum (see Spectrum Graph) using the data in Design Analysis_Design_Data

2. ACLR (see ACLR_Table Table) using the data in Design Analysis_Design_Data

3. Gain power pattern in upper hemisphere for near field (see PowerPattern DAV) using the data in WorkspaceVariables

4. CDF on EIRP (see CDF_EIRP Graph) using the data in WorkspaceVariables

5. Test points for CDF on EIRP (see 27TestPoints, StepTestPoints and UVTestPoints) using the data in WorkspaceVariables

6. Beam peak value on EIRP (see EIRP_BeamPeak Table) using the data in WorkspaceVariables

7. TRP of different test measurement (see TRP Table) using the data in WorkspaceVariables

8. EIRP on 85% point of CDF curve (see EIRP85%CDF Table) using the data in WorkspaceVariables

  

EIRP TRP and CDF on EIRP

OversamplingOption is set to ratio 1 to speed up the simulation. EIRP of uplink is the gain power for upper hemisphere. There are three Equation to get EIRP based on different test points. In Equation EIRP_Step, test points are chosen according to theta and phi which will caused non-uniform density test points on the hemisphere. Step is 12 degrees and there are total 248 test points. In Equation EIRP_27points, positions of 27 test points are gotten according to R4-1700100. In Equation EIRP_UV, test points are defined in UV coordinates refer to R4-1700095 and there are total 225 test points but only 152 test points are in the upper hemisphere. CDF on EIRP is calculated and shown in figure CDF_EIRP when beam direction is theta = 30deg and phi = 45degree. Test points of those three methods are also shown in figures. EIRP on 85% CDF curve is also gotten in the table EIRP85%CDF. If 85%CDF is the test point, value of this point will be defined as EIRP on 85% CDF, if not, interpolation value of the nearest points of 85% CDF will be defined as EIRP on 85%. TRP is based on the same test points of CDF on EIRP. TRP is calculated by different formulas on those three measurement grids. Because EIRP_Step is based on constant step size measurement grid and the other two are based on constant density measurement grid.

 

Beam Peak on EIRP

Beam peak is based on the maximum of EIRP on those three measurements grid. PeakSearchRange and PeakSearchStep are defined on the top of each Equation to define the range and step around maximum EIRP to search beam peak. Beam peak search range is from -PeakSearchRange to PeakSearchRange around location of maximum EIRP on AoD and ZoD. And PeakSearchRange and PeakSearchStep are defined on unit of degree.

 

Power Pattern

Power pattern is gotten by running equation EIRP_Step. Power Pattern are gotten with OversamplingOption ratio 1 and FileterEnable No to speed up. There are three parts in equation EIRP_Step, the first part is to calculate the gain power for upper hemisphere and the second part is to show the pattern and test points and the last is to calculate the CDF on EIRP. In this example, beam direction is set to theta 30 degree and phi 45 degree, and the results are given in upper hemisphere and the resolution is 12 degrees. 

 

ACLR measurement

ACLR is calculated by equation ACLR using spectrum data in Design Analysis_Design_Data. Please keep the parameters in ACLR equation shown below consistent with the parameters in Design.

bandwidth = 100e6; %%%Hz
FCarrier = 28e9; %%% Hz
CarrierNumRBs = 66;
SCS = 120e3; %%%Hz

Please run the equation if spectrum data are updated.

Spectrum shapping is added in Source to ensure ACLR performance.

 

How to model dual polarization of probe

Open the GUI of OTA_TestTx, go to page Probe Configuration and set Antennas Per Location (ProbeNumAntennasPerLocation) to be 2. Then go to page Element Pattern and insert probe element pattern. Please set the buswidth of output of OTA_TestTx to be 2 which is the signal on two probe elements separately.

 

If you want to get performance on near field scenario, please change the distance in equation.

 

NR uplink source is updated to 3GPP specification version v15.3.0.

NR Vector IODT

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This example workspace demonstrates SSB test vectors auto-generation. Other IODT test vectors can be generated in similar approach.

 

Equation "AutoGenTestVectors" specifies the behavior of generating test vectors for multiple test cases and Equation "SingleTC_Generation" would only run one specific TC for debug purpose.

If the saved files are used in MATLAB, please use "load" function to load the data in file and restore the complex signal accordingly, such as load('TC1_TimeDomain_SSB_Real.txt') + sqrt(-1) *load('TC1_TimeDomain_SSB_Real.txt')

Workspace.Name: ChannelSounding_MIMO_4x4
Workspace.Description:
Channel Sounding Simulation in 4x4 MIMO System

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This example workspace demonstrates the performance of channel sounding algorithm in 4x4 MIMO system.  

 

Simulation Instruction

  1. Set parameter 'NumBlock' to define the number of data block for simulation.
  2. Set parameter 'CarrierFreq' to define the carrier frequency of the MIMO system.
  3. Set parameter 'SampleRate', 'TriggerPeriod' and 'PulseLength' to define the channel sounding signal. For each period, the sample number of channel sounding waveform is SampleRate*TriggerPeriod and the valid sample number is specified by PulseLength.
  4. Set parameter 'UseRefSig' to specify whether using the reference signal or not. If set 'UseRefSig' to '1', reference signal will be enabled.
  5. Model 'MIMO_3DChannel' is used in this example and the channel configuration can be changed for different test cases. A 4x4 MIMO channel is set by default.
  6. Configurable parameters are provided for channel profile extraction in model 'ChannelSounding_Extractor'.  'MaxPathDelay' specifies the maximum path delay and 'PathDetThr' specifies the minimum path power to be detected.
  7. The results can be observed in the table 'Data_Result' and graph 'ChCIR' and 'ChPDP'. More results can be found in dataset 'Design1_Data'.
  8. Set parameter 'ShowBlockIndex' to choose the index of data block to show the results in table and graphs.
  9. Set parameter 'ShowTxIndex' and 'ShowRxIndex' to choose the index of Tx and Rx antenna pair to show the results in table and graphs.

    With default, the dataset does not exist in this workspace due to its huge size. To get the results, please run the simulation.

Workspace.Name: Beamforming_DigMod_BER
Workspace.Description:
Narrowband Hybrid Beamforming Architecture 

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Workspace

 

This example demonstrates a flexible and configurable narrowband hybrid beamforming system. The Digital Modulation source and receiver are used and so the license for DigMod is needed.

  • Supported Features:
            1. Support flexible beamforming structure, including full digital beamforming, hybrid beamforming and full RF/analog beamforming. 
            2. For hybrid beamforming and full RF/analog beamforming, a reference algorithm model is provided to train beamformer in transmitter and receiver given the ideal channel information.
            3. A 3D MIMO channel is provided supporting use-defined scenario per 3GPP 3D MIMO standard and NYU scenario for mmwave frequency.
            4. Support customer beam pattern import and RF impairment.
  • Note1

All configurations are collected in "Equations" Tab of the schematic and relavant comments are attached following the corresponding settings.
1. ULA and UPA are supported in y-z plane, which says antenna number in x-axis direction should equals to one.
2. The way to construct the vectors, such as TxPosition_X, TxPosition_Y, TxPosition_Z, TxAntennaArrayMask, TxPhaseShifterDistortion in Tx.As for TxPosition_X, TxPosition_Y and TxPosition_Z, the order of the elements in these vectors are antenna in y-axis first, in z-axis second and in x-axis third. The length of these vectors is Nt. The structure of counterparts in Rx is the same. As for TxAntennaArrayMask, the dimension is Nt-by-Ntrf. The first column corresponds to the connections between the first RF chain and each antenna elements, and the second column corresponds to the connections between the second RF chain and each antenna elements, and so on. The value of each element is 0 or 1. 1 indicates connected and 0 indicates disabled. The structure of counterparts in Rx is the same. As for TxPhaseShifterDistortion, the dimension is also Nt-by-Ntrf. The structure is the same as TxAntennaArrayMask. But the value of each element can be complex which represents the amplitude distortion and phase distortion.
3. The parameter "OSR" is OverSampling Rate which is four in the example.
4. "PathDelay" is a parameter for channel modeling and the values in the example are all zero (in terms of seconds). Please keep these values zeros, because only narrowband transmission is supported in this demo. Both reference 2-path and 4-path channel configurations are provided for demonstration.
6. The angle scopes for plotting are [0,180] for zenith and 0,360] for azimuth, so the mirror radiation pattern would show in case of ULA and UPA configuration. The plotting granularity is 1 degree.

 

  • Note2:
    1. The DigMod source and receiver only support single RF chain, so the maximum number of RF chains in transmitter and receiver are 1 in this example. The maximum number of antennas in transmitter and receiver is 256.|
    2. SubtractionDuetoCH = 0.306dB need subtracted from the signal's simulation SNR due to the power boost introduced by 3D channel model. Please note that the value is only available in current configuration and it should be adjusted according to the channel configuration (including parameter "Seed" and the number of antennas).

    All configurations are collected in Equations Tab of the schematic and relavant comments are attached following the corresponding settings.
    1. ULA and UPA are supported in y-z plane, which says antenna number in x-axis direction should equals to one.
    2. The way to construct the vectors, such as TxPosition_X, TxPosition_Y, TxPosition_Z, TxAntennaArrayMask, TxPhaseShifterDistortion in Tx.As for TxPosition_X, TxPosition_Y and TxPosition_Z, the order of the elements in these vectors are antenna in y-axis first, in z-axis second and in x-axis third. The length of these vectors is Nt. The structure of counterparts in Rx is the same. As for TxAntennaArrayMask, the dimension is Nt-by-Ntrf. The first column corresponds to the connections between the first RF chain and each antenna elements, and the second column corresponds to the connections between the second RF chain and each antenna elements, and so on. The value of each element is 0 or 1. 1 indicates connected and 0 indicates disabled. The structure of counterparts in Rx is the same. As for TxPhaseShifterDistortion, the dimension is also Nt-by-Ntrf. The structure is the same as TxAntennaArrayMask. But the value of each element can be complex which represents the amplitude distortion and phase distortion.
    3. Since data flow is delayed, the parameter nDiscard is introduced to align the reference bits and demodulated bits, then, a reasonable BER can be obtained. The parameter OSR is OverSampling Rate which is four in the example and the corresponding filter length in Tx and Rx is 41.
