Workspace.Name: Beamforming_NarrowBand_Source
Workspace.Description:
Narrowband Hybrid Beamforming Measurement

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This example provides the measurement for beamforming transmission with narrowband hybrid beamforming system.

 

Supported features:

·         Support flexible beamforming structure, including full digital beamforming, hybrid beamforming and full RF/analog beamforming.

·         Support narrow band single-carrier transmission

·         Support RF impairments

·         Support Taylor window for RF beamforming

·         Support antenna coupling

·         Support CCDF and spectrum measurement

·         Support transmitter dynamic 3D beam plotting for combined signal and each RF channel

·         Support customer beam pattern import with EMpro and HFSS formats

·         Support EVM measurement and constellation output

 

The parameters to configure the simulation are located in Equation Tab of Design1 with the following categories.

·         System configuration: set key parameters for the whole system, including central frequency, sample rate, power and RF chains. Also users can set desired beam direction for each RF chains.

·         Antenna array configuration: define antenna array structure and the mapping from RF chains to antennas.

·         Impairment analysis: set the impairments in antenna array, RF power amplifiers.

·         Source Configuration: configure single-carrier source

Notes:

1.       For antenna array, ULA (uniform linear array) and UPA (uniform planar array) arrays are supported. And the antenna array is expected to be placed on Y-Z plane which means the number of antennas in x-axis (NumOfAntx) should be equal to 1.

2.       For antenna pattern predefined for three sector antenna when AntennaPatternType = Three Sector Antenna for Y-Z URA, the generated antenna pattern towards x-axis which is consistent with the assumption of antenna array in Y-Z plane.

3.   As a result, to have custom antenna pattern work properly, it is expected that custom 3D antenna beam pattern towards x-axis when AntennaPatternType = Pattern File.

4.     For EVM measurement, the default receiver beamforming is optimal as the recevier beams (defined by RxTheta and RxPhi in Equations Tab) are exactly pointed to transmit beam directions. Users can change thest two values if reveiver beamforming is not ideal.

With default, the dataset does not exist in this workspace due to its huge size. To get the results, please run the simulation.

Workspace.Name: Beamforming_WideBand_BER
Workspace.Description:
OFDM-based Wideband Hybrid Beamforming Systems

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Workspace

 

This example demonstrates a complete link-level OFDM-based wideband hybrid beamforming system: it comprises of complete source, channel and receiver.

  • Supported Features:
            1. Support flexible beamforming structure, including full digital beamforming, hybrid beamforming and full RF/analog beamforming. 
            2. For hybrid beamforming and full RF/analog beamforming, a reference algorithm model is provided to train wideband OFDM-based RF beamforming in transmitter and receiver given estimated channel status independent of digital beamforming process (i.e. MIMO precoding), where the training solution is based on a pre-defined training process.
            3. OFDM MIMO source and receiver can be configured to wideband signal with different frame structure. In typical settings, there are two preambles, the first preamble is used for the synchronization in the receiver, and the second preamble is used to train transmitter RF beamforming and receiver RF beamforming in the receiver. 
            4. In OFDM MIMO, digital beamforming process (MIMO precoding) can be turned on or off.
            5. A 3D MIMO channel is provided supporting user-defined scenario per 3GPP 3D MIMO standard and NYU scenario for mmWave frequency.
            6. Support custom antenna element pattern import and RF impairment, when custom antenna element pattern is imported, parameters BearingAngle, DowntiltAngle and SlantAngle can be set accordingly to rotate the antenna element pattern to appropriate coordinate system.
            7. Support transmitter and receiver dynamic 3D beam plotting
            8. Support BER measurement and received constellation plotting
  • Settings Notes:
    Flexible configurations are supported by the hybrid beamforming architecture.
    In the following, parameters configuration with respect to 3 types of beamforming architectures and the common parameters are listed.
    For easy comparison to ideal QPSK, current example configures the architecture to RF/analog beamforming and simulation with Omni antenna element pattern.
    The configuration for aforementioned three beamforming modes are
      Digital beamforming
      RF channels = 16 (from the output of FlexOFDM MIMO)
      TxAntennaArrayMask and RxAntennaArrayMask should be set to identity diagonal matrix
      The algorithm model to train RF beamforming is not used
      Digital beamforming process (MIMO precoding) can be enabled, and the precoding gain can be observed from the simulation.
          RF/analog beamforming
      RF channels = 1 (from the output of FlexOFDM MIMO)
      The algorithm model to train RF beamforming is used to get RF beaforming in both transmitter and receiver.
      Digital beamforming process (MIMO precoding) is not used
          Hybrid beamforming
      RF channels = 2, 4, or 8 (from the output of FlexOFDM MIMO)
      The algorithm model to train RF beamforming is used to get RF beaforming in both transmitter and receiver.
      Digital beamforming process (MIMO precoding) can be enabled, and the precoding gain can be observed from the simulation.
    Common parameters:
      FFT Size = 64, Bandwidth = 2G, Central Frequency = 28.5GHz
      Transmit antennas = 16, receiver antennas = 4
      MIMO channel is set to NYU use-defined with one or two predefined AOA and AOD.
      One OFDM symbol for Preamble 1 for synchronization
      Multiple OFDM symbols for Preamble 2 for RF beamforming training (defined in equation based on other parameters)
      In data part, one pilot is allocated per every three subcarriers for channel estimation. The total number of data symbols is configurable.
  • Regarding RF beamforming
    For RF/analog beamforming and hybrid beamforming, RF beamforming in both transmitter and receiver is the key advantage to improve signal quality (SNR). There is one reference algorithm model in this workspace to calculate optimal RF beamforming in both transmitter and receiver with the assistance of preamble data. Ideally, the maximum total SNR gain (in dB) of RF beamforming is 10*log10(Nt)+10*log10(Nr), where Nt is the number of transmitter antennas and Nr is the number of receiver antennas.
  • Other Configuration Notice
    All configurations are collected in "Equations" Tab of the schematic and relavant comments are attached following the corresponding settings and sampling rate.
    1. The number of antenna elements in x-axis direction should equals to one when UPA/ULA is applied.
    2. the way to construct the vectors, such as TxPosition_X, TxPosition_Y, TxPosition_Z, TxAntennaArrayMask, TxPhaseShifterDistortion in Tx.
    As for TxPosition_X, TxPosition_Y and TxPosition_Z, the order of the elements in these vectors are antenna in y-axis first, in z-axis second and in x-axis third. The length of these vectors is Nt. The
    structure of counterparts in Rx is similar. 
    As for TxAntennaArrayMask, the dimension is Nt-by-Ntrf. The first column correspond to the connections between the first RF chain and each antenna elements, and the second
    column corresponds to the connnections between the second RF chain and each antenna elements, and so on. The value of each element is 0 or 1. 1 indicates connected and 0 indicates disabled.
    The structure of counterparts in Rx is the same.
    As for TxPhaseShifterDistortion, the dimension is also Nt-by-Ntrf. The structure is the same as TxAntennaArrayMask. But the value of each element can be complex which
    represents the amplitude distortion and phase distortion.
    Where, Ntrf and Nrrf are the numbers of RF chains in Tx and Rx side, respectively.
    3. There is an equation related to visualization: "Plot_Omni". It's for Omni antenna configuration, and it dedicates to show the overall transmitting signal's beam shape, by which, we can inspect
    whether the estimation results coincide with the channel configurations.
    5. The angle scopes for plotting are [0,180] for zenith and 0,360] for azimuth, so the mirror radiation pattern would show in case of ULA and UPA configuration. The plotting granularity is 1
    degree.
    6. Configure the channel model accordingly if the number of streams are changed.
    7. If Digital Beamforming is applied, set TxAntennaArrayMask = eye(Nt) and RxAntennaArrayMask = eye(Nr),  but please keep parameters TxAntennaArrayMask in RF_Tx_WB and RxAntennaArrayMask in RF_Rx_WB as ones(Nt,Ntrf) and ones(Nr,Nrrf) respectively, since these two subnets are common for Preamble 1 part, Preamble 2 part and Data part. The real TxAntennaArrayMask and RxAntennaArrayMask can be set to other modules and it will work accordingly.
    8. If multi-path channel is introduced, the parameter TMax should be set longer than the multi-path delay to get a correct channel estimation.
    9. Usually, antenna engineers output antenna element radiation pattern file with the maximum power pointing to zenith, which conflicts with the antenna array placement in Y-Z plane, so please change DowntileAngle of each antenna element to -90 and remain BearingAngle and SlantAngle unchanged.
    10. SubtractionDuetoCH = 0.306dB (16Tx4Rx) and SubtractionDuetoCH = 0.345dB (64Tx16Rx, 64Tx8Rx) need subtracted from the signal's simulation SNR due to the power boost introduced by 3D channel model. Please note that the value is only available in current configuration and it should be adjusted according to the channel configuration (including parameter "Seed" and the number of antennas).
    11. Parameter SNR in "Interpolation Setting category" in RxAlgorithm tab of module FelxOFDM_Receiver_RF should equal to the simulation SNR.
  • Notes about 32-bit/64-bit SystemVue and Reasonable Configurations
    1. Memory allocation will probably fail when channel dimension larger than 16-by-16 is configured in 32-bit SystemVue environment. Therefore, 64-bit SystemVue is suggested with respect to this workspace.
    2. If more antenna elements number is needed, please increase the number of RF chains accordingly to avoid endless simulation. Based on the design, Preamble2 will transmit (Nt/Ntrf)*(Nr/Nrrf) OFDM-type training symbols. Upon current number of RF chains (Ntrf=Nrrf=1), Preamble2 will transmit Nt*Nr OFDM-type training symbols. To be specific, if 64Tx64Rx, 128Tx64Rx and 256Tx64Rx means Preamble2 contains 4096, 8192 and 16384 OFDM-type symbols, respectively, which will be heavily time-consuming configurations and they are not reasonable configurations in reality as well.

      With default, the dataset does not exist in this workspace due to its huge size. To get the results, please run the simulation.

Workspace.Name: Beamforming_WideBand_Source
Workspace.Description:
Wideband OFDM Beamforming Measurement

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This example provides the measurement for beamforming transmission with wideband OFDM system.

Supported features:

·         Support flexible beamforming structure, including full digital beamforming, hybrid beamforming and full RF/analog beamforming.

·         Support OFDM MIMO transmission

·         Support RF impairments

·         Support Taylor window for RF beamforming

·         Support antenna coupling

·         Support CCDF and spectrum measurement

·         Support transmitter dynamic 3D beam plotting for combined signal and each RF channel

·         Support customer beam pattern import with EMpro and HFSS formats

·         Support EVM measurement and constellation output

 

The parameters to configure the simulation are located in Equation Tab of Design1 with the following categories.

·         System configuration: set key parameters for the whole system, including central frequency, sample rate, power and RF chains. Also users can set desired beam direction for each RF chains.

·         Antenna array configuration: define antenna array structure and the mapping from RF chains to antennas.

·         Impairment analysis: set the impairments in antenna array, RF power amplifiers.

·         OFDM source configuration: configure OFDM MIMO source

It is suggested to change parameters in System configuration, Antenna array configuration and Impairment analysis per system configuration, and leave the parameter in OFDM source configuration unchanged for OFDM MIMO source if there is no need to change OFDM signals.

 Notes:

1.       For antenna array, ULA (uniform linear array) and UPA (uniform planar array) arrays are supported. And the antenna array is expected to be placed on Y-Z plane which means the number of antennas in x-axis (NumOfAntx) should be equal to 1.

2.       For antenna pattern predefined for three sector antenna when AntennaPatternType = Three Sector Antenna for Y-Z URA, the generated antenna pattern towards x-axis which is consistent with the assumption of antenna array in Y-Z plane.

3.   As a result, to have custom antenna pattern work properly, it is expected that custom 3D antenna beam pattern towards x-axis when AntennaPatternType = Pattern File.

4.     For EVM measurement, the default receiver beamforming is optimal as the recevier beams (defined by RxTheta and RxPhi in Equations Tab) are exactly pointed to transmit beam directions. Users can change thest two values if reveiver beamforming is not ideal.

 With default, the dataset does not exist in this workspace due to its huge size. To get the results, please run the simulation.

Workspace.Name: MIMO_SM_STC_BER
Workspace.Description:
MIMO_SM_STC_BER

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This example workspace demonstrates uncoded BER performance for basic MIMO and STC transmitter and receiver under Rayleigh Fading Channel.

 

For MIMO SM (Spatial Multiplexing) mode, multiple symbol streams are transmitted over antennas. In the receiver side, the MIMO decoder model is to recover the symbols with different decoder methods. In general, the ML method has the best performance, and non-linear SIC (Successive Interference Cancellation) with ZF and MMSE has the suboptimal performance. At last the traditional linear method with ZF and MMSE has worst performance.

In this workspace, simulation results for SM 2x2 QPSK system with different methods have been provided.

 

For TD (Transmit Diversity) mode, the same symbol is transmitted on all antennas, so the symbol rate is not increased compared to SISO case. In this release, NumTx only supports 2 and 4, and the precoding matrix defined in 6.3.4.3 of 36.211 for LTE is used in this example for both NumTx=2 and NumTx=4.

 

To run the simulation, please follow the instructions below.

1.       Define MIMO antennal configurations. Set the NumTx and NumRx parameters. For SM mode, NumRx should be equal to or greater than NumRx. For TD, mode, currently NumTx just supports 2 and 4, and NumRx could be any value.

2.       Set the transmission mode, from TD or SM.

3.       Set the modulation type for the symbols. The types supported is the same as the types defined in the Mapper model.

4.       For SM mode, select the decoder method, and SNR value which is required by some methods, such as Linear MMSE and SIC MMSE.

5.       Set the number of symbols (samples) for the simulation.

6.       All of above are set in the Parameter tab of the MIMO_STC_SM_Fading design. At last, set the SNR sweep points.

 

In the meanwhile, the SISO_AWGN_Fading design is provided for SISO uncoded BER performance under Rayleigh Fading Channel and AWGN Channel as a comparison.

Workspace.Name: MU-MIMO_Capacity
Workspace.Description:
MU-MIMO_Capacity

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This example workspace demonstrates multi-user MIMO (MU-MIMO) capacity results with semi-orthogonal user scheduling and power allocation.

 

Compared to single-user MIMO (SU-MIMO), MU-MIMO schemes can have two direct gains in multiple access capacity due to multi-user multiplexing schemes.

1.       Spatial multiplexing gain. The gain is achieved by taking advantage of spatial separation between users.

2.       Multiuser diversity gain with a large number of users K.

 

With a large number of users K at BS, this enables BS to choose a user group with good spatial separations  which achieve better spatial multiplexing gain, and also BS can choose users with better channel conditions to transmit which increases SNR  as multiuser diversity gain (roughly logK times higher).

 

In this example, the semi-orthogonal user selection algorithm follows the paper “On the optimality of multiantenna broadcast scheduling using zero-forcing beamforming” as in IEEE Jour. Select. Areas in Comm., vol. 24, no. 3, pp. 528–541, March 2006.

Three steps are needed in this simulation:

1.       Generate channel transfer matrix for each user

2.       In UserScheduler model, analyses the channel matrix of each user, find the users with semi-orthogonal user selection algorithm, and then get the power allocated to each user with waterfilling algorithm and precoding matrix.

3.       Calculate sum-rate capacity with all active users.

 

From this simulation, we can see multiuser diversity gain along with K. In this release, NumRx only supports 1.

Workspace.Name: 5G_F-OFDM_BER
Workspace.Description:
F-OFDM Transmission and BER Measurement

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This example workspace demonstrates F-OFDM(Filtered OFDM) concept with  transmitters and receivers.

 

In F-OFDM scheme, different Users in OFDM structure are transmitted on different frequency subbands with different subcarrier intervals(ie, different sample rate).  So users are no longer orthogonal. 

 

In this example, 2 F-OFDM users are multiplexed in Frequency domain. Each of them has different subcarrier spacing, and has the same final sample rate.  F-OFDM user 1 is demodulated by its receiver, and user 2 is assumed as interference.

 

In the parameter tab of Design1, some parameters are important:

  1. BaseSampleRate:  sample rate for F-OFDM user1
  2. StartLocationSubband: F-OFDM user1. It is the start location of subbands

In graph Spectrum, you can find that 2 users are separated in frequency. In graph Constellation, you can see the constellation of user1 after the receiver.

 

Note1: The synchronization algorithm is not available in FOFDM receiver. Hence a parameter ReceiverDelay is used to specify actual samples delayed in the received signal (which should be in range [0, one FOFDM symbol]. The length of one FOFDM symbol is (1+CP)*NumSubcarriers*2^OversampleOption.

Note2: When two UEs are combined, it is assurmed final sample rate of each UE is the same.

Note3: With the default setting, the uncoded BER result is shown as well as theoretical QPSK result. The performance degradation is due to impairment introduced by the interference signal, filter and FOFDM baseband receiver.

Note4: SampleStar in BER model is related to the parameter 'NumSymsChannelEst' in F_OFDM_Receiver.

Note 5: The values of pilots are set by function 'randn', which may cause different value at the output of models. But it would have litter effect on the BER measurement.

 

 

Things to Try

1. Try different filter length and filter bandwidth and verify the spectrum, especially out-of-band radiation. Check the out-of-band spectrum with different filter lengths and OFDM, FBMC and F-OFDM.

2. You can experiment with other modulation methods. The reference in the workspace is QPSK. And addition 16QAM and 64 QAM testing is expected to compare the performance with ideal cases. Also try different filter length to compare the results.

3. For F-OFDM, it has less sensitive to timing/frequency misalignments in different UEs (subbands). Try to see the performance compared to OFDM and UF-OFDM.

4. Also another key feature for F-OFDM is that each UE (subband) may have different subcarriers to make using the same ‘BaseSampleRate’ as intermediate frequency compared to UF-OFDM. Verify the whole transceiver with different subcarrier allocation.

Workspace.Name: 5G_FBMC_BER
Workspace.Description:
FBMC BER Measurement

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This example workspace demonstrates BER vs SNR measurements and spectrum performance for a FBMC system in AWGN (Additive White Gaussian Noise) channel and fading channel. Performance of FBMC system is compared with that of ideal synchronizated and ideal channel estimation OFDM system. Two implementations are given for FBMC system. The number of FFT points is extended to implement the filter bank and PPN_FFT is also provided to reduce computational complexity. OQAM is adopted in the FBMC syetem. The frame of FBMC is composed of preamble symbols and data symbols. Preamble is consist of two superimposed ZC (Zadoff-Chu) sequence. Time & Frequency synchronization, channel estimation and equalization is done in the receiver.

 

Simulation Instruction

  1. Set the 'NumSubcarriers' parameter  to define the number of  total subcarriers.
  2. The 'ActiveSubcAlloc' parameter defined the allocation of active subcarriers. This parameter is a array and the fisrt row of the array is the beginning allocation of active subcarriers and the second row is the end allocation of active subcarriers. The range of the array is from -NumSubc/2 to NumSubc/2-1. According to "ActiveSubcAlloc",  the 'NumActiveSubc' parameter acting as active subcarriers number is given in the equations.
  3. The 'FilterOverlapFactor' parameter is the overlapping factor of prototye filter used in FBMC system and three options of 'FilterOverlapFactor' is provided in the example with corresponding frequency coefficients in frequency domain defined as parament 'FilterCoef'. Parament 'FilterCoef' is defined as a column vector and the elements in odd row are negative and  the elements in even row are positive. ‘FilterOverlapFactor’ can be set to 2, 3 and 4. Correspondingly the parameter ‘FilterCoef’ should be changed to [1,-sqrt(2)/2], [1,-0.911438,0.411438] and [1,-0.971960,sqrt(2)/2,-0.235147].
  4. The 'NumPreambleSyms' and 'NumDataSyms' define the number of preamble symbols and data symbols in one frame.
  5. In order to see attenuation of the spectrum, the 'OversampleRatio' parameter is used to define oversample ratio.
  6. The 'FilterBankStructure' is used to choose the implementation of FBMC. Extended IFFT and PPN_IFFT is provided.
  7. Pilots is also offered. The 'PilotsEnable' is defined to use pilot or not. If pilot is uesd, the 'PilotIndex' parameter defined the subcarriers that allocated to pilot and the 'PilotSequence' is the value of pilot. The number of 'PilotIndex' should be equal to the number of data in 'PilotSquence.'
  8. Ideal synchronized FBMC system also can be gotten by set the parameter 'IdealSync' of  FBMC_Receiver to be 'YES', 'PhaseTrackingEnable' to be 'NO', 'Tmax' should be set to '1/SampleRate' and 'Fmax' should be set to '0'. And ideal synchronization infromation such as fractional frequency offset, integral frequency offset and frame timing should be set in the parameter of FBMC_Receiver in this case. To considering the influence of cycle prefix(CP), the performance figure should be rewritten by Eb/N0. 
  9. Parameter ‘Tmax’ and ‘Fmax’ are used for channel estimation. Parameter ‘Tmax’ defines the maximum delay of multipath. If ‘Tmax’ is much bigger than the maximum delay, much noise would be introduced. Therefore, in AWGN channel there is no multipath, ‘Tmax’ should be set not much bigger than ‘1/BaseSampleRate’ to get better channel estimation performance. In fading channel, the value of ‘Tmax’ should be depends on the maximum delay. It is the same case for ‘Fmax’.
  10. Parameter 'PreambleEnable' is provided in FBMC_Source to generate FBMC signal with/without preamble. Make sure 'PreambleEnable' is set to 'YES' when FBMC_Receiver is used.

Workspace.Name: 5G_FBMC_ConnectedSolution
Workspace.Description:
FBMC Connected Solution

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This example workspace demonstrates the connected solution for a FBMC system with/without LDPC coding in AWGN (Additive White Gaussian Noise) channel. LTE system is also provided for compare. Two implementations are given for FBMC system. The FBMC and LTE signal are generated by source and sent to signal generator. Spectrum could be seen by VSA. And the FBMC signal gotten through instrument is demodulated by FBMC_Receiver. Constellation of the FBMC signal is given too.

The number of FFT points is extended to implement the filter bank and PPN_FFT is also provided to reduce computational complexity. OQAM is adopted in the FBMC system. The frame of FBMC is composed of preamble symbols and data symbols. Preamble is consisted of two superimposed ZC (Zadoff-Chu) sequence. Time & Frequency synchronization, channel estimation and equalization is done in the receiver.

LDPC encoding and decoding are the same as those in WLAN 11ac library. The code rate can only be selected from 4 options: 1/2, 2/3, 3/4,5/6. The coded length is selected from 3 options: 1944, 1296, 648. A soft demapper is provided for LDPC decoding. It only supports QPSK, 16QAM and 64QAM now.

 

Simulation Instruction

  1. Set the 'NumSubcarriers' parameter  to define the number of  total subcarriers.
  2. The 'ActiveSubcAlloc' parameter defined the allocation of active subcarriers. This parameter is a row and the odd element of the row are the beginning allocation of active subcarriers and the even elements of the row are the end allocation of active subcarriers. The range of the array is from -NumSubc/2 to NumSubc/2-1. According to "ActiveSubcAlloc",  the 'NumActiveSubc' parameter acting as active subcarriers number is given in the equations.
  3. The 'FilterOverlapFactor' parameter is the overlapping factor of prototye filter used in FBMC system and three options of 'FilterOverlapFactor' is provided in the example with corresponding frequency coefficients in frequency domain defined as parament 'FilterCoef'. Parament 'FilterCoef' is defined as a column vector and the elements in odd row are negative and  the elements in even row are positive.‘FilterOverlapFactor’ can be set to 2, 3 and 4. Correspondingly the parameter ‘FilterCoef’ should be changed to [1,-sqrt(2)/2], [1,-0.911438,0.411438] and [1,-0.971960,sqrt(2)/2,-0.235147].
  4. The 'NumPreambleSyms' and 'NumDataSyms' define the number of preamble symbols and data symbols in one frame.
  5. In order to see attenuation of the spectrum, the 'OversampleRatio' parameter is used to define oversample ratio.
  6. The 'FilterBankStructure' is used to choose the implementation of FBMC. Extended IFFT and PPN_IFFT is provided.
  7. Pilots is also offered. The 'PilotsEnable' is defined to use pilot or not. If pilot is uesd, the 'PilotIndex' parameter defined the subcarriers that allocated to pilot and the 'PilotSequence' is the value of pilot. The number of 'PilotIndex' should be equal to the number of data in 'PilotSquence.'

  8. When the parameter 'IdealSync' of FBMC_Receiver to be 'YES',  synchronization informationshould be set by parameter 'FractionalFreq', 'IntegralFreq' and 'FrameTiming'. And parameter of workspace 'PhaseTracking' is set to 'NO' in this figure.

  9. Parameter ‘Tmax’ and ‘Fmax’ are used for channel estimation. Parameter ‘Tmax’ defines the maximum delay of multipath. If ‘Tmax’ is much bigger than the maximum delay, much noise would be introduced. Therefore, in AWGN channel there is no multipath, ‘Tmax’ should be set not much bigger than ‘1/BaseSampleRate’ to get better channel estimation performance. In fading channel, the value of ‘Tmax’ should be depends on the maximum delay. It is the same case for ‘Fmax’.

  10. Parameter 'PreambleEnable' is provided in FBMC_Source to generate FBMC signal with/without preamble. Make sure 'PreambleEnable' is set to 'YES' when FBMC_Receiver is used.

Workspace.Name: 5G_FBMC_LDPC_BER
Workspace.Description:
FBMC LDPC BER Measurement

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This example workspace demonstrates Coded and Uncoded BER vs SNR measurements  for a FBMC system with LDPC encoding in AWGN (Additive White Gaussian Noise) channel and fading channel. 

 

Two implementations are given for FBMC system. The number of FFT points is extended to implement the filter bank and PPN_FFT is also provided to reduce computational complexity. OQAM is adopted in the FBMC syetem. The frame of FBMC is composed of preamble symbols and data symbols. Preamble is consist of two superimposed ZC (Zadoff-Chu) sequence. Time & Frequency synchronization, channel estimation and equalization is done in the receiver.

 

LDPC encoding and decoding are the same as those in WLAN 11ac library. The code rate can only be selected from 4 options: 1/2, 2/3 ,3/4,5/6. The coded length are  selected from 3 options: 1944,1296,648.

 

An soft demapper is provided for LDPC decoding. It only support QPSK, 16QAM and 64QAM now.

 

 

Simulation Instruction

  1. Set the 'NumSubcarriers' parameter  to define the number of  total subcarriers.
  2. The 'ActiveSubcAlloc' parameter defined the allocation of active subcarriers. This parameter is a array and the fisrt row of the array is the beginning allocation of active subcarriers and the second row is the end allocation of active subcarriers. The range of the array is from -NumSubc/2 to NumSubc/2-1. According to "ActiveSubcAlloc",  the 'NumActiveSubc' parameter acting as active subcarriers number is given in the equations.
  3. The 'FilterOverlapFactor' parameter is the overlapping factor of prototye filter used in FBMC system and three options of 'FilterOverlapFactor' is provided in the example with corresponding frequency coefficients in frequency domain defined as parament 'FilterCoef'. Parament 'FilterCoef' is defined as a column vector and the elements in odd row are negative and  the elements in even row are positive.‘FilterOverlapFactor’ can be set to 2, 3 and 4. Correspondingly the parameter ‘FilterCoef’ should be changed to [1,-sqrt(2)/2], [1,-0.911438,0.411438] and [1,-0.971960,sqrt(2)/2,-0.235147].
  4. The 'NumPreambleSyms' and 'NumDataSyms' define the number of preamble symbols and data symbols in one frame.
  5. In order to see attenuation of the spectrum, the 'OversampleRatio' parameter is used to define oversample ratio.
  6. The 'FilterBankStructure' is used to choose the implementation of FBMC. Extended IFFT and PPN_IFFT is provided.
  7. Pilots is also offered. The 'PilotsEnable' is defined to use pilot or not. If pilot is uesd, the 'PilotIndex' parameter defined the subcarriers that allocated to pilot and the 'PilotSequence' is the value of pilot. The number of 'PilotIndex' should be equal to the number of data in 'PilotSquence.'

  8. The figure of coded and uncoded BER vs SNR is based on ideal synchronization FBMC system by setting the parameter 'IdealSync' of FBMC_Receiver to be 'YES' and synchronization information could be set by parameter 'FractionalFreq', 'IntegralFreq' and 'FrameTiming'. And parameter of workspace 'PhaseTracking' is set to 'NO' in this figure.

  9. Parameter ‘Tmax’ and ‘Fmax’ are used for channel estimation. Parameter ‘Tmax’ defines the maximum delay of multipath. If ‘Tmax’ is much bigger than the maximum delay, much noise would be introduced. Therefore, in AWGN channel there is no multipath, ‘Tmax’ should be set not much bigger than ‘1/BaseSampleRate’ to get better channel estimation performance. In fading channel, the value of ‘Tmax’ should be depends on the maximum delay. It is the same case for ‘Fmax’.

  10. Parameter 'PreambleEnable' is provided in FBMC_Source to generate FBMC signal with/without preamble. Make sure 'PreambleEnable' is set to 'YES' when FBMC_Receiver is used.

Workspace.Name: 5G_FBMC_Source
Workspace.Description:
FBMC_Source  Measurement

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This example workspace demonstrates spectrum performance for a FBMC system in AWGN (Additive White Gaussian Noise) channel. Performance of FBMC system is compared with that of OFDM system. Two implementations are given for FBMC system. The number of FFT points is extended to implement the filter bank and PPN_FFT is also provided to reduce computational complexity. OQAM is adopted in the FBMC syetem. The frame of FBMC is composed of preamble symbols and data symbols. Preamble is consist of two superimposed ZC (Zadoff-Chu) sequence.

Narrow band FBMC source and wideband FBMC source are provided in this example. A simple EVM model is provided to measure the EVM. SNR could be set in the Equations. A amplifier  is added to wideband FBMC source to simulate the performance result from wideband transmission system in mmwave. This amplifier could also be repalced with other RF transmit model designed by user.

Simulation Instruction

  1. Set the 'NumSubcarriers' parameter  to define the number of  total subcarriers.
  2. The 'ActiveSubcAlloc' parameter defined the allocation of active subcarriers. This parameter is a array and the fisrt row of the array is the beginning allocation of active subcarriers and the second row is the end allocation of active subcarriers.The range of the array is from -NumSubc/2 to NumSubc/2-1. According to "ActiveSubcAlloc",  the 'NumActiveSubc' parameter acting as active subcarriers number is given in the equations.
  3. The 'FilterOverlapFactor' parameter is the overlapping factor of prototye filter used in FBMC system and three options of 'FilterOverlapFactor' is provided in the example with corresponding frequency coefficients in frequency domain defined as parament 'FilterCoef'. Parament 'FilterCoef' is defined as a column vector and the elements in odd row are negative and  the elements in even row are positive. The three cases of 'FilterOverlapFactor' in 5G_FBMC_Source is 2,3 and 4. Correspondingly the parameter ‘FilterCoef’ should be changed to [1,-sqrt(2)/2],[1,-0.911438,0.411438] and [1,-0.971960,sqrt(2)/2,-0.235147].
  4. The 'NumPreambleSyms' and 'NumDataSyms' define the number of preamble symbols and data symbols in one frame. In order to make repeat structure in preamble, 'NumPreambleSyms' should be no less than 'FilterOverlapFactor'+2.
  5. In order to see attenuation of the spectrum, the 'OversampleRatio' parameter is used to define oversample ratio.
  6. The 'FilterBankStructure' is used to choose the implementation of FBMC. Extended IFFT and PPN_IFFT is provided.
  7. Pilots is also offered. The 'PilotsEnable' is defined to use pilot or not. If pilot is uesd, the 'PilotIndex' parameter defined the subcarriers that allocated to pilot and the 'PilotSequence' is the value of pilot. The number of 'PilotIndex' should be equal to the number of data in 'PilotSquence.'
  8. Parameter 'PreambleEnable' is provided in FBMC_Source to generate FBMC signal with/without preamble. Make sure 'PreambleEnable' is set to 'YES' when FBMC_Receiver is used. FBMC_Receiver is used in FBMC_EVM too.

Workspace.Name: 5G_FlexOFDM_MIMO_BER
Workspace.Description:
Flexible OFDM Measurement

Keysight Technologies SystemVue

 

This example workspace demonstrates swept BER vs SNR measurement for flexible OFDM system. SISO flexOFDM and MIMO flexOFDM with/without LDPC coded are tested in AWGN (Additive White Gaussian Noise) channel and fading channel.

SystemVue FlexOFDM Application can generate various OFDM waveforms. One Flexible OFDM frame consists of idle, preamble (Preamble 1 and Preamble 2) and payload data (Data 1 and Data 2) including pilots. Customers can configure their own OFDM frame according to their requirement. In receiver Preamble1 is used for synchronization and the default data of Preamble1 are the same in different antennas. If the data of Preamble1 are not the same in different antennas, performance degradation would appear. Preamle2 or Pilots could be chosen to do channel estimation. Preamble 2 can be switched ON or OFF. Data 2 (Payload 2) also can be turn ON or OFF. There are only the Data 1 (Payload 1) and the Preamble1 which should be always presence for receiver.

In MIMO mode of FlexOFDM, only 1x1, 2x2, 4x4, 8x8 are supported in this example. In fading channel, 1x2, 2x2, 2x4, 4x4, 2x8, 4x8, 8x8 are supported. 

 

Simulation Instruction

 

To get the simulation run, the following parameters should be set properly.

1.       In MIMO page of UI on FlexOFDM_MIMO_Source_RF, ‘NumOfSubcarriersPerBlock’ should be set as the divisor of ‘NumUsefulSubcarriers’. ‘NumOfSymbolsPerBlock’ should be set as the divisor of ‘NumOfSym’.

2.       In Preamble page of UI on FlexOFDM_MIMO_Source_RF, the length of ‘Preamble_CarrierIndex’ should be consistent with the value in ‘Preamble_NumOfCarriers’. The parameter ‘Preamble1_Seq’ and ‘Preamble2_Seq’ are the value of Preamble in all antennas, and the data are mapping to the location in the sequence of antenna 1, antenna 2 and so on.

3.       In Data page on FlexOFDM_MIMO_Source_RF, ‘Data_NumOfCarriers’ could be an array, the element of the array is the number of data carriers per symbol. The length of ‘Data_NumOfCarriers’ should be set as the divisor of ‘NumOfSym’. ‘Data_CarrierIndex’ should be consistent with the value in ‘Data_NumOfCarriers’. 

4.       In Pilot page on FlexOFDM_MIMO_Source_RF, the value of parameter ‘Pilot1_Seq’ are the value of pilots in all antennas, and the value are mapping to the location in the sequence of antenna 1, antenna 2 and so on.

5.       In MIMO page of UI on FlexOFDM_MIMO_Receiver_RF, two kinds of the structure on Preamble2 and pilots are provided according to LTE system (Non-Overlapping) and WLAN system (Overlapping). If Preamble2 is chosen to estimate the channel, only Overlapping type is available.

6.       In RxAlgorithm page of UI on FlexOFDM_MIMO_Receiver_RF, Preamble2 or pilots is chosen to do channel estimation by parameter ‘PilotsBasedChannelEst’. ‘PhaseTrackingEnable’ is available when channel estimation is based on Preamble2.

7.    The values of pilots and preamble are set by function 'randn', which may cause different value at the output of models. But it would have litter effect on the BER measurement.

8.    Most of the parameters are set in Equation considering the relationship between parameters and the consistence of source and receiver. If parameter is changed in GUI, please change the value of the certain variable in the Equation.

 

In Equations, common setting is given at the top. Then three kinds of setting are proposed according to the different setting on 'PilotsBasedChannelEst' and 'MIMOType'.And the performance of these two examples in AWGN channel and fading channel are given in the figure. In order to get better channel estimation performance, please change the setting of 'FrequencyInterval' and 'TimeInterval' for interpolation in channel estimation according to the pilots pattern. Also, setting proper 'Tmax' and 'Fmax' for different channel. 'Tmax' is set to 0.01us in AWGN channel and set to 1.1 us in EVA fading channel. And the DataAdjust is set to 0 in AWGN and  13 in fading channel in this example. The setting of AWGN and fading channel in the example is shown below.

Things to Try

     1.       Try different frame structure, modulation and pilots pattern and different receiver algorithm to see the influence on the BER curve in AWGN channel.

      2.       Try different fading scenarios with different receiver parameter such as ‘Tmax’, ‘Fmax’ and ‘DataAdjust’ to see the BLER performance in each channel.

      3.       Try to using preamble or pilots to do channel estimation in slow channel and fast channel to see the different range of application.

      4.       Compare the performance with LDPC coding or not.

      5.       Compare the performance with interleaving or not and try different parameter on interleaving.

      6.       Try different number of transmitter antennas and receiver antennas.

Workspace.Name: 5G_FlexOFDM_MIMO_ConnectedSolution
Workspace.Description:
Flexible OFDM MIMO Connected Solution

Keysight Technologies SystemVue

This example workspace demontrates the connected solution with flexible OFDM MIMO 2x2 system and MIMO 2x8 system.

For OFDM MIMO 2x2 system

·         In transmitter side, three different signal generators are supported.

·         ESG/MXG

·         M9381A

·         M8190A

Note for ESG/MXG, users need to run MXG_MIMO_Download equation to turn on the signals.

·         In receiver side, a VSA 89600B source model is used to capture multi-channel signals from the hardware.

·         Also a reference design FlexOFDM_MIMO_2x2_BER is provided for pure software BER simulation.

For OFDM MIMO 2x8 system

·         In transmitter side, one signal generator is supported for high bandwidth signal.

·         M8190A

·         In receiver side, a VSA 89600B source model is used to capture multi-channel signals from the hardware, e.g. M9703A.

·         Also a reference design FlexOFDM_MIMO_2x2_BER is provided for pure software BER simulation. In the receiver, a hybrid receiver beamforming structure is employed with 8 receiver antennas and 2 RF chains. The HBF_Controller_WB model will calculate the receiver beamforming weights based on received preamble signals to adjust receiver beamforming beams.

 

Instruction:

  • Update FlexOFDM parameters in Equations Tab of the designs, and get reasonable results in pure software software BER simulation in FlexOFDM_MIMO_2x2_BER or FlexOFDM_MIMO_2x8_BER.
  • Download signals to signal generators
    • Activate corresponding models for desired instruments, and deactivate the others.
    • Set instrument address in models. With the default settings, one frame data is downloaded. For instance, for ESG/MXG, we need to set ESG or MXG, and their IP address, and make sure the instruments are connected correctly as the instructions in the documentation of SignalDownloader_E4438C. Then we can run MXG_MIMO_Download equation to download the signals. Refer to the documentation of downloader models for detailed parameter settings.
  • Capture the signals from instruments via VSA 89600 software
    • Before invoking VSA 89600 software in SystemVue, open standalone VSA 89600 software to connect to multi-channel instruments (e.g. scope).
    • Run FlexOFDM_MIMO_2x2_Rx or FlexOFDM_MIMO_2x8_Rx design, where we can open VSA 89600 GUI to check the signals and set the configurations. Although OFDM MIMO receiver can demodulate the signals captured at any position of frame data, it is suggested that the signals are captured with a trigger from signal generators so that the signals are captured at the beginning of (or ahead of) frame data.
    • With the default setting, the receiver can demodulate one frame data as only one frame data are downloaded.
    • After the simulation, we can get BER and constellations from captured signals.

Workspace.Name: 5G_FlexOFDM_MIMO_Source
Workspace.Description:
Flexible OFDM Source Measurement

Keysight Technologies SystemVue

 

This example workspace demonstrates the generation of MIMO flexible OFDM signal.

Various OFDM waveforms can be generated by SystemVue FlexOFDM Application. One flexible OFDM frame consists of idle, preamble (Preamble 1 and Preamble 2) and payload data (Data 1 and Data 2) including pilots. By using different configuration, users can get different OFDM frames according to their requirement.  In FlexOFDM_EVM model, Preamble1 is used for synchronization and the default data of Preamble1 are the same in different antennas. If the data of Preamble1 are not the same in different antennas, synchronization performance degradation would appear (in FlexOFDM_MIMO_4x4 Type 0). Preamle2 or Pilots could be chosen to do channel estimation. Preamble 2 can be switched ON or OFF. Data 2 (Payload 2) also can be turn ON or OFF. There are only the Data 1 (Payload 1) and the Preamble1 which should be always presence for receiver.

The output of FlexOFDM_MIMO_Source is connected to VSA software from which we can see the spectrum and demodulation performance in VSA custom OFDM system. Parameter should be consistent with that in VSA. Please refer to the document in VSA for detail. Configuration files generated by FlexOFDM_MIMO_Source can make the connection with VSA much easier.

 

Simulation Instruction

 

To get the simulation run, the following parameters should be set properly.

1.       In MIMO page of UI on FlexOFDM_MIMO_Source_RF, ‘NumOfSubcarriersPerBlock’ should be set as the divisor of ‘NumUsefulSubcarriers’. ‘NumOfSymbolsPerBlock’ should be set as the divisor of ‘NumOfSym’.

2.       In Preamble page of UI on FlexOFDM_MIMO_Source_RF, the length of ‘Preamble_CarrierIndex’ should be consistent with the value in ‘Preamble_NumOfCarriers’. The parameter ‘Preamble1_Seq’ and ‘Preamble2_Seq’ are the value of Preamble in all antennas, and the data are mapping to the location in the sequence of antenna 1, antenna 2 and so on.

3.       In Data page on FlexOFDM_MIMO_Source_RF, ‘Data_NumOfCarriers’ could be an array, the element of the array is the number of data carriers per symbol. The length of ‘Data_NumOfCarriers’ should be set as the divisor of ‘NumOfSym’. ‘Data_CarrierIndex’ should be consistent with the value in ‘Data_NumOfCarriers’. 

4.       In Pilot page on FlexOFDM_MIMO_Source_RF, the value of parameter ‘Pilot1_Seq’ are the value of pilots in all antennas, and the value are mapping to the location in the sequence of antenna 1, antenna 2 and so on.

5.       In MIMO page of UI on FlexOFDM_MIMO_Receiver_RF, two kinds of the structure on Preamble2 and pilots are provided according to LTE system (Non-Overlapping) and WLAN system (Overlapping). If Preamble2 is chosen to estimate the channel, only Overlapping type is available.

6.    In RxAlgorithm page of UI on FlexOFDM_MIMO_Receiver_RF, Preamble2 or pilots is chosen to do channel estimation by parameter ‘PilotsBasedChannelEst’. ‘PhaseTrackingEnable’ is available when channel estimation is based on Preamble2.

7.   When the synchronization performance degradated, smaller value of PeakThreshold in FlexOFDM_EVM model will make it easier to get the frame synchronization.

8.   Please change the parameters in the equation for the consistency of FlexOFDM_MIMO_Source and FlexOFDM_EVM. If parameters are changed by GUI, please change the parameters in FlexOFDM_MIMO_Source and FlexOFDM_EVM at the same time.

9.   Parameter 'PrecodingEnable' is not supported without the feedback of receiver. If 'PrecodingEnable' is set to 'Yes', please make sure the input port 'MIMOPrecoding' is connected.

10. The value of Parament 'Pilot1_Seq' of FlexOFDM_MIMO_4x4 is set by function 'randn', which makes the output of FlexOFDM_MIMO_Souce different in every simulation. Change to the values of pilots to constant may make the output of FlexOFDM_MIMO_Souce keep the same. 

 

There are two designs in this example. One is for MIMO 2x2 and the other is 4x4. The maximum anttena number in VAS is 4. In each Equation, two types of parameter setting are given.  One type is called non-overlapping in VSA which is MIMOType = 0 in FlexOFDM_EVM. The other is called Overlapping in VSA which is MIMOType = 1 in FlexOFDM_EVM. Please make sure the number of symbols is bigger than NumOfTx in Overlapping mode. Please make sure the 'QAM_Identifiers' and the 'QAM Levels' is consistent with that in VSA.

In FlexOFDM_MIMO_Source_RF GUI, when Generate Configuration File is enabled, the corresponding files for VSA demoudalation will be generated. In these two examples, after VSA 89600 software is invoked, users need to load these generated files in VSA Custom OFDM Demod UI for Pilot IQ , Preamble IQ, Resource Map and Resouce Modulation respectively.

Things to Try

1.       Try two different pilots pattern and using VSA to do demodulation. 1x1, 2x2 and 4x4 are supported in VSA. See the spectrum, demodulation constellation and EVM in VSA.

2.       Try different parameter such as modulation, pilots pattern, frame structure and demodulation methods and see the influence on EVM.

Workspace.Name: 5G_GFDM_Source
Workspace.Description:
GFDM Source Characteristics

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This example workspace demonstrates spectrum performance for a generalized frequency division multiplexing (GFDM) system. Performance of GFDM system is compared with that of OFDM system. The implementation is based on the FFT/IFFT algorithm with reasonable computational increase compared with traditional OFDM system. It provides the flexibility to choose a pulse shape by changing the filter that designed in the Equation of subnetwork GFDM_Source. Because GFDM is transmitted by block, not only the pulse shaping but also the transition between blocks is important for the spectrum. In order to achieve smooth transitions, a guard symbol (zero symbol) can be inserted into each block. As cyclic prefix (CP) would break the smooth transition, we can see the improvement introduced by guard symbol without CP.

 

 

Simulation Instruction

  1. The 'Fcarrier' is the Carrier Frequency.
  2. Set the 'NumTimeslots' parameter to define the number of time slots in a data block.
  3. Set the 'NumSubcarriers' parameter  to define the number of  subcarriers in each time slot.
  4. The 'NumActiveSubcarriers' parameter defined the number of active subcarriers in each time slot. 'NumActiveSubcarriers' should be less or equal to 'NumSubcarriers'. If 'NumActiveSubcarrier' is less than 'NumSubcarrier', the null subcarriers are inserted at the edge of the spectrum symmetrically.
  5. In order to see attenuation of the spectrum, the 'OversampleRatio' parameter is used to define oversample ratio.
  6. The 'RollOff' parameter is the roll off factor of the raised cosine (RC) filter which is the default filter used in the example.
  7. Choose 'AddGuardSymbol' to see the improvement on out of band radiation as a result of guard symbol. Make sure the zero symbol is at the beginning of the data block.

Workspace.Name: 5G_LDPC_BER
Workspace.Description:
LDPC_BER  Measurement

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This example workspace demonstrates BER vs Eb/N0 performance for Low Density Parity Check (LDPC) encoding and decoding in AWGN (Additive White Gaussian Noise) channel. To make generic LDPC models flexible in 5G library, the parity check matrix can be specified either from model parameter or from file. In this example, the parity check matrix of WLAN11ac and DVBS2 are adopted to show how to design LDPC encoding and decoding.

 

 

Simulation Instruction

  1. Set the 'CodeRate' parameter  to define the code rate of LDPC encoding and decoding. It can be selected from 4 options: 1/2, 2/3, 3/4 and 5/6.

  2. The 'CodeLength' parameter defined the code length of LDPC encoding and decoding. 1944, 1296 and 648 can be selected for WLAN11ac. 64800 and 16200 can be selected for DVBS2.

  3. A soft demapper is provided for LDPC decoding. It only supports QPSK, 16QAM and 64QAM which is defined by parameter 'ModType'.

Workspace.Name: 5G_UF-OFDM_BER_with_Interference
Workspace.Description:
UF-OFDM BER Measurement with Interference of Timing and Frequency Offset 

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This example workspace demonstrates uncoded BER vs SNR measurements for a universal-filtered Orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (UF-OFDM) system in AWGN (Additive White Gaussian Noise) channel when there is another UF-OFDM system treated as interference in the condition of timing and frequency offset. Performance of UF-OFDM system is compared with that of OFDM system. The OFDM system is provided by setting FilterLength and FilterCoef to be 1. In UF-OFDM system, active subcarriers are composed of some subbands which are consisted of pilots and data. Number of subcarriers in every subband is the same. The time domain signal of every subband passed through a filter and the transmitter signal is the superposition of that. It provides the flexibility to choose a pulse shape by changing the filter that is controlled by filter coefficient and filter length. In this example the filter coefficient in Equation is gotten by chebyshev window with length 16 and Fourier transform sidelobe magnitude 120 dB. The different location of every subband is implemented by multiplying the time domain data with certain frequency offset.The power of every subband is normalized. In receiver, pilots in every subband are used for channel estimation and one dimention interpolation is done for channel response of data.

In the figure of BER vs SNR, one guard means that one subcarriers is kept as guard between two subband. Interference is added by multiplied the signal of interference user with frequency offset.

 

Simulation Instruction

1.     The 'NumSubcarriers' is the total subcarriers and the DFT size.

2.     Set the 'NumSubbands' parameter to define the number of subbands in the total subcarriers and ‘NumSubcarriersPerSubband’ is the number of subcarriers in every subband.

3.     Set the 'StarLocationSubband' parameter to define the index of the first subcarrier in every subband and the size of this parameter should be equal to the number of subband. The element of this parameter should be in the range of [-NumSubcarriers/2, NumSubcarriers/2-1].

4.     The 'BaseFilterLength' parameter defined the length of filter without oversampling, and its new value FilterLength should be equal to the size of ‘FilterCoef’ which is given in the Equation.

5.     The parament 'PilotsLocation' is the relative location according to the index of first subcarrier in every subband. The range of it is in [0, NumSubcarriersPerSubband-1]. And ‘PilotsSeq’ is the sequence value of pilots. The size of ‘PilotsSeq’ could be bigger than the size of 'PilotsLocation' so that every UF-OFDM symbol can be allocated with different pilot values to avoid the spur in the specturm. Please set 'PilotsEnable' to 'YES' when UFMC_Receiver is used.

6.     Considering the unflatness of the filter in the subband, parameter ‘CompensateFilterResponse’ will multiply the data and pilots in subband with filter compensated coefficients.

7.   The normalized timing and frequency offset is set in Parameter Tab.

8.   The interference user can be turned on or off by the EnableInterferenceUser parameter. When off, the BER performance is pure UF-OFDM BER without any interference signal.

9.   In this example, the SweepSNR sweep is provided to simulate BER vs. SNR for target user with or without interference signal; The SweepTimingOffset sweep is provided to simulate MSE vs. Timing offset for target user with interference signal. The SweepFreqOffset sweep is provided to simulate MSE vs. Frequency offset for target user with interference signal. For both timing and frequency offset, we can see that UF-OFDM (with filter length 16) is more robust than OFDM-like (with filter length 1).

 

Things to Try

            1.       Try UF-OFDM AWGN performance with QPSK, 16QAM and 64 QAM. The reference in the workspace is QPSK.

      2.       Try different time offset and frequency offset of the interference user to confirm UF-OFDM can support relaxed synchronization requirement.

      3.       Try different filter and see the influence on the BER and MSE on frequency offset and time offset.

      4.       Try different pilot density to check the pilot effect on BER performance.

Notes: due to large data, the data of S1 (SpectrumAnalyzerEnv) are removed in the datasets in this example.

Workspace.Name: 5G_UF-OFDM_Source
Workspace.Description:
UF-OFDM Source Characteristics

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This example workspace demonstrates spectrum performance for a universal-filtered Orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (UF-OFDM) system. Active subcarriers are composed of some subbands which are consisted of pilots and data. Number of subcarriers in every subband is the same. The time domain signal of every subband passed through a filter and the transmitter signal is the superposition of that. It provides the flexibility to choose a pulse shape by changing the filter that is controlled by filter coefficient and filter length. In this example the filter coefficient in Equation is gotten by chebyshev window with length 16 and Fourier transform sidelobe magnitude 40 dB or 120 dB. The different location of every subband is implemented by multiplying the time domain data with certain frequency offset. When the FilterCoef and the FilterLength is set to 1, UF-OFDM system will turn to OFDM system. Please make sure the frequence filter coefficients on active subcarrier is not equal to zero, otherwise the result of UF-OFDM_EVM would be meaningless.

 

 

Simulation Instruction

1.     The 'NumSubcarriers' is the total subcarriers and the DFT size.

 

2.     Set the 'NumSubbands' parameter to define the number of subbands in the total subcarriers and ‘NumSubcarriersPerSubband’ is the number of subcarriers in every subband.

 

3.     Set the 'StarLocationSubband' parameter to define the index of the first subcarrier in every subband and the size of this parameter should be equal to the number of subband. The element of this parameter should be in the range of [-NumSubcarriers/2, NumSubcarriers/2-1].

 

4.     The 'BaseFilterLength' parameter defined the length of filter without ovsampling, and its new value FilterLength should be equal to the size of ‘FilterCoef’ which is given in the Equation.

 

5.     The parament 'PilotsLocation' is the relative location according to the index of first subcarrier in every subband. The range of it is in [0, NumSubcarriersPerSubband-1]. And ‘PilotsSeq’ is the sequence value of pilots. The size of ‘PilotsSeq’ could be bigger than the size of 'PilotsLocation' so that every UFMC symbol can be allocated with different pilot values to avoid the spur in the specturm. Those parameter could be disabled when parameter 'PilotsEnable' is set to NO.

 

6.     Considering the unflatness of the filter in the subband, parameter ‘CompensateFilterResponse’ will multiply the data and pilots in subband with filter compensated coefficients.

 

7.    If UF-OFDM_Receiver is used, please set PilotsEnable to 'YES'. In this example, if PilotsEnable is set to 'NO', UFMC_EVM model would be turned to disabled automatically.

 

8.   The parament 'NumSubcarriersPerSubband' should be a positive even integer (>=4).

 

9.   The values of pilots are set by function 'randn', which may cause different value at the output of models. But it would have litter effect on the BER measurement. PilotsSeq is the sequence of pilots which is defined in Equations.

 

 

 

Things to Try

1.       You can experiment with other modulation methods and verify the EVM and CCDF curves.

2.       You can try different types of filtering with different filter lengths and verify the spectrum, especially out-of-band radiation. Check the out-of-band spectrum and OFDM, FBMC and F-OFDM.

3.       Try two subbands and see the interference from the other one and decide the number of subcarriers used as guard. Filter may have important effect on it.

4.       Using fix PilotSeq or unfix PilotsSeq and see the influence on the spectrum.

Workspace.Name: NOMA_LTE_A_SISO_Throughput
Workspace.Description:
NOMA_LTE_A_SISO_Throughput

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This example workspace demonstrates NOMA (Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access) access link-level performance with 2 UEs for LTE-Advanced downlink SISO system in AWGN environment. In NOMA access scheme, different UES are transmitted on the same frequency with different power. In the receiver, for the UE with higher power, it just demodulate the signal regardless of the signal of lower power UE. For the UE with lower power, firstly it needs to demodulate the signal of higher power UE using SIC (successive interference cancellation) method, then demodulate its own signal.

 

In the design “NOMA_LTE_A_Design”, the input parameters includes

1.       Bandwidth: the bandwidth of LTE-A signal

2.       SINR0 and SINR0: the ratio of signal to interference and noise for UE0 and UE1. SINR0 should be larger than SINR1 in this simulation, and the difference should be larger enough in order to have SIC work properly.

3.       SINR_Table and MCS_Table: the mapping of SINR to MCS in order to select best MCS given current SINR. With the default values, the MCS selection is set with BLER=10%.

4.       NumFrames: define how many frames will be simulated.

 

In the design “NOMA_LTE_A_Design”, FTPA (Fractional Transmit Power Allocation) method is used to determine the power allocation among two users given the SINRs. And MCS for each UE is selected according to SINR and MCS table. With the default, all RB resources are allocated to these two UEs.

 

In the design "NOMA_LTE_A_Design", NOMA source and receiver are created based on LTE_A.

  1. Subnet "NOMA_LTE_A_DL_Src" shows the new NOMA source, a new UE is added with channel coding and constellation mapping, then the constellations of new UE and exised UE are superposed with different power.
  2. Subnet "NOMA_LTE_A_DL_Rrc" shows the new NOMA receiver,  a new SIC procedure is added after layer demapper and deprecoder. For the high power UE, the SIC is bypassed, for the low power UE, SIC can help remove the interference from high power UE.

As a comparison, a corresponding OFDMA access performance is shown in the design “OFDMA_LTE_A_Design”, where two UEs are assigned to different RB resources with half of total bandwidth respectively.

 

The equation “Compare Throughput” is used to compare throughput simulation results of NOMA and OFDMA.

Workspace.Name: 5GMIMOChannel
Workspace.Description:
5G MIMO Channel Model

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This example workspace demonstrates how to use the 5G MIMO channel model.

 

Simulation Instruction

  1. 3GPP channel model is implemented bsed on 3GPP TR 38.901 V14.0.0, the supported features are listed in the table below.

    Section of 3GPP TR 38.901 V14.0.0

    Support Status

    7.1 Coordinate system

    YES

    7.3 Antenna modelling

    YES

    7.4.1 Pathloss

    YES

    7.4.2 LOS probability

    YES

    7.4.3 O2I penetration loss

    YES

    7.5 Fast fading model

    YES

    7.6.1 Oxygen absorption

    YES, except for large channel bandwidth

    7.6.2 Large bandwidth and large antenna array

    NO

    7.6.3 Spatial consistency

    NO

    7.6.4.1 Blockage model A

    YES

    7.6.4.2 Blockage model B

    NO

    7.6.5 Correlation modelling for multi-frequency simulations

    NO

    7.6.6 Time-varying Doppler shift

    NO

    7.6.7 UT rotation

    YES, just static case

    7.6.8 Explicit ground reflection model

    NO

    7.7.1 Clustered Delay Line (CDL) models

    YES

    7.7.2 Tapped Delay Line (TDL) models

    Can be supported by CommsChannel model

    7.7.3 Scaling of delays

    YES

    7.7.5.1 CDL extension: Scaling of angles

    YES

    7.7.6 K-factor for LOS channel models

    YES

    8 Map-based hybrid channel model

    NO

  2. Example "CDL_A" is an 2x2 MIMO case and shows how to set the pre-defined CDL model. Channel impulse response and spectrum of each Tx and Rx antenna pair can be observed in dynamic graphs.
  3. Example "CDL_Custom" is an SISO case and shows how to set the custom CDL model. Normal and simplified models are compared and different channel impulse responses can be observed in both dynamic and static graphs.
  4. Example "Scenario_UMi" shows how to set the pre-defined scenario. Channel impulse response and spectrum can be observed in graphs.
  5. Example "TDL_A" shows how to implement the NLOS TDL model. TDL-A model is used in this case.
  6. Example "TDL_D" shows how to implement the LOS TDL model. TDL-D model is used in this case.
  7. Example "Doppler" shows how to verify the doppler spectrum and a single path channel is used for this case. The dataset is not stored in this workspace due to the large size of data. To observe the doppler spectrum in graph "Doppler_Power", analysis "Doppler_DF" should be rerun to get the data.
  8. Example "Doppler_TDL" shows how to verify the doppler spectrum for the TDL model. The U-shape spectrum can be observed in the graph.The dataset is not stored in this workspace due to the large size of data. To observe the doppler spectrum in graph "Doppler_TDL_Power", analysis "Doppler_TDL_DF" should be rerun to get the data.
  9. The channel mode is drop-based. For drop interval, during this time segment, all the large-scale parameters are constant. Usually, we run the in-drop simulation, so can set 'DropInterval' to a value greater than the simulation time.

Workspace.Name: V5G_DL_Throughput
Workspace.Description:
V5G Downlink Throughput

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Workspace

 

This workspace demonstrates complete link-level V5G (Verizon 5G) downlink shared channel transmission, which comprises of complete source, channel and receiver.

  • Supported Features:
            1. Complete xPDSCH physical layer simulation, including digital baseband source, digital baseband receiver, analog source, analog receiver and channel.
            2. Simplified channel model for beamforming evaluation, which is a revision of delay-scaled CDL model (please refer to TR38.900).
            2. BRS configurations "One Slot" and "One Subframe" are supported.
            3. PRACH configurations #0 and #1 ae supported.
  • Included Designs
                1. SISO: 1-layer transmission in complete V5G DL shared channel simulation with hybrid beamformin
            2. MIMO: 2-layer transmission, hybrid beamforming
            3. SISO Baseline: 1-layer transmission, no beamforming
            4. SIMO_RxDiversity: two branches are selected dynamically, hybrid beamforming
            5. SIMO_RxDiversityRxAntennaElementPattern: four RFICs are configured in RX side for diversity receiving.
            5. SISO_EMProRxBeamPattern; beam pattern files for RX side generated by EMPro are included in the simulation
            6. SISO_EMProTxRxBeamPattern: beam pattern files for both RX side and TX side generated by EMPro are included in the simulation
            7. SISO_DFRF: RF part design is included
            8. SISO_2UserTx_1UserRev: 2 users are configured in the source and one of them can be chosen to analyze the performance
           
  • Notes:
                1. UPA (Uniform Planer Array) is applied to TX side, so number of antennas in Y-axis and number of antennas in Z-axis should be specified in TX. In RX side, there are different antenna array configuration approaches. In designs without beam pattern importing, UPA is applied, but in others, RX antenna array topology is implicitly included in EMPro, HFSS and CST files.
            2. Regarding the simplified channel modeling, section 7.7.1 of 3GPP TR38.901 says "For modeling effect of beamforming in a simplified way, a brick-wall window can be applied to a delay-scaled CDL model. The power shall be normalized after applying the window.", but it does propose any approach to implement the simplified model. In our 3D channel model, there is a parameter named "UseOneRayPerCluster". If it's enabled, only one ray is modeled for each cluster. The approach has already been verified in our previous 5G library. Both MIMO design and SISO design enable "UseOneRayPerCluster" for beamforming evaluation.
            3. To get reasonable performance curve in simulation, TX/RX sweeping beams and channels' AoA/ZoA/AoD/ZoD need predefined carefully. For example, if AoA = [30], ZoA = [90], AoD = [315] and ZoD = [75] are the channel parameters, the channel directions would better be the member of corresponding TX and RX sweeping beams.
            4. Only one user is supported in RX side, while multiple users are supported to configure in source. SISO_2UserTx_1UserRev demoes the case, where multipler users can be configured in the source and user of interest can be specified in the receiver for receiving.
            5. xPDCCH is not included for demodulation, although "SearchSpaceIndex" as a xPDCCH-related parameter appears in the parameter page of the schematic and xPBCH, ePBCH and CSI-RS are also precluded currently.
            6. EVM, BER and Throughput/BLER can be analyzed.
            7. Beam pattern can be shown dynamically, while it will slow down the simulation speed heavily.
            8. The output buswidth of TX basedband source can be set to 1~16 upon the paramter NumTxPorts in V5G_DL_Src model. For data transmission, if there are multiple ports, the first port is mapped to the first line of the maximum 16-width bus, the second port is mapped to the second line of the 16-width bus, and so on. For example, given NumBRSPorts = 8 and AP_Layer_Config = 6, then the first 8 ports of the 16-width bus will be used to transmit BRS and the first and fifth ports of the 16-width bus will be used to transmit xPDSCH.
            9. MCS = 3 is configured in most of the reference designs, where the system will run in low SNR range in SISO case (around 1~1.5 dB). The performance curve for SISO is evaluated in terms of SNR subtracting beamforming gain named "BFGain_Expected" in the equation page of the schematic (in some design, BFGain_Expected may be splitted into TxBFGain_Expected and RxBFGain_Expected). For other MCS configurations, please refer to section 8.1.5.1 of V5G_213_v1.4. Briefly, QPSK is applied in MCS range [0, 5], 16QAM is applied in MCS range [6, 10] and 64QAM is applied in MCS range [11, 14].
            10. If too small SNR is set, the synchronization may fail in some cases.
            11. "Perf_MCS11" and "Perf_MCS3" are added to show performance comparison between baseline and system with BF under MCS=3, as well as between HARQ is on and off under MCS=3 and MCS=11. Obviously, when MCS=11, operating SNR is around 14dB. It shows HARQ-on outperforms HARQ-off in all SNR range under MCS=11, but story is different when MCS=3. The intersection in "Perf_MCS3" is caused by TX beam index report error. Since TX Beam Index is updated every 25 subframes, once there is a TX Beam Index report error, the following 25 subframes are definitely lost and what's more, the combination among the first failed transmission and following upto three transmission is useless for following decoding. It seems in a real system, BSI need filtered before use.
            12. SISO_DFRF design imports more realistic RF modeling into simulation, where impairments can be introduced easily.
            13. Co-sim of SystemVue and pattern files generated by EMPro, HFSS and CST is a hot topic. Hereby, multiple co-sim approaches are provided for reference.
                  All these kinds of simulation depend on pattern files and we take pattern files generated by EMPro as example.
                  Three designs are related to co-sim: SIMO_RxDiversityRxAntennaElementPattern, SISO_EMProRxBeamPattern and SISOProTxRxBeamPattern.
                  SIMO_RxDiversityRxAntennaElementPattern uses RFIC#1, RFIC#2, RFIC#3 and RFIC#4, each of which is consititued of two elements. The elements' pattern files of RFIC # are RFIC#_elements_001.uan and RFIC#_elements_002.uan. In the design the phase and topology informaion are included in the pattern files.
                  SISO_EMProRxBeamPattern and SISOProTxRxBeamPattern demo another more efficient and more realistic way to do simulation in Massive MIMO scenario. They import synthesized beam pattern files, but not antenna element files in simulation. There are seven beam pattern files for TX, namely TxArray001_001.uan ~ TxArray001_007.uan and four beam pattern files for RX, namely RxArray001_001.uan ~ RxArray001_004.uan. Please notice that beam pattern files are different from antenna element pattern files. Antenna element pattern files only characterrize the radiation of each element, rather, beam pattern files describe synthesized beam radiation with sharp beam in specific directions. 
                  SISO_EMProRxBeamPattern only applies beam pattern files in RX side, but SISOProTxRxBeamPattern applies beam pattern files in both TX and RX side.
                  By virtue of the introduction of beam pattern files in simulation, for a 1-layer transmission, channel model only needs to model a 1-by-1 channel regarding how many elements there are, which speed up Massive MIMO dramatically.
            14. AP_Layer_Config follows

  • Value

    Message

    0

Workspace.Name: V5G_DL_Tx
Workspace.Description:
V5G_DL_Tx

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This example workspace demonstrates spectrum and CCDF measurements for a V5G (Verizon 5G)downlink transmitter with different number of antennas. There are three folders in this workspace:

  • V5G DL Src Tx Measurements: provides spectrum, CCDF measurements and link to the Keysight 89600 VSA software (needs to be installed separately) for a 1 antenna system. To link to VSA software, users need to activate VSA_89600B_Sink model and need to have a Custom OFDM Demod license or a Pre-5G Demod license in VSA software based on which Demod is selected in VSA. In this example, two setup files for both Demod options are provided.
  • V5G DL Src 2Ant Tx Measurements: provides spectrum, CCDF measurementsfor a 2 antenna system.
  • V5G DL Src 8CC Tx Measurements: generate 8CC V5G single antenna downlink signal and mesurement in VSA software. It will be quite slow to do the measurement with VSA because of the high sample rate and huge numbers of input data for VSA.
  • V5G DL Src Tx Measurements with V5G DL Rcv: use V5G_DL_Rcv as receiver to measure EVM
  • The version of VSA should be 23.00 or later versions which can support V5G signal.
  • A VSA setup file can be gotten when SaveVSASetupFile is set to Yes in V5G_DL_Src. Only SISO setup file is supported. Please update the antenna port in the setup file to be consistent with the port that connected to the VSA model. Make sure BRS signal is transmitted in the port that is connected to VSA model because it is used for synchronization.
  • Follow the steps when using VSA setup file generated by V5G_DL_Src. First, disable VSA_89600B_Sink and run simulation. Then enable VSA_89600B_Sink and set the setup file generated by V5G_DL_Src. Then run simulation and get the result.
Notes:
  • The output buswidth of TX basedband source can be set to 1~16 upon the paramter NumTxPorts in V5G_DL_Src model. For data transmission, if there are multiple ports, the first port is mapped to the first line of the maximum 16-width bus, the second port is mapped to the second line of the 16-width bus, and so on. For example, given NumBRSPorts = 8 and AP_Layer_Config = 6, then the first 8 ports of the 16-width bus will be used to transmit BRS and the first and fifth ports of the 16-width bus will be used to transmit xPDSCH. Another example is if NumBRSPorts = 1 and AP_Layer_Config = 3, then the first port of the 16-width bus will be used to transmit BRS and the fourth port of the 16-width will be used to transmit data, upon which if you expect to view the data spectrum, the fourth port needs measured.

Workspace.Name: DigMod_LDPC_BER
Workspace.Description:
LDPC_BER  Measurement

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This example workspace demonstrates BER vs Eb/N0 performance for Low Density Parity Check (LDPC) encoding and decoding in AWGN (Additive White Gaussian Noise) channel. To make generic LDPC models flexible in DigMod library, the parity check matrix can be specified either from model parameter or from file. In this example, the parity check matrix of WLAN11ac and DVBS2 are adopted to show how to design LDPC encoding and decoding.

 

 

Simulation Instruction

  1. Set the 'CodeRate' parameter  to define the code rate of LDPC encoding and decoding. It can be selected from 4 options: 1/2, 2/3, 3/4 and 5/6.

  2. The 'CodeLength' parameter defined the code length of LDPC encoding and decoding. 1944, 1296 and 648 can be selected for WLAN11ac. 64800 and 16200 can be selected for DVBS2.

  3. A soft demapper is provided for LDPC decoding. It only supports QPSK, 16QAM and 64QAM which is defined by parameter 'ModType'.

Workspace.Name: DigMod_CDMA_RakeCombiner
Workspace.Description:
CDMA Tx and Rx using Rake Receiver

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This workspace is to demostrate DSSS source and rake receiver to simulate a two users CDMA system using SystemVue DigMod library.

 

There are two DSSS sources with different Walsh-Codes as spreading code and both sources has the same frame structure (PreambleLength and PayloadLength). The spreading factor is 64.

 

Forlder 1. CDMA_TxRx consists of schematic DigMod_CDMA_Rake_TxRx which shows the Rake receiver performance when both CDMA sources have same transmit power with 20dB Gaussian noise in a multipath enviorment. After running this schematic, we can see received constellation, estimated frequency offset, frequency tracking using PLL, Synchronization index and etc.

 

Forlder 2. CDMA_BER consists of schematic DigMod_CDMA_Rake_BER (almost same as DigMod_CDMA_Rake_TxRx) is to measure BER. After sweep EbN0 parameter, we can get BER vs Eb/N0 and EVM vs Eb/N0 in CDMA system.

 

Forlder 3. CDMA_Interference consists of schematic DigMod_CDMA_Rake_BER_Inter which the second CDMA's power can be swept. After sweep Inter_Power_dB parameter, we can get BER vs Interference Power in CDMA system.

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This workspace is to demostrate to measure BER using DigMod source and Rake receiver for DSSS with Keysight instruments (such as N5182B MXG and N9030A PXA)

 

DigMod_DSSS_Tx_MXG schematic is to download DigMod DSSS source with differential modulation into MXG. Its spreading code is 64 length Zadoff-Chu complex sequence. Pls go to schematic and set IP address in SignalDownloader_E4438C block.
