Workspace.Name: DigMod_DSSS_TxRx_EQ
Workspace.Description:
DSSS Tx and Rx with Equalizer

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This workspace is to demostrate DSSS source and receiver using DigMod_SourceL_RF and DigMod_ReceiverL_EQ_RF when a multipath channel. 

 

For DSSS system, equalizer (both LE and DFE) also can be used as receiver as well as Rake combiner in DSSS with short spreading factor. This example showes the performance of Decision Feedback Equalizer for both DSSS and w/o DSSS system. It consists of two examples. The channel impulse response in both examples as follows (sampling rate is 1/T).

                                                   1.   0.184 + j*0.132

                                                   2.  -0.346 + j*0.303

                                                   3.    0.620 - j*0.300

                                                   4.    0.360 - j*0.285

                                                   5.    0.145 + j*0.174

                   

Schematic DigMod_DFE_BER is a system without DSSS and uses  DFE as receiver and run it to get BER vs Eb/N0 to compare with the BER vs Eb/N0 from a DSSS system.

 

Schematic DigMod_DSSS_DFE_BER is a system with DSSS and uses  DFE as receiver and run it to get BER vs Eb/N0. In this example, the spreading code is 7 length barker code [ +1, +1, +1, -1, -1, +1, -1] and the spreading factor just 7.

 

According to BER_vs_EbN0, both BER vs Eb/N0 curves are almsot close for both DSSS and No DSSS systems after DFE. DSSS system can work at a lower SNR enviornment.

Workspace.Name: DigMod_RakeCombiner
Workspace.Description:
DSSS Tx and Rx using Rake Receiver

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This workspace is to demostrate DSSS source and rake receiver using SystemVue DigMod library.

 

The workspace consists of two schematics. The DigMod_DSSS_BER_TxRx schematic shows DSSS source with 127 length Gold sequence as spreading code and receiver including framing synchronization, carrier frequency synchronization, channel estimator, rake combiner and carrier frequency tracking using phase locked loop (PLL).

 

This example consist of two schematics (DigMod_DSSS_Rake_TxRx and DigMod_DSSS_Rake_BER). Schemtaic

 

DigMod_DSSS_Rake_TxRx shows the performance of each receiver functions (such as frequency synchronization and tracking, rake combiner and etc) in multipath channel and 2000 frequency offset between transmitter and receiver. When Eb/N0 is 2dB, the frequency synchronization detects the frequency offset is about  1980 Hz and have about 20 Hz residual frequency error using DigMod's frequency synchronization algorithm. After Rake combiner, the frequency tracking algorithm (PLL) can track this 20Hz residual frequency error and remove its effect.

 

 

DigMod_DSSS_Rake_BER run BER vs Eb/N0 curve in multipath enviornment. The default is QPSK modulation.

Workspace.Description:
DSSS Spreading Code Generation

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This workspace is to demostrate to generate spreading codes for DSSS source and receiver in SystemVue DigMod library.

 

There are four kinds of Spreading code for DSSS system are generated in this woekspace. These four kinds of spreading codes are Gold code, m-sequence (maximal length sequence), Walsh code (also to generate Hadamard code, OVSF code in 3GPP  by selecting WalshCodeType parameter ) and Zadoff-Chu complex sequence.

 

After running each schematic, one txt file which includes the spreading code will be generated in the directory. We can use an edit to open this txt file and copy the full first line. Then, we can paste it to SpreadingCode parameter in both top level DSSS source and Receiver.

Workspace.Name: DigMod_TxRx_DSSS_AWGN
Workspace.Description:
Digital Modulation Tx and Rx with DSSS in AWGN

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This workspace is to demostrate Digital Modulation source and receiver using DigMod_SourceL_RF and DigMod_ReceiverL_EQ_RF with DSSS (Direct Sequence Spectrum System) in AWGN environment. .

 

The source consists of Preamble and data Payload parts. Both Preamble and data Payload part can be set as BPSK, QPSK, 8-PSK, 16-QAM, 32-QAM, 64-QAM, 128-QAM, 256-QAM, 512-QAM, 1024-QAM, 2048-QAM, 4096-QAM, 16-APSK, 32-APSK, 16 Star-QAM, 32 Star-QAM and Custom APSK. Transmit shaping filter can be selected as Raised Cosine or Root Raised Cosine. The bandwidth is determined by the ChipRate parameter. Oversampling ratio is determined by SampsPerChip parameter.

 

The spreading code is the 7 length barker code [+1, +1, +1, -1, -1, +1, -1].

 

The Design folder  consists both schematics DigMod_DSSS_TxRx_BER_EbN0 and DigMod_DSSS_TxRx_BER_SNR. We can run BER and also can sweep EbN0 or SNR to get BER vs EbN0 or BER vs SNR curve for each linear modulation. Equation Theoretial_QAM_BER calculates 1024-QAM, 256-QAM, 64-QAM, 16-QAM and QPSK's BER vs EbN0 curves. Workspace.Name: DigMod_MMSE_DFE_Transceiver
Workspace.Description:
Digital Modulation Tx and Rx (with MMSE- DFE)

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This workspace is to demostrate Digital Modulation source and receiver using SystemVue data flow model and MATLAB Script model.

 

The source consists of Preamble and data Payload parts. Both Preamble and data Payload part can be set as

  • BPSK, QPSK, 8-PSK, 16-QAM, 32-QAM, 64-QAM, 128-QAM, 256-QAM, 512-QAM, 1024-QAM, 2048-QAM, 4096-QAM, 16-APSK, 32-APSK, 16 Star-QAM, 32 Star-QAM and Custom APSK.
  • Transmit shaping filter can be selected as Raised Cosine or Root Raised Cosine.
  • The bandwidth is determined by the ChipRate parameter.
  • Oversampling ratio is determined by SampsPerChip parameter.

 

In the receiver side, it consists of receiver filter (Root Raised Cosine or No), frame synchronization, automatic gain control (AGC), carrier frequency synchronization, carrier phase estimator. The equalizer is the fast computation MMSE Decision feedback Equalizer.

 

This workspace consists of three folders (1. MMSE-DFE, 2. MMSE-DFE BER vs EbN0 and  3. MMSE-DFE BER vs SNR).

 

Folder 1. MMSE-DFE have one schematic DigMod_MMSE-DFE_TxRx and can show equalized constellation, estimated frequency offset, synchronization index EVM, BER and etc after running it.

 

Folder 2. MMSE-DFE BER vs EbN0 have two schematic DigMod_RFxcvr_BER and DigMod_RFxcvr_ChCoding_BER.  Both schematic can sweep EbN0, bitwidths of ADC (AtoD Analog to Digital Convertor). DigMod_RFxcvr_BER does not include channel coding and channel decoding and get raw BER (uncoded BER) and Schematic DigMod_RFxcvr_ChCoding_BER includes channel coding and decoding (ReedSolomon Encoder (255, 240) and 1/2 convolutional coder) and can get coded BER.

 

Folder 3. MMSE-DFE BER vs SNR have two schematic DigMod_RFxcvr_BER_SNR and DigMod_RFxcvr_ChCoding_BER_SNR (same as Folder 2 use SNR to replace EbN0) and can get raw BER vs SNR and coded BER vs SNR curves.

Workspace.Name: DigMod_TxRx_AWGN
Workspace.Description:
Digital Modulation Tx and Rx (without Intersymbol Interference and Equalizer)

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This workspace is to demostrate Digital Modulation source and receiver using DigMod_SourceL_RF and DigMod_ReceiverL_RF when the system has not intersymbol interference and equalizer.  There are frame synchronization, automatic gain control (AGC), carrier frequency synchronization, carrier phase estimator, carrier frequency tracking (PLL) and equalization in the receiver. This example showes the effect of receiver algorithms such as frame synchronization AGC, carrier frequency synchronization, carrier phase estimator and carrier frequency tracking after adding carrier phase, carrier frequency offset and AWGN.

 

The source consists of Preamble and data Payload parts. Both Preamble and data Payload part can be set as BPSK, QPSK, 8-PSK, 16-QAM, 32-QAM, 64-QAM, 128-QAM, 256-QAM, 512-QAM, 1024-QAM, 2048-QAM, 4096-QAM, 16-APSK, 32-APSK, 16 Star-QAM, 32 Star-QAM and Custom APSK. Transmit shaping filter can be selected as Raised Cosine or Root Raised Cosine. The bandwidth is determined by the ChipRate parameter. Oversampling ratio is determined by SampsPerChip parameter.

 

There are four folders in this examples. Each folder consists of several test cases.

 

Folder 1. FrameSync_AGC consists of 1.1 WoFrameSyncEffect and 1.2 WoAGC two examples.

 

Schematic DigMod_TxRx_wo_FrameSync in 1.1 WoFrameSyncEffect is to show the received constellation when the frame synchronization doesn't work. The Root Raised Cosine filter has 80 samples dealy in the receiver, FrameSyn_Algorithm =W/o FrameSync and KnownDelay=30 (a wrong sync index).  After running this schematic, the constellation is a cloud and can't recognizet 64 points for 64-QAM because of bad frame synchronization.

 

Schematic DigMod_TxRx_wo_AGC in 1.2 WoAGC folder is to show the received constellation without AGC. FrameSyn_Algorithm =DiffCorr or Corr and AGC_Algorithm=NO_AGC.  After running this schematic, the constellation is a 64-points similiar as 64-QAM. But the received constallation's magnitude is much small than the normal 64-QAM constellation. We will get 0.5 BER in this case.

 

Folder 2. CarrierPhase consists of 2.1 CarrierPhaseEffect and 2.2 CarrierPhaseEstimator two examples.

 

Schematic DigMod_TxRx_withCarrierPhase in 2.1 CarrierPhaseEffect is to show the effect of carrier phase. In source, set the InitialPhase=135 degree and set FrameSync_Algorithm=DiffCorr, FreqSync_Mode=W/o FreqSync and PhaseEstimator=No. Run the schematic and see 64-QAM constellation rotates 135 degree.

 

Schematic DigMod_TxRx_withPhaseEstimator in 2.2 CarrierPhaseEstimator is same as the previous DigMod_TxRx_withCarrierPhase setting except PhaseEstimator=Yes. After running this schematic, the 64-QAM constellation hasn't the fixed phase rotation.

 

Folder 3. CarrierFrequencyOffset consists of 3.1 CarrierFrequencyOffsetEffect, 3.2 CarrierFrequencySync, 3.3 CarrierFrequencyTracking_PLL and 3.4 CarrierFreqSync_and_Tracking four examples.

 

Schematic DigMod_TxRx_withCarrierFreqOffset in 3.1 CarrierFrequencyOffsetEffect folder is to show the effect of carrier frequency offset between transmitter and receiver. The FCarrier=FCarrier+50 means to add 50 Hz carrier frequency offset between source and receiver. Set FreqSync_Mode=W/o FreqSync in receiver and run this schematic. The constellation becomes 9 rings for 64-QAM in its constellation figure.

 

Schematic DigMod_TxRx_withCarrierFreqSync in 3.2 CarrierFrequencySync folder is to show the effect of carrier frequency synchronization algorithm. The FCarrier=FCarrier+50 means to add 50 Hz carrier frequency offset between source and receiver. Set FreqSync_Mode=Corr or CIR_Corr in receiver and run this schematic. The constellation becomes the normal 64-QAM constellation. But, the constellation has small shift which is caused by the residual frequency error.

 

Schematic DigMod_TxRx_withCarrierFreqTracking_PLL in 3.3 CarrierFrequencyTracking_PLL folder is to show the effect of carrier frequency tracking (PLL) algorithm when the frequency offset is small. The FCarrier=FCarrier+50 means to add 50 Hz carrier frequency offset between source and receiver. Set FreqSync_Mode=W/o FreqSync and set FreqTrackMode=DD-PLL and set PLL_Bandwidth=60Hz in receiver and run this schematic. The constellation becomes the normal 64-QAM constellation. The frequency offset was removed by the DD-PLL.

 

Schematic DigMod_TxRx_withFreqSync_and_Tracking in 3.4 CarrierFreqSync_and_Tracking folder is to show the effect of both carrier freqency synchronization and carrier frequency tracking (PLL) algorithm when the frequency offset is large. The FCarrier=FCarrier+24909.9 means to add 24909.9 Hz carrier frequency offset between source and receiver. Set FreqSync_Mode=Corr or CIR_Corr and set FreqTrackMode=DD-PLL and set PLL_Bandwidth=4Hz in receiver and run this schematic. The constellation becomes the normal 64-QAM constellation. The frequency offset was removed by the carrier frequency synchronization algorithm and tracking algorithm.

 

Folder 4. DigMod_TxRx_NoISI_BER consists schematic to run BER and also can sweep EbN0 to get BER vs EbN0 for each linear modulation. Equation Theoretial_QAM_BER calculates 1024-QAM, 256-QAM, 64-QAM, 16-QAM and QPSK's BER vs EbN0 curves. Graph QAM_BER_vs_EbN0 shows SystemVue simulation of 1024-QAM, 256-QAM, 64-QAM, 16-QAM and QPSK's BER vs EbN0 curves and compares with theoretical 1024-QAM, 256-QAM, 64-QAM, 16-QAM and QPSK curves.

 

Note: To decrease the size of example, all the default datasets are deleted, please re-run the analysis to show the graphs.

Workspace.Name: DigMod_TxRx_DFE
Workspace.Description:
Digital Modulation Tx and Rx with DFE

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This workspace is to demostrate Digital Modulation source and receiver using DigMod_SourceL_RF and DigMod_ReceiverL_EQ_RF when the system has multi-path channel and equalizer.  There are frame synchronization, automatic gain control (AGC), carrier frequency synchronization, carrier phase estimator, carrier frequency tracking (PLL) and equalization in the receiver.

 

This example showes the performance of Decision Feedback Equalizer and Fractional Space DFE (FS-DFE). It consists of 1.DFE_FeedbackTaps_Effect and 2. DFE_BER two folders.

 

Folder 1. DFE_FeedbackTaps_Effect consists of five examples using DFE with different feedback taps from (0 to 4).

 

The discrete-time channel model is [0.227, 0.460, 0.688, 0.460, 0.227] which is from John G. Proakis, Digital Communications, Fourth Edition, McGraw Hill, 2011. All examples haven't add noise and just to see the effect of feedback taps in decision feedback equalizer. After running all these five schematics, we can see constellations, EVM and BER become better and better when Feedback.

 

Folder 2. DFE_BER consists of four examples using DFE and FS-DFE and run to get BER vs Eb/N0 curves.

 

The discrete-time channel model is [0.407, 0.815, 0.407] which is also from John G. Proakis, Digital Communications, Fourth Edition, McGraw Hill, 2011.This forder consists of four schematics and two examples using DFE with different feedback taps and other two examples using fraction space DFE with different fractional space T/4 and T/2. After running all these four examples, we can see the performance of fractional space DFE is better than DFE.

Workspace.Name: DigMod_TxRx_LE
Workspace.Description:
Digital Modulation Tx and Rx with Linear Equalizer)

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This workspace is to demostrate Digital Modulation source and receiver using DigMod_SourceL_RF and DigMod_ReceiverL_EQ_RF when the system has multi-path channel and equalizer.  There are frame synchronization, automatic gain control (AGC), carrier frequency synchronization, carrier phase estimator, carrier frequency tracking (PLL) and equalization in the receiver.

 

This example showes the effect of linear equalizer.  The linear equalizer is a T/2 fractional space equalizer (FSE) with 25 taps. There are three folders to show the effect of linear equalizer parameters (such as training sequence, scaling factor alpha for LMS algorithm, LMS, RLS and RLS/LMS and etc).

 

The channel is a digital microwave wireless channel and its symbol rate is 22.5MHz and its 27 T/2 channel impulse response coefficients are as follows.

                                          1.    0.0024320-j*0.0029041,

                                          2.   -0.0485812+j*0.0064138,

                                          3.   -0.0731322+j*0.0136050,

                                          4.   -0.0799314+j*0.0066369, 

                                          5.     0.0184484 -j*0.0111444,

                                          6.     0.6113653-j*0.0641460, 

                                          7.     1.3812122-j*0.1017416, 

                                          8.     1.2697090+j*0.0082850, 

                                          9.     0.3724493+j*0.2400930,

                                         10.   -0.1415443+j*0.3563844,

                                         11.  - 0.0277736+j*0.2160805,

                                         12.    0.1101153-j*0.0072676, 
                                          13.   0.0663287-j*0.0717074, 

                                          14.   0.0052693+j*0.00355592,

                                          15.   0.0011962+j*0.05117560,

                                          16.   0.0078385+j*0.02020538,

                                          17.  -0.0301209-j*0.0151185,

                                          18.  -0.1217017+j*0.0044331, 
                                          19.  -0.2123630+j*0.0359529,

                                           20. -0.2011702+j*0.0074156,

                                           21. -0.0770560-j*0.0474872,

                                           22.  0.0297523-j*0.0586389,

                                           23.  0.0490209-j*0.02209540,

                                           24.  0.0262517+j*0.0183877, 
                                           25. -0.0015701+j*0.0305474,

                                           26. -0.0171064+j*0.0230189,

                                           27. -0.0127459+j*0.0105955

 

Folder 1. LMS_ChangeTrainSeq_Length consists of DigMod_LE_LongTrainSeq and DigMod_LE_ShortTrainSeq two examples.

 

This forder consists of two schematic and equalizer algorithm adopts LMS algorithm. Schematic DigMod_LE_LongTrainSeq has 1500 trainging sequence and DigMod_LE_ShortTrainSeq  has 500 training sequence. The alpha values of LMS algorithm are all set to 0.004 in both schematics. After running both schematic, for the short traing sequence, the equalizer was not convergence after traing because of short traing sequence. So, its constellation was poor and MSE (mean square error) was large for payload part. But, for the long trainging sequence, the equalizer was convergence after traing because of enough traing sequence. So, its constellation was good and MSE (mean square error) was small for payload part.

 

Folder 2. LMS_Change_alpha_factor consists of DigMod_LE_large_alpha and DigMod_LE_small_alpha two examples.

 

This forder consists of two schematic and equalizer algorithm adopts LMS algorithm and traning sequence length is 1000 in both schematics. Schematic DigMod_LE_large_alpha has a little large alpha value (0.005) and  Schematic DigMod_LE_small_alpha has a little small alpha value (0.002). After running both schematic, for the small alpha example, the equalizer was not convergence after traing because of small alpha  for equalizer coefficients upgrade. So, its constellation was poor and MSE (mean square error) was large for payload part. But, for the lare alpha example, the equalizer was convergence. So, its constellation was good and MSE (mean square error) was small for payload part.

 

Folder 3.RLS_and_LMS consists of DigMod_LE_RLS, DigMod_LE_RLSLMS and DigMod_LE_LMS three examples.

 

The preamble length is set to 400 in all these three schematic. Schematic DigMod_LE_RLS adopts RLS algorithm to update coefficients, schematic DigMod_LE_RLSLMS adopts RLS/LMS algorithm (RLS in training phase and LMS in payload part) and schematic DigMod_LE_LMS adopts LMS algorithm to update coefficients. After running these three schematics, results are shown in Graph3 subforder. RLS's convergence speed is much faster than LMS algorithm. In order to reduce complexity, RLS/LMS is a good choice.

 

Note: To decrease the size of example, all the default datasets are deleted, please re-run the analysis to show the graphs.

Workspace.Name: DigMod_DigitalDemod_LinearModulation
Workspace.Description:
DigMod_DigitalDemod_LinearModulation

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This example simulates the whole process of the linear communication system. 

  • 1. The origial message is generated by RandomBits.
  • 2. The baseband signal is generated by DigitalMod, and the SetSampleRate model is used to set the symbol rate. The passband signal is generated by upconverting the baseband signal by Modulator.
  • 3. The AWGN channel is simulated by the AddNDensity model.
  • 4. The received  signal is first downconverted into baseband signal. After that, a filter which is adopted as the match filter is used. Passing through the filter, the best sample is chosen for the DigMod_DigitalDemod. And for those linear digital modulation formats, DigMod_DigitalDemod takes one sample as input and demodulates it into bits.
  • 5. BER_FER model test the BER performance and save the result into the data set. There will be a delay between the TEST and REF port for the BER_FER. The delay is generated by the filters.
  • 6. By using sweep analysis, the BER performance with EbNo can be got and drawn into the BERvsEbNo graphs.
  • 7. By changing the parameter ModType, the worksapce can simulate the BER performance of the according modulation format.

Workspace.Name: DigMod_DigitalDemod_NonlinearModulation
Workspace.Description:
DigMod_DigitalDemod_NonlinearModulation

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This example simulates the whole process of the communication system of several digital modulation formats that SystemVue supports. 

  • 1. The origial message is generated by RandomBits.
  • 2. The baseband signal is generated by DigitalMod.
  • 3. The rf link including the AWGN channel is implemented by the RF_Link_Channel subnetwork.
  • 4. The received downconverted baseband signal is demodulated by 2 methods.
    • For DBPSK, pi/2-DBPSK, DQPSK, pi/4-DQPSK, D8PSK, pi/8-D8PSK, EDGE-8PSK, CQPSK, pi/4-CQPSK, a filter which is adopted as the match filter is used. After passing through the filter, the best sample is chosen for the DigMod_DigitalDemod. And for those digital modulation formats, DigMod_DigitalDemod takes one sample as input and demodulates it into bits.
    • For SOQPSK-MIL, SOQPSK-TG, MSK, GMSK, M_ary CPM, Multi-h CPM, IJF-OQPSK, FQPSK, EFQPSK and FSK, the DigitalMod_DigitalDemod model takes the whole baseband signal as input and demodulated it into bits under ML criterion.
  • 5. BER_FER model test the BER performance and save the result into the data set. There will be a delay between the TEST and REF port for the BER_FER. The delay is generated by the filters or signal generation or signal demodulation algorighms. More details can be got from the help documents.
  • 6. By using sweep analysis, the BER performance with EbNo can be got and drawn into the BERvsEbNo_xxxx graphs.

Workspace.Name: FH_SS
Workspace.Description:
Gererating and Analyzing Frequency Hopping Spread Spectrum Signals

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

Spread spectrum is a key technology in secure, wireless communications. One type of spread spectrum is frequency hopping. Each spread spectrum system uses a pseudo-random number (PN) generator to produce an output sequence which is uniformly “random” and nonrepeatable. The most common type of PN generator is a shift register with linear feedback (LSFR).

 

This workspace is to demonstrate how to generate and analyze frequency hopping spread spectrum signals.  In the designs,  using DigMod source and equalizer receiver.  It also can be used with Keysight instruments (such as M8190A, M9703A or M93XX) for downloading FH SS signal to Keysight signal generator and for capturing waveform from Keysight Signal Analyzer to do more measurements.  

 

FH_SS_Sim schematic is a simulation design for the performance analysis of a FH SS transiver.

Workspace.Name: ISDB_OneLayer_BER_AWGN_IdealSyncChEsti
Workspace.Description:
ISDBT One Lyaer BER example

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This example demonstrates the link level ISDB-T one layer BER simulation process with ideal channel estimation under AWGN channel. In this example:

  1. Synchronization is ideal
    • Bypass the synchronization models by setting the BlockSync and FreqSync parameters of ISDBT_OneLayReceiver in Design1 to NO.
  2. Channel estimation is ideal
    • Bypass the power normalization model (RMS_Calibration) in the ISDBT_OneLaySource model, i.e.
      • set the PowerCalibration parameter of ISDBT_OneLaySource in Design1 to NO
    • Bypass time windowing (may introduce delay) in the ISDBT_OneLaySource model, i.e.
      • set the TimeWindowingRatio parameter to 0
    • Remove FFT window offset
      • set the FFTWindowOffset parameter of ISDBT_OneLayOFDMDemod in ISDBT_OneLayReceiver to 0
    • Bypass channel estimation/equalization models in the ISDBT_OneLayOFDMDemod model, i.e.
      • override the CFR (channel frequency response) of ISDBT_2DChEstimator to 1

According to DVB-T specification ETSI EN 300 744 V1.5.1 (2004-11), the required C/N for BER 2x10^-4 after Viterbi in Gaussian channel is

    • 3.1 dB for QPSK and 1/2 code rate
    • 8.8 dB for 16-QAM and 1/2 code rate
    • 14.4 dB for 64-QAM and 1/2 code rate

It takes about 2 minutes to get the BER results in a PC with a 3.0 GHz Core 2 Duo CPU.

Workspace.Name: AlgorithmReference_BeiDou2_B1_Tx
Workspace.Description:
Beidou B1 Source

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This workspace is to generate Beidou B1 source according to "BeiDou Navigation Satellite System Signal In Space
Interface Control Document (Test Version)", China Satellite Navigation Office, December 2011.

 

1. "BeiDou2 B1 Code"

The rate of the ranging code in channel I of carrier B1 is 2.046 Mcps, and the length is 2046 chips. The ranging code in channel I of carrier B1 is a balanced Gold code truncating the last one chip. The Gold code is generated by means of Modulo-2 addition of G1 and G2 sequences which are respectively derived from two 11-bit linear shift registers.

The generator polynomials for G1 and G2 are as follows:
G1(X)=1+X+X^7+X^8+X^9+X^10+X^11

G2(X)=1+X+X^2+X^3+X^4+X^5+X^8+X^9+X^11
The initial phases of G1 and G2 are:
G1: 01010101010
G2: 01010101010

 

The different phase shift of G2 sequence is accomplished by respective tapping in the shift register generating G2 sequence. By means of Modulo-2 addition of G2 with different phase shift and G1, a ranging code in channel I is generated for each satellite.

2. "Beidou2 B1 RF TX"

This design generate uncoded Beidou B1 source by using I range code with an RF transmission design. 

 

The key parameters are as follows:

Carrier frequency:                                              1561.098 MHz
Modulation:                                                         Quadrature Phase Shift Keying(QPSK)
Ranging code rate Channel I:                           2.046 Mcps
Ranging code length Channel I:                        2046 chips
Channel I of GEO satellites:                              500 bps
Data rate Channel I of MEO/IGSO satellites:  50 bps
Secondary code rate:                                        1 Kbps
Access mode:                                                    Code Division Multiple Access(CDMA)
Polarization:                                                        Right-Handed Circular Polarization(RHCP)

Workspace.Name: BDS_B1I_AcquisitionTracking
Workspace.Description:
BDS B1I Code Acquisition and Tracking

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Workspace

 

This example demonstrates how to demodulate navigation message by using Acquisition and Tracking model based on Systemvue platform.

Acquisition model is used to detect all visible satellites specified in parameter SatelliteList. For each satellite, a B1I code replica with stepping frequency carrier is generated to correlate the input signal. If the correlation peak is larger than threshold, B1I code is wiped off from the input signal and FFT (Fast Fourier Transform) operation is applied to estimate fine carrier Doppler frequency. The search process is a two-dimension process.

Tracking model is used to track satellites and demodulate navigation message. For a certain channel, the corresponding tracking loop will generate the replica of carrier wave and spreading code of a satellite according to acquisition results of this satellite. During tracking phase, a tracking loop measures tracking errors with which to tune local code and carrier wave to align with the received signal.

For acquisition model, data from input ReceiveSignal is baseband signal. Input LockFlagIn(0: unlocked, 1: locked) is locked PRN list from tracking model. It will inform acquisition model which satellites have been locked. Acquisition model will detect the remaining unlocked satellites. Acquisition model will output PRNs of detected satellites and corresponding precise carrier frequency (in Hz, error<25Hz) and code phase (in sample) according to output bus width. For example, if output bus width is 3 and current acquired satellite number is 4, acquisition model will output results of 3 acquired satellites in order of signal strength. If output bus width is 3 and currently acquired satellite number is 2, acquisition model will output 2 acquired satellites results in order of signal strength and 0 will be fulfilled to the remaining ports.

For tracking model, the number of tracking channels specified by output bus width may vary from the number of acquisition channels specified by input bus width. Each firing, all tracking channels are checked and idle/unlocked channels are identified. If a new satellite is acquired, it will be assigned to an idle/unlocked tracking channel. Idle/unlocked tracking channels with lower bus index will be used firstly. 

 

There are 2 folders in this workspace: 

1. BDS B1I Scenario

In this design, BDS_B1I_ScenarioGen model generates BDS signal. We can set ChannelNum of BDS_B1I_ScenarioGen model to control how many satellites we want to simulate. By default, SatelliteList are [1,3,9,10] .

 

2. BDS B1I Single Source

In this design, BDS_B1I_Source model generates BDS signal. We can set PRN of BDS_B1I_Source model to control which satellite we want to simulate. There are 4 options to control doppler information so that we can get 4 types of signal(0:no doppler shift; 1:code doppler shift only; 2:carrier doppler shift only; 3:code doppler shift and carrier doppler shift).

Workspace.Name: BDS_B1I_Scenario_N5182B
Workspace.Description:
BDS B1I Scenario Instrument Connection example

 

This example illustrates how to download BDS scenario waveform with user defined receiver trace.

 

SignalDownloader_E4438C is used to download waveform into instrument, so this example can support N5182B. Note that N5182B BBG memory size should be at least 500MSa to play the 120s scenario waveform (2x oversampling).

 

The user should get the IP address of N5182B and set it to the model, and then wait about 35 minutes for the case in the example . After downloading, user should check if the frequency and power of N5182B are consistent with expectation.

 

Note that the waveform downloaded into instrument is repeatedly played. So in this example , after 120s, the signal from N5182B would not valid for receivers. User can reset the waveform to get it played from begining by set the trigger type of N5182B to Reset & Run.

Workspace.Name: BDS_SatellitesSelection
Workspace.Description:
BDS SatellitesSelection example

 

This example shows the satellites selection process. Four models are included:

1. BDS_TrajectoryGen : User can generate a trajectory. In this example, it is used to generate a fix position on which user watches the sky.

2. BDS_CoordinateTransform: It is used to transfer the (Latitude,Longitude,Altitude) to ECEF(x,y,z) which is the format for trajectory input of BDS_SatelliteSelection model.

3. BDS_SatPosCalc: Given the time and almanac(The ephemeris is not availiable now ,so pls leave it blank), it generates the postions of 32 BDS satellites in the form of ECEF(x,y,z).

4. BDS_SatelliteSelection : This model is used to select the satellites which have elevation angles larger than mask(defaultly, it is 0 degree).

 

In this example, Users may change parameter SatType in BDS_SatelliteSelection to choose which kind of satellites to select. Users may change the postion in BDS_TrajectoryGen to see different view from different position. Users may also change the simulation time and satellites number in parameters tab.

 

In SatPosSkyView figure, the satellites with elevation angles less than 0 degree are regarded as invisible. So they are displayed in the edge of the circle. In equation1, User can modify numSatellitesDisplay which controls the displayed satellites in figure SatPosSkyView.

 

In PRNvsChannel figure, the PRNs in each channel are displayed. When the satellites is invisible, its PRN is artificially modified to a negative value.

 

Note: To decrease the size of example, all the default datasets are deleted, please re-run the analysis to show the graphs.

Workspace.Name: AlgorithmReference_GNSS_BOC1
Workspace.Description:
Generating Generic Global Navigation Satellite Signals

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Workspace

 

 This example illustrates the usage of generic building blocks for creating generic satcom signaling with Binary Offset Carrier (BOC) and Binary Phase Shift Keying (BPSK) using Keysight SystemVue.    

 

BOC_n_1_RF_TX_Design can generate BOC(n,1) signal by setting the variable SC_RATE=n in Equation part. The variable OUT_RATE represents oversampling ratio of the BOC(n,1) signal. The default values of SC_RATE and OUT_RATE are 1 and 20 respectively. That means to generate BOC(1,1) signal with 20 oversampling ratio.

 

BPSK_RF_TX_Design can generate BPSK with spreading code, which is GPS L1 signal.  The variable OUT_RATE represents oversampling ratio of this BPSK signal. The default value of OUT_RATE is 20. That means to generate BPSK(1) signal with 20 oversampling ratio.

 

Both spectrums of BPSK(1) and BOC(1,1) are compared in the graph.

Workspace.Name: AlgorithmReference_GNSS_BOC_n_m
Workspace.Description:
Generating Generic Global Navigation Satellite Signals

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Workspace

 

This example illustrates the usage of generic building blocks for creating generic satcom signaling with Binary Offset Carrier (BOC) using Keysight SystemVue.   The blocks used in this example are all from the standard "Algorithm" library within SystemVue.  

 

In this particular design, a binary offset carrier, BOC(n,m), waveform is created is generated for fs = n and fc = m, i.e. BOC(15,2.5). 

 

BOC_n_m_RF_TX_Design can generate BOC(n,m) signal by setting the variable SC_RATE=n and SP_RATE=m in Equation part. The variable OUT_RATE represents oversampling ratio of the BOC(n,m) signal. The default values of SC_RATE, SP_RATE and OUT_RATE are 15, 2.5 and 60 respectively. That means to generate BOC(15,2.5) signal with 60 oversampling ratio.

GLONASS L1 Source and Application

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

GLONASS (GLOBAL NAVIGATION SATTELITE SYSTEM) applications have data coding requirements defined in the technical specification ICD L1, L2 GLONASS (Edition 5.1 2008).

 

The modulating sequence used for modulation of carrier frequencies sub-bands (when generating standard accuracy signals) in L1 for GLONASS satellites and L1 is generated by the Modulo-2 addition of the following three binary signals:

  1. PR ranging code transmitted at 511 kbps;
  2. Navigation message transmitted at 50 bps, and 100 Hz auxiliary meander sequence.

"GLONASS RF TX"

This design demonstrates the use of the C/A code and P code with an RF transmission design.  The Navigation message data rate is 50 bps and PR ranging code rate is 511 kbps. 10220 PR code chips occur for each data bit. 

 

In this example, Navigation message bits are set with random bits.

 

The GLONASS L2 carrier is not modeled in this example.

Workspace.Name: AlgorithmReference_GPS_Codes_and_RF_TX
Workspace.Description:
GPS Codes and Application

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

GPS navigation (NAV) applications have data coding requirements defined in the technical specification ICD-GPS-200C (Navstar GPS Space Segment / Navigation User Interfaces).  For GPS NAV applications, two basic ranging codes are generated (among several others).  The precision (P) code is the principal NAV ranging code.  The coarse/acquisition (C/A) code is used primarily for acquisition of the P code.  See the IDC documents for details on GSP codes.

 

1. "GPS C/A Gold Code"

This design demonstrates the C/A code for GPS applications.  This is a Gold code, Gi(t), of 1 millisecond in length at a chipping rate of 1023 Kbps.  A Gold code is generated by the Modulo-2 addition of two Linear Feedback Shift Register (G1 and G2) sequences that have specific autocorrelation properties.  The GPS Gold code generator applies a selected delay to the G2 sequence to meet the GPS C/A code specification.  The delayed G2 sequence is called G2i.  The GPS C/A code Gi(t) is the Modulo-2 addition of G1 and G2i.  This results in 36 mutually exclusive C/A codes.

 

The SystemVue GoldCode model supports many types of Gold codes include that required for GPS applications.  The GoldCodePolynomial option named "G1[10 3]&G2[10 9 8 6 3 2]_GPS" is for GPS applications and when selected the PhaseSelect option can be set to result in the GPS C/A Gi(t) output.  The GoldCode model also outputs the G1 and G2 codes for reference.

2. "GPS P Code"

This design demonstrates the P code for GPS applications.  This is a ranging code, Pi(t), of 7 days in length at a chipping rate of 10.23 Mbps. The 7 day sequence is the Modulo-2 sum of two sub-sequences referred to as X1 and X2i. Their lengths are 15,345,000 chips and 15,345,037 chips, respectively. The X2i sequence is an X2 sequence selectively delayed by 1 to 37 chips thereby allowing the basic code generation technique to produce a set of 37 mutually exclusive P-code sequences of 7 days in length.  Each Pi(t) pattern is the Modulo-2 sum of two extended patterns clocked at 10.23 Mbps (X1 and X2i).

 

X1 itself is generated by the Modulo-2 sum of the output of two 12-stage registers (X1A and X1B) short cycled to 4092 and 4093 chips respectively.

 

When the X1A short cycles are counted to 3750, the X1 epoch is generated. The X1 epoch occurs every 1.5 seconds after 15,345,000 chips of the X1 pattern have been generated. At each X1 epoch, the X1A shift register is initialized and the X1B shift register is initialized. The first chip of the X1A sequence and the first chip of the X1B sequence occur simultaneously in the first chip interval of any X1 period. 

 

The shortened X1B cycle causes precession of the X1B sequence with respect to the X1A sequence during subsequent cycles of the X1A sequence in the X1 period. Reinitialization of the X1A shift register produces a 4092 chip sequence by omitting the last 3 chips (001) of the natural 4095 chip X1A sequence. Re-initialization of the X1B shift register produces a 4093 chip sequence by omitting the last 2 chips (01) of the natural 4095 chip X1B sequence. This results in the phase of the X1B sequence lagging by one chip for each X1A cycle in the X1 period. The X1 period is defined as the 3750 X1A cycles (15,345,000 chips) which is not an integer number of X1B cycles. To accommodate this situation, the X1B shift register is held in the final state (chip 4093) of its 3749th cycle. It remains in this state until the X1A shift register completes its 3750th cycle (343 additional chips). The completion of the 3750th X1A cycle establishes the next X1 epoch which re-initializes both the X1A and X1B shift registers starting a new X1 cycle.

 

The X2i sequences are generated by first producing an X2 sequence and then delaying it by a selected integer number of chips, i, ranging from 1 to 37. Each of the X2i sequences is then Modulo-2 added to the X1 sequence thereby producing up to 37 unique P(t) sequences.

 

The X2A and X2B shift registers, used to generate X2, operate in a similar manner to the X1A and X1B shift registers. They are short-cycled, X2A to 4092 and X2B to 4093, so that they have the same relative precession rate as the X1 shift registers. X2A epochs are counted to include 3750 cycles and X2B is held in the last state at 3749 cycle until X2A completes its 3750th cycle. The X2A and X2B epochs are made to precess with respect to the X1A and X1B epochs by causing the X2 period to be 37 chips longer than the X1 period. When the X2A is in the last state of its 3750th cycle and X2B is in the last state of its 3749th cycle, their transitions to their respective initial states are delayed by 37 chip time durations.

 

The Pi(t) code is the Modulo-2 sum of X1 and X2i. The analysis for the P code design is set up for one X1 epoch time duration (1.5 sec) and does not include initialization of the GPS week

 

The X1 Epoch time interval requires over 15M simulation samples and takes a substantial time to simulate.

3. "GPS RF TX"

This design demonstrates the use of the C/A code and P code with an RF transmission design.  The system data rate is 50 bps.  20460 C/A code chips occur for each data bit.  204600 P code chips occur for each data bit. 

 

For GPS applications, the RF (L-band) signal is contained within two 20.46-MHz bands centered about L1 and L2. The carrier frequencies for the L1 and L2 signals shall be coherently derived from a common frequency source within the satellite vehicle. The nominal frequency of this source -- as it appears to an observer on the ground -- is 10.23 MHz.  The nominal carrier frequencies (f0) shall be 1575.42 MHz, and 1227.6 MHz for L1 and L2, respectively.

 

The L1 carrier is quadrature modulated with the C/A code plus data applied to the Q-channel and the P code plus data applied to the I-channel.  When Pi(t) equals one, a 180-degree phase reversal of the P-carrier occurs; when Gi(t) equals one, the C/A carrier advances 90 degrees; when the Gi(t) equals zero, the C/A carrier shall be retarded 90 degrees (such that when Gi(t) changes state, a 180-degree phase reversal of the C/A carrier occurs).

 

The L2 carrier is not modeled in this example.

Workspace.Name: AlgorithmReference_GPS_L1C_Source_RF_TX
Workspace.Description:
GPS L1C Source

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

GPS navigation (NAV) applications have data coding requirements defined in the interface specification IS-GPS-800(04 September 2008), "Navstar GPS Space Segment/User Segment L1C Interfaces.".  This example is to generate L1CPi and L1CDi ranging code, L1C overlay code, L1CD BOC(1,1) and L1CP TMBOC source.

 

1. "GPS L1C Ranging Code"

 

This design generates the L1CPi and L1CDi ranging code for  for GPS L1C source.

 

The PRN ranging codes L1CPi(t) and L1CDi(t) for PRN signal number i are independent, time synchronized, and 10 milliseconds in length at a chipping rate of 1.023 Mbps, for total length of 10230 chips.

 

Both L1CPi(t) and L1CDi(t) are constructed using the same method. Each ranging code is derived from a unique length-10223 sequence  with a common 7-bit expansion sequence inserted at a PRN signal number-dependent point. The unique length-10223 sequence for each ranging code is derived from a single fixed length-10223 sequence called a Legendre sequence
L(t), for t = 0, …, 10222. L(t) is defined as,
L(0) = 0 ;
L(t) = 1, if there exists an integer x such that t is congruent to x2 modulo 10223;
L(t) = 0, if there exists no integer x such that t is congruent to x2 modulo 10223.
Table 6.2-1 in Section 6.2.3 provides the generated sequence of the above defined L(t).
The above Legendre sequence is used to construct the unique length-10223 sequence used for each ranging code.
This sequence, called a Weil-code, is the exclusive-or of L(t) and a shift of L(t). A Weil-code Wi(t ; w) is specified
by Weil Index w, ranging from 1 to 5111, which represents the shift of L(t) and is defined as,
Wi(t ; w) = L(t) ⊕ L( (t + w) modulo 10223 ) for t = 0 to 10222,

Finally, the ranging code is constructed by inserting a fixed expansion sequence into the Weil-code. The expansion sequence is the seven bit values 0 1 1 0 1 0 0. The insert point is specified by Insertion Index p, where p = 1 to 10223. The expansion sequence is inserted before the pth value of the Weil-code.
Thus the ranging code L1CPi(t)/L1CDi(t) is defined as,
                         L1CPi(t)/L1CDi(t) = Wi(t ; w), for t = 0, 1, . . . , p – 2;
                         L1CPi(t)/L1CDi(t) = 0, for t = p – 1;
                         L1CPi(t)/L1CDi(t) = 1, for t = p;
                         L1CPi(t)/L1CDi(t) = 1, for t = p + 1;
                         L1CPi(t)/L1CDi(t) = 0, for t = p + 2;
                         L1CPi(t)/L1CDi(t) = 1, for t = p + 3;
                         L1CPi(t)/L1CDi(t) = 0, for t = p + 4;
                         L1CPi(t)/L1CDi(t) = 0, for t = p + 5;
                         L1CPi(t)/L1CDi(t) = Wi(t – 7 ; w), for t = p + 6, p + 7, . . ., 10229.

 

2. "GPS L1C Overlay Code"

This design generates the L1COi  overlay code for  for GPS L1C source.

 

There is an overlay modulation code L1COi(t) for PRN signal number i which also is independent, time synchronized, and 18 seconds in length at a rate of 100 bps, for total length of 1800 bits. The overlay code, L1COi(t), is modulo-2 added to L1CPi(t).

 

The overlay codes L1COi(t) are constructed using Linear Feedback Shift Register (LFSR) methods. These codes are 2047 bits long truncated to 1800-bits long sequences and are constructed using 11-stage LFSR generators as described below. This section provides the code generation method for the first 63 PRN numbers and Section 6.3.1.2 provides the generation method for the additional PRN signal numbers 64 through 210.
The overlay codes are derived from addition (exclusive-or) of two sequences. The two sequences, denoted as S1 and S2, are each derived from a PRN signal number-dependent code generator polynomial represented by Pi(x).
The generator polynomial for S1 is defined as,
                                  11            j
                      P(x) =  Σ      m x,
                        i        j= 0     ij
where the coefficient mi, j is defined for each PRN signal number, i. For PRN signal numbers 1 - 63, only the sequence S1 is used and, as such, S2 is not needed. The sequence S2 is added to S1 sequence to generate the additional PRN signal numbers 64 through 210 as further described in Section 6.3.1.2. The generator polynomial coefficient mi, j for PRN signal numbers 1 - 63 are specified in Table 3.2-3. Table 3.2-3 also specifies the initial 11 bits of the sequence, which is also the initial condition of the code generator for each PRN signal number. The final
11 bits of the sequence are also shown in Table 3.2-3; these are the last 11 values after the code generator is clocked for 1800 bits. The L1CO-code generator is conceptually described in Figure 3.2-2.

 

3. "GPS L1C Channel Coding"

This design implement FEC channel coding for  the L1CD signal.

 

The message modulated onto the L1CD signal consists of subframe, frame, and superframe. Subframe and frame are shown in Figure 3.2-3. A frame is divided into three subframes of varying length. Multiple frames (i.e. superframe) are required to broadcast a complete data message set to users.

Each frame shall consist of 9 bits of “Time of Interval” (TOI) data in subframe 1, 600 bits of “non-variable” clock
and ephemeris data with Cyclic Redundancy Check (CRC) in subframe 2, and 274 bits of “variable” data with CRC in subframe 3. The content of subframe 3 nominally varies from one frame to the next and is identified by a page number. The content of subframe 2 is nominally non-variant over a period of multiple frames.

Subframe 1 provides 9-bit TOI data that corresponds to the time epoch at the start (leading edge) of the next
following frame (reference paragraph 3.5.2). The 9-bit TOI data shall be encoded into 52-symbol code using Bose, Chaudhuri, and Hocquenghem (BCH) code as defined in paragraph 3.2.3.2.

Subframes 2 and 3 shall utilize 24-bit CRC parity algorithm as defined in paragraph 3.2.3.3 with a separate CRC for each subframe. Each of the two subframes (2 and 3) shall be further encoded using Low Density Parity Check (LDPC) Forward Error Correction (FEC) code as defined in paragraph 3.2.3.4. The FEC encoded symbols shall be interleaved, as defined in paragraph 3.2.3.5, prior to being modulo-2 added to L1CD-code.
The resulting 1800 symbols, DL1C(t), representing one message frame, shall be broadcast at 100 symbols per second.

.

4. "GPS L1CD RF TX BOC_1_1"

This design generates the L1CD signal by using L1CDi ranging code.

 

The bitstream of L1CD signal is modulated on L1 carrier frequency using BOC (1, 1) modulation, with a subcarrier frequency of 1.023 MHz and a chipping rate of 1.023 Mbps. Each bit of the bitstream is applied to a BOC(1,1) spreading symbol consisting of one cycle of a 1.023 MHz squarewave, defined as binary 10 (1= positive binary bit value, see Figure 3.3-2a) with total duration 1/1.023 microseconds. The BOC(1,1) spreading symbols are defined using sine-phasing, so are aligned with bits of L1CD-code. Contrary to convention, a “0” is in-phase with the carrier and a “1” is 180 out of phase with the carrier.

 

The parameter OversamplingRatio is to set the oversampling ratio of GPS L1CD signal.

 

5. "GPS L1CP RF TX TMBOC"

This design generate L1CP signal by using L1CPi ranging code and L1COi overlay code. 

 

The bitstream of L1CP signal is modulated on L1 carrier frequency using TMBOC modulation technique.
The L1CP TMBOC technique uses a mixture of BOC (1, 1) spreading symbols and BOC(6,1) spreading symbols, where each BOC(6,1) spreading symbol consists of 6 cycles of a 6 x 1.023 MHz squarewave, defined as binary 101010101010 (1= binary bit value), with total duration 1/1.023 microseconds (see Figure 3.3-2b).

 

The pattern of BOC(1,1) and BOC(6,1) spreading symbols repeats every 10230 spreading symbols corresponding to a new bit of L1CO-code. Let the index of the spreading symbols L1CP be t = 0, 1, . . ., 10229, where t = 0 is the first spreading symbol in the next bit of L1CO-code. Write t as t = ut + 33 vt, where ut = 0, . . ., 32 and vt = 0, . . ., 309. Then all spreading symbols in L1CP are BOC(1,1), except for those that are BOC(6,1) that occur for those t with ut =0, 4, 6, and 29 (i.e, t = 0, 4, 6, 29, 33, 37, 39, 62, …, 10197, 10201, 10203, 10226). This pattern is shown in
Figure 3.3-2c. The BOC(1,1) and BOC(6,1) spreading symbols are defined using sine-phasing, so are aligned with bits of L1CPcode.

 

The parameter OversamplingRatio is to set the oversampling ratio of GPS L1CP signal.


6. "GPS L1C RF TX "

This design generate L1C fully coded source by combining L1CP and L1CD. 

 

Section 3.2.1.6 defines the Signal Component Phase Relationship (TBD). There are 4 alternatives to define phase relationship between L1CD and L1CP. In this example, we adopts Alternative 1.

Note: one of the following four alternative paragraphs will be selected once the GPS Block IIIA design is defined. Each of these alternatives defines a different phase relationship information between the two L1C components, as well as the relative phase relationship between L1CP and L1 C/A signal (reference IS-GPS-200).
These phase relationships will be fixed and the phase relationship will be finalized once the Block IIIA SV design is selected


Alternative 1. Carriers of the two L1C components defined in Section 3.1 shall be in phase quadrature within ±100 milliradians. The L1CP signal carrier shall lag the L1CD carrier by 90 degrees, so that L1CP carrier phase is the same (within ±100 milliradians) as C/A-code carrier phase, and L1CD carrier phase is the same (within
±100 milliradians) as P(Y)-code carrier phase. Referring to the phase of the L1CD carrier when L1CDi(t) equals zero as the "zero phase angle", the L1CD and L1CP values shall control the respective signal phases in the following manner: when L1CDi(t) equals one, a 180-degree phase reversal of the L1CD-carrier occurs; when
L1CPi(t) equals one, the L1CP carrier advances 90 degrees; when the L1CPi(t) equals zero, the L1CP carrier shall be retarded 90 degrees (such that when L1CPi(t) changes state, a 180-degree phase reversal of the L1CP carrier occurs).

 

The parameter OversamplingRatio is to set the oversampling ratio of GPS L1CP signal.


Note: To decrease the size of example, all the default datasets are deleted, please re-run the analysis to show the graphs.

GPS L1 Source and Application

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

When the X1A short cycles are counted to 3750, the X1 epoch is generated. The X1 epoch occurs every 1.5 seconds after 15,345,000 chips of the X1 pattern have been generated. At each X1 epoch, the X1A shift register is initialized and the X1B shift register is initialized. The X2i sequences are generated by first producing an X2 sequence and then delaying it by a selected integer number of chips, i, ranging from 1 to 37. Each of the X2i sequences is then Modulo-2 added to the X1 sequence thereby producing up to 37 unique P(t) sequences.

They are short-cycled, X2A to 4092 and X2B to 4093, so that they have the same relative precession rate as the X1 shift registers. X2A epochs are counted to include 3750 cycles and X2B is held in the last state at 3749 cycle until X2A completes its 3750th cycle. The X2A and X2B epochs are made to precess with respect to the X1A and X1B epochs by causing the X2 period to be 37 chips longer than the X1 period. When the X2A is in the last state of its 3750th cycle and X2B is in the last state of its 3749th cycle, their transitions to their respective initial states are delayed by 37 chip time durations.

 

The Pi(t) code is the Modulo-2 sum of X1 and X2i. The analysis for the P code design is set up for one X1 epoch time duration (1.5 sec) and does not include initialization of the GPS week

 

The X1 Epoch time interval requires over 15M simulation samples and takes a substantial time to simulate.

3. "GPS RF TX"

This design demonstrates the use of the C/A code and P code with an RF transmission design.  The system data rate is 50 bps.  20460 C/A code chips occur for each data bit.  204600 P code chips occur for each data bit. 

 

For GPS applications, the RF (L-band) signal is contained within two 20.46-MHz bands centered about L1 and L2. The carrier frequencies for the L1 and L2 signals shall be coherently derived from a common frequency source within the satellite vehicle. The nominal frequency of this source -- as it appears to an observer on the ground -- is 10.23 MHz.  The nominal carrier frequencies (f0) shall be 1575.42 MHz, and 1227.6 MHz for L1 and L2, respectively.

 

The L1 carrier is quadrature modulated with the C/A code plus data applied to the Q-channel and the P code plus data applied to the I-channel.  When Pi(t) equals one, a 180-degree phase reversal of the P-carrier occurs; when Gi(t) equals one, the C/A carrier advances 90 degrees; when the Gi(t) equals zero, the C/A carrier shall be retarded 90 degrees (such that when Gi(t) changes state, a 180-degree phase reversal of the C/A carrier occurs).

 

The L2 carrier is not modeled in this example.

Workspace.Name: AlgorithmReference_GPS_L2C_Source_and_RF_TX
Workspace.Description:
GPS L2C Source

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

GPS navigation (NAV) applications have data coding requirements defined in the technical specification IS-GPS-200D (Navstar GPS Space Segment / Navigation User Interfaces).  This example is to generate L2 CM-code, L2 CL-Code and L2C source.

 

1. "GPS L2 CM-Code"

This design generates the L2 CM-code for GPS L2C applications.  

 

The PRN L2 CM-code for SV ID number i is a ranging code, CM,i(t), which is 20 milliseconds in length at a chipping rate of 511.5 Kbps. The epochs of the L2 CM-code are synchronized with the X1 epochs of the P-code. The CM,i(t) sequence is a linear pattern which is short cycled every count of 10230 chips by resetting with a specified initial state. Assignment of initial states by GPS PRN signal number is given in Table 3-II.

2. "GPS L2 CL-Code"

This design generates the L2 CL code for GPS L2C applications. 

 

The PRN L2 CL-code for SV ID number i is a ranging code, CL,i(t), which is 1.5 seconds in length at a chipping rate of 511.5 Kbps. The epochs of the L2 CL-code are synchronized with the X1 epochs of the P-code. The CL,i(t) sequence is a linear pattern which is generated using the same code generator polynomial as the one used for CM,i(t). However, the CL,i(t) sequence is short cycled by resetting with a specified initial state every code count of 767250 chips. Assignment of initial states by GPS PRN signal number is given in Table 3-II.

3. "GPS L2CM CL RF TX"

This design generates L2 CM and L2 CL source. 

 

For Block IIR-M, Block IIF, and subsequent blocks of SVs, civil navigation (CNAV) data, DC(t), also includes SV
ephemerides, system time, SV clock behavior, status messages, etc. The DC(t) is a 25 bps data stream which is coded by a rate ½ convolutional coder. When selected by ground command, the resulting 50 sps symbol stream is modulo-2 added to the L2 CM-code; the resultant bit-train is combined with L2 CL-code using chip by chip timedivision multiplexing method (i.e. alternating between L2 CM ⊕ data and L2 CL chips); the multiplexed bit-train is used to modulate the L2 carrier.

 

4. "GPS L2C RF"

This design demonstrates the use of the L2 CM code, L2 CL code and P code with an RF transmission design. 

 

In this example, In-Phase is to transmit the P-code with or without NAV data D(t); Quadrature-Phase is to transmit L2 CM-code with DC(t) and the L2 CL-code with no data.

 

For Block IIR-M, IIF, and subsequent blocks of SVs, phase quadrature relationship between the two L2 carrier
components can be the same as for the two L1 carrier components as described above. However, for the L2 case, the civil signal carrier component is modulated by any one of three (IIF) or four (IIR-M) different bit trains as
described in paragraph 3.2.3. Moreover, the two L2 carrier components can be in same phase. The resultant
composite transmitted signal phases will vary as a function of the binary state of the modulating signals as well as the signal power ratio and phase quadrature relationship. Beyond these considerations, additional carrier
components in Block IIR-M, IIF, and subsequent blocks of SVs will result in composite transmitted signal phase
relationships other than the nominal special case of Table 3-IV.

Workspace.Name: AlgorithmReference_GPS_L2_Source_and_RF_TX
Workspace.Description:
GPS L2 Source and Application

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

GPS navigation (NAV) applications have data coding requirements defined in the technical specification IS-GPS-200D (Navstar GPS Space Segment / Navigation User Interfaces).  For GPS NAV applications, two basic ranging codes are generated (among several others).  The precision (P) code is the principal NAV ranging code.  The coarse/acquisition (C/A) code is used primarily for acquisition of the P code.  See the IDC documents for details on GSP codes.

 

1. "GPS C/A Gold Code"

This design demonstrates the C/A code for GPS applications.  This is a Gold code, Gi(t), of 1 millisecond in length at a chipping rate of 1023 Kbps.  A Gold code is generated by the Modulo-2 addition of two Linear Feedback Shift Register (G1 and G2) sequences that have specific autocorrelation properties.  The GPS Gold code generator applies a selected delay to the G2 sequence to meet the GPS C/A code specification.  The delayed G2 sequence is called G2i.  The GPS C/A code Gi(t) is the Modulo-2 addition of G1 and G2i.  This results in 36 mutually exclusive C/A codes.

 

The SystemVue GoldCode model supports many types of Gold codes include that required for GPS applications.  The GoldCodePolynomial option named "G1[10 3]&G2[10 9 8 6 3 2]_GPS" is for GPS applications and when selected the PhaseSelect option can be set to result in the GPS C/A Gi(t) output.  The GoldCode model also outputs the G1 and G2 codes for reference.

2. "GPS P Code"

This design demonstrates the P code for GPS applications.  This is a ranging code, Pi(t), of 7 days in length at a chipping rate of 10.23 Mbps. The 7 day sequence is the Modulo-2 sum of two sub-sequences referred to as X1 and X2i. Their lengths are 15,345,000 chips and 15,345,037 chips, respectively. The X2i sequence is an X2 sequence selectively delayed by 1 to 37 chips thereby allowing the basic code generation technique to produce a set of 37 mutually exclusive P-code sequences of 7 days in length.  Each Pi(t) pattern is the Modulo-2 sum of two extended patterns clocked at 10.23 Mbps (X1 and X2i).

 

X1 itself is generated by the Modulo-2 sum of the output of two 12-stage registers (X1A and X1B) short cycled to 4092 and 4093 chips respectively.

 

When the X1A short cycles are counted to 3750, the X1 epoch is generated. The X1 epoch occurs every 1.5 seconds after 15,345,000 chips of the X1 pattern have been generated. At each X1 epoch, the X1A shift register is initialized and the X1B shift register is initialized. The first chip of the X1A sequence and the first chip of the X1B sequence occur simultaneously in the first chip interval of any X1 period. 

 

The shortened X1B cycle causes precession of the X1B sequence with respect to the X1A sequence during subsequent cycles of the X1A sequence in the X1 period. Reinitialization of the X1A shift register produces a 4092 chip sequence by omitting the last 3 chips (001) of the natural 4095 chip X1A sequence. Re-initialization of the X1B shift register produces a 4093 chip sequence by omitting the last 2 chips (01) of the natural 4095 chip X1B sequence. This results in the phase of the X1B sequence lagging by one chip for each X1A cycle in the X1 period. The X1 period is defined as the 3750 X1A cycles (15,345,000 chips) which is not an integer number of X1B cycles. To accommodate this situation, the X1B shift register is held in the final state (chip 4093) of its 3749th cycle. It remains in this state until the X1A shift register completes its 3750th cycle (343 additional chips). The completion of the 3750th X1A cycle establishes the next X1 epoch which re-initializes both the X1A and X1B shift registers starting a new X1 cycle.

 

The X2i sequences are generated by first producing an X2 sequence and then delaying it by a selected integer number of chips, i, ranging from 1 to 37. Each of the X2i sequences is then Modulo-2 added to the X1 sequence thereby producing up to 37 unique P(t) sequences.

 

The X2A and X2B shift registers, used to generate X2, operate in a similar manner to the X1A and X1B shift registers. They are short-cycled, X2A to 4092 and X2B to 4093, so that they have the same relative precession rate as the X1 shift registers. X2A epochs are counted to include 3750 cycles and X2B is held in the last state at 3749 cycle until X2A completes its 3750th cycle. The X2A and X2B epochs are made to precess with respect to the X1A and X1B epochs by causing the X2 period to be 37 chips longer than the X1 period. When the X2A is in the last state of its 3750th cycle and X2B is in the last state of its 3749th cycle, their transitions to their respective initial states are delayed by 37 chip time durations.

 

The Pi(t) code is the Modulo-2 sum of X1 and X2i. The analysis for the P code design is set up for one X1 epoch time duration (1.5 sec) and does not include initialization of the GPS week

 

The X1 Epoch time interval requires over 15M simulation samples and takes a substantial time to simulate.

3. "GPS L2 P with NAV data RF TX"

This design demonstrates the use of the P code with an RF transmission design.  The system data rate is 50 bps.  204600 P code chips occur for each data bit. 

 

For Block II/IIA and IIR, the L2 is BPSK modulated by only one of those two bit trains; the bit train to be used for L2 modulation is selected by ground command. A third modulation mode is also selectable on the L2 channel by ground command: it utilizes the P(Y)-code without the NAV data as the modulating signal. For a particular SV, all transmitted signal elements (carriers, codes and data) are coherently derived from the same onboard frequency source.

4. "GPS L2 CA with NAV data RF TX"

This design demonstrates the use of the P code with an RF transmission design.  The NAV  D(t)system data rate is 50 bps.  20460 CA code chips occur for each data bit. 

 

For Block II/IIA and IIR, the L2 is BPSK modulated by only one of those two bit trains; the bit train to be used for L2 modulation is selected by ground command. A third modulation mode is also selectable on the L2 channel by ground command: it utilizes the P(Y)-code without the NAV data as the modulating signal. For a particular SV, all transmitted signal elements (carriers, codes and data) are coherently derived from the same onboard frequency source.

Workspace.Name: AlgorithmReference_GPS_L5_Source_and_RF_TX
Workspace.Description:
GPS L5 Source

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

GPS navigation (NAV) applications have data coding requirements defined in the interface specification IS-GPS-705(IRN-705-003), "Navstar GPS Space Segment/User Segment L5 Interfaces, ARINC Engineering Services, LLC, El Segundo,California, September 22, 2005.".  This example is to generate L5 XA code, L5 XIi code, L5 XQiCode and the fully coded L5 source.

 

1. "GPS L5 Code"

This design generates the L5 XA code, L5 XIi code and L5 XQi code for GPS L5 source.

The natural 8191 chips of the XA sequence is shortened to 8190 chips to cause precession of the second XA sequence with respect to the natural 8191 chip XB sequence, as shown in Figure 3-6. Re-initialization of the XA shift register produces a 10230-chip sequence by omitting the last 6151 chips of the second natural XA sequence, or reinitializing to all 1s at the 1 ms epoch. The XB shift
register is simply allowed to run its natural course until the next 1 ms epoch when it is reinitialized at its initial state, B0, based upon PRN number and phase.
This results in the phase of the XB sequence leading by one chip during the second XA sequence in the 1-millisecond period. Depending upon the initial state of the XB sequence, a third 8191-chip sequence may be started before the 10230-chip sequence is completed.

 

Each I5i(t) pattern (I5-code) and Q5i(t) pattern (Q5-code) are the modulo-2 sum of two extended patterns clocked at 10.23 Mbps (XA and XBIi or XBQi). XA is an 8190 length code, with an initial condition of all 1s, that is short cycled 1-chip before its natural conclusion and restarted to run over a period of 1millisecond (synchronized with the L1 frequency C/A-code) for a total of 10,230 chips. The XBIi and XBQi, with initial conditions indicated in Table 3-I, are 8191 length codes that are not short cycled. They are restarted at their natural completion and run over a period of 1 millisecond (synchronized with the XA code) for a total of 10,230 chips.

2. "GPS L5 RF TX"

This design generate fully coded L5 source by using L5 XA code, L5 XIi code and XQi codewith an RF transmission design. 

 

The L5 signal is contained within a 24 MHz band centered about the L5 nominal frequency. The carrier frequencies for the L1, L2 and L5 signals shall be coherently derived from a common frequency source within the SV. The nominal frequency of this source -- as it appears to an observer on the ground -- is 10.23 MHz. The SV carrier frequency and clock rates -- as they would appear to an observer located in the SV -- are offset to compensate for relativistic effects. The clock rates are offset by Δ f/f = -4.4647E-10, equivalent to a change in the I5 and Q5-code chipping rate of 10.23 MHz offset by a Δ f = -4.5674E-3 Hz. This is equal to 10.22999999543 MHz. The nominal carrier frequency (f0) -- as it appears to an observer on the ground –shall be 1176.45 MHz, or 115 times 10.23 MHz.

 

The two L5 carrier components modulated by the two separate bit trains (I5-code plus data and Q5-code with no data) shall be in phase quadrature (within ±100 milliradians) with the Q5 signal carrier lagging the I5 signal by 90 degrees. Referring to the phase of the I5 carrier when I5i(t) equals zero as the "zero phase angle", the I5 and Q5-code generator output shall control the respective signal phases in the following manner: when I5i(t) equals one, a 180-degree phase reversal of the I5-carrier occurs; when Q5i(t) equals one, the Q5 carrier advances 90 degrees; when the Q5i(t) equals zero, the Q5 carrier shall be retarded 90 degrees (such that when Q5i(t) changes state, a 180-degree phase reversal of the Q5 carrier occurs). The resultant nominal composite transmitted signal phases as a function of the binary state of the modulating signals are as shown in Table 3-II.

 

Nominal Composite  L5 Signal Phase            I5                 Q5
                               0°                                          0                    0
                            -90°                                         1                     0
                           +90°                                         0                     1
                           180°                                         1                     1

Workspace.Name: GNSS_BOC1_AcquisitionTracking
Workspace.Description:
GNSS BOC1 Acquisition and Tracking

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Workspace

 

This example demonstrates how to demodulate navigation message by using Acquisition and Tracking model based on Systemvue platform.

 

Acquisition model is used to detect all visible satellites specified in parameter SatelliteList. For each satellite, a C/A code replica with stepping frequency carrier is generated to correlate the input signal. If the correlation peak is larger than threshold, C/A code is wiped off from the input signal and FFT (Fast Fourier Transform) operation is applied to estimate fine carrier Doppler frequency. The search process is a two-dimension process.

 

Tracking model is used to track satellites and demodulate navigation message. For a certain channel, the corresponding tracking loop will generate the replica of carrier wave and spreading code of a satellite according to acquisition results of this satellite. During tracking phase, a tracking loop measures tracking errors with which to tune local code and carrier wave to align with the received signal.

 

For acquisition model, data from input ReceiveSignal is baseband signal. Input LockFlagIn(0: unlocked, 1: locked) is locked PRN list from tracking model. It will inform acquisition model which satellites have been locked. Acquisition model will detect the remaining unlocked satellites. Acquisition model will output PRNs of detected satellites and corresponding precise carrier frequency (in Hz, error<25Hz) and code phase (in sample) according to output bus width. For example, if output bus width is 3 and current acquired satellite number is 4, acquisition model will output results of 3 acquired satellites in order of signal strength. If output bus width is 3 and currently acquired satellite number is 2, acquisition model will output 2 acquired satellites results in order of signal strength and 0 will be fulfilled to the remaining ports.

 

For tracking model, the number of tracking channels specified by output bus width may vary from the number of acquisition channels specified by input bus width. Each firing, all tracking channels are checked and idle/unlocked channels are identified. If a new satellite is acquired, it will be assigned to an idle/unlocked tracking channel. Idle/unlocked tracking channels with lower bus index will be used firstly. 

 

In this design, we can set PRN to control which satellite to simulate. By default, SatelliteList are [5,15,26] .

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Workspace

 

This example demonstrates how to demodulate navigation message by using Acquisition and Tracking model based on Systemvue platform.

Acquisition model is used to detect all visible satellites specified in parameter SatelliteList. For each satellite, a C/A code replica with stepping frequency carrier is generated to correlate the input signal. For a certain channel, the corresponding tracking loop will generate the replica of carrier wave and spreading code of a satellite according to acquisition results of this satellite. During tracking phase, a tracking loop measures tracking errors with which to tune local code and carrier wave to align with the received signal.

For acquisition model, data from input ReceiveSignal is baseband signal. Input LockFlagIn(0: unlocked, 1: locked) is locked PRN list from tracking model. It will inform acquisition model which satellites have been locked. Acquisition model will detect the remaining unlocked satellites. Acquisition model will output PRNs of detected satellites and corresponding precise carrier frequency (in Hz, error<25Hz) and code phase (in sample) according to output bus width. For example, if output bus width is 3 and current acquired satellite number is 4, acquisition model will output results of 3 acquired satellites in order of signal strength. If output bus width is 3 and currently acquired satellite number is 2, acquisition model will output 2 acquired satellites results in order of signal strength and 0 will be fulfilled to the remaining ports.

For tracking model, the number of tracking channels specified by output bus width may vary from the number of acquisition channels specified by input bus width. Idle/unlocked tracking channels with lower bus index will be used firstly. 

 

There are 2 folders in this workspace: 

1. GPS CA Scenario

In this design, GPS_CA_ScenarioGen model generates GPS signal. We can set ChannelNum of GPS_CA_ScenarioGen model to control how many satellites we want to simulate. Satellite PRN are [2,5,9,15,26] if we set ChannelNum to 3. By default, SatelliteList are [2,5,9,15,26,28] .

 

2. GPS CA Single Source

In this design, GPS_CA_Source model generates GPS signal. We can set PRN of GPS_CA_Source model to control which satellite we want to simulate. There are 4 options to control doppler information so that we can get 4 types of signal(0:no doppler shift; 1:code doppler shift only; 2:carrier doppler shift only; 3:code doppler shift and carrier doppler shift).

Workspace.Name: GPS_CA_Positioning
Workspace.Description:
GPS CA Positioning

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Workspace

 

This example demonstrates the  typical process of GPS receiver including acquisition, tracking and positioning.

 

In Equation GlobalVars, you can configure the OSR, channel number and positioning number, which affect the positioning time and precision.

 

In Design1, the Receiver trajectory is  calculated in the equation GlobalVars. So it can be replaced by other trajectory. The default trajectory is a circle around Keysight beijing site.

 

After running simulation, you can check the positioning precision in equation errorCalcMoving, the errorRMS shows the precision. And you can find the comparison of reference trajectory and positioning trajectory in Graph RxTraceLLA, Speed  and Acceleration.

Workspace.Name: GPS_CA_Positioning_Rinex
Workspace.Description:
GPS CA Positioning(Rinex)

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Workspace

 

This example demonstrates the  typical process of GPS receiver including acquisition, tracking and positioning.

 

In the scenario, the rinex ephemeris file is used. In this case, the almanac file and ionosphere parameters are ignored. Now, only the navigation message rinex file (*.xxn) is supported. The rinex file always records the ephemeris parameters in one day. So a proper date and time should be set in that day, otherwise an error is reported.

 

And the receiver hasn't supported rinex now, so the positioning model should use the AutoDetect mode.

 

In Equation GlobalVars, you can configure the OSR, channel number and positioning number, which affect the positioning time and precision.

 

In Design1, the Receiver trajectory is  calculated in the equation GlobalVars. So it can be replaced by other trajectory. The default trajectory is a circle around Keysight beijing site.

 

After running simulation, you can check the positioning precision in equation errorCalcMoving, the errorRMS shows the precision. And you can find the comparison of reference trajectory and positioning trajectory in Graph RxTraceLLA, Speed  and Acceleration.

Workspace.Name: GPS_CA_Scenario_N5182B
Workspace.Description:
GPS C/A Scenario Instrument Connection example

 

This example illustrates how to download GPS scenario waveform with user defined receiver trace.

 

SignalDownloader_E4438C is used to download waveform into instrument, so this example can support N5182B. Note that N5182B BBG memory size should be at least 500MSa to play the 240s scenario waveform (2x oversampling).

 

The user should get the IP address of N5182B and set it to the model, and then wait about 35 minutes for the case in the example . After downloading, user should check if the frequency and power of N5182B are consistent with expectation.

 

Note that the waveform downloaded into instrument is repeatedly played. So in this example , after 240s, the signal from N5182B would not valid for receivers. User can reset the waveform to get it played from begining by set the trigger type of N5182B to Reset & Run.

Workspace.Description:
GPS C/A Scenario Waveform example

 

This example analyzes the spectrum and Complementary Cumulative Distribution Function (CCDF) of the GPS signal received at the Rx antenna.

 

Users may change variables in the GlobalVars Equation to see the spectrum/CCDF with different parameters.

 

Users may also save the baseband I/Q data to files or download it to Keysight N5182B signal generation instrument for receiver verification.

Workspace.Name: GPS_CNR_Estimation
Workspace.Description:
GPS CNR Estimation example

 

This example shows how to estimate CNR. In this example, two sources are included:

1.     Single satellite generator

This model generates GPS single satellite signal with user-defined Doppler option. Users can specify almanac file, date and time of the starting point of output signal, satellite ID, and if Doppler effects are added by setting different parameters. In addition, DopplerOption enable users to do receiving algorithm investigation with flexible signal construction.

2.     Scenario generator

This model simulates the GPS scenario with specified receiver trace and almanac file and generates baseband signals that should be received by GPS receivers.

 

In this example, if consider noise density is -174dBm by default, users can set different signal power in oscillator according to different CNR.

 

In CNR Estimation model, the peak value of correlation result is used to calculate signal power. After removing two chips around the peak value in correlation result, the left is used to calculate noise average. By configuring different parameters settings, users can specify:

1.     The number of frequency bins and frequency step in signal search

2.     Threshold for PAR

3.     Coherent accumulation time to achieve different signal sensitivity

4.     Which satellite to search

5.     Whether to print log, users can set threshold according to PAR value in log

 

Note that after removing two chips around the peak value in correlation result, the left include other satellites signal.
