Workspace.Name: GPS_SatellitesSelection
Workspace.Description:
GPS SatellitesSelection example

 

This example shows the satellites selection process. Four models are included:

1. GPS_TrajectoryGen : User can generate a trajectory. In this example, it is used to generate a fix position on which user watches the sky.

2. GPS_CoordinateTransform: It is used to transfer the (Latitude,Longitude,Altitude) to ECEF(x,y,z) which is the format for trajectory input of GPS_SatelliteSelection model.

3. GPS_SatPosCalc: Given the time and almanac(The ephemeris is not availiable now ,so pls leave it blank), it generates the postions of 32 GPS satellites in the form of ECEF(x,y,z).

4. GPS_SatelliteSelection : This model is used to select the satellites which have elevation angles larger than mask(defaultly, it is 5 degree).

 

In this example, 16 satellites are selected in 16 channels. The PRNs in first 8 channels are displayed. Also, the sky view of 8 satellites with the highest elevation angles in user's postion is displayed. 

Users may change the postion in GPS_TrajectoryGen to see different view from differenr position. Users may also change the simulation time and satellites number  in parameters tab.

 

In SatPosSkyView figure, the satellites with elevation angles less than 0 degree are regarded as invisible. So they are displayed in the edge of the circle. In equation1, User can modify numSatellitesDisplay which controls the displayed satellites in figure SatPosSkyView.

 

In PRNvsChannel figure, the PRNs in each channel are displayed. When the satellites is invisible, its PRN is artificially modified to a negative value.

Workspace.Name: 3GPP_LTE_CFR_EVM
Workspace.Description:
Crest Factor Reduction for 3GPP LTE DL Source

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Workspace

 

This example illustrates the usage of crest factor reduction for 3GPP LTE Downlink OFDMA signal using Keysight SystemVue.   The blocks used in this example are all from the standard "Algorithm" library within SystemVue. Where a standard algorithmic model was not sufficient, SystemVue's MATLAB Script model interface was used. To see the underlying MATLAB Script algorithm for these blcoks simply double click on the part symbol to see the source code.

 

Crest factor reduction (CFR) is a technique for reducing the peak-to average ratio (PAR) of an orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) waveform. The algoithm used is based on a modified version of the algorithm in "Constrained Clipping for Crest Factor Reduction in Multiple-user OFDM", In Proc. IEEE Radio and Wireless Symposium, pp.341-344, Jan. 2007.  This CFR algorithm consists of one IFFT, time domain polar clipping, in-band and out-of-band post-processing and one FFT. 

 

In this workspace, 3GPP LTE downlink OFDMA signal just works on 10MHz bandwidth and the oversampling ratio is 4. It does not support other bandwidths (such as 1.4, 3, 5, 15 and 20 MHz).

 

LTE_DL_TxSpectrum just measures CCDF and spectrum without CFR.

LTE_DL_Clipping has time domain clipping and measures  CCDF and spectrum.

LTE_DL_CFR_EVM implements CFR algorithm and measure CCDF, spectrum and EVM.

To save and display the spectrum data, please re-run these 3 designs and set the Data Persistence active in their Analysis.

LTE_DL_CFR_BER measures BER/FER with CFR algorithm.

 

In sub-network LTE_DL_Src_CFR, there are two MATLAB Script blocks (M1 and M2). M1 is for time domain clipping, its parameter threshold is the maximum permssible amplitude. M2 is for in-band and out-of-band post-processing, its parameter EVM_Th is the EVM threshold. Customers can modify both threshold of M1 and EVM_Th of M2.

 

To save and display the spectrum data, please re-run

Workspace.Name: 3GPP_LTE_ControlInfo_ChannelCoding
Workspace.Description:
3GPP_LTE_ControlInfo_ChannelCoding

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This example workspace demonstrates the 3GPP LTE Downlink/Uplink Control Infomation Channel coding, channel decoding and swept BER vs SNR measurements. There are five folders in this workspace:

  • Uplink control information on PUCCH: provides the swept BER VS SNR measurements on PUCCH
  • Uplink control information on PUSCH: provides the swept BER VS SNR measurements on PUSCH
  • Downlink PBCH: provides the swept BER VS SNR measurements on PBCH
  • Downlink PDCCH: provides the swept BER VS SNR measurements on PDCCH

Swept BER VS SNR Simulation Instruction

To enable the swept BER VS SNR simulation, the following settings must be met.

1.       set the 'SNR' parameter to tunable to sweep the parameter. 

2.       Use the 'BER' part to measure the simulated BER. Note that the two input ports should come from the data outputs of Channel decoder parts and Control Info Bits parts.

 

Simulation Control Instruction

1.       To get stable BER performance, the "Data Flow Analysis -> Options -> Repeatable Random Sequences" option is selected to get the fixed noise. With fixed noise, the waterfall BER curve could be gotten even when the simulation frame length is not long.

2.       To enable random noise, deactivate the "Data Flow Analysis -> Options -> Repeatable Random Sequences" option.

3.       The default setting is that the "Data Flow Analysis -> Options -> Repeatable Random Sequences" option is selected in this workspace.

  • Downlink PCFICH: provides the comparison of CFIs before encoding and after decoding 
  • Downlink PHICH: provides the comparison of HIs before encoding and after decoding 

 Comparison Simulation Instruction

1.       Set the parameter (CFI or HI) in Equation below the Graph folder. 

2.       Compare the output of decoder parts and the parameter.

Workspace.Name: 3GPP_LTE_DL_ChannelCoding
Workspace.Description:
3GPP_LTE_DL_ChannelCoding

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This example workspace demonstrates the 3GPP LTE Downlink Channel coding, channel decoding and swept Throughput vs SNR measurements. There are three folders in this workspace:

  • LTE_DL_Throughput: provides the swept Throughput VS SNR measurements

Swept Throughput VS SNR Simulation Instruction

To enable the swept closed-loop HARQ throughout VS SNR simulation, the following settings must be met.

  1. Set the 'NumHARQ' parameter to specify the number of HARQ processes.
  2. Set the 'MaxHARQTrans' parameter to specify maximum number of HARQ transmission; The 'RV_Sequence' parameter specifies the redundancy version coding sequence whose array size should be equal to the 'MaxHARQTrans' parameter.
  3. set the 'SNR' parameter to tunable to sweep the parameter. 
  4. Connect the 'HARQ_Bits' port in the crc-decoder back to the 'HARQ_Bits' port in the HARQ_Controller. Note that a Delay part (with the delay of NumHARQ) is placed between these two 'HARQ_Bits' ports in the crc-decoder and the HARQ_Controller.
  5. Use the 'LTE_Throughput' part to measure the simulated throughput. Note that the two input ports should come from the crc-decoder corresponding output ports.

 

Simulation Control Instruction

 

1. To get stable BER performance, the "Data Flow Analysis -> Options -> Repeatable Random Sequences" option is selected to get the fixed noise. With fixed noise, the waterfall BER curve could be gotten even when the simulation frame length is not long.
2. To enable random noise, deactivate the "Data Flow Analysis -> Options -> Repeatable Random Sequences" option.

3. The default setting is that the "Data Flow Analysis -> Options -> Repeatable Random Sequences" option is selected for LTE_DL_ChannelCoding_Throughput in this workspace.

 
  • LTE_DL_Channel_Coding: provides the flattened channel coding procedure for downlink
  • LTE_DL_Channel_Decoding: provides the flattened channel decoding procedure for downlink

Workspace.Name: 3GPP_LTE_DL_MIMO_Throughput
Workspace.Description:
3GPP_LTE_DL_MIMO_Throughput

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This example workspace demonstrates swept Thoughput vs SNR measurements for LTE downlink in a fading environment. Three configurations are tested: a 2x2 (MIMO Transmit Diversity), a 1x2 (SIMO) and 2x2 (MIMO Closed-loop Spatial Multiplexing)

 

As can be observed in the graphs the performance of the 2x2 (MIMO Transmit Diverity) system is better compared to the 1x2 (SIMO) one, and the performance of 2x2 (MIMO Closed-loop Spatial Multiplexing) is the worst.

 

Closed-loop HARQ Simulation Instruction

To enable the closed-loop HARQ simulation for UE1, the following settings must be met.

  1. Set the 'UE1_HARQ_Enable' parameter in LTE top-level sources and receivers to YES.
  2. Set the 'UE1_NumHARQ' parameter to specify the number of HARQ processes.
  3. Set the 'UE1_MaxHARQTrans' parameter to specify maximum number of HARQ transmission; The 'UE1_RV_Sequence' parameter specifies the redundancy version coding sequence whose array size should be equal to the 'UE1_MaxHARQTrans' parameter.
  4. Set the 'ReceiverDelay' parameter in LTE top-level receivers to 'one subframe delay (1ms)', which means one subframe is delayed in the receivers.
  5. Connect the 'UE1_HARQ_Bits' port in the receiver back to the 'UE1_HARQ_Bits' port in the source. Note that a Delay part (with the delay of (UE1_NumHARQ-1)) is placed between these two 'UE1_HARQ_Bits' ports in the receiver and the source.
  6. Use the 'LTE_Throughput' part to measure the simulated throughput. Note that the two input ports should come from the receiver corresponding output ports, and the measurement should at least begin with the second subframe (i.e. set SubframeStart >=1).

Simulation Control Instruction

 

1. To get stable BER performance, the "Data Flow Analysis -> Options -> Repeatable Random Sequences" option is selected to get the fixed noise. With fixed noise, the waterfall BER curve could be gotten even when the simulation frame length is not long.
2. To enable random noise, deactivate the "Data Flow Analysis -> Options -> Repeatable Random Sequences" option.

3. The default setting is that the "Data Flow Analysis -> Options -> Repeatable Random Sequences" option is selected for all desgins in this workspace.

Workspace.Name: 3GPP_LTE_DL_SISO_BER
Workspace.Description:
3GPP_LTE_DL_SISO_BER

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This example workspace demonstrates swept BER and BLER vs SNR measurements for an LTE downlink SISO system. Two environments are tested: AWGN (Additive White Gaussian Noise) and fading.

 

 

Non-HARQ Simulation Instruction

To enable the non-HARQ simulation for UE1, the following settings must be met.

  1. Set the 'UE1_HARQ_Enable' parameter in LTE top-level sources and receivers to NO. Ignore the  'UE1_NumHARQ'  and 'UE1_MaxHARQTrans' parameters
  2. The first value in the 'UE1_RV_Sequence' parameter (i.e. UE1_RV_Sequence(1)) is read as the redundancy version coding index.
  3. Set the 'ReceiverDelay' parameter in LTE top-level receivers to 'one frame delay (10ms)', which means one frame is delayed in the receivers.
  4. Leave the 'HARQ_Bits' port in sources unconnected.
  5. Use the 'LTE_BER_FER'' part to measure the simulated BER/FER. Note that the input port to the 'Ref' part should not come from the source that is sent to the LTE source because of platform limit, and the measurement should at least begin with the second frame (i.e. set FrameStart >=1).

 

Simulation Control Instruction

 

1. To get stable BER performance, the "Data Flow Analysis -> Options -> Repeatable Random Sequences" option is selected to get the fixed noise. With fixed noise, the waterfall BER curve could be gotten even when the simulation frame length is not long.
2. To enable random noise, deactivate the "Data Flow Analysis -> Options -> Repeatable Random Sequences" option.

3. The default setting is that the "Data Flow Analysis -> Options -> Repeatable Random Sequences" option is selected for all desgins in this workspace.

 

Simulation Time

 

LTE_FDD_DL_AWGN_BER: About 2 minutes each simulation point in the machine with Intel Xeon 2.0GHz, 4G RAM, Windows XP system.

LTE_FDD_DL_Fading_BER: About 12 minutes each simulation point in the machine with Intel Xeon 2.0GHz, 4G RAM, Windows XP system.

 

To reproduce the reference dataset, please double click LTE_FDD_DL_AWGN_BER_Analysis, select configuration Ideal_Sync, then run AWGN_BER.

  • LTE DL 2Ant Src Tx Measurements: provides spectrum and CCDF measurements for a 2 antenna system.
  • LTE DL 4Ant Src Tx Measurements: provides spectrum and CCDF measurements for a 4 antenna system.

Workspace.Name: 3GPP_LTE_DL_TxEVM
Workspace.Description:
3GPP_LTE_DL_TxEVM

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This example workspace demonstrates EVM measurements for an LTE downlink transmitter with different transmit antennas. There are 2 folders in this workspace:

  • LTE DL EVM Measurement1: provides EVM measurements for a 1 antenna system.
  • LTE DL EVM Measurement2: provides EVM measurements for a 2 antenna system.
The available results from these measurements including:

  • The information about the quality of the signal being analyzed , such as EVM, EVMPk, DataEVM, SyncCorr and so on.

  • Separate measurements and display for user channels and signals: P-SS, S-SS, PBCH, PCFICH, PHICH, PDCCH and PDSCH.

  • Constellation for all channels (re-run to display these data).

  • Normalized equalizer channel frequency response over subcarriers.

  • RB Error Mag Spectrum shows the EVM of each resource block (RB) in the selected layer. 

  • Measured MIMO Information in MIMO case.

 
The EVM model support 1, 2 and 4 transmit antennas system measurement. The algorithm that performs the synchronization, demodulation and EVM analysis in the EVM model is the same as the one used in Keysight 89600 VSA. 
 
 
NOTE: For visibility of graph Constellation and RBErrorMagSpectrum, SaveConstelltion setup for EVM model should be YES. Otherwise errors might be seen in Error Window due to unavailability of the data to be plotted in these graphs. The workspace and EVM measurements, however, will still be working.

Workspace.Name: 3GPP_LTE_SignalDownload
Workspace.Description:
3GPP_LTE_SignalDownload

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This example workspace demonstrates how to download LTE signal generated by LTE sources in SystemVue LTE library to Keysight signal generators such as E4438C. The phase discontinuity between every two consecutive frames is eliminated. There are two top level designs in this workspace:

  • Download LTE downlink signal: LTE_DL_SignalDownload
  • Download LTE uplink signal: LTE_UL_SignalDownload

It should be noted that only RRC and Ideal Lowpass FIR filters are supported in this example. The LTE_DL_Src and LTE_UL_Src are modified to eliminate the phase discontinuity in the frame boundary in this workspace. Please do NOT remove the LTE_DL_Src and LTE_UL_Src model designs in this example.

 

Download Instructions

  1. Configure the LTE source parameters such as Bandwidth, OversamplingOption and RB_Alloc.
  2. Set the downloading configurations such as FCarrier and address of the instrument.
  3. Specify the number of frames to download by setting the parameter NumFrames.
  4. Make sure the computer is connected with the instrument and run the analysis.

Workspace.Name: 3GPP_LTE_UL_BER
Workspace.Description:
3GPP_LTE_UL_BER

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This example workspace demonstrates BER and BLER vs SNR measurements for an LTE uplink system in both AWGN (Additive White Gaussian Noise) and fading channel.

 

It should be noted that ideal frequency and timing synchronization was employed to get the reference simulation datasets (LTE_FDD_UL_AWGN_QPSK and LTE_TDD_UL_AWGN_16QAM, LTE_FDD_UL_AWGN_64QAM) in AWGN channel.

 

To use ideal frequency and timing synchronization in AWGN channel, users can open the LTE_UL_Receiver model, find LTE_UL_TimeFreqSync model, set UseDesiredValue to 1:YES, then set DesiredDelay and DesiredFreq to the ideal timing index and frequency offset. For the default parameter configurations in this example, users can set DesiredDelay to 6 and DesiredFreq to 0.

 

 

Simulation Control Instruction

 

1. To get stable BER performance, the "Data Flow Analysis -> Options -> Repeatable Random Sequences" option is selected to get the fixed noise. With fixed noise, the waterfall BER curve could be gotten even when the simulation frame length is not long.
2. To enable random noise, deactivate the "Data Flow Analysis -> Options -> Repeatable Random Sequences" option.

3. The default setting is that the "Data Flow Analysis -> Options -> Repeatable Random Sequences" option is selected for all desgins in this workspace.

 

Simulation Time

 

1. LTE_FDD_UL_AWGN_BER: about 30 minutes for each simulation point in the machine with Intel Xeon 2.0GHz, 4G RAM, Windows XP system.

2. LTE_TDD_UL_AWGN_BER: about 50 minutes for each simulation point in the machine with Intel Xeon 2.0GHz, 4G RAM, Windows XP system.

3. LTE_FDD_UL_Fading_BER: about 2 hours for each simulation point in the machine with Intel Xeon 2.0GHz, 4G RAM, Windows XP system.

Workspace.Name: 3GPP_LTE_UL_ChannelCoding
Workspace.Description:
3GPP_LTE_UL_ChannelCoding

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This example workspace demonstrates the 3GPP LTE Uplink FDD Channel coding, channel decoding and swept BER and BLER vs SNR measurements. There are three folders in this workspace:

  • LTE_UL_BER: provides the swept BER and BLER VS SNR measurements(QPSK, 1/3 coding rate)

UL Channel coding BER Simulation Instruction

The HARQ transmission is not included in the uplink channel coding BER simulation. The number of raw bits is specified by 'TransblockSize'. The number of available modulation symbols is not calculated by Resource Block allocation, it is specified by 'NumChBits' directly. To enable the BER simulation for uplink channel coding, the following settings must be met.

  1. Set the Payload_Config' parameter in the design to 'TransblockSize', the parameter 'ChBit_Config' to 'Channel bit size'.
  2. The parameter 'NumHARQ' and 'MaxHARQTrans' are ineffective.
  3. Set the 'SubframeIgnored' parameter in LTE RateDematch to '0', which means no delay.
  4. Set the parameter SNR to tunable to sweep it.
  5. Use the 'BER_FER' part to measure the simulated BER.Note that the input port to the 'Ref' part should not come from the source that is sent to the LTE encoder because of platform limit.

 

Simulation Control Instruction

 

1. To get stable BER performance, the "Data Flow Analysis -> Options -> Repeatable Random Sequences" option is selected to get the fixed noise. With fixed noise, the waterfall BER curve could be gotten even when the simulation frame length is not long.
2. To enable random noise, deactivate the "Data Flow Analysis -> Options -> Repeatable Random Sequences" option.

3. The default setting is that the "Data Flow Analysis -> Options -> Repeatable Random Sequences" option is selected for LTE_UL_ChannelCoding_BER in this workspace.

 

  • LTE_UL_Channel_Coding: provides the flattened channel coding procedure for uplink

The intermediate channel coding result are printed to files.

  • LTE_UL_Channel_Decoding: provides the flattened channel decoding procedure for uplink

UL Channel Decoding simulation instruction:

    1. The input sequence is got from the simulation result of LTE_UL_ChannelCoding.dsn. The parameters should be set to the same as in the LTE_UL_Channel_Coding.dsn.
    2. CRC_Check equals to '1' means CRC check succeed, CRC_Check equals to '0' means CRC check failed.
    3.  The intermediate channel decoding result are printed to files.
  • It should be noted that when ChBit_Config is selected as 'Channel bit size', uplink control information (RI, HARQ-ACK, CQI) would not be transmitted. Hence, in this case, RI_NumInfoBits, HARQACK_NumInfoBits and CQI_NumInfoBits should be set to [0].
  • When PUSCH_TransMode is selected as 'Control Only', ChBit_Config should be set to 'REs Per Subframe', at the same time, CQI_NumInfoBits should not be set to '0' as the number of CQI coded symbols is always not 0 in this case according to the specifications.

Workspace.Name: 3GPP_LTE_UL_SISO_Throughput
Workspace.Description:
3GPP_LTE_UL_SISO_Throughput

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This example workspace demonstrates Throughput vs SNR measurements for an LTE uplink system in AWGN (Additive White Gaussian Noise) channel with SISO.

 

In AWGN_HARQ folder, closed-loop HARQ transmission is enabled. While in AWGN_NoHARQ folder, there is no HARQ retransmission.

 

Closed-loop HARQ Simulation Instruction

To enable the closed-loop HARQ simulation, the following settings must be met.

  1. Set the 'HARQ_Enable' parameter in LTE top-level sources and receivers to YES. In this example workspace, users can just set the HARQ_Enable in the Parameters Tab.
  2. Set the 'NumHARQ' parameter to specify the number of HARQ processes.
  3. Set the 'MaxHARQTrans' parameter to specify maximum number of HARQ transmission; The 'RV_Sequence' parameter specifies the redundancy version coding sequence whose array size should be equal to the 'MaxHARQTrans' parameter.
  4. Set the 'ReceiverDelay' parameter in LTE top-level receivers to 'one subframe delay (1ms)', which means one subframe is delayed in the receivers.
  5. Connect the 'HARQ_Bits' port in the receiver back to the 'HARQ_Bits' port in the source. Note that a Delay part (with the delay of (NumHARQ-1) is placed between these two 'HARQ_Bits' ports in the receiver and the source.
  6. Use the 'LTE_Throughput' part to measure the simulated throughput. Note that the two input ports should come from the corresponding receiver output ports, and the measurement should at least begin with the second subframe (i.e. set SubframeStart >=1).
  7. FIR Filter in the top-level source is not supported in HARQ simulation in current implementation. Hence, SpectrumShapingType must be selected as 0:TimeWindowing.

It should be noted that real frequency and timing synchronization was employed to get the reference simulation datasets LTE_FDD_UL_AWGN_QPSK_HARQ, LTE_TDD_UL_AWGN_16QAM_HARQ and LTE_FDD_UL_AWGN_64QAM_HARQ in AWGN channel, while ideal frequency and timing synchronization was employed to get the reference simulation datasets LTE_FDD_UL_AWGN_QPSK_NoHARQ, LTE_TDD_UL_AWGN_16QAM_NoHARQ, LTE_FDD_UL_AWGN_64QAM_NoHARQ in AWGN channel.

 

To use ideal frequency and timing synchronization in AWGN channel, users can open the LTE_UL_Receiver model, find LTE_UL_TimeFreqSync model, set UseDesiredValue to 1:YES, then set DesiredDelay and DesiredFreq to the ideal timing index and frequency offset. For the default parameter configurations in this example, users can set DesiredDelay to 6 (where 6 is the delay of signal source) and DesiredFreq to 0.

 

Simulation Control Instruction

 

1. To get stable BER performance, the "Data Flow Analysis -> Options -> Repeatable Random Sequences" option is selected to get the fixed noise. With fixed noise, the waterfall BER curve could be gotten even when the simulation frame length is not long.
2. To enable random noise, deactivate the "Data Flow Analysis -> Options -> Repeatable Random Sequences" option.

3. The default setting is that the "Data Flow Analysis -> Options -> Repeatable Random Sequences" option is selected for all desgins in this workspace.

 

Simulation Time

 

1. LTE_FDD_UL_AWGN_Throughput_HARQ: about 20 minutes for each simulation point in the machine with Intel Xeon 2.0GHz, 4G RAM, Windows XP system.

2. LTE_TDD_UL_AWGN_Throughput_HARQ: about 36 minutes for each simulation point in the machine with Intel Xeon 2.0GHz, 4G RAM, Windows XP system.

3. LTE_FDD_UL_AWGN_Throughput_NoHARQ: about 20 minutes for each simulation point in the machine with Intel Xeon 2.0GHz, 4G RAM, Windows XP system.

4. LTE_TDD_UL_AWGN_Throughput_NoHARQ: about 36 minutes for each simulation point in the machine with Intel Xeon 2.0GHz, 4G RAM, Windows XP system.

3GPP_LTE_UL_TX

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This example workspace demonstrates a spectrum and a CCDF measurement of an LTE uplink transmitter.

 

The spectrum measurement is performed using the SpectrumAnalyzer part. The resulting spectrum is shown in the LTE_UL_Tx_Spectrum Measurements graph.

 

The CCDF measurement is performed using the CCDF part. The resulting CCDF curve is shown in the LTE_UL_Tx_CCDF_Measurements graph. A reference curve (CCDF of white gaussian noise) is also plotted on this graph.

 

This example also connects the LTE uplink transmitter with 89600 VSA software (needs to be installed separately). The compatible version of VSA software is Version 11.00.

3GPP_LTE_UL_TxEVM

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This example workspace demonstrates EVM measurements for an LTE uplink transmitter with different signal format. There are 2 folders in this workspace:

  • LTE UL EVM Measurement1: provides EVM measurement for uplink signal with PUCCH, PUSCH and SRS.
  • LTE UL EVM Measurement2: provides EVM measurement for uplink signal with PRACH.
The available results from these measurements including:

  • The information about the quality of the signal being analyzed , such as EVM, EVMPk, DataEVM, SyncCorr and so on.

  • RB Error Mag Spectrum shows the EVM of each resource block (RB). 

The algorithm that performs the synchronization, demodulation and EVM analysis in the EVM model is the same as the one used in Keysight 89600 VSA.

Workspace.Name: LTE_Advanced_DL_AMC
Workspace.Description:
LTE_A_DL_AMC

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

Note: This example is for LTE Advanced library (version 2014.05) based on SystemVue 2013.08SP1.

This example workspace demonstrates swept throughput vs SNR measurements for LTE-Advanced downlink SISO and MIMO channel.

 

Simulation Control Instruction of Design "LTE_A_DL_SISO_THROUGHPUT"

 

This design demonstrates swept throughput vs SNR measurements for LTE-Advanced downlink SISO channel in an AWGN environment.

 

Besides HARQ-ACK bits, the UE (LTE_A_DL_Rcv) will also report the CQI to BS(LTE_A_DL_Src). The UE will generate CQI index according to the SNR value. The SNR-to-CQI mapping table is defined by the parameter SNRToCQI and the formulas below : 

        CQI = 0,   when SNR<SNRToCQI(0);

        CQI = n,   when SNRToCQI(n-1)<=SNR<SNRToCQI(n), 1<=n<=14;

        CQI = 15, when SNR>=SNRToCQI(14).

SNRToCQI must be an array with 15 elements in ascending order. The SNR value is either user-defined or estimated automatically which is determined by parameter SNREstimatorMode. If SNREstimatorMode is set to "Ideal", the SNR value needs to be specified manually in the parameters page. If SNREstimatorMode is set to "BasedOnPSS", the SNR value will be automatically calculated based on PSS and smoothed by a filter. SNRFilterAlpha defines the coefficient of the smoothing filter.

The BS will choose corresponding MCS according to the CQI feedback and the 16-element array parameter CQIToMCS.

 

To get throughput performance with certain MCS or AMC, please run the analysis "LTE_A_DL_SISO_THROUGHPUT_Analysis". If UE1_AMC_Enable is set to YES, AMC simulation will be running, or fixed MCS simulation will be running.

 

To compare throughput performance with different MCS and AMC, please run the equation "LTE_A_DL_SISO_THROUGHPUT_Sweep". It will cost quite a long time to run all simulations with different MCS and AMC sequentially. The swept result is stored in dataset "LTE_A_DL_SISO_Throughput_Sweep_Data" and showed in graph "LTE_A_DL_SISO_THROUGHPUT_Graph". Please note that some parameters will use the value defined in the equation instead of that in the parameters page when running the swept simulation.

 

Simulation Control Instruction of Design "LTE_A_DL_MIMO_THROUGHPUT"

 

This design demonstrates open loop throughput measurements for LTE Advanced downlink 2x2 system with Spatial Multiplexing in a fading environment.

 

The parameter settings are similar with design LTE_A_DL_SISO_THROUGHPUT.

 

To get throughput performance with certain MCS or AMC, please run the analysis "LTE_A_DL_MIMO_THROUGHPUT_Analysis". If AMC_Enable is set to YES, AMC simulation will be running, or fixed MCS simulation will be running.


To compare throughput performance with different MCS and AMC, please run the equation "LTE_A_DL_MIMO_THROUGHPUT_Sweep". It will cost quite a long time to run all simulations with different MCS and AMC sequentially. The swept result is stored in dataset "LTE_A_DL_MIMO_Throughput_Sweep_Data" and showed in graphs "LTE_A_DL_MIMO_THROUGHPUT_CW1_Graph". Please note that some parameters will use the value defined in the equation instead of that in the parameters page when running the swept simulation.

Workspace.Description:
LTE-Advanced Downlink Carrier Aggregation Generation

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Workspace

 

This example is to generate LTE-Advanced downlink signals with carrier aggregation.

 

The frequency band(center frequency),  bandwidth of the component carrier, oversampling ratio and the number of Tx antennas can be chagned in the parameter tab.

2x20MHz_CCs_40MHz

This folder includes schematic to generate 40MHz LTE-Advanced carrier aggregation (two 20MHz component carriers). Enable the  SignalDownloader_E4438C model and it can be used to download the 40MHz LTE-A DL signal into Keysight ESG/MXG.

3x20MHz_CCs_60MHz

This folder includes schematic to generate 60MHz LTE-Advanced carrier aggregation (three 20MHz component carriers). Enable the SignalDownloader_E4438C model and it can be used to download the 40MHz LTE-A DL signal into Keysight ESG/MXG.

 

4x20MHz_CCs_80MHz

This folder includes schematic to generate 80MHz LTE-Advanced carrier aggregation (four 20MHz component carriers). Enable the SignalDownloader_E4438C model and it can be used to download the 40MHz LTE-A DL signal into Keysight ESG/MXG. The default oversampling ratio is 3. The maximum sampling rate of ESG/MXG is 100MHz, The sampling rate of 80MHz LTE CA signal with 3x upsampling is 30.72MHzx3=92.16MHz.

5x20MHz_CCs_100MHz

This folder includes schematic to generate 100MHz LTE-Advanced carrier aggregation (five 20MHz component carriers). The default upsampling ratio is 4. The maximum sampling rate of ESG/MXG is 100MHz, The sampling rate of 100MHz LTE CA signal with 4x oversampling is 30.72MHzx4=122.88MHz. This 100MHz LTE-A CA signal (upsampling ratio =4) can be downloaded into MXG.

Workspace.Name: LTE_Advanced_DL_MIMO_2x2_Throughput
Workspace.Description:
LTE_Advanced_DL_MIMO_2X2_Throughput

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This example workspace demonstrates close loop throughput measurements for LTE Advanced downlink 2x2 system with Spatial Multiplexing in a fading environment.

 

Closed-loop HARQ Simulation Instruction (Folder LTE-A DL MIMO 2X2 SM Fading Throughput)

To enable the closed-loop HARQ simulation for UE1, the following settings must be met.

  1. Set the 'UE1_HARQ_Enable' parameter in LTE-A top-level sources and receivers to YES.
  2. Set the 'UE1_NumHARQ' parameter to specify the number of HARQ processes.
  3. Set the 'UE1_MaxHARQTrans' parameter to specify maximum number of HARQ transmission; The 'UE1_RV_Sequence' parameter specifies the redundancy version coding sequence whose array size should be equal to the 'UE1_MaxHARQTrans' parameter.
  4. Set the 'ReceiverDelay' parameter in LTE top-level receivers to 'one subframe delay (1ms)', which means one subframe is delayed in the receivers.
  5. Connect the 'UE1_HARQ_Bits' port in the receiver back to the 'UE1_HARQ_Bits' port in the source. Note that a Delay part (with the delay of (UE1_NumHARQ-1)) is placed between these two 'UE1_HARQ_Bits' ports in the receiver and the source.
  6. Use the 'LTE_Throughput' part to measure the simulated throughput. Note that the two input ports should come from the receiver corresponding output ports, and the measurement should at least begin with the second subframe (i.e. set SubframeStart >=1).

Closed-loop PMI feedback Simulation Instruction (Folder LTE-A DL MIMO 2x2 CLSM Fading Throughput)

To enable the closed-loop PMI feedback simulation for UE1, the following settings must be met.

  1. Set the 'UE1_CL_Precoding_Enable' parameter to YES.
  2. Set the 'UE1_PMI_Delay' parameter to specify the delay of PMI feedback.
  3. Set the 'ReceiverDelay' parameter in LTE top-level receivers to 'one subframe delay (1ms)', which means one subframe is delayed in the receivers.
  4. Connect the 'UE1_PMI' port in the receiver back to the 'UE1_PMI' port in the source. Note that a Delay part (with the delay of (UE1_PMI_Delay-1)) is placed between these two 'UE1_PMI' ports in the receiver and the source.
  5. Use the 'LTE_Throughput' part to measure the simulated throughput. Note that the two input ports should come from the receiver corresponding output ports, and the measurement should at least begin with the second subframe (i.e. set SubframeStart >=1).

The reference data set is get in EVA channel with 5Hz max Doppler shift. The bandwidth is 10 MHz. 21 RBs are allocated for UE1 PDSCH (Release 10). The mapping tyep is 16QAM. The code rate is 1/2. 5000 subframes are simulated.

Workspace.Name: LTE_Advanced_DL_MIMO_2x2_Throughput_IRC_Receiver
Workspace.Description:
LTE_Advanced_DL_MIMO_2X2_Throughput_IRC_Receiver

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This example workspace demonstrates closed loop throughput measurements for LTE Advanced downlink 2x2 system with Spatial Multiplexing in an interference scenario, where two interfering cells are introduced. Interference Rejection Combing (IRC) receiver is applied in the UE side to suppress the inter-cell interference. The simulation results show that IRC receiver works better than MMSE receiver and ZF receiver in interference scenario, since interference covariance matrix is taken into account in IRC receiver.

 

Closed-loop HARQ Simulation Instruction

To enable the closed-loop HARQ simulation for UE1, the following settings must be met.

  1. Set the 'UE1_HARQ_Enable' parameter in LTE-A top-level sources and receivers to YES.
  2. Set the 'UE1_NumHARQ' parameter to specify the number of HARQ processes.
  3. Set the 'UE1_MaxHARQTrans' parameter to specify maximum number of HARQ transmission; The 'UE1_RV_Sequence' parameter specifies the redundancy version coding sequence whose array size should be equal to the 'UE1_MaxHARQTrans' parameter.
  4. Set the 'ReceiverDelay' parameter in LTE top-level receivers to 'one subframe delay (1ms)', which means one subframe is delayed in the receivers.
  5. Connect the 'UE1_HARQ_Bits' port in the receiver back to the 'UE1_HARQ_Bits' port in the source. Note that a Delay part (with the delay of (UE1_NumHARQ-1)) is placed between these two 'UE1_HARQ_Bits' ports in the receiver and the source.
  6. Use the 'LTE_Throughput' part to measure the simulated throughput. Note that the two input ports should come from the receiver corresponding output ports, and the measurement should at least begin with the second subframe (i.e. set SubframeStart >=1).

Interference Scenario

Most configurations follow Table 8.2.1.4.1B-1 in 3GPP TS 36.101(d21), while some parameters are different:

  1. Payloads are transmitted in each subframe.
  2. The code rate in each subframe is 1/3.
  3. Use 1-layer TM4 instead of TM6
  4. PMI reporting interval is 1 in the simulation

Other Notice

  1. If MMSE-IRC receiver is enabled, the MMSE channel estimation is mandatory.
  2. Channel modelings between each cell to the user are the same, except they are implicitly initialized with different random seeds.
  3. The channel model refers to section B.2 in 3GPP TS 36.101(d21)

Workspace.Name: LTE_Advanced_DL_SISO_BER
Workspace.Description:
LTE_A_DL_SISO_BER

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This example workspace demonstrates open loop BER measurements of LTE-Advanced downlink SISO system in AWGN environment.

 

MMSE channel estimation is employed to get the reference data set. The PSS Ra and SSS Ra are set to 10dB in order to get accurate timing and frequency synchronization in the low SNR AWGN channel. The bandwidth is 5MHz. The mapping type is QPSK. The code rate is 1/3. 1000 frames are simulated. The RB allocation type is selected as RB indices (2D) to avoid the overlap of RB allocation for PDSCH with PSS, SSS and PBCH. 

 

To reproduce the reference dataset, please double click LTE_A_DL_SISO_BER_ Analysis, select configuration Ideal_Sync, then run Sweep_LTE_A_DL_SISO_BER.

 

It should be noted that if there is overlap of PDSCH and PSS, SSS or PBCH. DMRS would not be transmitted on those RBs, then the channel estimation may be inaccurate and the PDSCH on those RBs may not be demodulated correctly.

Workspace.Name: LTE_Advanced_DL_SISO_DPS
Workspace.Description:
LTE_A_DL_SISO_DPS

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

Note: This example is for LTE Advanced library (version 2014.05) based on SystemVue 2013.08SP1.

This example workspace demonstrates dynamic point selection in LTE-Advanced.

 

There are two transmission points (LTE_A_DL_Src) with different cell ID (set in GlobalVars) in the design. The UE (LTE_A_DL_Rcv) receives the combination of the two signals, which are transmitted from two Tx points (TP) and passed through two independent fading channels. Two different configuration of CSI RS are transmitted from two TPs respectively. The resources occupied by CSI RS in one TP is configured to transmit zero power CSI RS in the other TP, i.e. there is no interferece between the CSI RS processes transmitted from two TPs.

At the beginning, data (PDSCH) is transmitted from TP1.The UE then demodulates the received data with cell ID of TP1. At the same time, UE estimates the channel condition of two TPs using CSI RS processes. Based on the channel state, the TP with better channel condition will be selected in future transmission. The delay of the CQI feedback is set by CQI_Delay in GlobalVars.

 

It should be noted that in this example, only SISO is supported.

 

The BER/BLER are shown in the graphs. The performance of DPS and single Tx point are compared, where single Tx point means there is only one transmission point, UE receives signal from this TP without interference. As can be seen from the curves, around 2dB improvement can be got from DPS with default configuration (FDD, 5MHz bandwidth, 25RB allocated)

 

To configure the single TP simulation, please set SimMode to 1, then select configuration as SingleTxPoint in LTE_A_DL_SISO_DPS_Analysis.

Workspace.Name: LTE_Advanced_DL_Tx
Workspace.Description:
LTE_Advanced_DL_TX

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

LTE Advanced DL 8Ant Src Tx Measurements

 

This folder demonstrates spectrum and CCDF measurements for an LTE advanced downlink transmitter with 8 antennas.

 

1. Both release 8 and release 10 are supported in LTE_Advanced DL source. The release version for each UE can be set respectively.

2. In this example, UE1 and UE4 are active. UE1 is configured with 8 Tx antennas following Release 10. UE4 is configured with 2 Tx antennas following Release 8.

 

In this folder, VSA 89600 MIMO sink with 8 antennas is provided. Be sure that 89600 software after 19.0 version is installed . For your convenience, the setup file of VSA 89600 is provided in the same folder.

 

By default, the VSA sink is disabled.

 

LTE Advanced DL 256QAM

 

This folder is to generate LTE-Advanced downlink signals with 256QAM. And the schematic is to generate 40MHz LTE-Advanced carrier aggregation (two 20MHz component carriers).

 

1.VSA 89600 software is connected to do the demodulation.

2.To change the central frequency of CC1 and CC2, change the equations in the Equation Tab.

3.FDD or TDD can be set by FrameMode parameter in Parameter Tab.

4.LTE EVM model is added to calculate the EVM of CC2. Only one component carrier is supported in LTE_DL_EVM model. Please change the paramters of EVM model, if EVM of CC1 is wanted.

 

Notes:

 

1. A new parameter Enable256QAM is added in the LTE-A source (also shown in "Parameter" Tab of each design). To enable 256QAM for R12, set this parameter to Yes.

2. With defalut setting, "MCS Index" is set in UE1_Config, which means the Modulation Order and TB size will be chosen according to this new R12 MCS table below. To enable 256QAM, set UE1_Payload to from 20 to 27. Please refer to 3GPP TS 36.306 V12.5.0 for detail.

3. VSA 20.0 version is needed to support 256QAM demodulation. Make sure Enable Higher Order Modulation in MeasSetup > LTE-Advanced Demod Properties > Advanced(CCx) tab where x specifies the component carrier is enable.

Workspace.Name: LTE_Advanced_PUCCH_Decoding
Workspace.Description:
LTE_Advanced_PUCCH_ChannelCoding

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This example workspace demonstrates the 3GPP LTE Advanced Uplink Control Infomation Channel coding, channel decoding and swept BER vs SNR measurements.

  • Uplink control information on PUCCH: provides the swept BER VS SNR measurements on PUCCH

Swept BER VS SNR Simulation Instruction

To enable the swept BER VS SNR simulation, the following settings must be met.

1.       set the 'SNR' parameter to tunable to sweep the parameter. 

2.       Use the 'BER' part to measure the simulated BER. Note that the two input ports should come from the data outputs of Channel decoder parts and Control Info Bits parts.

 

Simulation Control Instruction

1.       To get stable BER performance, the "Data Flow Analysis -> Options -> Repeatable Random Sequences" option is selected to get the fixed noise. With fixed noise, the waterfall BER curve could be gotten even when the simulation frame length is not long.

2.       To enable random noise, deactivate the "Data Flow Analysis -> Options -> Repeatable Random Sequences" option.

3.       The default setting is that the "Data Flow Analysis -> Options -> Repeatable Random Sequences" option is selected in this workspace.

Workspace.Name: LTE_Advanced_UL_AMC
Workspace.Description:
LTE_A_UL_AMC

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

Note: This example is for LTE Advanced library (version 2014.05) based on SystemVue 2013.08SP1.

Simulation Control Instruction of Design "LTE_A_UL_SISO_THROUGHPUT"

 

 This design demonstrates swept throughput vs SNR measurements for LTE-Advanced uplink SISO in AWGN environment.

 

Besides HARQ-ACK bits, the BS (LTE_A_UL_Rcv) will also report the CQI to UE(LTE_A_UL_Src). The BS will generate CQI index according to the SNR value. The SNR-to-CQI mapping table is defined by the parameter SNRToCQI and the formulas below : 

        CQI = 0,   when SNR<SNRToCQI(0);

        CQI = n,   when SNRToCQI(n-1)<=SNR<SNRToCQI(n), 1<=n<=14;

        CQI = 15, when SNR>=SNRToCQI(14).

SNRToCQI must be an array with 15 elements in ascending order. The SNR value needs to be specified manually in the parameters page.

The UE will choose corresponding MCS according to the CQI feedback and the 16-element array parameter CQIToMCS.

 

To get throughput performance with certain MCS or AMC, please run the analysis "LTE_A_UL_SISO_THROUGHPUT_Analysis". If AMC_Enable is set to YES, AMC simulation will be running, or fixed MCS simulation will be running.

 

To compare throughput performance with different MCS and AMC, please run the equation "LTE_A_UL_SISO_THROUGHPUT_Sweep". It will cost quite a long time to run all simulations with different MCS and AMC sequentially. The swept result is stored in dataset "LTE_A_UL_SISO_Throughput_Sweep_Data" and showed in graph "LTE_A_UL_SISO_THROUGHPUT_Graph". Please note that some parameters will use the value defined in the equation instead of that in the parameters page when running the swept simulation.

Workspace.Name: LTE_Advanced_UL_MIMO_2x2_Throughput
Workspace.Description:
LTE_Advanced_UL_MIMO_2X2_Throughput

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

 

This example workspace demonstrates close loop throughput measurements for LTE Advanced uplink 2x2 with HARQ retransmission in a fading environment.

 

Closed-loop HARQ Simulation Instruction

To enable the closed-loop HARQ simulation for PUSCH, the following settings must be met.

  1. Set the 'HARQ_Enable' parameter in LTE-A top-level sources and receivers to YES.
  2. Set the 'NumHARQ' parameter to specify the number of HARQ processes.
  3. Set the 'MaxHARQTrans' parameter to specify maximum number of HARQ transmission; The 'RV_Sequence' parameter specifies the redundancy version coding sequence whose array size should be equal to the 'MaxHARQTrans' parameter.
  4. Set the 'ReceiverDelay' parameter in LTE-A top-level receivers to 'one subframe delay (1ms)', which means one subframe is delayed in the receivers.
  5. Connect the 'HARQ_Bits' port in the receiver back to the 'HARQ_Bits' port in the source. Note that a Delay part (with the delay of (NumHARQ-1)) is placed between these two 'HARQ_Bits' ports in the receiver and the source.
  6. Use the 'LTE_Throughput' part to measure the simulated throughput. Note that the two input ports should come from the receiver corresponding output ports, and the measurement should at least begin with the second subframe (i.e. set SubframeStart >=1).

The reference data set LTE_A_UL_2x2_InH_QPSK is simulation results for FDD LTE-A uplink 2x2 system. The bandwidth is 5MHz. All 25RBs are allocated for PUSCH. The mapping type is QPSK. The code rate is 1/3. 2000 subframes are simulated in  InH channel with 5Hz max Doppler shift.

The new LTEAdvanced_Channel model from MIMO Channel kits is employed in the simulation.

  2. Set the 'NumHARQ' parameter to specify the number of HARQ processes.

  4. Set the 'ReceiverDelay' parameter in LTE-A top-level receivers to 'one subframe delay (1ms)', which means one subframe is delayed in the receivers.
  5. Connect the 'HARQ_Bits' port in the receiver back to the 'HARQ_Bits' port in the source. Note that a Delay part (with the delay of (NumHARQ-1)) is placed between these two 'HARQ_Bits' ports in the receiver and the source.

Workspace.Name: LTE_Advanced_UL_SISO_BER
Workspace.Description:
LTE_Advanced_UL_SISO_BER

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This example workspace demonstrates open loop BER measurements for LTE Advanced uplink SISO in AWGN environment.

 

The reference dataset LTE_A_UL_SISO_AWGN_QPSK shows the simulation results of 5MHz system using MMSE channel estimation and ideal timing and frequency synchronization. All 25 RBs are allocated for PUSCH. The mapping type is QPSK. The code rate is 1/3. 1000 frames are simulated.

 

To reproduce the reference dataset, please double click LTE_A_UL_SISO_BER_ Analysis, select configuration Ideal_Sync, then run Sweep_LTE_A_UL_SISO_BER.

 

Configuration Ideal_sync uses the modified version of LTE_A_UL_Receiver model which can be found in the workspace tree. Double click LTE_A_UL_Receiver from the workspace tree to see the detailed implementation of the receiver. As can be seen in LTE_A_UL_TimeFreqSync model, UseDesiredValue is set to 1:YES, DesiredDelay and DesiredFreq are set to the ideal timing index and frequency offset. For the default parameter configurations in this example, DesiredDelay is to 6 and DesiredFreq is set to 0. The delay is caused by the time windowing in the transmitter side.

 

Choose configuration default in LTE_A_UL_SISO_BER_ Analysis, and then the built-in LTE_A_UL_Receiver@LTE Advanced Library is used. Hence real timing and synchronization is used, i.e. in LTE_A_UL_TimeFreqSync model, UseDesiredValue is set to 0:NO. With real timing and synchronization, the BER performance would be degraded. Please set higher SNR range in Sweep_LTE_A_UL_SISO_BER, e.g. 1 to 6.

 

256QAM is supported when Enable256QAM is set to yes.

Workspace.Name: LTE_Advanced_NBIoT_DL_BER
Workspace.Description:
LTE_Advanced_NBIoT_DL_BER

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This example workspace demonstrates a NPDSCH/NPDCCH BER measurement of an LTE Advanced NBIoT downlink transmitter and receiver. SISO, 1x2, 2x1 and 2x2 (MIMO Transmit Diversity) performance are shown in the graphs and the coded rate is set to 1/3. For SISO, AWGN channel is used. For 2x2 and 2x1 MIMO transmit diversity mode, MIMO Transmit Diversity is selected to get the BER performance. For 1x2 mode, MIMO Receiver Diversity is selected to get the BER performance.

 

To view the BER results of 1X2, 2X1 and 2X2, please execute the simulation. Those results are not stored in this example to reduce the file size.

 

NPDSCH (physical downlink shared channel) ,NPBCH (physical broadcast channel),NRS (Narrowband Reference Signal) and NPSS/NSSS (primary and secondary synchronization channels) are inserted in to the frame.

In the receiver, timing and frequency synchronization are supported. Auto detection of CellID sector and group would be given.

 

For this example, the stand-alone operation mode is supported. Payloads subcarriers are allocated to the subcarriers around DC, halfcarriershift is enable at the same time. 

 

LowIFReceiver can be used to compensate the gain imbalance and phase imbalance.

Workspace.Name: LTE_Advanced_NBIoT_DL_GuardBand
Workspace.Description:
LTE_Advanced_NBIoT_DL_GuardBand

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This example workspace demonstrates NBIoT system performance when it's deployed in the guard band of a LTE carrier. EVM measurement is given.

 

The number of Tx antennas and the number of Rx antennas are 1 for this version.

NPDSCH (physical downlink shared channel) ,NPDCCH (physical downlink control channel) ,NPBCH (physical broadcast channel),NRS (Narrowband Reference Signal) and NPSS/NSSS (primary and secondary synchronization channels) are inserted in to the frame.

 

1.4MHz and 15MHz LTE carrier is not supported in this example.

 

'FreqOffset' specifies the center frequency offset between NBIoT carrier and LTE carrier. By setting this parameter, NBIoT carrier can be placed in the guard band of LTE carrier. Error will be given if NBIoT is outside of the guard band of LTE carrier by an improper FreqOffset.

 

'PowerOffset' specifies the amount of power of NBIoT that is greater than the power of LTE carrier.

 

The sampling rate used by transmitter is determined by the SystemBandwidth and LTE_OversamplingOption(in Equations). Considerring that a NBIoT UE receiver can't adopt such a high sampling rate, we apply a downsampling filter before the NBIoT DL Receiver model. The signal will be downsampled to a sampling rate used by receiver, ReceiverSampleRate = 1.92e6*(2^Rvr_OversamplingOption) as in Equations. We find the design of this downsampling filter may degrade the waveform quality. We suggest the downsampling ratio should not be greater than 8.

EVM measurement is given.  The OperationMode of LTE_A_NBIoT_DL_Source model and LTE_A_NBIoT_DL_Receiver model are either 1 (inband-same PCID) or 3 (inband-different PCID). NPDSCH (physical downlink shared channel) ,NPDCCH (physical downlink control channel) ,NPBCH (physical broadcast channel),NRS (Narrowband Reference Signal) and NPSS/NSSS (primary and secondary synchronization channels) are inserted in to the frame.

'PRB_Index' specifies the PRB index occupied by NBIoT carrier inside of a LTE carrier. By setting this parameter, NBIoT carrier can be placed in one of the PRBs of LTE carrier. Error will be given if PRB_Index is out of range.

 

'PowerOffset' specifies the amount of power of NBIoT that is greater than the power of LTE carrier.

 

The sampling rate used by transmitter is determined by the SystemBandwidth and LTE_OversamplingOption(in Equations). Considerring that a NBIoT UE receiver can't adopt such a high sampling rate, we apply a downsampling filter before the NBIoT DL Receiver model. The signal will be downsampled to a sampling rate used by receiver, ReceiverSampleRate = 1.92e6*(2^Rvr_OversamplingOption) as in Equations. We find the design of this downsampling filter may degrade the waveform quality. We suggest the downsampling ratio should not be greater than 8.

Workspace.Name: LTE_Advanced_NBIoT_DL_Instruments
Workspace.Description:
LTE_Advanced_NBIoT_DL_Instruments

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

 

This example workspace demonstrates the usage of NBIoT source and receiver model with hardware instruments. It is comprised of two designs. Design1 is to download a NB-IoT downlink waveform into a Signal Generator. Design2 is to capture a signal from Signal Analyzer via VSA and measure its EVM. To ensure an accurate measurement, it’s required the Event1 of MXG is connected with the Ext Trig1 of MXA. And it’s also recommended to connected the 10MHz reference signal of the two instruments.

 

Signal downloading (Folder /Source)

The IP address of target MXG should be set in the ‘IPAddress’ of Design1 Parameters tab.

 

Signal analyzing (Folder /Analyzer)

The connection of Signal Analyzer with VSA should be setup well beforehand. It’s better to provide a VSA setup file which would allow the VSA to work properly after its being launched.

Workspace.Name: LTE_Advanced_NBIoT_DL_Tx
Workspace.Description:
LTE_Advanced_NBIoT_DL_Tx

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This example workspace demonstrates a spectrum, a CCDF and EVM measurement of an LTE Advanced NBIoT downlink transmitter.

 

Two examples with different antenna configuration have been given, one is SISO, and the other is 2x2.

NPDSCH (physical downlink shared channel) ,NPDCCH (physical downlink control channel) ,NPBCH (physical broadcast channel),NRS (Narrowband Reference Signal) and NPSS/NSSS (primary and secondary synchronization channels) are inserted in to the frame.

 

For this example, the stand-alone operation mode is supported. NBIoT that is allocated to the subcarriers around DC, halfcarriershift is enabled at the same time. 

 

Filter is used to get the spectrum of NBIoT. LTE_A_NBIoT_DL_Receiver is used to demodulator NPDSCH which is gotten for EVM measurement. Time domain windowing is added in the source in order to shape the spectrum of the transmitting signal and improve the performance in the receiver.

 

LowIFReceiver can be used to compensate the gain imbalance and phase imbalance.

 

If you experience a slow simulation, please disable the SpectrumAnalyzerEnv model, which is used to plot the spectrum, and try again.

 

LTE_A_NBIoT_DL_EVM is uesd in the example. Dynamic plot is adopted when ContinuousMode is set to Yes.The EVM result is based on frame. But ResLenInSlots is set to 40 when AnalysisBoundary is set to Frame in order to considering all the data. Gap is not supported in EVM model.

Workspace.Name: LTE_Advanced_NBIoT_UL_BER
Workspace.Description:
LTE_Advanced_NBIoT_UL_BER

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This example workspace analyzes Rx BER and Throughput results of an LTE Advanced NB-IoT uplink transmitter.

 

For this example, Design1 demonstrates the open loop BER measurement according to the demodulated bits and Design2 is to measure close-loop throughput according to the CRC parity check.

 

Open-loop BER measurement (Folder NBIoT_UL_BER)

 

For model "LTE_A_NBIoT_UL_Receiver", "ChannelBits" are the decision bits based on constellation demapper output, while  "RawBits" are the channel decoded bits and are the payload bits in one TB of NPUSCH. In this example, the plotted BER curve is the "ChannelBits" BER results vs. SNR.

 

Closed-loop HARQ Simulation Instruction (Folder NBIoT_UL_Throughput)

To enable the closed-loop HARQ simulation for UE, the following settings must be met.

  1. Set the 'HARQ_Enable' parameter to YES.
  2. Set the 'NumHARQ' parameter to specify the number of HARQ processes.
  3. Set the 'MaxHARQTrans' parameter to specify maximum number of HARQ transmission; The 'RV_Sequence' parameter specifies the redundancy version coding sequence whose array size should be equal to the 'MaxHARQTrans' parameter.
  4. Connect the 'HARQ_Bits' port in the receiver back to the 'HARQ_Bits' port in the source. Note that a Delay part (with the delay of (NumHARQ-1)) is placed between these two 'HARQ_Bits' ports in the receiver and the source.
  5. Use the 'LTE_Throughput' part to measure the simulated throughput. Note that the two input ports should come from the receiver corresponding output ports, and the measurement should at least begin with the second subframe (i.e. set SubframeStart >=1).

This example workspace demonstrates the generation of LTE Advanced NB-IoT uplink NPRACH.

 

The spectrum measurements for one antenna is performed using the SpectrumAnalyzer part respectively. Signal's spectrum should not exceed the spectrum mask in any case.

 

The CCDF measurements for one antennas are performed using the CCDF part respectively. The resulting CCDF curves are shown in the CCDF graph. Reference curves (CCDF of white gaussian noise) are also plotted on the graph.

For 3.75KHz, the base sample rate is 240KHz

Workspace.Name: MSR_BS_ACLR
Workspace.Description:
MSR Base Station Adjacent Channel Leakage power Ratio (ACLR)

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This example demonstrates how to measure the MSR base station Adjacent Channel Leakage power Ratio (ACLR) according to clause 6.6.4 of 3GPP TS 37.141.

Adjacent Channel Leakage power Ratio (ACLR) is the ratio of the filtered mean power centred on the assigned channel frequency to the filtered mean power centred on an adjacent channel frequency. The requirement applies to frequency ranges outside the Base Station RF bandwidth. The test purpose is to verify that the adjacent channel leakage power ratio requirement shall be met as specified by the minimum requirement.

In this example, one LTE carrier from MSR Band 14(758MHz - 768MHz) and one WCDMA carrier from MSR Band 12 (729MHz - 746MHz) are combined using SingalCombiner part. The MSR bands definition can be found in Table 4.4-1 of 3GPP TS 37.104.

Equation TestConfiguration specifies the used MSR Band and the signal configurations of each carrier e.g. sampling rate and bandwidth.

The spectrum graph "MSR_spec_Power" shows the combined spectrum, while the spectrum graph "MSR_spec_Power with individual spectrums" shows the combined spectrum along with individual standard spectrum.

Table "ACLR" shows the measured ACLR of each carrier and CACLR which are calculated in equation CalculateACLR.

 

TRY THIS:

  1. Change GCType in Amplifier in Design1 to add PA nonlinearities.
  2. Change MSR bands in equation TestConfiguration by setting F_Block1_BWlow, F_Block1_BWhigh, F_Block2_BWlow, F_Block2_BWhigh, F_BWmid.
  3. Change the signal configuration in equation TestConfiguration.

Workspace.Name: MSR_BS_InbandGeneralBlocking
Workspace.Description:
MSR Base Station In-band General Blocking

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This example demonstrates how to measure the MSR base station in-band selectivity and blocking according to clause 7.4 of 3GPP TS 37.141. 

The in-band selectivity and blocking characteristics are measures of the receiver ability to receive a wanted signal at its assigned channel in the presence of an unwanted interferer inside the operating band and are defined by a wideband and a narrowband blocking requirement. This example tests the wideband blocking requirement. The interfering signal shall be a UTRA FDD signal.

In this example, one GSM carrier and one WCDMA carrier from MSR Band 8 (880MHz - 915MHz) are combined using SingalCombiner part. The interfering signal is a UTRA FDD signal. The MSR bands definition can be found in Table 4.4-1 of 3GPP TS 37.104.

Equation TestConfiguration specifies the used MSR Band and the signal configurations of each carrier e.g. sampling rate and bandwidth.

The spectrum graph "MSR_spec_Power" shows the combined spectrum, while the spectrum graph "MSR_spec_Power with individual spectrums" shows the combined spectrum along with individual standard spectrum.

Table "BER" shows the measured bit error rate of each carrier.

 

TRY THIS:

  1. Change MSR bands in equation TestConfiguration by setting F_BWlow, F_BWhigh and F_BWmid.
  2. Change the interferer configuraiton in equation TestConfiguration.
  3. Change the wanted signal configuration in equation TestConfiguration.
  4. Sweep the FreqOffsetStep of the interferer signal with step size 1MHz using "Sweep1".

Workspace.Name: MSR_BS_MaxOutputPower
Workspace.Description:
MSR Base Station Maximum Output Power

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This example demonstrates how to measure the MSR base station maximum output power according to clause 6.2 of 3GPP TS 37.141.

Output power of the Base Station is the mean power delivered to a load with resistance equal to the nominal load impedance of the transmitter. The maximum carrier output power, Pmax,c of the Base Station is the mean power level measured at the antenna connector during the transmitter ON period for a specific carrier in a specified reference condition. The test purpose is to verify the accuracy of the maximum carrier output power across the frequency range and under normal and extreme conditions for all transmitters in the BS.

In this example, five LTE signals and six WCDMA signals are combined at Fc = 2.14e9 Hz in MSR Band 1 (2110MHz - 2170MHz) as defined in Table 4.4-1 of 3GPP TS 37.104 using SingalCombiner part. Equation TestConfiguration specifies the used MSR Band and the signal configurations of each carrier e.g. sampling rate, bandwidth and power.

 

The spectrum graph "MSR_spec_Power" shows the combined spectrum, while the spectrum graph "MSR_spec_Power with individual spectrums" shows the combined spectrum along with individual standard spectrum.

Table "OutputPower_dBm" shows the measured carrier output power caculated in equation PowerCalculation.

 

TRY THIS:

  1. Change GCType in Amplifier in Design1 to add PA nonlinearities.
  2. Change MSR band in equation TestConfiguration by setting F_BWlow, F_BWhigh and F_BWmid.
  3. Change the signal configuration in equation TestConfiguration.
  4. Specify different LTE carriers and WCDMA carriers to measure by setting MeasLTECarrierIndex and MeasWCDMACarrierIndex in equation PowerCalculation.

MSR Base Station Narrow Band Blocking

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

This example demonstrates how to measure the MSR base station in-band selectivity and blocking according to clause 7.4 of 3GPP TS 37.141.

The in-band selectivity and blocking characteristics are measures of the receiver ability to receive a wanted signal at its assigned channel in the presence of an unwanted interferer inside the operating band and are defined by a wideband and a narrowband blocking requirement. This example tests the narrowband blocking requirement. The interfering signal shall be an E-UTRA 1RB signal.

In this example, one GSM carrier and one LTE carrier from MSR Band 8 (880MHz - 915MHz) are combined using SingalCombiner part. The interfering signal is an E-UTRA 1RB signal. The MSR bands definition can be found in Table 4.4-1 of 3GPP TS 37.104.

The spectrum graph "MSR_spec_Power" shows the combined spectrum, while the spectrum graph "MSR_spec_Power with individual spectrums" shows the combined spectrum along with individual standard spectrum.

Table "Performance" shows the measured bit error rate of GSM carrier and throughput fraction of LTE carrier.

 

TRY THIS:

  1. Change MSR bands in equation TestConfiguration by setting F_BWlow, F_BWhigh and F_BWmid.
  2. Change the interferer configuraiton in equation TestConfiguration
  3. Change the wanted signal configuration in equation TestConfiguration.
  4. Sweep the interfering RB centre frequency offset i.e. m in Table Table 7.4.5.2-1of TS 37.141 using Sweep1
  5. Adjust the noise density in AddNDensity model in the design.

MSR Base Station Out Of Band Blocking

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This example demonstrates how to measure the MSR base station out of band blocking according to clause 7.5 of 3GPP TS 37.141.

The Out-of-band blocking characteristic is a measure of the receiver ability to receive a wanted signal at its assigned channel in the presence of an unwanted interferer outside the uplink operating band. The test stresses the ability of the BS receiver to withstand high-level interference from unwanted signals at specified frequency bands, without undue degradation of its sensitivity.

In this example, one LTE carrier and one WCDMA carrier from MSR Band 11 (1427.9MHz - 1447.9MHz) and one LTE carrier and one WCDMA carrier from MSR Band 10( 1710MHz - 1770MHz) are combined using SingalCombiner part. The interfering signal is a CW signal. The MSR bands definition can be found in Table 4.4-1 of 3GPP TS 37.104.

Equation TestConfiguration specifies the used MSR Band and the signal configurations of each carrier e.g. sampling rate and bandwidth.

The spectrum graph "MSR_spec_Power" shows the combined spectrum, while the spectrum graph "MSR_spec_Power with individual spectrums" shows the combined spectrum along with individual standard spectrum.

Table "TestResults" shows the measured bit error rate of WCDMA carrier and throughput fraction of LTE carrier.

 

TRY THIS:

  1. Change MSR bands in equation TestConfiguration by setting F_F_Block1_BWlow, F_F_Block1_BWhigh, F_Block2_BWlow, F_Block2_BWlhigh and F_BWmid.
  2. Change the interferer configuraiton in equation TestConfiguration.
  3. Change the wanted signal configuration in equation TestConfiguration.
  4. Sweep the interfere frequency offset using Sweep1.
  5. Adjust the noise density in AddNdensity model in the design.

Workspace.Description:
MSR Base Station Transmitted Signal Quality

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This example demonstrates how to measure the MSR base station transmitted signal quality according to clause 6.5 of 3GPP TS 37.141.

Modulation quality is defined by the difference between the measured carrier signal and a reference signal. Modulation quality can e.g. be expressed as Error Vector Magnitude (EVM), Peak Code domain Error (PCDE) or Relative Code domain Error (RCDE). The test purpose is to verify that modulation quality is within the limit specified by the minimum requirement.

In this example, one LTE carrier from MSR Band 7(2620MHz - 2690MHz) and one WCDMA carrier from MSR Band 1 (2110MHz - 2170MHz) are combined using SingalCombiner part. The MSR bands definition can be found in Table 4.4-1 of 3GPP TS 37.104.

 

Equation TestConfiguration specifies the used MSR Band and the signal configurations of each carrier e.g. sampling rate and bandwidth.

The spectrum graph "MSR_spec_Power" shows the combined spectrum, while the spectrum graph "MSR_spec_Power with individual spectrums" shows the combined spectrum along with individual standard spectrum.

Table "EVM" shows the measured EVM of each carrier.

 

TRY THIS:

  1. Change GCType in Amplifier in Design1 to add PA nonlinearities.
  2. Change MSR bands in equation TestConfiguration by setting F_Block1_BWlow, F_Block1_BWhigh, F_Block2_BWlow, F_Block2_BWhigh, F_BWmid.
  3. Change the signal configuration in equation TestConfiguration.

Workspace.Name: WiMAX_DL_MIMO_Fading_BER
Workspace.Description:
WiMAX_DL_MIMO_Fading_BER

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This example workspace demonstrates a swept BER vs. SNR measurement for a WiMAX 2X2 MIMO system in fading channel.

1. Users can change Rate_ID from 0 to 6 and get BER and PER results for different modulations and code rates. Also DecoderType can be selected with Hard, Soft or CSI and STCDeocder can be MMSE or ZF.

 

2. The WiMAX MIMO channel is based on WiMAX Forum MRCT supporting both pedestrian and vehicular environments. Also users can define specific fading MIMO channel mode by defining the parameters of Delay, Power, Ricean_factor, MeanAoA and MeanAoD. The antenna correlation could be High, Medium, Low or None.

 

3. Current settings are: Rate_ID=0 (QPSK 1/2), CTC, STC_Matrix=Matrix_B.

 

4. Test Benches: about 3 hours in the machine with Intel Core2 Duo 2.4GHz, 4G RAM, Windows 7 system.

Workspace.Name: Bluetooth_InterferencePerformance_Measurement
Workspace.Description:
Bluetooth C/I Performance

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This example analyzes the Bluetooth Rx performance in the presence of co-/adjacent channel interference.

 

Two designs are provided. 

1. EDR_CoACInterference: demonstrates Bluetooth Rx performance in the presence of co-/adjacent channel Bluetooth interference.

The test procedure refers to 5.1.24 TP/RCV/CA/09/C (EDR C/I Performance).

o    The default wanted signal and interferer are pi/4-DQPSK modulated packet 2-DH5. To test 8DPSK signal, please reset the packet type in Parameters.

o    This design gives the co-channel interference test of the lowest operation frequency using a minimum number of 16 000 000 payload bits as the default configuration. The operation frequency and signal power of the wanted signal and interferer are set in the Equations. Users can edit the Equations for other test case with reference 5.1.24 TP/RCV/CA/09/C (EDR C/I Performance) of Bluetooth Test Specification Ver. 1.2/2.0/2.0+EDR/2.1/2.1+EDR.

o     

About 12 minutes in the machine with Intel Core2 Duo 2.4GHz, 4G RAM, Windows 7 system.

 

2. EDR_withWLANInterference: demonstrates Bluetooth Rx performance in the presence of adjacent channel WLAN interference. 

o    The Bluetooth signal operation frequency is 2.405 GHz. and the interferer is the WLAN 11n 20MHz signal which works on 2.417 GHz.

o    In the default test configuration, Bluetooth packet type is 3-DH5 with 8DPSK modulation and with the maximum length payload containing PN9. To test other packet type, please reset the LinkType and ACLPacketType or eSCOPacketType.

o    The operation frequency and signal power of the wanted signal and interferer as well as the number of test bits are set in the Equations. Users can edit the Equations for other test case.

o    About 12 minutes in the machine with Intel Core2 Duo 2.4GHz, 4G RAM, Windows 7 system.

 

The Packet Error Rate/Bit Error Rate is provided for these 2 test cases.

Bluetooth_EDR_Sensitivity

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This example shows the EDR Sensitivity test using a non-ideal transmitter of the Bluetooth signals. 

 

Two designs are provided. 

1. BDR_Sensitivity_Measurement: measures BER of Bluetooth basic data rate source.

The test procedure is defined in the equation runBDRBerMeas.

o    The packet type is DH5 GFSK modulation and with the maximum length payload containing PN9. To test other packet type, please reset the LinkType and ACLPacketType or eSCOPacketType in the equation runBDRBerMeas.

o    The input power to the receiver (EVM model) is -70dBm

o    This examples gives the procedure of the lowest operation frequency using a minimum number of 16 000 000 payload bits.

o    To get the mid and highest operating frequency test result, please re-set the FCarrier in the equation runBDRBerMeas and run it. 

 

2. EDR_Sensitivity: demonstrate the EDR Sensitivity test defined in 5.1.22 RCV/CA/07/C (EDR Sensitivity).

The test procedure is defined in the equation runEDRBerMeas.

o    The packet type is 2-DH5 with pi/4- DQPSK modulation and with the maximum length payload containing PN9. To test other packet type, please reset the LinkType and ACLPacketType or eSCOPacketType.

o    The input power to the receiver (EVM model) is -70dBm

o    This examples gives the procedure of the lowest operation frequency using a minimum number of 16 000 000 payload bits.

o    To get the mid and highest operating frequency test result, please re-set the FCarrier in the equation runEDRBerMeas and run it. 

 

 The Packet Error Rate is provided for these 2 test cases.

Workspace.Description:
Bluetooth_TX_Measurement

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This example analyzes measurement results of the Bluetooth signals. 

 

Two designs are provided. 

  • BDR_Tx_Measurement: measures output power, modulation characteristics, ICFT(initial carrier frequency tolerance) and the carrier frequency drift of Bluetooth basic data rate source.

To measure the modulation characteristics DeltaF1 and DeltaF2, the defined payload patterns should be used by set the model PayloadData in the schematic and run the Analysis. 

For DeltaF1, we should set the PayloadData as PayloadDataPatten1 (1 1 1 1 0 0 0 0) 

For DeltaF2, we should set the PayloadData as PayloadDataPatten2 (1 0 1 0 1 0 1 0)

In the case of modulation characteristics test, the reported BER results are not correct. To measure the BER, the PayloadData should be set to PN9 or PN15.

  • EDR_Tx_Measurement: measures output power, carrier frequency stability and modulation accuracy and BER for Bluetooth EDR source.

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

This example analyzes Rx BER and FER results on AWGN of the 802.11ac one antenna signals.

1Ant_AWGN: measures BER and FER on AWGN for 11ac single antenna source

 

802.11ac Signal Source in SystemVue

This 11ac source follows the TGac Draft Amendment (IEEE P802.11ac/D1.0) May 2011.

In this source, the Very High Throughput (VHT) PPDU format PHY is implemented, including L-STF, L-LTF, L-SIG, VHT-SIG-A, VHT-STF, VHT-LTFs, VHT-SIG-B and PSDU Data symbols. Users can easily see the implementation of each PPDU part by opening the WLAN_11ac_Source model.

Note: in order to run this workspace successfully, dlls for both WLAN (for 11a) and WLAN 11ac libraries are needed.

 

The supported features

· Up to 8 TX antennas

· 20, 40, 80, 160MHz and 80+80 (use two sources)

· Coded data for PSDU symbols

· 1 to 8 streams (with the same number of tx antennas)

· MCS: 0 to 9

· Modulation: BPSK, QPSK, 16QAM, 64QAM, 256QAM

· Cyclic shift (CSD) insertion

· 800 ns and 400 ns guard interval

 

Parameter Description:

1. Bandwidth: specify the bandwidth of 11ac signal, selected from 20MHz, 40MHz, 80MHz or 160MHz. For the case of 80+80MHz signal, users can use two 80MHz 11ac sources and combine them together to form the 80+80MHz signal

2. OversampleRatio: Specify the oversample ratio of 11ac signal, selected from 1x, 2x, 4x or 8x.

3. MCS: specify the modulation coding scheme. The mapping from MCS to modulation is shown below.

Workspace.Description:
WLAN_11ac_Rx_Sensitivity

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

This example analyzes Receiver minimum input sensitivity of the 802.11ac signals.

The packet error rate (PER) shall be less than 10% for a PSDU length of 4096 octets with the rate-dependent input levels listed in Table 22-21 (Receiver minimum input level sensitivity), and non-STBC modes, 800 ns GI and BCC.

For 80MHz, 64QAM, Rate 2/3, the minimum sensitivity is -60 dBm.

Workspace.Name: WLAN_11ac_Tx_1Ant
Workspace.Description:
WLAN_11ac_Tx_1Ant

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This example analyzes the spectrum and Complementary Cumulative Distribution Function (CCDF) of the 802.11ac non-80+80 MHz signals.

 

Users may also save the baseband I/Q data to files or download it to Keysight 89600B VSA software Rev14.0 for further analysis. In 89600B Rev14.0, the WLAN 11ac feature is employed to demodulate 11ac signals, and the WLAN 11ac setting for 20, 40, 80 or 160 MHz with single transmitter antenna and non-shortGI used is provided.

 

In the Tx_1Ant design, the parameters defined in the "Parameters" Tab are used to set 11ac 20, 40, 80 or 160 MHz signal, including the central frequency, MCS and the number of OFDM data symbols in each frame which is determined by the parameters of MCS, CodingType, AggregatedMPDU, NumMPDUPerUser, User0_MPDUDataLength, User0_MPDUMACHeader and ShortGI. The calculated number of data symbols will be displayed in the Errors window.

 

For 1 antenna case, the number of space-time streams is 1. And so the parameter STBC should be set to NO, the NumUsers should be set to 1 and the N_SS for this user should be set to 1.

In the Tx_1ant_80_80MHz design, the parameters defined in the "Parameters" Tab are used to set 11ac 80+80 MHz signal, including the central frequency for each 80MHz segment, MCS and the number of OFDM data symbols in each frame which is determined by the parameters of MCS, CodingType, AggregatedMPDU, NumMPDUPerUser, User0_MPDUDataLength and User0_MPDUMACHeader. WLAN_11ac_Tx_2Ants

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This example analyzes the spectrum and Complementary Cumulative Distribution Function (CCDF) of the 802.11ac non-80+80 MHz signals.

 

Users may also save the baseband I/Q data to files or download it to Keysight 89600B VSA software Rev14.0 for further analysis. In 89600B Rev14.0, the WLAN 11ac feature is employed to demodulate 11ac signals, and the WLAN 11ac setting for 20, 40, 80 or 160 MHz with two transmitter antennas is provided.

 

In the Tx_1Ant design, the parameters defined in the "Parameters" Tab are used to set 11ac 20, 40, 80 or 160 MHz signal, including the central frequency, MCS and the number of OFDM data symbols in each frame which is dertermined by the parameters of MCS, CodingType, AggregatedMPDU, NumMPDUPerUser, User0_MPDUDataLength and User0_MPDUMACHeader. The calculated number of data symbols will be displayed in the Errors window.

 

For 2 antennas case, the space-time streams should be no larger than 2. And so, if the STBC is set to YES, the number of users should be 1 and the N_SS for this user is 1. If the STBC is set to NO, the number of users can be set to 2, which user with N_SS as 1.

Workspace.Name: WLAN_11ac_Tx_EVM
Workspace.Description:
WLAN_11ac_TX_EVM

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This example analyzes EVM results of the 802.11ac signals. The test results are same as Keysight 89600 VSA.

 

Two designs are provided. 

  1. Tx_1Ant_EVM: measure EVM for 11ac single antenna source.
  2. Tx_2Ants_EVM: measure EVM for 11ac two-antenna source.
  3. It's better to re-set parameters listed in Parameters field to get EVM measurements under various conditions without change the schematic.
  4. If you re-set model parameters in schematic, please make sure this configuration is consistent with the schematic. Such as, the NumTx, NumSTS, STBC, MCS, and so on. For one transmit chain schematic, STBC should be set to NO, NumUsers and N_SS should be 1. For more transmit chains schematic, we must sure that, the total number of SS should be no larger than total number of space-time streams which should be no larger than transmit chains.

Two analyses are provided, Tx_1Ant Analysis and Tx_2Ants Analysis. We can right-click one and select Run to run the design.

 

Two data sets are provided, Tx_1Ant_Data and Tx_2Ants_Data. We can double-click them to see the measurement results.
