Workspace.Name: IIR_DDS
Workspace.Description:
Code Generation Example - IIR DDS

 

This example demonstrates how to build a Direct Digital Synthesizer (DDS) using an Infinte Impulse Response (IIR) filter.

 

The filter used is a simple two weight (all-pole) filter.  With a sampling rate of 100 MHz the system will produce a sine wave with frequency 8.04 MHz.

 

Try changing the gain labeled B to 0 and observe the output. Experiment with a few other values but be wary of overflow.

 

HDL Code Generation Control

 

HDL code generation is parameterized and controlled through the HDL Code Generator in the Workspace Tree. Right clicking the HDL Code Generator and selecting "Generate Now" or clicking "Generate" in the HDL Code Generator Options dialog will generate HDL code for the IIR_DDS subsystem.

 

HDL Code Generation Output

 

By default the generated HDL files are placed in the same directory as this example. To simulate the HDL code using ModelSim there is a batch file named IIR_DDS_SimTB.bat in the output directory which; when run will launch ModelSim, load the generated testbench and simulate the HDL. The testbech requires test vectors.

 

HDL Code Generation Subcirucit Selection

 

Subcircuits to be HDL code generator are selected in the HDL Code Generator Options dialog. A subcircuit to be code generated must have at least one input and output port.

 

Test Vector Generation

 

If Test Vector Generation is selected; dataflow models that generate test vectors for HDL simulation are automatically added to the SystemVue simulator at the ports of the top level subcircuit during code generation. The test vectors can then be used with the generated HDL testbench.

Workspace.Name: NCO_Quadrature_dithering
Workspace.Description:
Numerically-Controlled
Fixed-point Oscillator (NCO)

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Workspace

 

This example demonstrates a basic dual output 90 degree quadrature Numerically Controlled Oscillator (NCO) with dither. (You may need to re-simulate this example after opening, if you some warnings.)

 

The top-level schematic shows the NCO2 component (accessable in the NCO folder) that is controlled by sliders allowing the user to change the NCO Frequency and also the amount of Dither, which will change the Spur levels and thus the SFDR. Their values are displayed on the schematic. The Dither value modifies the 2^N noise source value. There is also a slider for the fixed-point address depth of the Lookup Tables (LUT), which defines the granularity of the phase resolution of the output signal.

 

The NCO2 component has an accumulator and 2 LUTS, containing sine and cosine samples. It can also be used to generate HDL or C++ code.

 

Open NCO2_HDL_Gen and click Generate. HDL code will be generated in the same directory of the workspace. And a HDL@ Data Flow model will also be added to Subnetwork1 in Design1, parameters have been specified for HDL co-simulation automatically.

 

Open Design1 Analysis, swith configuration to "NativeModel" for Fxp models simulation and switch to "HDLCoSim" for HDL co-simulation with ModelSim.

 

Notes:

  1. When the workspace is first opened the Freq= and SFDR= parameters on the schematic will show #Error. To clear that, after simulating, simply click on the value in each box.
  2. If the Freq MHz slider is moved rapidly the computed results may not keep up and display a different value. Move the slider in a small increment around the desired Freq and it will catch up.
  3. The displayed StepSize component value doesn't update and is often invalid. Double-clicking on it and returning will update the value.
  4. In order to do HDL co-simulation, you should install ModelSim SE 6.3g or later. And specify parameter "ModelSim Executable" as your installation location of modelsim.exe in Global Options -> Code Generation.

Workspace.Name: QPSK_transceiver_with_symbol_timing_recovery
Workspace.Description:
QPSK Transceiver with symbol timing recovery

 

This example workspace demonstrates a QPSK transmitter and receiver system built entirely from parts in the Hardware Design library. This makes it possible to generate HDL code for the entire system. Furthermore, the HDL Code Generator "QPSK_transceiver_ML402" is configured to implement the system on Xilinx ML402 FPGA board.

 

1. This QPSK transmitter/receiver system consists of:

 

a)  Bit_Source

It can generate pseudo-random bit sequence. The bit sequence is obtained by performing an XOR operation between a PN15_Bits and a PN9_Bits sequences. Both PN15_Bits and PN_9Bits are generated using an LFSR (Linear Feedback Shift Register). Their primitive ploynomials are:

 

PN15_Bits

p(x)=x^15 + x + 1

PN9_Bits

p(x)=x^9 + x^4 + 1

 

b) Tx

It is a QPSK modulator. After QPSK mapping, the signal is upsampled by 4 and goes through a square root raise cosine filter with a roll-off factor 0.5.

 

c) PN_AWGN

It is an approximation of an AWGN noise generator. According to the law of large number, eight pseudo-random integer generators are added together to approximate AWGN noise.

The eight pseudo-random integer generators are all implemented using LFSRs (a SerToPara part is used to convert 8 bits to an integer). The primitive polynomials for the LFSRs are:

PN9

p(x) = x^9 + x^4 + 1

PN10

p(x) = x^10 + x^3 + 1

PN11

p(x) = x^11 + x^2 + 1

PN12

p(x) = x^12 + x^6 + x^4 + x + 1

PN13

p(x) = x^13 + x^4 + x^3 + x + 1

PN14

p(x) = x^14 + x^10 + x^6 + x + 1

PN15

p(x) = x^15 + x + 1

PN16

p(x) = x^16 + x^12 + x^3 + x + 1

   

In "Design1 (Schematic)" Equation tab, there is a variable SNR, which can be used to control the power of AWGN. Only positive values are valid for this variable.set.

 

d) Rx

It consist of a matched filter, symbol timing synchronization with Gardner algorithm, and QPSK demodulator. It uses a polyphase filter to get 16 samples per symbol and adjust the sampling position according to the detected result of the Gardner detector.

 

The Gardner detector result is:

Er = YI(r-1/2) * [YI(r) - YI(r-1)] + YQ(r-1/2) * [YQ(r) - YQ(r-1)]

where YI(r) is the sample in I path and YI(r-1/2) is the sample half symbol behind YI(r); YQ(r) is the sample in Q path and YQ(r-1/2) is the sample half symbol behind YQ(r).

When Er is less than 0, the current sampling position is leading the optimal sampling position; otherwise, when Er is larger than 0, the current sampling position is lagging the optimal sampling position.

 

The detected Er value goes through a loop filter and is fed back to the polyphase filter to select the sampling position. In "loop_filter" model, the detected Er values are accumulated. When the accumulated value is larger than the parameter "loop_threshold" (specified in equation tab of "loop_filter" model), the sampling position is adjusted accordingly.

 

e) BER

This model is used to compare Tx and Rx bit streams. It outputs "err_num" and "total_num" to represent the numbers of error bits and total bits. Then BER ratio can be calculated. This model can also be implemented in FPGA, and "err_num" and "total_num" are output from FPGA for BER ratio calculation.

 

 

2. FPGA implementation on Xilinx ML402 board

 

HDL Code Generator "QPSK_transceiver_ML402" configures the subnetwork demod_awgn to implement it on Xilinx ML402 FPGA board.

 

Open it and click Generate. It will generate an ISE project and launch ISE automatically. You can insert Chipscope IP core in ISE project further if you want.

 

HDL Code Generator "QPSK_transceiver_ML402" has configured:

  • Clock inputs from SYSCLK on ML402, which is 100MHz
  • Using DCM to de-skew input clock and divide clock frequency by 2, so system clock is 50MHz
  • Using CPU Reset Button on ML402 as reset signal input
  • Using DIP Switches Connection pin 1 on ML402 as ce input, the whole design works while ce is high and holds while ce is low.
  • Using DIP Switches Connections pin 2~8 on ML402 as noise_power input
  • Specifying output signals on Single-Ended Expansion I/O Connectors on ML402

For more details of pin locations, please refer to ML402 user guide: http://www.xilinx.com/support/documentation/boards_and_kits/ug080.pdf

Workspace.Name: RSEncoder
Workspace.Description:
RS Encoder for HDL code generation, HDL co-simulation and FPGA Implementation

 

 

1. Fixed-point RS encoder

 

This example workspace demonstrates a RS encoder (RS_Enc model) built entirely from parts in the Hardware Design library. This makes it possible to generate HDL code for it.

 

An RS code is defined by the following parameters:

 

Parameter

Description

m

The code is defined in GF(2^m), a message symbol represents m bits.

PrimPoly

Primitive polynomial (Galois Field generator polynomial), m+1 terms with degree of m, highest degree item first. An integer is used to represent the primitive polynomial. For example, if m =8 and the primitive polynomial is  X^8 + X^4 + X^3 + X^2 + 1, then set parameters: m=8 and PrimPoly = 285 (100011101).

T

Number of error symbols that can be corrected; 2*T+1 is the minimum distance between any two codewords.

B

Degree of alpha, alpha^B is the first root of generator polynomial.

 

In this example, T is fixed and equal to 8. The other three parameters can be specified arbitrarily.

 

For example, the default specification implements a (255, 239) RS encoder. You can modify parameters m and PrimPoly to implement a different RS encoder. For example, you can set m = 7 and PrimPoly= 137, to implement a (127, 111) RS encoder. You can also modify this design easily to implement a different “T” RS encoder by changing the number of GF multipliers in RS_Enc model.

 

The RS encoder has two inputs: msg and msg_en.

 

msg_en is the enable signal which indicates whether the corresponding msg input is valid (1: valid; 0: invalid).

 

NOTE: An input msg block must arrive consecutively and msg_en must be invalid for at least 2*T clock cycles following msg block, because the encoder doesn’t change the sampling rate.

 

For example, in the (255, 239) encoder case, msg_en is high for 239 consecutive clock cycles and then low for 39 cycles (39>2*T). When msg_en is high, 239 input values are read from msg input. The output port “code” outputs 239 msg codes followed by 16 parity codes. The output port “code_valid” is high when msg and parity are output.

 

In equation page “rsenc MKS”, you can find function “codeGenPoly” which is used to deduce the generation polynomial.

 

In model RS_hardveri, random message code and msg_en are implemented with parts from the Hardware Design library, so you can use the generated HDL code to verify the RS encoder on an FPGA.

 

The output of the RS encoder implemented here is also compared to the output of the RS encoder in the Algorithm Design library (CoderRS) in "Design2" Schematic. The diffrence between the two encoder outputs is is plotted in graph "Design2_S3".

 

Because the Galois multiplier is implemented by a pure combinational logic, it may create critical path when m is very large. You may need to modify the architecture of the Galois multiplier manually to get specific timing performance.

 

Open "Design2 Analysis", set configuration as "NativeModel" and click "Calculate Now". It will simulate the fixed-point design and should be cycle accurate with hardware behavior.

 

2. HDL codes generation

 

Open "RS_Enc_HDL_Gen" in HDL_Code_Generators folder and click Generate. The HDL codes will be generated to RS_Enc_HDL folder in the same directory as the workspace, if you check "Use Default Directory". Or you can uncheck it and specify your desired directory.

 

When you generate HDL codes, if you leave "Automatically add generated model to Part model list" checked, then a "HDL@Data Flow" model will be added to part Data3 in RS_hardveri subnetwork. And the parameters of the "HDL@Data Flow" model will been automatically specified according to generated HDL codes.

 

3. HDL co-simulation

 

After generating HDL codes and adding "HDL@Data Flow" model, you can co-simulate the generated HDL codes with Modelsim.

 

Open "Design2 Analysis", set Configuration as "HDLCoSim" and click "Calculate Now". SystemVue will call ModelSim to simulate generated HDL codes and co-simulate with the other parts in the design.

 

Note:

(1) Before running HDL co-simulation, you should install ModelSim SE 6.3g or later. And open a HDL Code Generator, for example RS_Enc_HDL_Gen, and click "Global Options" to set "ModelSim Executable" as your installation location of modelsim.exe.

(2) In Design2, configuration "HDLCoSim" has been specified. It has set part Data3 in RS_hardveri as "RS_Enc_HDL_Gen (HDL@ Data Flow Models)". So when you run "Design2 Analysis" with configuration "HDLCoSim", the HDL co-simulation will be done.

 

4. FPGA implementation on Xilinx VC707 FPGA board

 

Open RS_Enc_Xilinx_VC707 in HDL_Code_Generators folder and click Generate. Once the build process of the partial configuration file finishes, you can switch the model RS_Enc into [HIL707] RS_Enc model and then run the simulation. This model will be executed from VC707 board via Hardware in the loop connection.

 

Note:

Before running HIL VC707 flow, you should install Vivado Design Suite 2015.03 or later and set "Xilinx Vivado Executable" in "Global Options".

 

 

 

 

 

 

Galois Field (2^m) Multiplier

Systolic_GF_2_m_Mpy model illustrates the multiplier on GF(2^m) with fixed point blocks.

 

You can specify parameters: m and PrimPoly (Primitive Polynomial) to implement an arbitrary GF field multiplier for m 3~16.

For example: m =8, primitive polynomial is  X^8 + X^4 + X^3 + X^2 + 1, then set parameters: m=8 and PrimPoly = 285 (100011101) to implement a GF multiplier for this GF field.

Workspace.Name: WiMAX_SVue_SDR_IQ_Modulator
Workspace.Description:
WiMAX SDR IQ Modulator Example

 

This is a multi-step example which simulates a fixed-point IQ modulator design , generates VHDL code from the fixed-point design, co-simulates with the generated VHDL code, and co-simulates the VHDL together with an RF transmitter design.  ModelSim SE and the 89600 VSA software (www.keysight.com/find/vsa) are required to perform the simulations.   There are several videos available which show the simulations from this example.  Please see the descriptions below.

 

·         Step1 SDR Fixed Point IQ Modulator

The Fxp Library is used to model a fixed point IQ modulator design.  The design consists of  I and Q data stored in the equation Read_File_MKS as I_ImportedVariable and  Q_Imported_Variable.  I and Q are upsampled by 4X and filtered with FIR filters.  FIR tap coefficients are stored in the equation Read_FIR_Taps.    The output of the IQ modulator generates a modulated signal with a carrier frequency of 11.2 MHz, which is analyzed and demodulated with the VSA software.  For a video demonstration, please see Discovering-SDR_Step1_Fixed_Point_IQ_mod.wmv

 

·         Step2 RF Design

I and Q data files are read to to generate a simulation signal source for an IF-RF transmitter design.   Several VSA elements are used to examine the non-linear waveform distortion introduced by the simulated pre-amplifier and power amplifier 

 

 

·         Step3a Generate HDL Code and Co-Sim model for Step4

VHDL code is generated for the fixed point IQ modulator design shown in Step1.  This step is implemented by a HDL Code Generator. Open "Step3a Generate HDL Code and Co-Sim model for Step4" and click Generate. It will generate VHDL codes and add a "HDL@ Data Flow" model to model list of subnetwork Data1 in Step4 automatically. And the parameters of added "HDL@ Data Flow" models have been specified automatically according to generated HDL codes. The generated files are placed in the same directory as this example. For a video demonstration, please see Discovering- SDR_Step_3-4_SDR_IQmod_HDLgen_and_CoSim.wmv

 

·         Step3b Generate HDL Code and Co-Sim model for Step5

It is similar as "Step3a Generate HDL code and Co-Sim model for Step4". Open it and click Generate to generate VHDL code and add a "HDL@ Data Flow" model to model list of subnetwork Data2 in Step5 automatically.

 

·         Step4 HDL CoSim

Run DF4 with configuration HDLCoSim to co-simulate with the VHDL generated in Step3a.  The VHDL co-simulation results are analyzed and demodulated with the VSA software. For a video demonstration, please see Discovering- SDR_Step_3-4_SDR_IQmod_HDLgen_and_CoSim.wmv

 

·         Step5 CoSimulate HDL with RF Design

Run DF5 with configuration HDLCoSim. VHDL co-simulation from Step4 is combined with the RF transmitter design from Step2 for an RF/mixed-signal simulation.  The VSA software is used to analyze and demodulate the fixed point and non-linear waveform distortion at the  pre-amplifier and power amplifier outputs. For a video demonstration, please see Discovering - SDR_Step5_Combining_HDL_with_RF.wmv

Workspace.Name: TCM
Workspace.Description:
Code Generation Example - Convolutional Trellis Coder/Decoder

 

This system shows a testbench to simulate and test a realization of a convolutional trellis coder and a corresponding Viterbi decoder.

The testbench first generates an input signal which is passed to the trellis coder. The coder generates the complex symbols which are then passed through a complex AWGN baseband channel. The complex receive signal (i.e. I and Q) is then passed to the Viterbi decoder. The decoded bitstream is then returned.

 

Input signal

 

The input signal can be set to e.g. a random bit sequence. However, some formatting is required as the Viterbi decoder requires trailing zeros at the end of each block.

 

Convolutional Trellis Coder

 

The implemented convolutional trellis coder (constraint length K=3, code rate 1/2) generates 4-QAM symbols.
Compared to a BPSK transmission which has a free euclidean distance of 4*sqrt(E) (where E is the energy per bit) the implemented trellis coder achieves a free euclidean distance of 10*sqrt(E)

 

HDL Code Generation Control

 

HDL code generation is parameterized and controlled through the HDL Code Generator in the Workspace Tree. Right clicking the HDL Code Generator and selecting "Generate Now" or clicking "Generate" in the HDL Code Generator Options dialog will generate HDL code for the Coder\Decoder subsystem.

 

HDL Code Generation Output

 

By default the generated HDL files are placed in the same directory as this example. To simulate the HDL code using ModelSim there is a batch file named TrellisCoder_Decoder_SimTB.bat in the output directory which; when run will launch ModelSim, load the generated testbench and simulate the HDL. The testbech requires test vectors.

 

HDL Code Generation Subcirucit Selection

 

Subcircuits to be HDL code generator are selected in the HDL Code Generator Options dialog. A subcircuit to be code generated must have at least one input and output port.

 

Test Vector Generation

 

If Test Vector Generation is selected; dataflow models that generate test vectors for HDL simulation are automatically added to the SystemVue simulator at the ports of the top level subcircuit during code generation. The test vectors can then be used with the generated HDL testbench.

Workspace.Name: WLAN_11a_tx_Nallatech
Workspace.Description:
Xilinx IP Integrator : 802.11a Transmitter

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

1. This example implements an 802.11a transmitter which uses HDL synthesizable models from Hardware Design library and XilinxIPIntegrator models to generate 802.11a transmitted signal. The transmitted signal can be demodulated by VSA 89600B and the transmitter can be used to generate HDL codes and implement on Nallatech Virtex-4 XtremeDSP Development Kit.

 

2. This example uses XilinxIPIntegrator to leverage FFT and FIFO IP core generated by Xilinx CORE Generator. In order to use XilinxIPIntegrator, you must install Xilinx ISE and ModelSim. Besides, you need compile Xilinx Simulation Libraries for ModelSim in advance. Please refer to document of XilinxIPIntegrator for details.

 

3. Before starting to simulate and generate HDL codes, you need generate FFT and FIFO IP core using CORE Generator at first as the generated IP cores are not included in the example folder.

 

4. The steps of generating FFT IP core:

        i) Double click model X1 in subnetwork wlan_11a_OFDM_symbol_gen and input a writable path in XilinxIPIntegrator GUI for IP generation.

        ii) Click Launch CORE Generator to open CORE Generator GUI.

        iii) In CORE Generator GUI, click Project -> Project Options and configure FPGA part as: Virtex4 / xc4vsx35 / ff668 / -10

        iv) In CORE Generator GUI, click Project -> Import Existing Customized IP and select xfft_v7_1_r4.xco that is located in this example folder.

        v) Click Generate on the FFT IP core GUI to generate this IP core.

        vi) After the IP core is generated, click "Update IP Information in Selected Path" in XilinxIPIntegrator GUI of X1 model to update the generated IP core to SystemVue.

 

You can follow the same flow to generate FIFO IP core. It uses fifo_generator_v8_1.xco parameters settings to generate this IP core.

 

5. After generating FFT and FIFO IP cores, you can run simulation and observe constellation and EVM with VSA 89600B.

 

6. A HDL Code Generator "Nallatech_V4" has been configured to generate the ISE project for implementing the 802.11a transmitter on Nallatech Virtex-4 XtremeDSP Development Kit, you can use it to generate bit file.

For details of the Nallatech Virtex-4 XtremeDSP Development Kit, please refer to: http://www.nallatech.com/Development-Kits/virtex-4-xtremedsp-development-kit.html 

 

7. You can set system clock frequency as 80MHz for Nallatech Virtex-4 XtremeDSP Development Kit and use osc_clock.bit located in the example folder to program the Virtex2 FPGA on the Nallatech FPGA board and use the generated bit file from this example to program the Virtex4 FPGA on the Nallatech FPGA board. Then the I and Q baseband analog signals will be outputted from DAC1 and DAC2 ports of the Nallatech Virtex-4 XtremeDSP Development Kit.

Workspace.Name: M9703_FPGA_Design_Template
Workspace.Description:
M9703 Design Template

 

This workspace is the design template for M9703 8-channels digitizer FPGAs development. You can start M9703 FPGAs design from this workspace.

 

You just need drag and drop subnetwork "M9703_TEMPLATE" to a schematic and double click it to open its GUI. Then you can define the FPGAs interface on the GUI. After that, you just need edit subnetwork "M9703_FPGAx" for the corresponding FPGA on M9703A, where x is 0, 1, 2, 3.

 

Except subnetworks "M9703_FPGA0" ~ "M9703_FPGA3", the other subnetworks are pre-defined well. So please don't modify them.

 

The output of the subnetwork "M9703_TEMPLATE" is a pair of signals for each FPGA:

        FPGAx_DataOut

        FPGAx_ValidOut

FPGAx_DataOut is only valid when the correspond FPGAx_ValidOut is 1. A subnetwork "ValidExtract" is provided in "Auxiliary_Subnets" folder of the workspace to help you to extract valid FPGAx_DataOut only. Then you can connect the extracted data with the float-point models. As Dynamic Data Flow is used in subnetwork "ValidExtract", please note the limitation of Dynamic Data Flow. For details of Dynamic Data Flow, please refer to documentation: Home > Simulation > Data Flow > Introduction to Dynamci Data Flow Simulation.

 

In "Auxiliary_Subnets" folder of workspace tree, there are another two subnets ADCConvert_16To8 and ADCConvert_32To16. They can help you to convert parallel ADC input bus with ADCValid (one valid ADC input data every two samples) to parallel ADC input bus without ADCValid (all samples are valid). They can be used in M9703_FPGA0 ~ M9703_FPGA3 subnets.

ADCConvert_16To8 is used for Normal, all 8 channels mode. For example, ADC input for FPGA0 is that ADC(0:15) is from IN1 and ADC(16:31) is from IN2. In addition, ADCValid is alternate 0 and 1. You can connect ADC(0:15) and ADCValid to input ports of ADCConvert_16To8 subnet and connect this subnet's output to a bus with width of 8. Then you can get 8 parallel ADC input for IN1 and all samples are valid. In the same manner, you can use another ADCConvert_16To8 subnet for IN2.

 

ADCConvert_32To16 is used for Interleaved, 1+3+5+7 or Interleaved, 2+4+6+8 mode. For example, in Interleaved, 1+3+5+7 mode, ADC input for FPGA0 is that ADC(0:31) is from IN1 and ADCValid is alternate 0 and 1. You can connect ADC(0:31) and ADCValid to input ports of ADCConvert_32To16 subnet and connect this subnet's output to a bus with width of 16. Then you can get 16 parallel ADC input for IN1 and all samples are valid. In the same manner, you can use ADCConvert_32To16 subnet for IN2 in Interleaved, 2+4+6+8 mode.

Workspace.Name: M9703_MultiChannels_Calibration_InterFPGA
Workspace.Description:
Multi-Channels Calibration using SystemVue M9703 FPGA Design Flow

 

This workspace is an example that uses SystemVue M9703 FPGA design flow to calibrate magnitude and phase of M9703's two channels. It works for both M9703A and M9703B. The instruments connection is shown in "Design3 (Schematic)" and you can connection all instruments accordingly. Then you can run the simulation from Step1 to Step5 to do software simulation, download calibration reference signal to M8190 AWG and calibrate M9703 8-channels digitizer. You can observe the calibration results from the three figures:

 

DF1_Design3_I1:                          Time domain waveforms of reference channel and calibration channel

DF1_Design3_mag_factor3:      Magnitude ratio between reference channel and calibration channel  ( Magnitude(IN1) / Magnitude(IN3) )

DF1_Design3_phase_factor3:   Phase difference between reference channel and calibration channel; unit: degree  ( Phase(IN1) - Phase(IN3) )

 

In this example, the NCO generates the fixed 320MHz IF sine and cosine waveforms and the calibration reference waveform is for 100MHz bandwidth calibration. So this example can calibrate IN3 channel aligned to IN1 channel in frequency range 270MHz ~ 370MHz. The calibration reference waveform is generated in subent "freq_sequence". For the other IF frequency and bandwidth, it can be implemented based on this example.

 

The FPGA design for FPGA0 and FPGA1 of M9703A are the same, but we can configure different calibration FIR coefficients to their BlockRegisters. The diagram of FPGA design is shown in subnet "M9703_FPGA0".

 

It needs that this workspace is in a writable directory to download waveform to M8190. So if you installed this example wordspace in a read-only directory, you need save this workspace in a writable directory and then run the simulations step by step.

 

Calibration Instruction:

 

Step1:     

It's software simulaiton mode. Run simulaton and observe the magnitude ratio and phase difference, which should match what we set in S3 and S8 SineGen models. We generate 330MHz sine waveform with S8 for IN1 channel and set its magnitude as 1.1*625mV and phase as 0 degree. We generate 330MHz sine waveform with S3 for IN3 channel and set its magnitude as 625mV and phase as 5 degree.

 

So the expected simulation results are almost 1.1 in figure "DF1_Design3_mag_factor3" and almost 5 degree in figure "DF1_Design3_phase_factor3" when we bypass calibration FIR filters for both IN1 and IN3 channels. Then it means our design can detect the difference of magnitude and phase for two channels correctly. The software simulation results should prove that our FXP design meets our expection.

 

Then we can open  "HDL Code Generator1" to run the FPGA bit file generation flow. It will take about 2 hours to generate the FPGA programming file. A generated FPGA image folder has been placed in this example directory.

 

Step2:

Run the simulation. It will download calibration reference waveform (sine waveforms sequence) to M8190 for measurement.

 

Note: You have to launch M8190 Firmware before run this simulation, then SystemVue can connect with M8190 instrument. In addition, you should find the socket port number from the launched M8190 Firmware and fill the socket port number as parameter "SecAddress" of M8190 download model. For example, you may find "SCPI Access (Socket): TCPIP0::localhost::60005::SOCKET" from the launched M8190 Firmware, then you need set "SecAddress" of M8190 download model as 60005. Otherwise, when you run this simulation at Step2, SystemVue will post an error to tell that it can't connect with M8190 instrument.

 

Step3:  

In Design3 Schematic, open M9703CosimBus model's customUI and input your own generated FPGA Image folder path (or the pre-generated FPGA image folder in the example directory) and select your own connected M9703 address.

    

Run the simulation. It will ask M9703 to capture raw IQ output from reference channel and calibration channel. Observe the three results figures for magnitude/phase difference and waveform of I path output. They will show the IQ imbalance before the calibration.

 

After the simulation is over,  the equation of this example will extract the raw IQ data and calculate the coefficients of FIR compensation filter. It will be executed automatically in background.

 

Step4:  

Run the simulation. It will download a LFM (Linear Frequency Modulation) signal to M8190. The LFM signal will cover all frequency components of our bandwidth (270MHz ~ 370MHz). Then we can use the extracted compensation coefficients for the LFM signal to observe the calibration performance for the whole bandwidth.

 

Step5:  

Run the simulation. It will ask M9703 to capture calibrated IQ output from reference channel and calibration channel. And the current input signal for M9703 is LFM signal. Observe the three results figures for magnitude/phase difference and waveforms of I path output. Now the magnitude/phase difference should be very small and the time domain waveforms of reference and calibration channels should match very well.

 

 

 

 

 

DDC HDL Code Generation using Xilinx Vivado HLS Tool

 

In this example design, the DDC is designed using Xilinx Vivado HLS tool. We provide the C source code and directive file in the example folder. So you can modify the C source code to generate HDL codes to support different bandwidth for multi-channels calibration.

 

Under the multi-channels calibration example directory "Examples\Hardware Design\M9703_FDK\Multi_Channels_Calibration", the C source code files are placed in folder "cali_ddc_HLS\C_SourceCode". The top level files are "DownResample.cpp" and "DownResample.h". You can create a Vivado HLS project and add all files in "cali_ddc_HLS\C_SourceCode" folder as "Source" and set the top function as "DownResample".

 

The directive file is placed in folder "cali_ddc_HLS\Directives". Use this directive file in your Vivado HLS project, then you can generate your own HDL codes.

 

The pre-generated VHDL files are placed in folder "cali_ddc_HLS\vhdl" and the pre-generated FPGA programming files are placed in folder "M9703_MultiCh_Cali". The VHDL files and FPGA programming files are generated for default 3 stages halfband filters setting. The default target bandwidth for calibration is 100MHz. You can use the pre-generated VHDL files for HDL cosimulation in Step1 and use the pre-generated FPGA programming files for M9703A hardware cosimulation in Step3 and Step5 directly for the default setting.

 

If you want to modify the DDC to different settings, you can open "DownResample.h" to adjust the number of HALFBANDSTAGENUM to change the halfband filters stages.

When HALFBANDSTAGENUM =1, only one halfband filter is used, the sample rate of compensation filter is 800MHz and the target calibration bandwidth is 400MHz.

When HALFBANDSTAGENUM =2, two halfband filters are used, the sample rate of compensation filter is 400MHz and the target calibration bandwidth is 200MHz.

When HALFBANDSTAGENUM =3, three halfband filters are used, the sample rate of compensation filter is 200MHz and the target calibration bandwidth is 100MHz. (Default settings)

Then you can run "Synthesis" of your own created Vivado HLS project to generate HDL files. Then you can use HDL model of SystemVue to wrap up your generated HDL files as a model and do HDL cosimulation in M9703 Template design subnet to verify its function. After that, you can run the automatic FPGA programming file generation flow to get the final FPGA programming files to run with M9703 hardware.

You can use the pre-generated VHDL files for HDL cosimulation in Step1 and use the pre-generated FPGA programming files for M9703A hardware cosimulation in Step3 and Step5 directly for the default setting.

 

If you want to modify the DDC to different settings, you can open "DownResample.h" to adjust the number of HALFBANDSTAGENUM to change the halfband filters stages.

When HALFBANDSTAGENUM =1, only one halfband filter is used, the sample rate of compensation filter is 800MHz and the target calibration bandwidth is 400MHz.

When HALFBANDSTAGENUM =2, two halfband filters are used, the sample rate of compensation filter is 400MHz and the target calibration bandwidth is 200MHz.

When HALFBANDSTAGENUM =3, three halfband filters are used, the sample rate of compensation filter is 200MHz and the target calibration bandwidth is 100MHz. (Default settings)

Then you can run "Synthesis" of your own created Vivado HLS project to generate HDL files. Then you can use HDL model of SystemVue to wrap up your generated HDL files as a model and do HDL cosimulation in M9703 Template design subnet to verify its function. After that, you can run the automatic FPGA programming file generation flow to get the final FPGA programming files to run with M9703 hardware.

Workspace.Name: M9703_real_time_2x2_MIMO_Using_M8190
Workspace.Description:
Real-time 2x2 MIMO Receiver Implemented on M9703's FPGA

 

This example uses SystemVue and M9703A or M9703B FPGA flow to design and implement a 2x2 MIMO receiver on M9703's FPGA based on 802.11ac standard. Going through this example can help you to understand SystemVue and U5303A FPGA flow better, especially how to use SystemVue Hardware Design Library, Xilinx IP cores and handcrafted HDL codes together to create a complicated design, and then simulate and implement the complicated design on M9703's open FPGA. In addition, it's a realistic example of MIMO receiver, you can add your own algorithm implementation based on this example to create your own MIMO receiver.

 

1. FPGA Design and Simulation for M9703's open FPGA

The first step of SystemVue and M9703 FPGA flow is the design and software simulation to test and debug your FPGA design.

 

You can review Schematic "Design2" for the top level design of FPGA entry and simulation. It uses WLAN_11ac_Source@WLAN 11ac Models from WLAN 11ac library to generate 2x2 MIMO transmitted signal. The 2x2 MIMO receiver FPGA design is in subnet M9703_FPGA0 of U5303A Design Template. In subnet M9703_FPGA0, DDC, synchronization and CE & MIMO Demapper are implemented by HDL codes that are generated using Xilinx Vivado HLS. These HDL codes are wrapped up with HDL Model and integrated into SystemVue graphic design. FFT is implemented using Xilinx CoreGenerator and integrated into SystemVue graphic design using XilinxIPIntegrator Model.

 

You can run "Design2 Analysis" for software simulation to verify this FPGA design. You can observe the demodulated constellation in "HDL_Cosim_Constellation".

Note: when you run "Design2 Analysis", SystemVue calls ModelSim for HDL co-simulation. ModelSim GUI will be launched to show waveform of CE & MIMO Demapper HDL code simulation. You need input run -all in ModelSim console to start the HDL simulation.

 

You can also import your own HDL codes to this design and embedded your own algorithm to this real-time MIMO receiver.

 

2. FPGA Programming File Automatic Generation for M9703's open FPGA

After software simulation results is ok, you can open HDL Code Generator1 and just click Generate to launch a fully automatic flow to generate the final FPGA programming file for U5303A.

 

3. Co-simulation between SystemVue and M9703 Hardware to verify the FPGA design

After M9703 FPGA programming file is generated, you can do the co-simulation between SystemVue and U5303A hardware to verify your FPGA function. And also, you can use SystemVue to generate 802.11ac 2x2 MIMO signal and download to M8190 AWG in the same design.

 

You can review Schematic "Design1" for the top level design of co-simulation between SystemVue and U5303A hardware.

  (1) Hardware connection

You should connect M8190's DIRECT OUT of channel 1and 2 to M9703's IN1 and IN2 respectively.

 

  (2) Parameter Settings

You should open Parameters tab of Design1 Schematic to specify some parameters for your hardware configuration, such as your M8190 and M9703 addresses and your M9703 FPGA programming file directory.

 

  (3) Run procedure

i) Download 802.11ac 2x2 MIMO waveform to M8190:

Open Design1 Schematic. Drag the slider bar Modulation Mode to your desired modulation, and drag the slider bar Simulation Mode to Download Waveform to M8190. Then run Design1 Analysis.

 

ii) Run the real-time demodulation on M9703 FPGA and display the constellation:

Drag the slider bar Simulation Mode to Real-time Demod with M9703 and run Design1 Analysis. Then you can observe the dynamic constellation.

Workspace.Name: U5303A_FPGA_Design_Template
Workspace.Description:
U5303A Design Template

 

This workspace is the design template for U5303A 2-channels digitizer FPGAs development. You can start U5303A FPGAs design from this workspace.

 

You just need drag and drop subnetwork "U5303_TEMPLATE" to a schematic and double click it to open its GUI. Then you can define the FPGAs interface on the GUI. After that, you just need edit subnetwork "U5303_FPGA0" for the corresponding FPGA on U5303A.

 

Except subnetworks "U5303_FPGA0", the other subnetworks are pre-defined well. So please don't modify them.

 

The output of the subnetwork "U5303_TEMPLATE" is a pair of signals for each FPGA:

        FPGA0_DataOut

        FPGA0_ValidOut

FPGA0_DataOut is only valid when the correspond FPGA0_ValidOut is 1. A subnetwork "ValidExtract" is provided in "Auxiliary_Subnets" folder of the workspace to help you to extract valid FPGA0_DataOut only. Then you can connect the extracted data with the float-point models. As Dynamic Data Flow is used in subnetwork "ValidExtract", please note the limitation of Dynamic Data Flow. For details of Dynamic Data Flow, please refer to documentation: Home > Simulation > Data Flow > Introduction to Dynamci Data Flow Simulation.

 

In "Auxiliary_Subnets" folder of workspace tree, there are another two subnets ADCConvert_16To8 and ADCConvert_32To16. They can help you to convert parallel ADC input bus with ADCValid (one valid ADC input data every two samples) to parallel ADC input bus without ADCValid (all samples are valid). They can be used in U5303_FPGA0 subnet.

ADCConvert_16To8 is used for Normal, 2 channels mode. For example, ADC input for FPGA0 is that ADC(0:15) is from IN1 and ADC(16:31) is from IN2. In addition, ADCValid is alternate 0 and 1. You can connect ADC(0:15) and ADCValid to input ports of ADCConvert_16To8 subnet and connect this subnet's output to a bus with width of 8. Then you can get 8 parallel ADC input for IN1 and all samples are valid. In the same manner, you can use another ADCConvert_16To8 subnet for IN2.

 

ADCConvert_32To16 is used for Interleaved, channel 1 or Interleaved, channel 2 mode. For example, in Interleaved, channel 1 mode, ADC input for FPGA0 is that ADC(0:31) is from IN1 and ADCValid is alternate 0 and 1. You can connect ADC(0:31) and ADCValid to input ports of ADCConvert_32To16 subnet and connect this subnet's output to a bus with width of 16. Then you can get 16 parallel ADC input for IN1 and all samples are valid. In the same manner, you can use ADCConvert_32To16 subnet for IN2 in Interleaved, channel 2 mode.

Workspace.Name: ESG MIMO Configuration Example
Workspace.Description:
ESG MIMO Configuration Example

Keysight Technologies SystemVue2008 Example Workspace

 

What you need to know before executing this example

       How to create and execute a Data Flow simulation in SystemVue2008.

 

What does this example do

        Execution of this example with 2 Keysight Signal Synthesizer such as ESG E4438C's will generate synchronized 2 RF signals for MIMO applications. both master and the slave E4438C's will generate a -25dBm CW signal at 2.002GHz with a 0.5uS pulse coming out of Event1 trigger output.

What HW does this example support

      2 Keysight ESG E4438C's. Make sure the EVENT 2 output of the master E4438C is connected to the PATT TRIG IN of both the master and slave.

 

How to execute this example

     You can execute the example as is, but it will NOT communicate to the HW.  To communicate to the HW, follow these steps:

     (1) Modify parameters of both "Master" and "Slave" SignalDownloader_E4438C parts in the shcematic: Change the "HWAvailable" to YES, and change the "PrimAddress" parameter to the Tcpip address of the corresponding E4438C instrument. 

    (2) Execute the simulation.

 

   How to find the Tcpip address: For ESG E4428C, you can find the Tcpip address of the instrument by following thess button clicks: Utility => GPIB/RS-232/LAN => LAN Setup and take the IP Address.  Also note that the 5025 secondary address ("SecAddress" parameter) is the designated Tcpip port for Keysight instruments.

 

Theory of Operation

    This example uses two Sine Wave Generators that are different only in the initial phase of 90 degrees to create coherent 2MHz sine and cosine baseband IQ signals. The generated IQ signals feed the I and Q inputs of the modulator that has a carrier frequency of 2GHz.  Hence the output of the modulator is simply a 2.002GHz CW signal, which goes into the HW and generates a physical 2.002GHz CW signal.

    The Event1 trigger is created with 25 samples duration (starting at the very first sample).  At 50MHz sample rate, this results in a pulse width of 0.5uS.

Workspace.Name: ESG SignalDownloader Example
Workspace.Description:
ESG Signal Downloader Example

Keysight Technologies SystemVue2008 Example Workspace

 

What you need to know before executing this example

       How to create and execute a Data Flow simulation in SystemVue2008.

 

What does this example do

        Execution of this example with an Keysight Signal Synthesizer such as ESG E4438C or MXG N5182A will generate a -25dBm CW signal at 2.002GHz with a 0.5uS pulse coming out of Event1 trigger output. 

What HW does this example support

      Keysight ESG E4438C or MXG N5182A.

 

How to execute this example

     You can execute the example as is, but it will NOT communicate to the HW.  To communicate to the HW, follow these steps:

     (1) Modify parameters of SignalDownloader_E4438C part "E4438C" in the shcematic: Change the "HWAvailable" to YES, and change the "PrimAddress" parameter to the Tcpip address of your ESG/MXG instrument. 

    (2) Execute the simulation.

    (3) It takes less than 20 Seconds to simulate and another 30 Seconds or so to download the generated 2.5M I/Q waveform sample pairs into the instrument. (The actual downloading time may vary depending on your LAN traffic). 

 

   How to find the Tcpip address: For ESG E4428C, you can find the Tcpip address of the instrument by following thess button clicks: Utility => GPIB/RS-232/LAN => LAN Setup and take the IP Address.  Also note that the 5025 secondary address ("SecAddress" parameter) is the designated Tcpip port for Keysight instruments.

 

Important Note about the HW

    Depending on the options installed in the Instrument, you might have different waveform memory available.  If you generate a waveform with tens of Mega I/Q samples, make sure your HW has enough waveform memory to hold the waveform. 

 

Theory of Operation

    This example uses two Sine Wave Generators that are different only in the initial phase of 90 degrees to create coherent 2MHz sine and cosine baseband IQ signals. The generated IQ signals feed the I and Q inputs of the modulator that has a carrier frequency of 2GHz.  Hence the output of the modulator is simply a 2.002GHz CW signal, which goes into the HW and generates a physical 2.002GHz CW signal.

    The Event1 trigger is created with 25 samples duration (starting at the very first sample).  At 50MHz sample rate, this results in a pulse width of 0.5uS.

Workspace.Name: Integrating_SV_with_instruments
Workspace.Description:
App Note: Connecting SystemVue to
RF signal sources and analyzers

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Tutorial Workspace

 

 

This example workspace is intended for use with SystemVue Application Note 5990-7757EN, which leads you through the steps to connect test equipment to SystemVue, and also provides some configuration reference tables.  This app note and other resources are available online at http://www.keysight.com/find/eesof-systemvue-dvt.

 

In this application note, you will

  • Create a modulated waveform using SystemVue
  • Download the waveform to an external RF signal source
  • Capture a real waveform from an RF signal analyzer, as a stumulus for further processing in SystemVue
  • Display and analyze the final processed waveform using the Keysight VSA software.

For this, you will need

  • App Note -  http://literature.cdn.keysight.com/litweb/pdf/5990-7757EN.pdf
  • Source - An Keysight E4438C ESG, or M5182 MXG, or similar Keysight RF source.
  • Analyzer - An Keysight N9030A PXA, MXA, or similar Keysight RF analyzer
  • VSA software - the 89600A/B VSA software, with option 105, and either option 200 or 300.  If you don't own the 89600 VSA software but would like a free 14-day trial license, visit http://www.keysight.com/find/89600B and click on "14-day licensing" and follow the instructions.

% CUT & PASTE THIS MATLAB SOURCE CODE INTO AN
% EQUATION OBJECT, USING MATLAB 2014A/2014B MODE, THEN RUN IT, TO PLOT THE S.A. TRACE

%

% create and bring to front figure number 1

figure(1)

% Plot trace data vs sweep point index
plot(1:nr_points,data)
% Adjust the x limits to the nr of points
% and the y limits for 100 dB of dynamic range
xlim([1 nr_points])
%ylim([ref_lev-100 ref_lev])
% activate the grid lines
grid on
title('Swept SA trace')
xlabel('Point index')
ylabel('Amplitude (dBm)')

Workspace.Name: M933x Signal Downloader Example
Workspace.Description:
M933x Arbitrary Waveform Generator Downloader Example

Keysight Technologies SystemVue 

Tutorial Workspace

 

This example demonstrates how you can download an I/Q signal to M9330 arbitrary waveform generator.

 

What do you need to know before running the example?

In default, the example is running in simulate mode. In order to connect to the real hardware, you need to follow the follow steps to make it run.

  • Make sure the M933x IVI driver installed properly.
  • Fill the instrument address as the real address. You can find the instrument address through Keysight IO Connection Expert.
  • Uncheck the simulate button.

Data Collection Mode

SignalDownloader_M933xA can collect the data in Time mode or Samples mode. If the design has no time specification, Sample mode should be used.

 

Resample

M933x's internal clock frequency is 1.25GHz. If the signal's sample rate is not equal to 1.25GHz, resampling method is provided in the signal downloader model. Alpha parameter is used for this purpose. Range of Alpha value is 0-1.0. The typical value is 0.8.

Workspace.Name: MXG MIMO Configuration Example
Workspace.Description:
MXG MIMO Configuration Example

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

What you need to know before executing this example

       How to create a Data Flow simulation and execute it using MATLAB Script in SystemVue.

 

What does this example do

        Execution of this example with 2 Keysight Signal Synthesizer such as MXG N5182A's will generate synchronized 2 RF signals for MIMO applications. Both the master and slave N5182A's will generate a -25dBm CW signal at 2.002GHz with the slave having a 0.5uS pulse coming out of Event 1 trigger output (which can be used to trigger measurement equipments).

 

What HW does this example support

      2 Keysight MXG N5182A's. Make sure the EVENT 1 output of the master N5182A is connected to the PAT TRIG IN of the slave.

 

How to execute this example

     You can execute the example as is, but it will NOT communicate to the HW.  To communicate to the HW, edit the "MXG_MIMO ~A" equation scripts as following:

    (1) Set "HW_Available = 1", and IP_Master, IP_Slave to their corresponding IP address, and IP_Slaves to include all slae's IPs seperated by semi-colon.

    (2) Click the "Go" button in the Equation editor to execute the equation script.

 

   How to find the Tcpip address: For N5182A, you can find the Tcpip address of the instrument by following thess button clicks: Utility => I/O Config => LAN Setup and take the IP Address.  Also note that the 5025 secondary address ("SecAddress" parameter) is the designated Tcpip port for Keysight instruments.

 

Theory of Operation

    This example uses two Sine Wave Generators that are different only in the initial phase of 90 degrees to create coherent 2MHz sine and cosine baseband IQ signals. The generated IQ signals feed the I and Q inputs of the modulator that has a carrier frequency of 2GHz.  Hence the output of the modulator is simply a 2.002GHz CW signal, which goes into the HW and generates a physical 2.002GHz CW signal.

    The Event1 trigger is created with 25 samples duration (starting at the very first sample).  At 50MHz sample rate, this results in a pulse width of 0.5uS.

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Examples

 

What you need to know before executing this example

       How to create and execute a Data Flow simulation in SystemVue and how to use CommandExpertLink.

 

What does this example do

        Executing DF1 (for LTE_FDD_UL_SRC schematic ) will create LTE FDD modulated RF signal at 2GHz carrier frequency using an Keysight ESG E4438C, or an N5182A or PSG. 

 

       Execute DF3 (for LTE_FDD_UL_CEReceiver) using an MXA N9020A will bring measurement data captured back into simulation for demodulation and get the BLER/Throughtput.

 

What HW does this example support

      One Keysight RF synthesizer such as ESG E4438C, PSG, MXG N5182A and one MXA N9020A. Connect RF output of the synthesizer to the RF input of the MXA, connect the EVENT 1 marker of RF synthesizer to the Trigger 1 input of the MXA, and connect the 10 MHZ reference between the two instruments as recommended by instrument documentation.

 

How to execute this example

    (1) Open the E4438C Signal Downloader part ("S11") in LTE_FDD_UL_SRC and change it "Primary Address" to the IP address of the RF synthesizer (make sure the RF synthesizer is connected to the LAN).

    (2) Execute the simulation DF1 to generate modulated RF signal.

    (3) Open the CommandExperLink ("C1") part in LTE_FDD_UL_CEReceiver and use "Select Instruments..." to select the RF synthesizer and MXA you have.

    (4) Execute simulation DF3 and it should measure 0% BLER (100% Tthroughtput).

    (5) Execute Sweep1, it will do a power sweep of 3 power levels on RF synthesizer and  

measure the corresponding BLER/Throughput accordingly.

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Template Workspace

 

 

This template is a simple example of a LTE FDD workspace that can be used as a starting point to create more complicated designs. 

LTE FDD system test

Two designs are provided

LTE_TDD_UL_SRC Design for generating LTE FDD system test data

This design is to demo how to generate LTE FDD test data.  In the design, a LTE FDD transmitter is included and the simulation data is generated.  A SignaldownloadE4438C is used to link to the Keysight E4438C signal generator.  Before running the simulation please make sure that the IP address for the signal generator is set right. In the test case, VSA software is not right tool to demod, decode, deframe the data.  We need a receiver from systemVue to recover the original data.

This design is to demo how to recover the LTE FDD test data.  In the design, a VSA source model is used to capture the test data from MXA/PSA/VSA/Scope/PXA and then send the data to a LTE FDD receiver.   For receiver measurements, VSA software is not right tool to demod, decode, deframe the data.  We need the LTE FDD receiver from systemVue to recover the original data. The Throughput, BLER can be measured using this design.

Workspace.Name: LTE_Advanced_DL_SISO_BER
Workspace.Description:
LTE_A_DL_SISO_BER

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This example workspace demonstrates open loop BER measurements of LTE-Advanced downlink SISO system in AWGN environment. Besides simulation, system test designs have been implemented for both signal generation and BER measurement using LTE-A receiver.

 

MMSE channel estimation is employed to get the reference data set. The PSS Ra and SSS Ra are set to 10dB in order to get accurate timing and frequency synchronization in the low SNR AWGN channel. The bandwidth is 5MHz. The mapping type is QPSK. The code rate is 1/3. 1000 frames are simulated. The RB allocation type is selected as RB indices (2D) to avoid the overlap of RB allocation for PDSCH with PSS, SSS and PBCH.  

 

It should be noted that if there is overlap of PDSCH and PSS, SSS or PBCH. DMRS would not be transmitted on those RBs, then the channel estimation may be inaccurate and the PDSCH on those RBs may not be demodulated correctly.

LTE_Advanced_UL_SISO_BER

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This example workspace demonstrates open loop BER measurements for LTE Advanced uplink SISO in AWGN environment. Besides simulation, system test designs have been implemented for both signal generation and BER measurement using LTE-A receiver.

 

MMSE channel estimation and ideal timing and frequency synchronization is employed to get the reference data set. The bandwidth is 5MHz. All 25 RBs are allocated for PUSCH. The mapping type is QPSK. The code rate is 1/3. 500 frames are simulated.

 

To use ideal frequency and timing synchronization in AWGN channel, users can open the LTE_A_UL_Receiver model, find LTE_A_UL_TimeFreqSync model, set UseDesiredValue to 1:YES, then set DesiredDelay and DesiredFreq to the ideal timing index and frequency offset. For the default parameter configurations in this example, users can set DesiredDelay to 6 and DesiredFreq to 0.

Workspace.Name: M8190_Calibration
Workspace.Description:
M8190 Calibration using Scalar Signal and Vector Signal

 Keysight Technologies SystemVue Workspace

 

This example illustrates how to use Keysight PSA, MXA or PXA to calibrate M8190 AWG with multitone scalar signal and digital modulation vector signal source in Keysight SystemVue.  

 

M8190_Calibration workspace consists of two kind of calibrations (Multitone scalar calibration and Digital Modulation Vector calibration).

 

Forder Part1_Multitone_ScalarSig_Calibration consists several schematics for Multiton signal downloading, calibration to get amplitude response at each tone position, apply for these scalar calibration coefficients into multitone, radar and LTE as well as LTE-A carrier aggregation signal. In each schematic, pls make sure the calibrated file name in CalFileName parameter is same as Multitone_Calibration.

 

Open 01_Multitone_Gen folder, click MultiTones (Schematic) and make sure component F1 was shorten and run this schematic. Then run this schematic to start to  download multitone signal into M8190. You can modify Freq_Start, Freq_Stop, Freq_Step, Samplingrate and M8190_Add (M8190 IP address).

 

Open 02_Multitone_ScalarSig_Cal folder, click MultiTones_Calibration (Schematic) and run it to start to do calibration through PSA, MXA or PXA. You can modify Freq_Start, Freq_Stop, Freq_Step, Samplingrate, M8190_Add (M8190 IP address), SA_Add (Keysight Vector Signal Analyzer such as PSA, MXA or PXA) before calibration. Please make sure PSA, MXA or PXA is available through Keysight IO library before calibration.

 

Open 01_Multitone_Gen folder, click MultiTones (Schematic) and make component F1 active (not shorten) to apply for getting calibration coefficients in previous step. Then run this schematic to start to  download calibrated multitone signal into M8190. We can use PSA, MXA or PXA to see spectrum of calibrated multitone and compare the spectrum without calibration.

 

Open 03_LFM_Radar_ScalarSig floder, click Radar_Sigal (Schematic) and make sure component F1 was shorten and download LFM radar signal into M8190. Make Component F1 active to apply for getting calibration coefficients in previous step and download calibrated LFM radar into M8190. We can use PSA, MXA or PXA to see spectrum of calibrated multitone and compare the spectrum without calibration.

 

Open 04_LTE LTE_A_ScalarSig, similiar as LFM Radar example. We also can apply for calibration LTE/LTE-A DL or carrier aggregation source into M8910 and  see the perofmance after calibarted waveform.

 

Forder Part2_DigitalMod_VectorSig_Calibration consists several schematics for digital modulation (QPSK, 16-QAM and etc) signal downloading, calibration to get AWG or M8190 channel response, calculate calibration filter coefficients (or pre-equalizer coefficients) using above channel response, then apply for this pre-equalizer coefficients into digital modulation, radar and LTE as well as LTE-A carrier aggregation signal. This method needs VSA89600 softawre Digital Demod option and save both real and imaginary of channel response. In each schematic, pls make sure the calibrated file name in CalFileName parameter is same as VSA_ChannelResponse_Read.

 

Open 01_BaiscDigitalMod folder, click DigitalModulation_1CH (Schematic) and make sure component F3 was shorten and run this schematic. Then run this schematic to start to  download digital modulation signal into M8190. You can modify ModType, ModFreq, Filter_RollOff, Filter_Interpolation, SymRate, Download_SamplingRate and M8190_Add (M8190 IP address).

 

After downloading digital modulation signal into M8190, run VSA89600 software, Select Window-->Trace Layout-->Grid 2x3. VSA89600 will have six traces in screen. Select MeasSetup-->Measurement Type: Digital Demod, then set parameters in Format (such as Modulation Type, Symbol Rate, Points/Symbol, Result Length), Filter (such as Measurement Filter, Reference Filter and etc) and etc. Click Compensate, select Equalizer Filter, set Filter Length and Convergence, click Reset Equalizer to reset equalizer. In both Traces E and F, select Channel1-->Ch Frequency Response. E selects to show Real part of Ch Frequency Response and F selects to show Imaginary part of Ch Frequency Response.

 

After VSA89600 setting, come back SystemVue to open 02_DigitalMod_VectorSig_Cal folder, click VSA_ChannelResponse_Read (Schematic) and run it to start to do calibration through PSA, MXA or PXA. You can modify, VSA_Address (IP address of computer installed VSA89600 software), Socket which is the VSA89600 LAN Socket port number in VSA SCPI Configuration, CalFileName is the file name to save save channel frequency response gotten from VSA89600 software. Pls set the suitable file name to save estimated channel frequency response.

 

Open 01_BaiscDigitalMod folder, click DigitalModulation_1CH (Schematic) and make component F3 active and run this schematic. Then run this schematic to start to  download the pre-equalized digital modulation signal into M8190. The F3 will read calibrated channel frequency response and transfer it into time-domain calibrated coefficients or pre-equalized coefficients.

 

Open 03_LFM_Radar_VectorSig floder, click Radar_Sigal_VectorSig (Schematic) and make sure component F3 was shorten and download LFM radar signal into M8190. Make Component F3 active to apply for getting calibration coefficients in previous step and download calibrated LFM radar into M8190. We can use PSA, MXA or PXA to see spectrum of calibrated multitone and compare the spectrum without calibration.

 

Open 04_LTE LTE_A_VectorSig, similiar as LFM Radar example. We also can apply for calibration LTE/LTE-A DL or carrier aggregation source into M8910 and  see the perofmance after calibarted waveform.

Workspace.Name: M8192SyncMultipleM8190Envs
Workspace.Description:
Use M8192 to Synchronize Multiple M8190's

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

What you need to know before executing this example

       How to create a Data Flow simulation, how to use MATLAB Script and how to use M8190 downloaders.

 

What does this example do

        Execution of this example will generate 4 RF CW signals using DUC mode of two Keysight M8190 arbitrary waveform generators, and it will also use M8192 to synchronize M8190 waveforms playout in master-slave(s) relationship. Each of the two M8190's will generate one RF at 1.1 GHz and another RF at 2.2 GHz. 

 

How to leverage this example

        As shown in this example, waveform generation/downloading is completely seperated from synchronization operations. You can use the same Matlab Script and functions defined in this example for applications that use M8192 to synchronize master-slave(s) M8190's. Just follow the same steps described in section How to execute this example below with appropriate waveform generation/downloading design schematic.

 

What HW does this example support

      2 Keysight M8190's and 1 Keysight M8192.

 

Specific HW Configuration

        Make sure to connect M8192 and M8190's properly for msater-slave(s) operation. For example: identify the master M8190 and properly connect its "SYS Clk Out" to M8192's "SYS Clk In", connect M8192's "SYS Clk Outx" to each M8190's "SYS Clk In" and connect M8192's "Trigger Outx" to each M8190's "Trigger In".

 

How to execute this example

     You can execute DownloadAndConfigure MATLAB Script as is, but it will NOT communicate to the HW.

 

To communicate to the HW, follow these steps:

  1. Modify MATLAB Script Equations Configuration Parameters, set "WaveformTarget = WaveformTargets.HW", and update the VISA address and socket commnuication addess and port of M8192 and M8190's. 
    • Make sure to correctly identify the master M8190 based on HW connections. (Refer to Specific HW Configuration section for details).
    • You can find TcpIp socket address and VISA INSTR address from M8190's Firmware user interface. For example: the string TCPIP0::localhost::60007::SOCKET is the TcpIp socket address, and the string TCPIP0::localhost::inst2::INSTR is the VISA INSTR address. You may need to replace host name 'localhost" with M8190 host controller's IP address if you are not running SystemVue inside M8190 host controller. 
    • Note how these parameters are also used in configuring the parameters of the two M8190 downloaders in the design "CWs (Schematic)".
  2. Run DownloadAndConfigure MATLAB Script. The comments in this script describe the operation flow for HW synchronization. See the implementation of the MATLAB Script functions for instrument control commands involved.

Important Note: The functions provided here only performs M8192-based synchronization. If M8190 cross module desckew is needed, use the tools in M8190 SW to perform deskew.

 

Advanced Topic

     You can modify the MATLAB Script code that controls M8190 by following the steps below:

    • In the design of "SignalDownloader_M8190Env", mouse right on the "Sink" part and select "Edit Equations", modify the MATLAB Script code to control M8190
    • Go back to the original schematic that uses M8190 downloader, in the "Model:" field, remove "@Instruments Subnetwork Models" so that the local model is used.

        Execution of this example will generate 2 RF CW signals using DUC mode of two 1 channel Keysight M8190 arbitrary waveform generators, and it will also use M8192 to synchronize M8190 waveforms playout in master-slave(s) relationship. How to leverage this example

        As shown in this example, waveform generation/downloading is completely seperated from synchronization operations. Specific HW Configuration

        Make sure to connect M8192 and M8190's properly for msater-slave(s) operation. For example: identify the master M8190 and properly connect its "SYS Clk Out" to M8192's "SYS Clk In", connect M8192's "SYS Clk Outx" to each M8190's "SYS Clk In" and connect M8192's "Trigger Outx" to each M8190's "Trigger In".

Workspace.Name: Wideband_OFDM_M8195_Test
Workspace.Description:
M8195 Direct-to-IF download Example

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This example creates a 2GHz bandwidth OFDM signal at 5GHz, then resamples it as a true baseband signal.  It then downloads this high-sample rate waveform to the M8195 wideband AWG.  By directly generating a 5GHz IF signal, one stage of BB-IF upconversion is avoided, resulting in a cleaner EVM. 

 

Notes

  • An OFDM signal with a high creast factor is used to demonstrate the dynamic range of the AWG (and any digitizers and mm-wave up/down conversions).  This clipping-to-noisefloor rnage sets a minimum floor on the effective EVM of the mesaurement system.
  • By using a custom OFDM signal, the 89600 VSA software can provide the digital demod and EVM analysis.  The signal is essentially a manually generated "WiGIG-like" signal
  • You can execute the example as is, but it will NOT communicate to the HW.  To communicate to the HW, edit the "M8195 (Schematic)" design to set "HW_Available = YES", and PrimaryAddress to the IP address of the PC that controls the M8195.

Workspace.Name: SignalDownloaderM9381_MIMO
Workspace.Description:
M9381A Signal Downloader MIMO Example

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This example shows how to configure a 2 channels M9381A MIMO system.

 

Hardware Configuration:

The system consists of 2 M9381A PXI VSGs in a single M9018A PXI chassis, with M9036A controller. It is configured as follows:

M9381A #1:

-   M9311A in slot 2

-   M9310A in slot 4

-   M9301A in slot 5

M9300A in slot 10

M9381A #2:

-   M9311A in slot 15

-   M9310A in slot 17

-   M9301A in slot 18

The normal cables should be installed on the instruments. Additionally, the 100 MHz reference cables from M9300A to the M9301A synthesizers should all be equal length. 

 

Instructions for Running:

  1. Install Keysight M9381A and M9018A IVI-COM driver from http://www.keysight.com/find/adnivicomdrivers

 

 

  1. Modify parameters of SignalDownloader_M9381A part in the schematic: In the "General" page, uncheck the "Offline" to parameter, change the "Address" of Channel 1 to the address of your M9381A#1, change the "Address" Channel 2 to the address of your M9381A#2, In the "MIMO Configuration" page, change the Address of "Reference Settings" to the address of your M9300A, and change the Address of "Chassis Settings" to the address of your M9018A.
  2. Run Analyses

Please reference the online help for more information about using SignalDownloader_M9381A.

N5106A (PXB) Signal Downloader

Keysight Technologies SystemVue2008 Example Workspace

 

What additional SW do you need for this example

      Keysight N5106A PXB MIMO Receiver Tester SW.  You MUST have PXB SW running before you run this example.

 

What you need to know before executing this example

       How to create and execute a Data Flow simulation in SystemVue2008.

 

What does this example do

        Execution of this example will configre the PXB for 2 channels with waveforms and Event Markers. 

 

How to execute this example

    Click on the schematic and then click the "Run Analysis" button on the tool bar. 

 

Theory of Operation

    This example will configure 2 channels of the PXB.  It will provide a Sine/Cosine IQ waveform (chan1.bin) to one channel, and a Ramp/Ramp IQ waveform (chan2.bin) and set up the sampling rate for both channels. It will then set up Event1 marker for the Sine/Cosine IQ channel, and set EVENT1, EVENT3 and EVENT4 markers for the Ramp/Ramp IQ channel.  All markers are of 10 smaples duration starting from the 1st sample. 

  

Further Exploration

    You can load a PXB setup file if you have created one in PXB SW.

Workspace.Name: WNW_OFDM_TxRx_CS
Workspace.Description:
Widband Network Waveforms(WNW)

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Template Workspace

 

 

This template is a simple example of a WNW Milcom workspace that can be used as a starting point to create more complicated designs.

 

WNW sytem simulation

WNW_OFDM_Rx Design for WNW simulation

This design is for demo how to use SystemVue OFDM libraryz to create a customized MilCom System. In the design, WNW transmitter, receiver and channel are included.  Unlike WiMax or LTE comertial systems the frame structure of the system is different.  Using WiMax and LTE solutions the measurements are not good enough to show the system performance.  The data displays shopw the design works very good.

WNW sytem test

Two designs are provided

WNW_OFDM_SRC Design for generating WNW system test data

This design is for demo how to generate WNW test data.  In the design, a WNW transmitter is included and the simulation data is generated.  A SignaldownloadE4438C is used to link to the Keysight E4438C signal generator.  Before run the simulation please make sure that the IP address for the signal generator is set right. Since this is a WNW signal, VSA software is not right tool to demod, decode, deframe the data.  We need a receiver from systemVue to recover the original data.

WNW_OFDM_VSA Design for recovering the original WNW data

This design is for demo how to recover the WNW test data.  In the design, a VSA source model is used to capture the test data from MXA/PSA/VSA/Scope/PXA and then send the data to a WNW receiver.   Since this is a WNW signal, VSA software is not right tool to demod, decode, deframe the data.  We need the WNW receiver from systemVue to recover the original data. The BER can be measured using this design.

Workspace.Name: UWB_Radar_Test
Workspace.Description:
RADAR System Simulation

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Workspace

 

This workspace provides an example for UWB Radar signal generation.

With unique advantages of high accuracy for target detection, high fidelity for precision with penetration and low cost for combining radar and communication systems, the Ultra Wideband (UWB) Radar is very popular in both commercial and defense industries.  To design and test the new UWB radar systems, different signal sources, target environment setup, signal processing and measurements are needed.  A platform is proposed for designing and testing UWB Radar. In the platform, SystemVue Integrated Test Solution (ITS) is used with Keysight Wideband Signal Source (81180A/81190A, M9390), Vector Signal Source PSG, Wideband Vector Signal Analyzer and High Performance Scope (90000/90000X series) and form a UWB component tester in which different UWB signals can be generated in SystemVue, send to wideband arbitrary waveform generator as hardware component test signal.  Also, different measurements are available in the platform.  The example shows that this platform can be used not only for UWB transmitter but also for receiver troubleshooting and test purpose. 

  • Top level design
    A linear FM signal source in the Radar library is used for modeling the UWB Radar signal.  The UWB environment model is used for the Radar detection environments setup. Then, we download the UWB signal from SystemVue to Keysight 81180A AWG through the SignalDownloader_81180 in which you should check the parameter PrimeAddress and set it to the address of your 81180A.   By using the AWG signal, the test signal can be connected to a Wideband PSG for RF UWB signal.  Then, you can use an Infiniium Scope 90K or a PXI VSA M9392 to measure the UWB signal. 
  • The recommended equipment list with options

·         DSOX93204A 32 GHz Digital Signal Oscilloscope with Options:

·         -            02G  2Gpts/ch memory

·         -            062  MATLAB Standard Digital Package

·         -            010  User Defined Function          

·         81180A Arbitrary Waveform Generator with Options:

·         -            264  Two channel 64M points memory

·         -            (2) F4G  Reconstruction filter set for 4Gsa/s, 1 channel          

·         89600 A/AN VSA Software with Options:

·         -            200  Basic Vector Signal Analysis

·         -            300  Hardware Connectivity

·         -            AYA  Vector Modulation Analysis         

·         E8267D  PSG Vector Signal Generator with Options:

·         -            520 or 532  Frequency range from 250 kHz to 20 GHz or 31.8 GHz

·         -            016  Wideband differential external I/Q inputs

·         -            H18 Wideband modulation less than 3.2 GHz For detailed information on the UWB test setup please read the document, UWB_Radar_Setup.doc.

Detailed information about the UWB test system setup can be found in the UWB_Radar_Setup.doc in the DIR, Examples\Instruments\Radar\.

 

 This example can be used as a template for generating custom waveforms.   Users can open these models and modify it as needed to create custom models for their own waveforms in the system simulation and testing.

Workspace.Name: EW_8_Emitters
Workspace.Description:
EW Receiver Test Signal Generation using Sequencer

Keysight Technologies SystemVue 

 

Required Softwares

Make sure you have installed Keysight IO Library Version 15 (or up) and Keysight Connection Expert softwares. SystemVue 2013.01 (or up) product.

 

This example shows how to generate a EW Receiver test signal using sequencer and play them out in M8190A or M9381A.

 

1. Run all Analysis by clcicking on Run Analysis -> Run all Analysis to generate four Radar signals and four Milcome signals at different carrier frequency of 1.3, 1.37, 1.48, 1.52, 1.54, 1.56, 1.6, and 1.69 GHz.

2. Open the Waveform Sequnce Composer UI by click on the  "WaveformSeq1"

Note under "Pattern" tab the sequence is composed from the waveform data at each corrresponding dataset.

3. Connect SystemVue to M8190A

·         Go to "Instrument" tab. Type the IP address of the M8190 instrument into the "Address" cell of in the table under "Instruments Selection" area.  As an alternative, you can click the "Select Instruments..." button to pick the instrument if it has been added into the "Keysight Connection Expert", or add it in the "Select Instruments" dialog.

Note that we encountered two cases

·         Old firmware for example 2.1.0.0 or early: 

We only see one string M8190A(xxx.xxx.xxx.xxx) where xxx.xxx.xxx.xxx is the address of the M8190A. We select (highlight) it to connect M8190A without any problem.

·         Later version:

Multiple strings relate to the M8190A can be observed like this:

TCPIP0::address::instX::INSTR resp.

TCPIP0::address::hislipX::INSTR resp.

TCPIP0::address::port::SOCKET

In this case the one related hislip must be selected.  If we select anything related SOCKET, SV will be crashed.

·         Adjust the instrument parameters if needed. Note that "AutoScale" parameter is set up to auto scale all waveforms.

·         Click the "Execute" button and the waveforms should be downloaded into the M8190 and the sequence will be played out. 

Further exploration

Playing out of the sequence can also be emulated by using "WaveformSequencer" part in a schematic. Look into the "Sequence" schematic (its Analysis is "DF4"). Note that you can simply drag the "Frequence Hopping Sequence" icon on the workspace tree and drop it into the schematic and a "WaveformSequencer" part will be automatically placed into the schematic and properly configured.

 

If VSA 89600 software is available, then enable the two VSA_89600_Sink's. Now you are able to see the emulated signal "live" in VSA 89600 application.

Playing out the composed sequence can be also emulated using "WaveformSequencer" part in a schematic. Look into the "Sequence" schematic (its Analysis is "DF4"). Note that you can simply drag the "Frequency Hopping Sequence" icon from the workspace tree and drop it into the schematic and a "WaveformSequencer" part will be automatically placed into the schematic and properly configured.

 

If VSA 89600 software is available, then enable the two VSA_89600_Sink's. Now you are able to see the emulated signal "live" in VSA 89600 application.

Use M8192 to Synchronize Multiple M8190's

Keysight Technologies SystemVue 

 

Required Software

Make sure you have installed Keysight IO Library Version 15 (or up) and Keysight Connection Expert software. Latest SystemVue relase.

 

This example shows how to generate two IQ pairs of test signals  with sequencer from two 2-channel M8190s and synchronize waveform playout with M8192.

 

1.      Generate Simulation Data:

Run the equation "Generate Signals" by click 'GO' to generate two Radar signals.

2.  Open the Waveform Sequence Composer UI by click on the  "WaveformSeq1"

     Note under "Pattern" tab the sequence is composed from the waveform data at each corresponding dataset listed in the UI

  • Go to "Instrument" tab. Type the IP address of the M8190 instrument into the "Address" cell of in the table under "Instruments Selection" area.  As an alternative, you can click the "Select Instruments..." button to pick the instrument if it has been added into the "Keysight Connection Expert", or add it in the "Select Instruments" dialog.

Multiple strings relate to the M8190A can be observed like this:

TCPIP0::address::instX::INSTR resp.

TCPIP0::address::hislipX::INSTR resp.

TCPIP0::address::port::SOCKET

Select the hislip one.        

  • Note that "SyncViaM8192" parameter is set to "YES".
  • Click the "Execute" button and the waveforms and sequence should be downloaded into the M8190. Note that no signal is output yet, signal output will be controlled by M8192 later.

3. Open the Waveform Sequence Composer UI by click on the  "WaveformSeq2" and repeat step 2 to download waveform and sequence into the second M8190. 

4. Update the instrument address information in Equations "Configuration Parameters".

  • Make sure to connect M8192 and M8190's properly for msater-slave(s) operation. For example: identify the master M8190 and properly connect its "SYS Clk Out" to M8192's "SYS Clk In", connect M8192's "SYS Clk Outx" to each M8190's "SYS Clk In" and connect M8192's "Trigger Outx" to each M8190's "Trigger In".

5. Run the equation "SyncAndRunM8190s" to generate outputs from both M8190s

6. Run the equation "ReleaseM8190s" to stop outputs from both M8190s.

  • Note: If you have executed step 5 to generate outputs signals from M8190s, you MUST perform step 6 to release and turn off M8190s before using step 2 and 3 to download new waveforms and sequences.
