Workspace.Name: OptimizationUsingSpectrasys
Workspace.Description:
Intermods with Optimization Workspace

Keysight Technologies Tutorial Workspace

 

ABSTRACT

This is a simple illustration of how do perform an optimization along a path in Spectrasys.

 

There is is companion material for this workspace.  Please click Help / Topics and Index and go to this section: Tutorials  > Simulation Control and Scripting  > Optimizing a Simulation, select the Intermod Optimization link, and follow the tutorial instructions.


BACKGROUND

Non-linear behavior models, like amplifier and mixers, will generate intermods and harmonics in Spectrasys. These intermods will propagate both forward and backwards along all paths. These intermods can be separated by intermod order and processed by path measurements. Spectrum identification information is available for every data point in a spectral plot.

 

Cascaded intermod equations are not used in Spectrasys. These equations make restrictive assumptions like a) frequency response is always flat, b) all stages are perfectly matched, c) intermods come from only one path, d) intermods never travel backwards, e) interfering tones generating intermods are never attenuated through the path, etc.. Instead, Spectrasys uses a SPARCA (Spectral Propagation and Root Cause Analysis) technique to overcome all of these limitations. Non-linear behavioral models create intermods and harmonics which propagate forwards and backwards. Measurements then operate on intermod and harmonic power found within the channel bandwidth.

 

To accomplish this Spectrasys knows the difference between intermods that are generated (GIMCP) in a particular stage versus those conducted (CIMCP) from prior stages. Generated and conducted intermods can be summed together to provide total intermod power (TIMCP) that is conducted to the following stage.

 

Measuring intermods and intercept points in Spectrasys is much like doing so in the lab. Interfering tones must be created at necessary frequencies to generate intermods that fall within the channel being measured.

 

SETUP

This example uses two cascaded amplifiers amongst other passive stages. A three tone signal source is used to create 2 interfering tones and a third signal used as a pilot to determine the gain of the channel at the same frequency as the third order intermods. The two interfering signals appear at 4100 and 4200 MHz each having a power of -20 dBm. The intermod and pilot frequencies are at 4000 MHz. The pilot signal power level is -100 dBm. The path frequency is also set to 4000 MHz so intermods will appear in the measured channel.

 

The channel measurement bandwidth is set to 10 kHz, which is wide enough to account for the intermod bandwidth but small enough to exclude the interfering tones. Intermods in Spectrasys will have bandwidths according to their intermod order and the bandwidths of the parent signals. For example, a 3rd order intermod with the equation of Fintermod = 2 x F1 - 3 x F2 would have the following bandwidth BWintermod = 2 x BW1 + 3 x BW2. Note: bandwidths never subtract.

 

If the channel measurement bandwidth is set narrower than BWintermod then the full intermod power will not appear in the spectrum plots nor the path measurements.

 

ANALYSIS

Intermod Table - This table shows a summary of intermod measurements. The cascaded gain (CGAIN) measurements show the gain of the channel at 4000 MHz. One interferer channel is shown at 4100 MHz (ICF and ICP). The total third order intermod channel power (TIMCP3) is shown as well at the percent third order intermod power (PRIM3). See the 'Percent IM3' heading for more information.

 

Percent IM3 - This level diagram show the percent contribution of the given stage to the total intermod power. From this graph it is relatively easy to see where the main offending stage is, the first RF amplifier.

 

Also it can be seen that the total percentage from all stages is greater than 100%. This difference is due to coherent addition. The measurement projects what the intermod power would be at the output of the path assuming linear operations. Since coherent addition can cause doubling or canceling the measurement is unable to accurately predict the contribution to the total in these cases. When 'Coherent Addition' is disabled the sum will equal 100%.

 

Intermod Diagram - This level diagram shows 3 basic intermod measurements along the path 1) total third order intermod channel power (TIMCP3), 2) generated third order intermod channel power (GIMCP3), and 3) conducted third order intermod channel power (CIMCP3). A lot of information can be gleaned off of this graph. First, TIMCP3 is equal to GIMCP3 and CIMCP3 ... except for backward propagating intermods ... like those that appear back at the path input. Second, generated intermods in the first RF amplifier stage dominate the intermod performance of the cascade chain.

 

EXERCISES

Redistribute the gain between the first and second amplifiers to lower the total third order intermod power while maintaining a cascaded gain of 10 dB.

 

One solution is to reduce the gain of the first RF amplifier stage from 20 dB to 16 dB and increase the 2nd RF amplifier stage from 10 dB to 14 dB. The cascaded gain will remain the same though the intermod performance improves by over 5 dB.

 

OPTIMIZATION

Any path measurement in Spectrasys can be optimized. To optimize a path measurement the following steps must be taken. 1) Create variables that the optimizer can tune, 2) place these variables in their respective models, and 3) create an optimization for the path using the desired measurements and variables.

 

Variables for gain and 1 dB compression point have been created for each RF amplifier. Intercept points have been tied to their respective compression points. These variables have been placed in their respective models.

 

An optimization has been created and two measurements have been selected for optimization, cascaded gain (CGAIN) and total third order intermod channel power (TIMCP3). Intermod performance cannot come at the expense of reducing the cascaded gain so a larger weighting will be given to the cascaded gain measurement. The goal will be improve the intermod performance from around -72 dBm to something less than -95 dBm.

 

Tuned variables have been added to the optimization and maximum gain and 1 dB compression limits have been added.

 

OPTIMIZATION EXERCISES

Right click on the 'Intermod Opt' optimization and select 'Optimize: Least Squares, Automatic'. The optimizer will change the gain and compression points of the amplifiers to achieve better intermod performance while maintaining the cascaded gain.

Workspace.Name: Receiver Monte Carlo
Workspace.Description:
Receiver Monte Carlo Workspace

Keysight Technologies Tutorial Workspace

 

ABSTRACT

This illustration shows the use of a monte carlo analysis in a receiver design.

 

BACKGROUND

Design variation is important to analyze to understand the impact of system performance.

 

To analyze a design including the effects of variation do the following:

  1. Set the statistics for each part parameter to be analyzed on the 'Part Statistics' tab of the part properties dialog box.
  2. Set each part parameter to be used by the Monte Carlo analysis as tunable on the 'Parameters' tab of the part properties dialog box.
  3. Add a Monte Carlo evaluation to the workspace tree.
  4. Select the analysis the Monte Carlo analysis will use on the 'General' tab of the Monte Carlo properties dialog box.
  5. Select the path dataset and its measurements to be analyzed on the 'Measurements' tab of the Monte Carlo properties dialog box.
  6. On the 'Variables' tab of the Monte Carlo properties dialog box select the variables to be analyzed. If the parameters are tunable clicking the 'Get Tuned Variables' button will automate this process.
  7. Run the Monte Carlo analysis.
  8. Create a rectangular plot.
  9. Select the Monte Carlo dataset as the default dataset for the graph.
  10. Use the histogram function on the path measurement at a given node for the graph measurement.

SETUP

A simple receiver has been created with a front end filter, LNA, and isolator. The 1800 MHz signal is down converted to a 500 MHz IF. Various gain and noise figure parameters for several of the parts have been set on the 'Part Statistics' page of the part properties. A Monte Carlo analysis has been created with 50 samples for the following measurements: CGAIN and CNF.

 

ANALYSIS

CGAIN Histogram - This graph shows a histogram plot of the system cascaded gain at the last node.

 

CNF Histogram - This graph shows a histogram plot of the cascaded noise figure at the last node.

 

EXERCISES

1. Change the number rounds of the monte carlo analysis and observe the effects.

2. Disable some of the variables used in the monte carlo analysis and observe the effects.

Workspace.Name: ParameterSweeping
Workspace.Description:
Parameter Sweeping in SystemVue

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example

 

This example uses a simple SineGen source and Sink to create a platform for multi-dimensional parametric sweeps. The amplitude, frequency and phase of the sinusoid generator are set to be tunable and hence can be selected as sweep parameters from analyses mounted on the basic data analysis process.

[Please run all analyses prior to examining the data displays.]

 

The amplitude is swept over the time sweep of the basic data analysis - providing a shared primary setup for two independent secondary analyses, one of frequency and the other of phase. A total of four analyses are thus performed, only the last two of which are used in the Equations page for post processing:

  1. Design1_Analysis - basic time domain behavior of sinusoid generator
  2. AmplitudeSweep - over the range [1,5]V in steps of 1 V
  3. FreqSweep - at [100,300,500] MHz over each amplitude of (2) at phase=0 deg.
  4. PhaseSweep - at [0,45,90] deg over each amplitude of (2) for frequency=300 MHz.

The extraction of specific sweep points in the swept-frequency and swept-phase analyses is done in the Equation block named SweepIndexing using MATLAB Script syntax. Note that phase is internally stored in radians so a search of 45*pi/180 is necessary to extract the waveforms with 45 degree phase shift.

 

Five graphs are displayed - two showing composite sweeps of frequency-over-amplitude and phase-over-amplitude and one each for arbitrry fixed values of frequency, amplitude anf phase. Note especially how the 'using' function is employed in switching between the datasets for making the access of the variables in the datasets easy, instead of using the 'getvariable' function to access each variable individually.

Workspace.Name: Plotting_nested_sweeps
Workspace.Description:
Plotting 2D Sweep Data

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example

 

This example workspace walks you through the post-processing equations needed to plot multi-variate data, including the ability to hold some of the independent variables to constant values, essentially reducing the dimensionality of the data.

 

In this example are:

  • the nominal case (no sweep),
  • a 1-dimensional sweep of the sinewave amplitude,
  • a 2-dimensional sweep of amplitude and # bits in an ideal digitizer.

When post-processing, it is helpful to visualize this data being accumulated in a dataset as a long, flat, 1-dimensional array of all values with no hierarchy.  The task of the equations is to isolate the values you want as a trace, and then preserve as much of the independent variables for that trace as possible.

Workspace.Name: Scripting_SinkFile_Output
Workspace.Description:
Incrementing Output File Names

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Tutorial Workspace

 

This tutorial workspace shows how to use a script to generate output files for each value in a sequence.  An array of 3 values is declared, then for each value of the array, a simulation is re-run with a parameter change on one of the blocks, and the Sink outputs ASCII text vectors to a different filename.

 

First, here is the master script: 

Amplitudes = [1 3 5];

 

% Run the analysis for each value of Amplitudes
for i = 1 : numel(Amplitudes)
    CurAmplitude = Amplitudes(i);
    runanalysis('Design1 Analysis');
end

Then the Sink is programmed to output to an incrementing file name, based on the sweep value.  Each time the simulation is re-run, the file name is different.  (please look at the "Filename" parameter on the "File Options" tab of the Sink)

=['C:\tmp\Run_' num2str(CurAmplitude) '.txt']

This results in 3 files being generated:

C:\tmp\Run_1.txt

C:\tmp\Run_3.txt

C:\tmp\Run_5.txt

Application: This can be used during regression tests to create or re-use a series of test vectors.

Workspace.Name: Buttons
Workspace.Description:
Buttons Scripts

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This example demonstrates a scripts ability to change a part's model, symbol, and parameter.

 

Click a button on the right to run the internal script, which perfoms the indicated action on the button. The first 4 buttons call the SwitchSource script, which executes a subroutine called RunModel. The RunModel subroutine creates a dataset based on the model name, removes any old data from it by clearing the cache, and then runs the Data Flow Analysis.

 

To view the script code inside a button simply right click the button and select properties. You'll notice in all three generator buttons an object for the S1 part of the 'Generator' schematic is created. The model and the symbol for the S1 part are then changed using the ChangeModel and ChangeSymbol built-in functions. The Ramp and Square Generator buttons have an additional step. The 'lolevel' parameter of the model is set to -1 V (so that the results of each generator would be in the same range)

 

The 'Run All 3 Sources' button performs all of the actions of the first three buttons. The last button calls the DeleteDataset script which was added to the workspace from the SystemVue Script Library.

Workspace.Name: Parameter Script
Workspace.Description:
Parameter Script Example

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Tutotial Workspace

 

The design for this script example shows that the output from the data flow IFFT part and the input signal are the same.

 

This example workspace uses a script which sets the Amplitude and Frequency parameters of the SineGen source S1.  The script then creates a new dataset and runs the analysis with the new parameters. The graphs are then switched to display the results from the new dataset.

 

The values that the script uses for the parameters are set in the equation block 'Parameters'. To run the script right click the 'Analysis' script and select 'Run'. You'll notice that a new dataset is created and the graphs reference this new dataset.

 

Open the 'Analysis' script to view the code inside. The script begins by getting the values from the equation block and setting the S1 part to an object. A subroutine called 'SetParameters' is then called, which begins by setting the parameter values for the S1 part,. The subroutine then creates a new dataset name based on the parameter values and configures the analysis to use the new dataset name. Next, the cache for the analysis is cleared and then the analysis is run. The final step of the subroutine is to change the context of each graph to the newly created dataset name. Open the graph properties and notice that the dataset it points to has changed. The graph will display the results from the new dataset.

 

Notice that throughout the script the function 'Show' is used. This function sends text to be displayed in the script processor. Open the Script Processor from the Tools menu. When you run the script you will see the messages from the script in the lower box of the Script Processor window.

 

The 'DeleteDatasets' script was added to this workspace from the SystemVue Script Library. Right click and run this script to delete all of the datasets in the workspace.

Workspace.Name: Script-Controlled Sweep
Workspace.Description:
Script-Controlled Sweep 

Keysight Technologies VB Script Example

 

(NOTE: Sweep data must be calculated before it can be displayed.)

 

This example demonstrates sweeping a variable which generates data variables of differing sizes, which cannot be swept using the normal technique.

 

Try running Sweep1. Notice the error: Some of the swept variables have changed size during the sweep and data could not be appended.  This is because the PathMeas variables change size during the sweep.  The number of values is the square of NumElements and since the vectors vary in size they cannot be concatinated to form a rectangular matrix.  Also notice that some of the swept variables, like ArrayMeas_Directivity_Pattern, don't change and can be fully calculated.

 

Now run Scripted Sweep, which will create a new dataset for each sweep pass, so that the variables don't need to be appended.

Workspace.Name: WLAN_11ac_1Ant
Workspace.Description:
WLAN 802.11ac BER Test

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This example works with the SystemVue TAP plugin in the same folder to do BER test. Please follow below steps to run this workspace:
1. Open schematic WLAN_11ac_1Ant_SRC, set PrimAddress of S3 to the IP address of you MXG
2. Make sure you have Test Automation Platform(TAP) installed on your PC
3. Make sure you have VSA 89600 installed on your PC, and it has connected to a MXA/PXA analyzer.
4. Open SystemVue.Plugins\SystemVue.Plugins.sln, build the solution, and copy the generated SystemVue.Plugins.dll to C:\Program Files\Keysight\TAP
5. Open SystemVue.Plugins\WLAN_11ac_1Ant_BER.TapPlan with TAP
6. Copy this workspace and the wlan_11ac.set in the same folder to a folder which you have write permission, and go to the SVOpenWorkspace test step of TAP, change the Filepath to the location you placed this workspace
7. Close SystemVue
8. In TAP, run the test plan, it will automatically launch SystemVue and open this workspace to do BER test.

Workspace.Name: 3GPP_NR_DL_Tx
Workspace.Description:
3GPP_NR_DL_Tx

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This workspace provides a VTB test bench to measure 3GPP new radio (NR) transmitter characteristics including spectrum, waveform, CCDF, Constellation, EVM and ACLR.

 

The centre frequency of the input signal to DUT (SVE_Link in the design) is set by FCarrier_In, while centre frequency of the output signal from DUT (SVE_Link in the design) is set by FCarrier_Out.

 

RF distortions in the modulator can be simulated by setting parameters GainImbalance, PhaseImbalance, etc. 

 

Test Models are provided in this workspace according to 3GPP TS 38.141 V16.1.0 (2019-09) . In this example, test model defined in TS38.141-1 (16.1.0)and TS38.141-2(16.1.0) are used. TDD and FDD are supported for FrequencyRange 1 (FR1) for Numerology 15kHz, 30kHz and 60kHz with normal cyclic prefix in this example. Only TDD model is supported for FrequencyRange 2  (FR2)  for Numerology 60kHz with normal cyclic prefix, and 120kHz.Set UseTestModel to YES, then you can select TestModel and Bandwidth to configure different test models. If UseTestModel is set to NO, then you can configure NR parameters to customize the generated signal.

 

When UseTestModel is set to YES, test model defined in TS38.141-1 . SSB is not enabled for test models.

When UseTestModel is set to NO. NR signal is configured by other parameters. In this case, there is no SSB for Numerology 2 (60kHz) according to the specification. And SSB for 240kHz is not supported now. When the Numerology is set 2 and 4, SSB_Enable should be set to NO. BWP is defined occupy the whole bandwidth of component carrier. Frequency location of SSB in component carrier are defined by SSB_RBOffset. SSB RB offset is according to the beginning of component carrie. RB offset of SSB is based on 15kHz for Numerology 0 and Numerology1, and based on 60kHz for Numerology 3 which is defined in specification 38.211. PDSCH_RBOffset and PDSCH_NumRBs define the frequency location of PDSCH in BWP. PDSCH RB offset is according to the beginning of BWP. Please make sure BWP and SSB is in the bandwidht and PDSCH is in the BWP. A low pass filter is added in EVM model and and the bandwidth of this filter is set as the same of bandwidth of component carrier.

 

SignalPower is defined the power of PDSCH. If SSB is in the location of PDSCH, SignalPower equals to the power of the transmitter. If SSB is outside PDSCH, signal power of transmitter is a bit bigger than SignalPower when UseTestModel is set to NO. When UsetTestModel is set to YES, number of RBs of PDSCH is given in Equation of different TestModel. PDCCH and PDSCH is not overlaped in time domian, the SignalPower may not be accurate when PDCCH is transmitted.

 

ACLR is valid for first adjacent bandwidth when OversamplingOption is no less than Ratio 4 and ACLR is valid for first and second adjacent bandwidth when OversamplingOption is no less than Ratio8. And the calculation of ACLR is based on TS 38.104 v13.0.

 

When OversamplingOption is more than ratio 2, the signal will be downsampled to ratio 2 and send to EVM model to do demodulation.

 

Frequency range of source and EVM model are defined by NR_Fc, considering influence of PhaseRotation. It's allowed not to be the same as the real operating frequency, indicated by FCarrier_In/FCarrier_Out. 

 

The number of simulated subframes for EVM measurements is to be 1 for one simulation in order to speed up when NumSubframes is set 1. And when NumSubframes is set to no less than 10, the demodulation of EVM is based on frame.

 

The results of every subcarriers such as constellation, channel type and errvectorspectrum can be saved by set parameter SaveSubcarriersResults to be YES.

 

The ideal low pass filter for spectrum shaping can be turned on/off by parameter EnableTxFilter. The number of taps can be set by FIR_Taps. If EnableTxFilter is set to NO, no spectrum shaping would be applied.

 

A filter will be added in EVM model before demodulation if EnableRxFilter is set to YES.

 

This VTB example is based on SystemVue 2020.

 

Try to change the parameters, run NR_DL_Tx_Analysis and check the simulation results.

  • Table ACLR_In shows ACLR results before DUT when OversamplingOption is set to no less than Ratio 4.
  • Table ACLR_Out shows ACLR results after DUT when OversamplingOption is set to no less than Ratio 4.
  • Graph CCDF shows the Complementary Cumulative Distribution Function of the transmitted signals before DUT and after DUT.
  • Graph Constellation shows the constellation of each physical channel and signal when SaveSubcarriersResults is set to YES. The constellation of PDSCH, PBCH, PSS and SSS are included when parameter UseTestModel is set to NO. PDSCH DMRS is shown in PDSCH channel and PBCH DMRS is shown in PBCH. If Modulation is changed, please select different input for PDSCH constellation. The constellation of PDSCH, PDSCH DMRS and PDCCH are shown when UseTestModel is set to YES.
  • Table Error Summary shows average EVM, peak EVM, frequency errors and other measured results of each frame got from EVM model
  • Table EVM lists EVM of each physical channel and signal
  • Graph NormalizedEqualizerChannelFrequencyResponse shows the normalized equalizer channel frequency response got from EVM model for all valid subcarriers of PDSCH and SSB when UseTestModel is set to No and for all valid subcarriers of PDSCH when UseTestModel is set to YES. It is the average channel frequency response in one slot which means the value on one subcarrier is the average of all values on that subcarrier in all symbols in one slot.
  • Graph Spectrum shows the spectrum in complex voltage of the transmitted signal before DUT and after DUT.
  • Graph Waveform shows the transmitted time domain waveform magitude before DUT and after DUT.

Workspace.Name: 3GPP_NR_UL_Tx
Workspace.Description:
3GPP NR Uplink Tx Characteristics

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Workspace

 

This VTB design measures 3GPP 5G NR uplink transmitter characteristics, including spectrum, waveform, CCDF, Constellation and EVM according to 3GPP TS 38.101 and 3GPP TS 38.521.

 

The center frequency of the input signal to DUT(SVE_Link in the design) is set by FCarrier_In, while center frequency of the output signal from DUT(SVE_Link in the design) is set by FCarrier_Out.

 

RF distortions in the modulator can be simulated by setting parameters GainImbalance, PhaseImbalance, etc.

 

NR uplink signal configuration:

  • NR_Fc specifies the carrier frequency of NR signal. It determines in which frequency range NR signal is generated, FR1 or FR2. It could be not the same as real simulation frequency indicated by FCarrier_In/FCarrier_Out.
  • Bandwidth specifies the full bandwidth of signal. Numerology determines the subcarrier spacing used by OFDM. Refer to 3GPP 38.101-1 Table 5.3.2-1 for the valid combination of Bandwidth and Numerology, and the maximum number of RB derived from them.
  • UseCommonConfig specifies whether to use the configuration defined by Table 6.1-1 in 3GPP 38.521-1/38.521-2.

If it’s No, the signal’s configuration is up to user by specifying PUSCH_RBOffset, PUSCH_NumRBs and Modulation in the example’s Parameter tab. For advanced user, more parameters are allowed to be configured by modifying their values in Equation tab (line 102~148).

  • PUSCH_RBOffset and PUSCH_NumRBs determine PUSCH’s frequency location. They are valid when UseCommonConfig is No. Note, PUSCH_RBOffset + PUSCH_NumRBs should not be greater than the maximum number of RBs in bandwidth.
  • CommonConfig_FR1 specifies the RB allocation type defined by Table 6.1-1 in 3GPP 38.521-1. It’s valid only when UseCommonConfig is YES and FCarrier_Out operating in FR1(450 MHz ~ 6000 MHz) .
  • CommonConfig_FR2 specifies the RB allocation type defined by Table 6.1-1 in 3GPP 38.521-2. It’s valid only when UseCommonConfig is YES and FCarrier_Out operating in FR2(24250 MHz ~ 52600 MHz) .
  • OFDM_Type specifies whether PUSCH is DFT-S-OFDM or CP-OFDM.
  • Modulation specifies the modulation format used by PUSCH.
  • ReportEVMIndB specifies the unit of EVM result.
  • EnableTxFilter enables an ideal low pass filter for spectrum shapping.
  • FIR_Taps specifies the number of filter taps when EnableTxFilter is true.
  • EnableRxFilter is to enable a filter used by EVM model.
  • SaveSubcarriersResults enables the output of some results vs. subcarriers such as constellation, channel type and errvectorspectrum.
  • NumSubframes set the measurement length of EVM.

Try to change the parameters, run NR_UL_Tx_Analysis and check the simulation results.

  • Table ACLR_In shows Adjacent Channel Leakage power Ratio before DUT as defined in section 6.5.2.4 of 3GPP TS 38.101-1
  • Table ACLR_Out shows Adjacent Channel Leakage power Ratio after DUT as defined in section 6.5.2.4 of 3GPP TS 38.101-1
    •
  • Graph CCDF shows the Complementary Cumulative Distribution Function of the transmitted signal before DUT and after DUT.
  • Graph Constellation shows the constellation of PUSCH when parameter SaveSubcarriersResults is set to YES.
  • Table Error Summary shows average EVM(dB), peak EVM(dB), frequency errors(Hz), IQ Offset(dB), Symbol Clock Error, Sync Correlation and Time Offset(s) of PUSCH.
  • Table EVM shows average EVM in dB of PUSCH and DMRS of PUSCH.
  • Graph NormalizedEqualizerChannelFrequencyResponse shows the normalized equalizer channel frequency response of PUSCH.
  • Graph Spectrum shows the spectrum in complex voltage of the transmitted signal before DUT and after DUT.
  • Graph Waveform shows the transmitted time domain waveform magnitude before DUT and after DUT.

Note:

  1. ACLR is valid for first adjacent bandwidth when OversamplingOption is no less than Ratio 4 and ACLR is valid for first and second adjacent bandwidth when OversamplingOption is no less than Ratio8. This example uses Ratio 4 by default.
  2. The EVM model's OversamplingOption is either Ratio 1 or Ratio 2. The input signal will be downsampled if the Source model uses OversamplingOption greater than Ratio 2.
  3. There is a known issue for EVM measurement. When OFDM_Type is DFT-s-OFDM and FCarrier_Out operating in Frequence Range 2, EVM result may be very poor in some cases. We will fix this defect in next release.
  4. There is a known issue for EVM measurement. When Modulation is pi/2 BPSK, EVM result will be very poor. We will fix this defect in next release.
  5. It’s recommended to modify this VTB workspace base on SystemVue 2018 Update 1.

Bluetooth C/I Performance

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

 

This workspace provides a VTB test bench to analyze Bluetooth Rx performance in the presence of co-/adjacent channel Bluetooth interference.

 

The test procedure refers to 5.1.24 TP/RCV/CA/09/C (EDR C/I Performance).

o    The default wanted signal and interferer are pi/4-DQPSK modulated packet 2-DH5. To test 8DPSK signal, please reset the packet type in Parameters.

o    This design gives the co-channel interference test of the lowest operation frequency using a minimum number of 16 000 000 payload bits as the default configuration. The operation frequency and signal power of the wanted signal and interferer are set in the Parameters. Users can change the parameters for other test case with reference 5.1.24 TP/RCV/CA/09/C (EDR C/I Performance) of Bluetooth Test Specification Ver. 1.2/2.0/2.0+EDR/2.1/2.1+EDR.

 

The center frequency of the input signal to DUT (SVE_Link in the design) is set by FCarrier_In, while center frequency of the output signal from DUT (SVE_Link in the design) is set by FCarrier_Out.

 

The transmitted wanted signal mean power is set by SignalPower. 

RF distortions can be introduced by setting parameters GainImbalance, PhaseImbalance, etc.

The number of bursts for BER measurements is specified by MeasBurst.

 

Try to change the parameters, run Bluetooth_EDR_CoACInterference_Analysis and check the simulation results.

Workspace.Name: VTB_Example
Workspace.Description:
VTB_Example

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This workspace provides a few simple VTB (Verification Test Bench) designs that demonstrate the basic VTB features. They are provided just for demonstration purposes and running them does NOT require any license other than the basic SystemVue one

None of the designs in this workspace will simulate in SystemVue because of the use of the SVE_Link model (the intent is to simulate them using SystemVue Engine in a cosimulation environment with another simulator, e.g. ADS or Golden Gate). To simulate them inside SystemVue, open the associated analysis and select the DF_Amp configuration. 

For more information on how to create VBT designs please refer to the following documentation sections:

  • Simulation > Verification Test Bench (VTB)
  • Tutorials > Verification Test Bench Tutorial

The VTB designs included in this workspace are:

 

EVM_Measurement

 

This VTB design performs an EVM measurement on a modulated signal. The symbol rate and modulation format of the signal can be set through the VTB parameters. The modulator output power as well as certain modulation impairments can also be set using the VTB parameters.

 

When adding impairments (IQ Offset, Gain and Phase Imbalance) the constellation plot (EVM_Meas_Tx_Constellation) may seem inconsistent with the trajectory one (EVM_Meas_Tx_Trajectory). For example, applying an offset only along the x-axis might show (in the constellation plot) as offset along the other axis, both axes, or the expected axis but in the opposite direction. The reason is that the constellation plot uses data generated by the EVM sink, whereas the trajectory plot uses data created by just filtering the signal with a Root Raised Cosine filter. The EVM sink performs demodulation on the input signal and may arbitrarily rotate it by any angle that is an integer multiple of the angle to which the constellation is phase invariant (rectangular QAM constellations are 90-degree phase invariant and Star-QAM constellations are 45-degree phase invariant).

 

 

QAM16_SER_vs_EbNo

 

This VTB design uses the BER_IS model to efficiently compute a BER waterfall curve for a 16-QAM system. VTB parameters include the signal symbol rate, modulator output power, and range of SNR values over which BER is computed.

 

ACPR_Meaasurement

 

This VTB design demonstrates how to post-process simulation data in a VTB design.  It measures ACPR for a modulated signal. The symbol rate and the modulation format of the signal can be set using VTB parameters. The modulator output power is also set using a VTB parameter. The signal at the output of the modulator goes through a non-linear amplifier whose output 1 dB compression point is a VTB parameter.

 

ACPR is measured by computing the spectrum power in different bands using a custom ACPR function defined inside the SystemVue workspace. This ACPR function is for demonstration purposes only. It does NOT comply with any standard. Four user defined variables have been created in the dataset (MyACPRMinus1_dB, MyACPRMinus2_dB, MyACPRPlus1_dB, MyACPRPlus2_dB) that are calculated by calling the ACPR function. This function takes as arguments data created by the simulation (S2_Power, and S2_Power_Freq) as well as values computed based on the top level design parameters (FCarrier, SymbolRate). To get these parameters in the dataset you need to check the Save Design Parameters to Dataset check box in the Options tab of the Data Flow analysis.

 

How to use this workspace

 

Use the example SVETester application to open this workspace and observe how the parameters of the VTB designs are presented in the SVETester GUI.

 

Change parameter values in the SVETester UI and run the simulation. Import the simulation results back into SystemVue (File > Import > ADX File...) and compare them with the results of running the same simulation inside SystemVue (to run the simulation inside SystemVue you need to select the DF_Amp configuration in the Data Flow Analysis dialog).

Workspace.Name: DPD_ET_VTB
Workspace.Description:
PA DPD+ET Simulation Solution

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Workspace

 

This VTB design demonstrates how you can employ DPD and ET to improve your PA’s linearity and efficiency.

This example is meant to show the concept of DPD whose algorithms are generic ones but not the state-of-the-art ones. We intend to educate designers on a method (but certainly not the only one) of simulating DPD+ET with ADS.

 

The configuration of this workspace:

 

  • The center frequency of the input signal to DUT(SVE_Link in the design) is set by FCarrier.
  • The PA input signal mean power is set by SignalPower.
  • Operation specifies which DPD step is performed. 0 denotes Extraction and 1 denotes Application.
  • WorkingFolderDirectory specifies the full path of a folder. This folder must be writable. It's used to exchange data between DPD operations. And, when ET is enabled, the file specified by ET_ShapingTable_FileName should also exist in this folder.
  • Below parameters are used to define the stimulus signal.
    • SignalType specifies the waveform type. I/Q File | LTE DL | LTE UL | WLAN 11ac | NR DL | NR UL.
    • OversamplingRatio specifies the oversampling ratio used by the signal.
    • Below parameters, they take effect only when SignalType is a specific type.
      • IQ_Waveform_I specifies the file name of I part when SignalType is I/Q File.
      • IQ_Waveform_Q specifies the file name of I part when SignalType is I/Q File.
      • IQ_Bandwidth specifies the nominal bandwidth when SignalType is I/Q File.
      • IQ_EffectiveBandwidth specifies the effective bandwidth (excluding guard band) when SignalType is I/Q File.
      • IQ_SampleRate specifies the sampling rate used by IQ waveform when SignalType is I/Q File.
      • IQ_WaveformLength specifies the number of samples contained in the IQ waveform file when SignalType is I/Q File.
      • LTE_Bandwidth specifies the bandwidth when SignalType is LTE DL/LTE UL. 0: 1.4MHz; 1: 3MHz; 2: 5MHz; 3: 10MHz; 4:15MHz; 5:20MHz.
      • LTE_Modulation specifies the modulation format when SignalType is LTE DL/LET UL. 0: QPSK; 1: 16QAM; 2: 64QAM.
      • WLAN11ac_Bandwidth specifies the bandwidth when SignalType is WLAN11ac. 0: 20MHz; 1: 40MHz; 2: 80MHz; 3: 160MHz.
      • WLAN11ac_MCS specifies the modulation format and coding rate when SignalType is WLAN11ac.

      • NR_Numerology specifies the subcarrier spacing when SignalType is NR_DL/NR_UL. 0: 15kHz; 1:30kHz; 2: 60kHz; 3: 120kHz.
      • NR_Modulation specifies the modulation format when SignalType is NR_DL/NR_UL. 0:BPSK; 1:QPSK; 2:16QAM; 3:64QAM;4: 256QAM. BPSK is only valid when SignalType is NR_UL and NR_UL_TransformPrecodingEnabled is YES.
      • NR_UL_TransformPrecodingEnabled specifies whether TransformPrecoding is enabled when SignalType is NR_UL. If it’s NO, NR uplink signal is CP-OFDM, otherwise, it’s DFT-OFDM.
  • Below parameters are used to configure CFR.
    • CFREnable specifies whether CFR is enabled.
    • Below parameters are active when CFREnable is Yes and SignalType is LTE_DL.
      • CFR_LTE_ClippingThreshold specifies the threshold for the simple clipping. The maximum magnitude of the clipped signal would be no larger than CFR_LTE_ClippingThreshold.
      • CFR_LTE_EVM_Threshold_QPSK specifies the EVM threshold set for QPSK symbols.
      • CFR_LTE_EVM_Threshold_16QAM specifies the EVM threshold set for 16QAM symbols.
      • CFR_LTE_EVM_Threshold_64QAM specifies the EVM threshold set for 64QAM symbols.
    • Below parameters are active when CFREnable is Yes and SignalType is not LTE_DL.
      • CFR_Algorithm specifies the CFR algorithm to use.
      • Below parameters are active when CFR_Algorithm is Clipping and Filtering.
        • CFR_ClippingThreshold specifies the clipping threshold in dB;
        • CFR_Filter_PassRipple specifies the passband ripple in dB.
        • CFR_Filter_MaximumOrder specifies the maximum filter order for Parks-McClellan filter.
      • Below parameters are active when CFR_Algorithm is Clipping and Filtering.           
        • CFR_TargetPAPR_dB specifies the target PAPR value after CFR. It must be >=3.
        • CFR_Max_IterationNum specifies the maximum iteration number. Its range is [1,20].
        • CFR_Beta specifies the Kaiser window adjustment parameter. Its range is [2, 20].
        • CFR_Max_Window_Length specifies the maximum Kaiser window length.
  • Below parameters are used to define the DPD.
    • DPD_ModelType specifies the DPD model to use. Memory Polynomial, Volterra Series and Look-Up Table.
    • Below parameters are active when DPD_ModelType is Memory Polynomial or Volterra Series.
      • DPD_ ModelIdentificationAlgorithm specifies the algorithm used for the DPD model identification: LSE using QR, LSE using SVD.
      • DPD_ MemoryOrder specifies the memory order of RF power amplifier deployed in wideband communication system.
      • DPD_ NonlinearOrder specifies the nonlinear order of RF power amplifier deployed in communication system.
      • DPD_NonlinearOrderSelection specifies whether to use odd order only for nonlinear effect.
    • Below parameters are active when DPD_ModelType is Volterra Series.
      • DPD_CrossTermOrder specifies the max order of the cross terms in Volterra polynomial.
    • Below parameters are active when DPD_ModelType is LUT.
      • DPD_LUTSize specifies the size of look up table.
      • DPD_LUTStep specifies the step of the input power of look up table.
  • Below parameters are used to define the ET.
    • ET_Enable specifies whether enable Envelope Tracking function.
    • ET_Vsupply specifies the fixed power supply voltage when ET_Enable is NO.

    • ET_ShapingTable_FileName specifies a local file name that has shaping table when ET_Enable is YES. This file must exist in the folder specified by WorkingFolderDirectory. The file format of the shaping table is the same as an example below.

BEGIN GMDIF

% Pin_dBm(1)   voltage(1)

 

-7.530000000e+00 1.250000000e+00

-1.150000000e+00 1.500000000e+00

1.935000000e+00 1.750000000e+00

4.070000000e+00 2.000000000e+00

...   ...

  • Meas_Option specifies the measurements to be performed. Reducing the measurements to be made can speed up the simulation.

All: All the measurements will be performed, including ACLR, EVM, AM-AM, AM-PM, Spectrum, and Waveform;

ACP and EVM: measure ACLR, EVM, and Spectrum.

ACP Only: measure ACLR and spectrum.

EVM only: measure EVM.

 

Run DPD_Analysis and check the simulation results.

    • Table ACLR_Original shows Adjacent Channel Leakage power Ratio measured on the original signal.
    • Table ACLR_PA shows Adjacent Channel Leakage power Ratio measured on the PA output signal without DPD.
    • Table ACLR_withDPD shows Adjacent Channel Leakage power Ratio measured on the PA output signal with DPD.
    • Graph CCDF shows the Complementary Cumulative Distribution Function measured on original signal, PA output signal without DPD and PA output signal with DPD.
    • Graph DPD_PA_AM_AM_Normalized shows the normalized AMAM curve measured on PA without DPD and PA with DPD.
    • Graph DPD_PA_AM_PM shows the AMPM curve measured on PA without DPD and PA with DPD.
    • Table DPD_PA_MeanPower_PeakPower shows the PAPR, Peak Power and Mean Power measured on PA output signal with DPD.
    • Table PA_MeanPower_PeakPower shows the PAPR, Peak Power and Mean Power measured on PA output signal without DPD.
    • Table EVM shows the EVM measured on original signal, PA output signal without DPD and PA output signal with DPD.
    • Table NMSE shows the NMSE which evaluate the accuracy of extracted DPD model. The lower the NMSE, the more accurate of DPD model.
    • Graph Spectrum shows the spectrum in complex voltage of original signal, PA output signal without DPD and PA output signal with DPD.
    • Graph Waveform shows the original time domain waveform.

 

Note:

    1. For those parameters set to be hidden in the workspace’s parameter list, they are internally determined in the Equation according to the specified SignalType. By doing this, the setup of signal can be simplified and easy to use.
    2. DPD is performed with two steps. Run first step by setting Operation to 0, and second step by setting Operation to 1. The measurements results are valid only after running step 1 and step 2. Only running one step may result in error or wrong measurement results.
    3. If the SignalType is I/Q File, the EVM measurement is invalid.
    4. The performance may be degraded if the stimulus signal is a burst one with idle part.
    5. Don't delete the data set DPD_ET_Application_Data. There are equations to do post processing.

Workspace.Name: GetShapingTable_VTB
Workspace.Description:
Get ET PA's Shaping Table

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Workspace

 

This VTB design demonstrates how to generate shaping table for an ET PA.

This model utilizes a CW signal as source and sweeps the PA Gain vs. PA output power of an ET PA with varying power supply voltage and PA input power. The swept power supply voltage is from VoltageStart to VoltageStop in a step of VoltageStep.  For each voltage, the PA input power is swept from PowerStart to PowerStop in a step of PowerStep. In a single measurement, PA gain and PA output power are measured. By plotting the trace, we can see how gain and gain compression vary. In turn, a shaping table is formulated from the trace by specifying a constant PA gain, Gain_target. Ultimately, the generated shaping table is saved into a file specified by ShapingTable_FileName.

FCarrier specifies the frequency of CW signal.

SamplingRateOfETPA specifies the time spacing between two sweepings. If the ETPA has memory effect, this parameter should be low enough, equivalent to the time between two sweepings long enough, to ensure the stimulus signal of this sweeping not fading into next sweeping.

 

Note:

     If runing this example with SystemVue, please short the SVE_Link model and enable ETPA model.

Workspace.Name: 3GPP_LTE_BS_AdjacentChannelSelectivity
Workspace.Description:
3GPP_LTE_BS_AdjacentChannelSelectivity

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This workspace provides a VTB test bench of Adjacent Channel Selectivity (ACS) of LTE BS receiver according to section 7.5 of 3GPP TS 36.104. Adjacent channel selectivity (ACS) is a measure of the receiver ability to receive a wanted signal at its assigned channel frequency in the presence of an adjacent channel signal with a specified center frequency offset of the interfering signal to the band edge of a victim system. The interfering signal shall be an E-UTRA signal as specified in Annex C of 3GPP TS 36.104. 

The wanted and the interfering signal should be configured according to Table 7.5.1-3, Table 7.5.1-4 and Table 7.5.1-5 for Wide Area BS, Local Area BS and Home BS, respectively.

The center frequency of the input signal to DUT (SVE_Link in the design) is set by FCarrier_In, while center frequency of the output signal from DUT (SVE_Link in the design) is set by FCarrier_Out.

 

RF distortions in the modulator can be simulated by setting parameters GainImbalance, PhaseImbalance, etc.

 

An AddNDensity model with NDensity = -173.975dBm is used to introduce thermal noise for room temperature (T = 300K). The noise figure is set by parameter NF.

 

The wanted signal mean power is set by parameter P_WantedSig, while the interfering signal mean power is set by parameter P_Interferer.

The ideal lowpass filter for spectrum shaping can be turned on/off by parameter EnableTxFilter. The number of taps can be set by FIR_Taps. If EnableTxFilter is set to NO, no spectrum shaping would be applied.

HARQ retransmission can be enabled by setting HARQ_Enable to YES. When HARQ retransmission is enabled, EnableTxFilter should be set to NO as ideal lowpass filter is not supported in HARQ retransmission in current SystemVue version. Number of HARQ processes is 8 for FDD and 7 for TDD. Maximum number of HARQ transmissions is set to 4. The redundancy version sequence is set to [0,1,2,3].

 

The interfering signal center frequency offset is set by parameter Foffset_Interferer. Foffset_Interferer<0 indicates the center frequency of the interferer is lower than the lower edge of the wanted signal, otherwise, the center frequency of the interferer is higher than the upper edge of the wanted signal.

The bandwidth of the interfering signal is determined by the bandwidth of the wanted signal according to Table 7.5.1-3 ~ Table 7.5.1-5, i.e. if Bandwidth of the wanted signal is smaller than 5MHz, the interfering signal would have same bandwidth as the wanted signal, otherwise, the bandwidth of the interfering signal is 5MHz.

A Parks-McClellan bandpass filter centered at FCarrier_Out is used in the receiver side. The PassBandwidth is set to the transmission bandwidth of the wanted signal, and the StopBandwidth is set to the channel bandwidth. For example, if Bandwidth of wanted signal is 5MHz, then PassBandwidth = 4.5MHz, StopBandwidth = 5MHz. This filter could be disabled by setting parameter EnableRxFilter to NO.

By default, the reference measurement channels specified in Annexes A of 3GPP TS 36.104 are used. If you want to customized the test configuration, please set UseFRC to NO and set the payload configuration and RB allocation.

 

Please note that those parameters with hide condition set to true will not be shown in ADS/GoldenGate environment.

Try to change the parameters, run LTE_BS_AdjacentChannelSelectivity_Analysis and check the simulation results in table ThroughputFraction to see whether the throughput meets the requirements. The throughput shall be ≥ 95% of the maximum throughput of the reference measurement channels.

Workspace.Name: 3GPP_LTE_BS_InChannelSelectivity
Workspace.Description:
3GPP_LTE_BS_InChannelSelectivity

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This workspace provides a VTB test bench of In-Channel Selectivity (ICS) of LTE BS receiver according to section 7.4 of 3GPP TS 36.104. In-channel selectivity (ICS) is a measure of the receiver ability to receive a wanted signal at its assigned resource block locations in the presence of an interfering signal received at a larger power spectral density. In this condition a throughput requirement shall be met for a specified reference measurement channel. The interfering signal shall be an E-UTRA signal as specified in Annex C and shall be time aligned with the wanted signal.

The wanted and the interfering signal should be configured according to Table 7.4.1-1, Table 7.4.1-2 and Table 7.4.1-3 for Wide Area BS, Local Area BS and Home BS, respectively.

The center frequency of the input signal to DUT (SVE_Link in the design) is set by FCarrier_In, while center frequency of the output signal from DUT (SVE_Link in the design) is set by FCarrier_Out.

 

RF distortions in the modulator can be simulated by setting parameters GainImbalance, PhaseImbalance, etc.

 

An AddNDensity model with NDensity = -173.975dBm is used to introduce thermal noise for room temperature (T = 300K). The noise figure is set by parameter NF.

 

The wanted signal mean power is set by parameter P_WantedSig, while the interfering signal mean power is set by parameter P_Interferer.

Wanted and interfering signal are placed adjacently around Fc. The type of the interfering signal is determined by the bandwidth of the wanted signal according to Table 7.4.1-1 ~ Table 7.4.1-3. The RB allocation of wanted signal and interfering signal are set as follows.

Workspace.Name: 3GPP_LTE_BS_ReferenceSensitivity
Workspace.Description:
3GPP_LTE_BS_ReferenceSensitivity

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This workspace provides a VTB test bench of reference sensitivity power level of LTE base station receiver according to section 7.2 of 3GPP TS 36.104. The reference sensitivity power level PREFSENS is the minimum mean power received at the antenna connector at which a throughput requirement shall be met for a specified reference measurement channel.   

 

The center frequency of the input signal to DUT (SVE_Link in the design) is set by FCarrier_In, while center frequency of the output signal from DUT (SVE_Link in the design) is set by FCarrier_Out.

 

RF distortions in the modulator can be simulated by setting parameters GainImbalance, PhaseImbalance, etc.

 

An AddNDensity model with NDensity = -173.975dBm is used to introduce thermal noise for room temperature (T = 300K). The noise figure is set by parameter NF.

 

The transmitted signal mean power is set by SignalPower. SignalPower specifies the mean power of the transmitted signal.

The ideal lowpass filter for spectrum shaping can be turned on/off by parameter EnableTxFilter. The number of taps can be set by FIR_Taps. If EnableTxFilter is set to NO, no spectrum shaping would be applied.

 

HARQ retransmission can be enabled by setting HARQ_Enable to YES. When HARQ retransmission is enabled, EnableTxFilter should be set to NO as ideal lowpass filter is not supported in HARQ retransmission in current SystemVue version. Number of HARQ processes is 8 for FDD and 7 for TDD. Maximum number of HARQ transmissions is set to 4. The redundancy version sequence is set to [0,1,2,3].

 

By default, the reference measurement channels specified in Annexes A of 3GPP TS 36.104 are used. If you want to customized the test configuration, please set UseFRC to NO and set the payload configuration and RB allocation.

3GPP_LTE_BS_Tx

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This workspace provides a VTB test bench to measure LTE base station transmitter characteristics including spectrum, waveform, CCDF, Constellation, EVM and ACLR according to 3GPP TS 36.104.

 

The center frequency of the input signal to DUT(SVE_Link in the design) is set by FCarrier_In, while center frequency of the output signal from DUT(SVE_Link in the design) is set by FCarrier_Out.

 

RF distortions in the modulator can be simulated by setting parameters GainImbalance, PhaseImbalance, etc.

 

E-UTRA Test Models are provided in this workspace according to 3GPP TS 36.141 V8.5.0(2009-12) for both FDD and TDD. Set UseTestModel to YES, then you can select TestModel and Bandwidth to configure different ETMs. If UseTestModel is set to NO, then you can configure LTE parameters to customize the generated signal.

 

The transmitted signal mean power is set by SignalPower. SignalPower specifies the mean power of the transmitted signal when all RBs (resource blocks) are allocated. For example, when Bandwidth is set to 10 MHz, and FullRB_Alloc is set to YES, i.e. all 50 RBs are allocated for UE1, then the mean power of the transmitted signal would be around SignalPower. Note that the measured signal power may be a little lower than SignalPower as there are some non-allocated REs in the PDCCH symbols. If FullRB_Alloc is set to NO, StartRB = 0 and NumRBs = 25, i.e. only 25 RBs (half of the total RBs) are allocated for UE1, then the mean power of the transmitted signal would be 3dB lower than SignalPower.

FullRB_Alloc indicates whether all RBs are allocated for UE1. If FullRB_Alloc is set to NO, RB allocation is defined by StartRB and NumRBs.

 

The ideal low pass filter for spectrum shaping can be turned on/off by parameter EnableTxFilter. The number of taps can be set by FIR_Taps. If EnableTxFilter is set to NO, no spectrum shaping would be applied.

 

The number of simulated frames for EVM measurements is set by parameter NumFrames.

 

SaveConstellation specifies whether to save constellation data (YES) for display or not (NO).

 

Please note that those parameters with hide condition set to true will not be shown in ADS/GoldenGate environment.

 

Try to change the parameters, run LTE_BS_Tx_Analysis and check the simulation results.

  • Table EVM lists EVM of each physical channel and signal according to section 6.5 of 3GPP TS 36.104
  • Graph NormalizedEqualizerChannelFrequencyResponse shows the normalized equalizer channel frequency response got from EVM model
  • Graph RBErrorMagSpectrum shows the error magnitude spectrum of each RB got from EVM model
  • Graph Spectrum shows the spectrum of the transmitted signal
  • Graph Waveform shows the transmitted time domain waveform

Workspace.Name: 3GPP_LTE_UE_AdjacentChannelSelectivity
Workspace.Description:
3GPP_LTE_UE_ AdjacentChannelSelectivity

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This workspace provides a VTB test bench of Adjacent Channel Selectivity (ACS) of LTE user equipment receiver according to section 7.5 of 3GPP TS 36.101. Adjacent Channel Selectivity (ACS) is a measure of a receiver's ability to receive a E-UTRA signal at its assigned channel frequency in the presence of an adjacent channel signal at a given frequency offset from the centre frequency of the assigned channel. ACS is the ratio of the receive filter attenuation on the assigned channel frequency to the receive filter attenuation on the adjacent channel(s).

 

The center frequency of the input signal to DUT (SVE_Link in the design) is set by FCarrier_In, while center frequency of the output signal from DUT (SVE_Link in the design) is set by FCarrier_Out.

 

RF distortions in the modulator can be simulated by setting parameters GainImbalance, PhaseImbalance, etc.

 

An AddNDensity model with NDensity = -173.975dBm is used to introduce thermal noise for room temperature (T = 300K). The noise figure is set by parameter NF.

 

The wanted signal mean power is set by parameter P_WantedSig, while the interfering signal mean power is set by parameter P_Interferer.  P_WantedSig and P_Interferer specifies the mean power of the wanted signal and interfering signal when all RBs (resource blocks) are allocated.

 

The ideal lowpass filter for spectrum shaping can be turned on/off for both wanted signal and interfering signal by parameter EnableTxFilter. The number of taps can be set by FIR_Taps. If EnableTxFilter is set to NO, no spectrum shaping would be applied.

The interfering signal center frequency offset is set by parameter Foffset_Interferer. Foffset_Interferer<0 indicates the center frequency of the interferer is lower than center frequency of the wanted signal by Foffset_Interferer, otherwise, the center frequency of the interferer is higher than the center frequency of the wanted signal by Foffset_Interferer. FCarrier_Interferer = FCarrier_In + Foffset_Interferer.

The bandwidth of the interfering signal is determined by the bandwidth of the wanted signal according to Table 7.5.1-2 ~ Table 7.5.1-3, i.e. if Bandwidth of the wanted signal is smaller than 5MHz, the interfering signal would have same bandwidth as the wanted signal, otherwise, the bandwidth of the interfering signal is 5MHz.

HARQ retransmission can be enabled by setting UE1_HARQ_Enable to YES. When HARQ retransmission is enabled, EnableTxFilter should be set to NO as ideal lowpass filter is not supported in HARQ retransmission in current SystemVue version. Number of HARQ processes is 8 for FDD and 7 for TDD. Maximum number of HARQ transmissions is set to 4. The redundancy version sequence is set to [0,1,2,3].

A Parks-McClellan bandpass filter centered at FCarrier_Out is used in the receiver side. The PassBandwidth is set to the transmission bandwidth of the wanted signal, and the StopBandwidth is set to the channel bandwidth. For example, if Bandwidth of wanted signal is 5MHz, then PassBandwidth = 4.5MHz, StopBandwidth = 5MHz. This filter could be disabled by setting parameter EnableRxFilter to NO.

By default, the reference measurement channels specified in Annexes A.3.2 of 3GPP TS 36.101 are used. If you want to customized the test configuration, please set UseFRC to NO and set the payload configuration and RB allocation.

Please note that those parameters with hide condition set to true will not be shown in ADS/GoldenGate environment.

Try to change the parameters, run LTE_UE_AdjacentChannelSelectivity_Analysis and check the simulation results in table ThroughputFraction to see whether the throughput meets the requirements. The throughput shall be ≥ 95% of the maximum throughput of the reference measurement channels as specified in Annexes A.3.2 of 3GPP TS 36.101.

Workspace.Name: 3GPP_LTE_UE_ReferenceSensitivity
Workspace.Description:
3GPP_LTE_UE_ReferenceSensitivity

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This workspace provides a VTB test bench of reference sensitivity power level of LTE UE receiver according to section 7.3 of 3GPP TS 36.101. The reference sensitivity power level REFSENS is the minimum mean power applied to both the UE antenna ports at which the throughput shall meet or exceed the requirements for the specified reference measurement channel.

 

The center frequency of the input signal to DUT (SVE_Link in the design) is set by FCarrier_In, while center frequency of the output signal from DUT (SVE_Link in the design) is set by FCarrier_Out.

 

RF distortions in the modulator can be simulated by setting parameters GainImbalance, PhaseImbalance, etc.

 

An AddNDensity model with NDensity = -173.975dBm is used to introduce thermal noise for room temperature (T = 300K). The noise figure is set by parameter NF.

 

The transmitted signal mean power is set by SignalPower. SignalPower specifies the mean power of the transmitted signal when all RBs (resource blocks) are allocated. In this example, by default, all RBs are always allocated no matter which Bandwidth is selected. Hence, the mean power of the input signal to the DUT (SVE_Link in the design) would be around SignalPower. Note that the mean power is a little lower than SignalPower, which is due to there are some non-allocated REs in the PDCCH symbols.

 

The ideal lowpass filter for spectrum shaping can be turned on/off by parameter EnableTxFilter. The number of taps can be set by FIR_Taps. If EnableTxFilter is set to NO, no spectrum shaping would be applied.

 

HARQ retransmission can be enabled by setting UE1_HARQ_Enable to YES. When HARQ retransmission is enabled, EnableTxFilter should be set to NO as ideal lowpass filter is not supported in HARQ retransmission in current SystemVue version. Number of HARQ processes is 8 for FDD and 7 for TDD. Maximum number of HARQ transmissions is set to 4. The redundancy version sequence is set to [0,1,2,3].

 

By default, the reference measurement channels specified in Annexes A.3.2 of 3GPP TS 36.101 are used. If you want to customized the test configuration, please set UseFRC to NO and set the payload configuration, RB allocation and PDCCH configuration.

 

Please note that those parameters with hide condition set to true will not be shown in ADS/GoldenGate environment.

 

Try to change the parameters, run 3GPP_LTE_UE_ReferenceSensitivity_Analysis and check the simulation results in table ThroughputFraction to see whether the throughput meets the requirements. The throughput shall be ≥ 95% of the maximum throughput of the reference measurement channels as specified in Annexes A.3.2 of 3GPP TS 36.101.

Workspace.Name: LTE_Advanced_BS_CA_Tx
Workspace.Description:
LTE-Advanced Base Station Carrier Aggregation Tx Characteristics

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Workspace

 

This VTB design measures LTE Advanced base station transmitter characteristics with carrier aggregation, including spectrum, waveform, CCDF, EVM and ACLR according to 3GPP TS 36.104.

 

The center frequency of the input signal to DUT(SVE_Link in the design) is set by FCarrier_In, while center frequency of the output signal from DUT(SVE_Link in the design) is set by FCarrier_Out.

 

The sampling rate of the aggregated signal is explicitly specified by OutputSampleRate. Make sure the sampling rate is sufficient to analyze the aggregated signal and can be handled by SystemVue simulation. Large OutputSampleRate would significantly slow down the simulation. The transmitted signal of each component carrier would be resampled and combined in model SignalCombiner. Also please make sure OutputSampleRate is multiple of the base sample rate of each component carrier.

 

Up to 5 component carriers are supported. The frequency offset (from FCarrier_In) of each component carrier (CC) is set by CC0_FreqOffset, CC1_FreqOffset, CC2_FreqOffset, CC3_FreqOffset and CC4_FreqOffset respectively. By setting those frequency offsets, this design can generate either contiguous or noncontiguous aggregated signal either intra-band or inter-band. Again, please make sure OutputSampleRate is sufficient to analyze the aggregated signal.

 

Component carrier 0 would always be transmitted, while other component carriers can be turned off by set CC#_Enable to NO. Each component carrier can be configured independently. By default, only two component carriers are enabled.

 

The ideal lowpass filter for spectrum shaping can be turned on/off by parameter EnableTxFilter. The number of taps can be set by FIR_Taps. If EnableTxFilter is set to NO, no spectrum shaping would be applied. The same spectrum shaping is implemented for each component carrier.

 

Users can select one component carrier for EVM measurement by setting parameter CCToMeas. It should be set in the range [0,4]. By default, a ParksMcClellan bandpass filter is used before EVM measurement. This filter can be disabled by setting EnableRxFilter to NO.

 

Please note that those parameters with hide condition set to true will not be shown in ADS/GoldenGate environment.

 

Try to change the parameters, run LTE_Advanced_BS_CA_Tx_Analysis and check the simulation results.

  • Table ACLR shows Adjacent Channel Leakage power Ratio as defined in section 6.6.2 of 3GPP TS 36.104. For this workspace, ACLR is valid only for contiguous spectrum of Carrier Aggregation with the measurement to the lowest and the highest component carrier. 
  • Graph CCDF shows the Complementary Cumulative Distribution Function of the transmitted signal
  • Graph Constellation shows the constellation of each physical channel and signal of component carrier 0
  • Table Error Summary shows average EVM, peak EVM, frequency errors and other measured results of each frame of component carrier 0
  • Table EVM lists EVM of each physical channel and signal of component carrier 0 according to section 6.5 of 3GPP TS 36.104
  • Graph NormalizedEqualizerChannelFrequencyResponse shows the normalized equalizer channel frequency response of component carrier 0
  • Graph RBErrorMagSpectrum shows the error magnitude spectrum of each RB of component carrier 0
  • Graph Spectrum shows the spectrum of the aggregated signal
  • Graph Waveform shows the transmitted time domain waveform

Workspace.Name: LTE_Advanced_UE_CA_Tx_Source
Workspace.Description:
LTE-Advanced Uplink Carrier Aggregation Tx Source

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Workspace

 

This VTB workspace is used to generate LTE-Advanced uplink carrier aggregation signal

 

 

The center frequency of the input signal to DUT(SVE_Link in the design) is set by FCarrier_In, while center frequency of the output signal from DUT(SVE_Link in the design) is set by FCarrier_Out.

 

The sampling rate of the aggregated signal is explicitly specified by OutputSampleRate. Make sure the sampling rate is sufficient to analyze the aggregated signal and can be handled by SystemVue simulation. Large OutputSampleRate would significantly slow down the simulation. The transmitted signal of each component carrier would be resampled and combined in model SignalCombiner. Also please make sure OutputSampleRate is multiple of the base sample rate of each component carrier.

 

Up to 5 component carriers are supported. The frequency of each component carrier (CC) is set by CC0_FCarrier, CC1_FCarrier, CC2_FCarrier, CC3_FCarrier and CC4_FCarrier respectively. By setting those center frequencies, this design can generate either contiguous or noncontiguous aggregated signal either intra-band or inter-band. Again, please make sure OutputSampleRate is sufficient to analyze the aggregated signal. 

 

Component carrier 0 would always be transmitted, while other component carriers can be turned off by set CC#_Enable to NO. Each component carrier can be configured independently.

 

The ideal lowpass filter for spectrum shaping can be turned on/off by parameter EnableTxFilter. The number of taps can be set by FIR_Taps. If EnableTxFilter is set to NO, no spectrum shaping would be applied. The same spectrum shaping is implemented for each component carrier.

 

A sink is used to save the generated signal from 0 to TimeStop.

 

Please note that those parameters with hide condition set to '1' will not be shown in ADS/GoldenGate environment.

 

Try to change the parameters, run LTE_Advanced_UE_CA_Tx_SouceOnly_Analysis and check the simulation results.

Workspace.Name: WLAN_802.11ac_AdjacentChannelRejection
Workspace.Description:
WLAN_802.11ac_AdjacentChannelRejection

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This workspace provides a VTB test bench to analyze Rx adjacent channel rejection of the 802.11ac one antenna receiver. Adjacent channel rejection for W MHz channels (where W is 20, 40, 80 or 160) shall be measured by setting the desired signal’s strength 3 dB above the rate dependent sensitivity specified in Table 22-21 (Receiver minimum input level sensitivity) of IEEE P802.11ac™/D1.0 and raising the power of the interfering signal of W MHz bandwidth until 10% PER is caused for a PSDU length of 4096 octets. The power difference between the interfering and desired channel is the corresponding adjacent channel rejection. The center frequency of the adjacent channel shall be placed W MHz away from the center frequency of the desired signal.

 

The center frequency of the input signal to DUT (SVE_Link in the design) is set by FCarrier_In, while center frequency of the output signal from DUT (SVE_Link in the design) is set by FCarrier_Out.

 

The wanted signal mean power is set by parameter P_WantedSig, while the interfering signal mean power is set by parameter P_InterferingSig.

 

A Butterworth IIR bandpass filter centered at FCarrier_Out is used in the receiver side. The PassBandwidth is set to the bandwidth of the wanted signal, the PassAtten is set to 3 and Order is set to 5. This filter could be disabled by setting parameter EnableRxFilter to NO.

An AddNDensity model with NDensity = -173.975dBm is used to introduce thermal noise for room temperature (T = 300K). The noise figure is set by parameter NF.

 

RF distortions can be introduced by setting parameters GainImbalance, PhaseImbalance, etc.

The number of frames to be simulated is specified by NumFrames.

 

Try to change the parameters, run WLAN_802.11ac_ACR_Analysis and check the simulation results in table FER to see whether the FER meets the requirements. The FER shall be ≤ 10%.

The center frequency of the nonadjacent channel shall be placed 2×W MHz or more away from the center frequency of the desired signal.

 

The center frequency of the input signal to DUT (SVE_Link in the design) is set by FCarrier_In, while center frequency of the output signal from DUT (SVE_Link in the design) is set by FCarrier_Out.

 

The wanted signal mean power is set by parameter P_WantedSig, while the interfering signal mean power is set by parameter P_InterferingSig. 

 

A Butterworth IIR bandpass filter centered at FCarrier_Out is used in the receiver side. The PassBandwidth is set to the bandwidth of the wanted signal, the PassAtten is set to 3 and Order is set to 5. This filter could be disabled by setting parameter EnableRxFilter to NO.

An AddNDensity model with NDensity = -173.975dBm is used to introduce thermal noise for room temperature (T = 300K). The noise figure is set by parameter NF.

 

RF distortions can be introduced by setting parameters GainImbalance, PhaseImbalance, etc.

The number of frames to be simulated is specified by NumFrames.

 

Try to change the parameters, run WLAN_802.11ac_NonACR_Analysis and check the simulation results in table FER to see whether the FER meets the requirements. The FER shall be ≤ 10%.

Workspace.Description:
WLAN_11ac_ReferenceSensitivity

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This workspace provides test bench to analyze receiver minimum input sensitivity of the 802.11ac signals. The packet error rate (PER) shall be less than 10% for a PSDU length of 4096 octets with the rate-dependent input levels listed in Table 22-21 (Receiver minimum input level sensitivity) of IEEE P802.11ac/D1.0, "Part 11: Wireless LAN Medium Access Control (MAC) and Physical Layer (PHY) specifications", May 2011. The test applies to non-STBC modes, 800 ns GI and BCC.

 

For example, for 80MHz, 64QAM, Rate 2/3, the minimum input level sensitivity is -60 dBm.

 

The center frequency of the input signal to DUT (SVE_Link in the design) is set by FCarrier_In, while center frequency of the output signal from DUT (SVE_Link in the design) is set by FCarrier_Out.

 

The transmitted signal mean power is set by SignalPower.

 

An AddNDensity model with NDensity = -173.975dBm is used to introduce thermal noise for room temperature (T = 300K). The noise figure is set by parameter NF.

 

RF distortions can be introduced by setting parameters GainImbalance, PhaseImbalance, etc.

The number of frames to be simulated is specified by NumFrames.

 

Try to change the parameters, run WLAN11ac_ReferenceSensitivity_Analysis and check the simulation results in table FER to see whether the FER meets the requirements. FER should be ≤ 10%.

Workspace.Name: WLAN_11ad_RxSensitivity
Workspace.Description:
WLAN_11ad_RxSensitivity

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This workspace provides a VTB test bench of reference sensitivity power level of WLAN 11ad receiver according to section 21.3.3 of IEEE P802.11ad/D4.0, July 2011. The reference sensitivity power level PREFSENS is the minimum mean power received at the antenna connector at which a PER requirement shall be met for a specified MCS.   

 

The center frequency of the input signal to DUT (SVE_Link in the design) is set by FCarrier_In, while center frequency of the output signal from DUT (SVE_Link in the design) is set by FCarrier_Out.

 

RF distortions can be introduced by setting parameters GainImbalance, PhaseImbalance, etc.

An AddNDensity model with NDensity = -173.975dBm is used to introduce thermal noise for room temperature (T = 300K). The noise figure is set to 10.

 

In this example, the output signal from WLAN_11ad_Source is the 1x-sampled complex baseband signals. Then the signal is oversampled in the filter models with the oversample ratio specified in the OversampleOption parameter. With the default, the pre-configured filter types for both SC and OFDM modulation are as follows:

  • SC: RaisedCosine filter with SymbolRate = 1.76e9 Hz, RollOff (Alpha) = 0.5
  • OFDM: Flat Top filter with PassFreq = 2.5e9 Hz, Order = 96

A bandpass Chebyshev II filter centered at FCarrier_Out is used in the receiver side. The PassBandwidth is set to the bandwidth of the wanted signal and the StopRipple is set to 50.

The transmitted signal mean power is set by SignalPower. 

 

Please note that those parameters with hide condition set to true will not be shown in ADS/GoldenGate environment.

 

User can modify the following parameters as defined in the "Parameter" tab of the "SISO_BER" design to set different signal configurations and run SISO_BER_Analysis and check the simulation results.

  • FCarrier_In and FCarrier_Out: the RF central carrier.
  • SignalPower: received signal power at the receiver antenna.
  • MCS: modulation and coding Scheme.
  • PSDU_Len: the PHY PSDU length in octets. For MCS 0, PSDU_Len should be set to 256 otherwise 4096.
  • FramesToMeas: the number of frames used for test.

 

For MCS0, the PER shall be less than 5% for a PSDU length of 256 octets. For the other MCSs, the PER shall be less than 1% for a PSDU length of 4096 octets.

 

Table 21-3 of the section 21.3.3.9 of IEEE P802.11ad/D4.0, July 2011 listed the MCS dependent input levels. It assumes 5 dB implementation loss and 10 dB noise factor (Noise Figure).

But in the current implementation, for some MCS cases (MCS 13 ~ 24), the implementation loss of the receiver is more than 5 dB which specified in the standard and for other cases, the implementation is less than 5 dB. Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This workspace provides test bench to analyze receiver minimum input sensitivity of the 802.11ax signals. The packet error rate (PER) shall be less than 10% for a PSDU length of 2048 octets for BPSK DCM enabled case and 4096 octets for other cases with the rate-dependent input levels listed in Table 28-46 (Receiver minimum input level sensitivity) of IEEE P802.11ax/D2.0, "Part 11: Wireless LAN Medium Access Control (MAC) and Physical Layer (PHY) specifications", October 2017. The test applies to non-STBC modes, 800 ns GI, BCC for 20MHz and LDPC for other bandwidth in SU cases.

 

For example, for 20MHz, 16QAM, Rate 1/2, DCM disabled the minimum input level sensitivity is -74 dBm.

In this example, DCM, GI type and MPDUDataLength are set in the equation. They can be changed if necessary.

 

The center frequency of the input signal to DUT (SVE_Link in the design) is set by FCarrier_In, while center frequency of the output signal from DUT (SVE_Link in the design) is set by FCarrier_Out.

 

The transmitted signal mean power is set by SignalPower.

 

An AddNDensity model with NDensity = -173.975dBm is used to introduce thermal noise for room temperature (T = 300K). The noise figure is set by parameter NF.

 

RF distortions can be introduced by setting parameters GainImbalance, PhaseImbalance, etc.

The number of frames to be simulated is specified by NumFrames.

 

Try to change the parameters, run WLAN11ac_ReferenceSensitivity_Analysis and check the simulation results in table FER to see whether the FER meets the requirements. FER should be ≤ 10%.

Workspace.Name: WLAN_802.11ax_Source
Workspace.Description:
WLAN_802.11ax_Tx_Source

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This workspace provides a VTB test bench to generate WLAN 802.11ax signal.

 

The center frequency of the input signal to DUT (SVE_Link in the design) is set by FCarrier_In, while center frequency of the output signal from DUT (SVE_Link in the design) is set by FCarrier_Out.

 

The transmitted signal mean power is set by SignalPower.

 

The number of OFDM data symbols in each frame is dertermined by CodingType and MPDUDataLength.

 

RF distortions can be introduced by setting parameters GainImbalance, PhaseImbalance, etc.

A sink is used to save the generated signal from 0 to TimeStop.

 

Try to change the parameters, run WLAN11ax_Tx_1Ant_SourceOnly_Analysis and check the simulation results.

Workspace.Name: WLAN_802.11ax_Tx
Workspace.Description:
WLAN_802.11ax_Tx

Keysight Technologies SystemVue Example Workspace

 

This workspace provides a VTB test bench to analyze the CCDF, Constellation, EVM, PAPR, spectrum and waveform of the signal generated by WLAN 802.11ax single antenna transmitter.

DCM is set to disabled in equation and MCS mask is also for DCM disabled cases. 

 

The center frequency of the input signal to DUT (SVE_Link in the design) is set by FCarrier_In, while center frequency of the output signal from DUT (SVE_Link in the design) is set by FCarrier_Out.

 

The transmitted signal mean power is set by SignalPower.

 

The number of OFDM data symbols in each frame is dertermined by CodingType and MPDUDataLength.

 

RF distortions can be introduced by setting parameters GainImbalance, PhaseImbalance, etc.

 

The number of frames for EVM measurements is specified by NumFrame.

 

SaveConstellation specifies whether to save constellation data (YES) for display or not (NO).

 

Try to change the parameters, run WLAN11ax_Tx_1Ant_Analysis and check the simulation results.

  • Graph Tx_CCDF shows the Complementary Cumulative Distribution Function of the transmitted signal
  • Graph Tx_Constellation shows the constellation of physical channel and signal when parameter SaveConstellation is set to YES.
    •
  • Table Tx_EVM lists average EVM and EVM for each frame
  • Table Tx_PAPR shows the Peak to Average Power Ratio
  • Graph Tx_Spectrum shows the spectrum of the transmitted signal
  • Graph Tx_SpectrumMask shows whether the transmit spectrum mask is met
  • Graph Tx_Waveform shows the transmitted time domain waveform

Note:

In WLAN_11ax_Source, you can use the parameter StationID_UE to set Station ID for each user. When you set the value 2046 for one user, it will be disabled and no data load is on this user's RU.

If you disable most users of all, it will cause the power of HE-DATA is low. In this case, some frames may be misdetected for EVM analysis. In order to detect more frames for EVM analysis, you can enable more users.
